The Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 5, verse 1:

The Truth (al-Haqq) chooses a beautiful connection, so the Exalted and Sublime begins this surah with His saying:

﴿O you who have believed, fulfill [all] contracts. Lawful for you are the animals of grazing livestock except for that which is recited to you, but not hunting while you are in the state of ihram. Indeed, Allah ordains what He wills.﴾ (1)

The beginning, then, is about the necessity of fulfilling contracts and the permissibility of consuming the animals of grazing livestock (bahimat al-an'am) as food. As we know, Surat al-Ma'idah comes in the Mushaf arrangement after Surat al-Nisa', which contains many contracts of faith (al-'uqud al-imaniyyah). Surat al-Nisa' included the contracts of marriage (al-inkah), dower (al-sadaq), bequest (al-wasiyyah), debt (al-dayn), and inheritance (al-mirath), all of which are rulings on contracts. It is as if the Truth, the Exalted and Sublime, after Surat al-Nisa' says to us: You have come to know what contracts are in Surat al-Nisa', so preserve them and fulfill them.

We observe that Surat al-Baqarah was followed by Surat Al 'Imran, and in both there is discussion of the materialistic Jews. Surat al-Nisa' and al-Ma'idah also address the civil society of Medina, after the Qur'an in Mecca had been addressing the matter of nurturing and planting the one divine belief (al-'aqidah al-ilahiyyah al-wahidah) and the prophethoods. Surat al-Baqarah and Surat Al 'Imran served the matter of methodical belief (al-'aqidah al-manhajiyyah) and the prophets, while Surat al-Nisa' contains the settling of the belief in judgment (al-'aqidah al-hukmiyyah).

Here we are before Surat al-Ma'idah, in which the Truth says: "O you who have believed, fulfill [all] contracts." The Truth addresses the believers by the relative pronoun (al-ism al-mawsul) and did not say: "O believers." This indicates that faith is not a passing matter that comes over a person for a period of time; rather, faith is something renewed with the renewal of action, when the believer implements the rulings brought by the contract of faith. And when the Truth directs His address to those who have believed, it confirms to us that He does not intrude upon anyone's life in order to burden him, even though He, the Exalted, as Lord of the worlds, has created the creation, brought existence into being, and subjected it to the creatures.

The Exalted and Sublime did not use this Truth to command mankind to believe; rather, He first called people, all of them, to faith. Whoever believes, the honor of responsibility (al-taklif) descends upon him, and the true saying becomes: "O you who have believed," meaning: O you who have affirmed belief in Allah as God. And the God must have attributes befitting divinity, such as absolute power, majesty, wisdom, and dominance. He, the Exalted, does not impose responsibility on one who has not believed in Him; rather, He calls the one who has not believed to faith. For this reason we find that all the verses of rulings begin with the true saying: "O you who have believed, prescribed for you," because for every faith there is a consequence.

"O you who have believed, fulfill [all] contracts." We know that language has a family of words. "Awfu" (fulfill), for example, has "wafa" (to fulfill), and its present form is "yafi," and among its verbs are "awfa" and "wafa," according to the different stages of strength and weakness, abundance and scarcity. An example of this is His saying, the Truth:

﴿And [of] Abraham who fulfilled [his commitments]﴾ (Surat al-Najm, 37). Our master Abraham, peace be upon him, accomplished many achievements: ﴿And [mention] when Abraham was tried by his Lord with commandments and he fulfilled them﴾ (part of verse 124, Surat al-Baqarah).

His saying, the Truth, "And [of] Abraham who fulfilled," must be an explanation of what Abraham did in facing trial. So "wafa'" (fulfillment) is completion (al-itmam), and the Truth says: "O you who have believed, fulfill [all] contracts," meaning: upon you, O you who have believed in Allah, is that you complete the contracts. Completion either extends to individuals and includes them, so that no individual is lacking, or it turns to the modes, so that no mode is disrupted. This is completion. A person may come with all the chapters of a book and read them, thereby having fulfilled the reading of all the parts; but the Truth wants a person to perfect the execution of every detail in the book of responsibility.

He, the Exalted, has asked us to bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, to establish prayer, to give zakat, to fast Ramadan, and to perform the pilgrimage to the House for whoever is able to find a way to it. A person may perform all these acts and thereby have discharged the responsibility; but there is another person who performs each part in its entirety, without abbreviating any of it, rather he fulfills it without deceit.

The Truth here addresses the believers: "O you who have believed, fulfill [all] contracts," meaning that we are before "faith" and "contract." We have explained the meaning of faith. As for the contract (al-'aqd), it is the documented relationship between two parties, and each party must abide by what is upon him and take what is his. The contract is called "'aqd" because 'aqd is the tying of anything such that it does not come undone afterward. For this reason we call what settles in people's perceptions and souls "'aqidah" (creed), because it is the tied matter, not the passing matter that comes today and ends tomorrow. In the view of jurisprudence (al-fiqh), the tied thing is the matter that does not float up to the mind to be investigated anew, but rather is settled and fixed in the heart. The Exalted commands the fulfillment of contracts, and the contracts, as we know, are the plural of "'aqd." In Islam there are many contracts, beginning with the first contract, the contract of the primordial covenant (al-dharr):

﴿And [mention] when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants and made them testify of themselves, [saying], "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we have testified."﴾ (part of verse 172, Surat al-A'raf).

He, the Exalted, desires the fulfillment of this first covenant, so that a person does not, at the hour of application, flee from it. Then we come to the covenant of vicegerency on earth (al-istikhlaf fi al-ard), by which Adam and his descendants after him were made vicegerents upon it. Beware of thinking that you are the origin in the cosmos when the causes persist for you and some things submit to you for a time. Do not think that things have submitted to you by your skill alone. When you sow seeds in the earth and water the earth, know that the crop grows by Allah's subjugation of His earth to you.

Beware, for a moment when you mount the colt, of thinking that you are the horseman who tamed the colt. Rather, it is the Truth's subjugation of the horse to you. Sometimes the horse bolts, so that the rider falls from its back. Let us pay attention to the detail that must not be absent from us: had Allah not made the horses submissive to us, we would not have been able to ride them.

﴿Do they not see that We have created for them from what Our hands have made grazing livestock, so they are their owners? And We have subjugated them to them, so some of them they ride and some of them they eat.﴾ (Surat Ya-Sin, 71–72)

And the believer must also remember that the Truth, the Exalted, subjected the camel to its owner, and made a small child command the camel so that it lies down on the ground, to place heavy loads upon it, and commands it so that it stands up. But if it encounters a serpent or a snake, it does not dare to subdue them. This is a reminder from the Truth to the creation of His absolute power, for He subjected the large one to them while frightening them many times over with the small-bodied serpent.

﴿And We have subjugated them to them, so some of them they ride and some of them they eat.﴾ (Surat Ya-Sin, 72)

From subjugation comes the submission of the rest of the creatures to man. The donkey, in the hands of the farmer, carries the manure to the land from the remains of human and animal waste, and the donkey does not speak in objection. The farmer rises in his life and becomes a village watchman (shaykh al-khafar); he orders the donkey to be bathed, buys it a saddle to ride to meet the official at the center, and the donkey has not disobeyed in either situation. This is subjugation.

Beware of thinking that your skill alone, O human, is what subjected the creatures to you. If the matter depended on skill alone, a human would subdue the small flea that attacks him at any time, and that small flea may frighten you all night, and an entire family may stay up for the sake of killing a single flea.

﴿The seeker and the sought are weak﴾ (part of verse 73, Surat al-Hajj).

Therefore the Truth has commanded us to say before beginning any work, "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful." Beware of approaching work by your strength alone; work is only made to obey you because He, the Exalted, has subjected it to you, and you begin work in the name of Allah because He, the Exalted, is the One who made you vicegerent and subjected to you the subjugated creatures.

Then there is that covenant in which the Truth said to Adam: ﴿Whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor suffer﴾ (part of verse 123, Surat Ta-Ha).

And the covenant in which the Truth said: ﴿Whoever follows My guidance, there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve﴾ (part of verse 38, Surat al-Baqarah).

This is a covenant for all mankind. The Muslims pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, at al-'Aqabah that they would support him and protect him from what they protect themselves from, and they pledged to the Messenger at al-Hudaybiyah.

Indeed the Exalted Truth commands the fulfillment of all contracts, and everything that results from the summit of creeds, which is faith in Allah. Whatever comes from Allah in which you believe is considered a contract in which you are a partner, because a contract is always between two parties, and Allah did not compel anyone to believe in Him, but man believes in Allah by choice. And since the believer has believed in Allah by his own free choice, he must follow His method.

The one who believes is the one who goes to the Truth saying: "O Lord, what You command, I will do." This is an acknowledgment of the contract, and writing any faith-based contract is its implementation, and the signing with Allah. Thereby the servant shares with Allah in this mutual agreement, because the servant's faith in Allah makes him a party to the contract.

God legislates for him, and the servant implements the legislation in order to receive the fullest reward.

The contract, then, may be between the servant and his Lord, or between the servant and the creatures of Allah who are equal to him, or between the servant and himself. But they have applied to the contract between a person and himself the name "'ahd" (covenant), which is a vow: for example, the servant vows to fast or to pray, and it is obligatory upon the servant to carry out what he has vowed, as long as he has covenanted with Allah on that. The contract between the servant and other men, and likewise the contract between him and himself, both stem from the foundational contract, which is the first contract: faith in Allah.

Thus the saying of the Truth, "Fulfill [all] contracts," means: carry out what Allah has commanded, as lawful, and abstain from what the Truth has made unlawful. There is no need, then, to dispute the meaning of "contracts" or to ask: are they the contracts between the servant and his Lord, or between the servant and people, or between the servant and himself? Every contract that flows from the summit contract is a contract upon the believer and an obligation upon him to fulfill it. "O you who have believed, fulfill [all] contracts. Lawful for you are the animals of grazing livestock." The Exalted opens the surah with the fulfillment of contracts, then the declaration of the permissibility of the animals of grazing livestock. We know that man arrived upon the cosmos after it, and that the Exalted created the cosmos first and then created man in it. This is from Allah's mercy toward man: He did not create man first, but created the sun for him and prepared the cosmos before man was created. When man arrived upon the cosmos, he found in it the sustenance of life: from the inanimate, from plants, and from animals.

The summit of things subjected to man is the animal, because the inanimate and plants serve the animal, and the animal shares with man that it has life, blood, and limbs. The Truth here announces the highest rank in service to man, which is the animals of grazing livestock: "Lawful for you are the animals of grazing livestock," and He commands us to fulfill the contracts, and to Him, the Exalted and Sublime, belongs all right. He has presented us the price by creating the cosmos subjected to us, and the summit of subjected creatures is the livestock. Thus "Lawful for you are the animals of grazing livestock" is a preceding justification from the Truth. We note that it came here in the passive voice in "uhilla" (were made lawful), because faith made us a party to the animals of grazing livestock being lawful to us.

The scholars paused at "bahimat al-an'am." In the Arabic language we find the pattern "fa'il" which comes in the sense of "fa'il" (active) and comes in the sense of "maf'ul" (passive), as when we say "Allah is Raheem" meaning He is merciful: He is the active one (fa'il). And we say "so-and-so is qatil" meaning killed, that is, passive object (maf'ul bihi). "Bahimat al-an'am" here may carry either meaning. Is it in the sense of the active or the passive? If we consider that it is "mubhamah" (ambiguous/obscure) because its affairs are unknown and hard for us to grasp, we do not know its movements, its signals, or its languages by which it communicates, then it would be "fa'ilah" in the sense of "maf'ulah," and it could also be "fa'ilah" in the sense of "fa'il," because it does not understand us and we are the ones who are obscure to it. We say: it is governed by subjugation.

Man did not classify its food, which is fodder, except after he saw it free and unrestrained heading toward the fodder to eat it. So it was the one that taught man the category of its food. Let no person say: it is a beast that does not understand; let him know that it was not created to understand human affairs, since it is subjected to him, and he may learn from it.

Our evidence is that Allah bestowed favor upon some of His chosen creatures by teaching them the speech of birds. The hoopoe was distressed when it saw the queen of Sheba and her people prostrating to the sun instead of Allah, and it being a bird, it understood...

And after that, the Truth says:

﴿O you who believe, do not violate the rites of Allah, nor the sacred month, nor the offering, nor the garlands, nor those coming to the Sacred House seeking bounty from their Lord and good pleasure. And when you have come out of the state of ihram, then hunt. And do not let the hatred of a people, because they blocked you from al-Masjid al-Haram, incite you to transgress. And cooperate in righteousness and piety, but do not cooperate in sin and aggression. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is severe in punishment.﴾

At the beginning of this verse He says: "O you who believe, do not violate the rites of Allah." It comes after a verse that made things lawful, as if the Truth is saying to the servant: as long as I have given you, I also withhold from you. I have given you things and withheld other things from you. When Allah, glorified is He, forbids a person something and prevents him from it, He is giving that thing to a fellow believer. Since this is the case, you cannot and should not look only at what has been taken from you, but look at what has been taken from others in relation to you.

For example, when the Truth commands: "Do not steal," you are one individual and He, glorified is He, restricts your freedom by this command, and at the same time He restricts the freedom of all people in relation to you. When you compare the command in relation to yourself, you find that you are the primary beneficiary, because all people will be applying Allah's ruling that they not steal anything from you. In this there is a service to every servant. Suppose one person steals; he will not be able to steal from everyone. Even if a thousand people steal from one person, what remains for him?

And when the Truth commands the servant not to look at the forbidden things (muharram) of others, the apparent meaning of the command is a restriction on the servant's movement. In reality, He, glorified is He, has restricted the movement of all people for the sake of this servant, and commanded them not to look at the forbidden things of others.

So, O Muslim, whenever you see a prohibition that Allah has commanded, do not direct the prohibition only at yourself, but direct it also at all people in relation to you. And when the Truth says: "O you who believe, do not violate the rites of Allah," meaning do not make the rites of Allah lawful. The rites (sha'a'ir, sing. sha'ira) are all the markers of the religion. We say, "This state's emblem is the eagle." This means that when we see the emblem we know the country, and likewise the flags of states: this is the flag of Egypt, that is the flag of England, and a third is the flag of France. Every governorate in Egypt, for example, adopts for itself an emblem and a flag. So the emblem (sha'ar) is the marker that indicates the thing. The rites of Allah are the markers of the religion of Allah, centered on "do" and "do not do," in time and place, in beliefs and rulings.

However, the term "rites" (sha'a'ir) came to be dominated by what we call the rites of Hajj. The first operation in the rites of Hajj is the ihram, meaning we must not neglect the ihram. Among the rites of Hajj is the tawaf, so do not violate the rites of Allah. It is obligatory for you to circumambulate the House, and likewise the sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwa, the standing at 'Arafat, and the stoning of the jamarat. All of these are rites of Allah, which He commanded the believers not to violate; that is, He, glorified is He, commanded them not to be negligent regarding them, because these rites are the faith-based discipline. We should consider that Allah's command to every pilgrim or umrah performer to enter ihram is a command to withdraw for a period from blessings, because a person goes for Hajj on a journey to the Benefactor. A person changes his clothes into uniform garments in which no one is distinguished over another, because in ordinary daily life people are distinguished by their attire, and clothing indicates their social positions. When they all take off their clothes and wear a uniform garment, the distinguishing mark becomes the declaration of loyalty to Allah.

Likewise, when the command comes that a person should not cut a single hair, whether he is great in his society or poor, and all people appear and look at one another, they find that they are equal despite the differences in their ranks and stations. The humility of the great is equal to the humility of the small. That is a faith-based discipline not only between a person and his equal, but a discipline with the whole cosmos, with all its kinds. The tree near the Haram is forbidden to every person to cut or to cut a part of it, and thus plants in the Haram are safe, and likewise the doves and the animals, and the person too is safe, because all are within the sanctuary of the Lord of all. That is a matter that produces a trembling and faith-based awe in the human soul. The period of Hajj is the period of faith-based discipline, in which all kinds of existence are in harmony. The human being is equal to the human being, does not touch the animal, nor the plant. And the inanimate remains, which serves all the kinds of the cosmos, because the animal serves the human, the plant serves the animal, and the inanimate serves all. It serves without being served. And the Truth ordains protection for the inanimate even within the Ka'ba itself, commanding people to touch or kiss the Black Stone if that is possible, or to gesture toward it.

So this lofty master, the human being, above plants and animals, comes to an inanimate object and venerates and honors it. The one who cannot kiss the Black Stone greets it by pointing with his hand, so that his Hajj may be accepted. Therefore people crowd to go to the Black Stone. Thus the inanimate is preserved in the Sacred House of Allah. Allah compensates it by making it a place of worship (mansak) and a rite, and making people crowd around it and kiss it, while a person does not kiss an animal or a plant. But he kisses the inanimate, the lowest of kinds. This is the peak of cosmic balance: the chosen human, exalted above the kinds, goes humbly to kiss or touch the Black Stone by the command of Allah.

And the human stones another stone, which is the symbol of Iblis, so that the human knows that stoneness is not a value in itself, but the commands of the Supreme Commander. Thus the mind of a human does not settle into glorifying a stone. The pilgrim kisses a stone, and stones another stone.

"O you who believe, do not violate the rites of Allah," because Allah made the rites to achieve faith-based discipline and to keep alive the remembrance that vicegerency belongs to Allah, so that no one claims to be原 original in the cosmos. Rather, all are servants of Allah, and the whole existence is a chain of service: the human serves the human, the animal serves the human, the plant serves the human and the animal, and the inanimate serves all. Yet no one is better than another. Indeed, the inanimate itself glorifies Allah's praise, while a human may not glorify Him.

﴿Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to bear it and feared it, and the human bore it. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant.﴾ (Surah al-Ahzab)

This command not to violate the rites of Allah makes each rite take a share of honor and respect. No one should suppose that any rite will take sanctity in itself; rather, all sanctity is granted by Allah, and Allah can take it away.

"Do not violate the rites of Allah, nor the sacred month": meaning do not make the sacred month lawful; that is, you must treat this sacred month as inviolable. Allah made it a sacred month for the benefit of humans, and by it He, glorified is He, protects the honor and humiliation of people before their enemy. It protects the brokenness of the weak before the strong. The strong man capable of fighting may feel inclined to stop warring for a period to catch his breath. If he did so, it would be a declaration of cowardice before the adversary. Therefore the Truth brings a time in which He says: "I have made war forbidden in the sacred months." Here the fighter says: "Allah has forbidden fighting in the sacred months." That is a protection for the human, and so that he may taste the pleasure of security, peace and tranquility. The strong human may come to love peace after that.

Why then did the Truth mention the sacred month here, when we know the sacred months are four? If we consider the sacred months as a genus, it applies to each of the four months. If we take the sacred month to be the months of Hajj, namely Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and the first ten nights of Dhu al-Hijjah, then the meaning is correct, and we know the sacred months are four: three consecutive, namely Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah and Muharram, and one separate, which is Rajab. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, knows that every act must have a time and must have a place. When there is no event, there is no time and no place. Time and place came into being only after Allah brought something into existence in His cosmos. Let no one say: "When was Allah, and where was Allah?" because "when" and "where" are among the creatures of Allah. He, glorified is He, made for every event a time and a place. Therefore the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, comes to protect the honor of people and to make for them, from His merciful legislation, a cover in which their weak may take shelter, and their strong may reconsider, perhaps he will desist from his error and injustice. So He established forbidden places and forbidden times. The forbidden places are those around the Haram: "And whoever enters it is safe" (Surah Al 'Imran, 97).

Here a person makes his brother secure when he enters the Haram. Likewise in time, He, glorified is He, made the sacred months.

The Truth made the event subject to time and place. In earlier times the strong would fight and draw near to victory, and when the sacred month arrived he would continue the war, then announce that the sacred month would come after the war. Therefore He, glorified is He, commands that the time of the sacred month not be changed, because Allah wants by the sacred month to end the frenzy of war.

Then the Truth says: "nor the offering." The hady is what is brought as a gift to the Haram. It is the plural of hadiyya. There are those who present a gift to the Ka'ba, and the collection of gifts is called hady. The offering for the Haram is what Allah made for the Haram. In earlier times the Haram was in a valley without cultivation, and it had few animals. They used to bring the offering with them when they performed Hajj. Therefore Allah forbade approaching the offering, because they are gifts to the Haram. The pilgrims come in many groups, and when many people come to a valley without cultivation, they need food. It is not right for a believer to make the offering something other than what it was given for. A person who has accompanied it may desire to eat meat while on the way to the Ka'ba, and so slaughters it to eat from it. This act is forbidden, because the offering came to the Haram and must be offered and presented to the Haram. A person must also protect the offering of others.

"Nor the garlands." The garlands (qala'id) are the plural of qiladah, which is what is hung around the neck. In earlier times the one going to Hajj feared that the offering would stray from him, so they would place a garland around the neck of the offering, so that whoever saw it would know it was an offering going to the Haram. The general offering is the one with no garlands around its neck. The garlands express the offering that has garlands around its neck, indicating it and showing that it is offered to the Haram. The prohibition here may even extend to making lawful the garland around the offering's neck, so that the wisdom is not lost. When the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, expresses a matter through a phrase, He expresses it in a phrase that conveys the meaning eloquently.

In earlier times, when they could not find a garland, they would take the bark of a tree and a piece of its skin, cut a piece from it, and tie it around the neck of the offering, so that people would know this is an offering going to the Haram. Allah guarantees the sustenance of the one who comes to it, not only from ordinary food but He also feeds him meat, and makes that among the rites. Is it not He who called these people to Hajj? Are these not the guests of the Most Merciful?

When one of us slaughters animals for his guests, what then of the Supreme Truth, glorified and exalted is He? Therefore He made the offering food for His guests. People crowd at Mina and 'Arafat in countless numbers, and Allah must honor them with the most delicious and best food. The poor person goes to the slaughterhouse, takes the best of the meat, dries it in the air and the sun, and stores it so he may eat from it for a long time. This is known as qadid. The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, gives the ruling in a manner of utmost eloquence: He forbids even the garland of the offering to be touched by anyone.

He, glorified is He, says: "nor the sacred month, nor the offering, nor the garlands, nor those coming to the Sacred House seeking bounty from their Lord and good pleasure." That is, do not prevent people going to the Sacred House of Allah, and do not turn them away from the way, for they are the delegation of Allah. This statement came before the Truth revealed His words:

﴿Indeed, the polytheists are unclean﴾ (Surah al-Tawbah, 28).

Non-Muslims used to perform Hajj to the Sacred House of Allah before this verse was revealed, and the ruling had not yet been issued. We ask: Do those who disbelieve in Allah seek bounty from Allah? Yes, for the bounty of Allah overspreads all, even the disbeliever

Afterwards, the Truth (God) comes with the command prohibiting certain things, following His saying, "The grazing livestock have been made lawful for you" (5:1). God wished to specify what He had made lawful from the livestock. He made lawful two of the sheep, two of the goats, two of the camels and two of the cattle. The Messenger (ﷺ) added to these the gazelles, the wild oxen, and every four-legged animal of the sea. God's saying, "except what is recited to you," indicated that there would be a prohibition to come, which the Truth would make clear through the Qur'an, identifying what God forbids.

﴿Prohibited to you are carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, that which has been dedicated to other than God, the strangled animal, the animal beaten to death, the animal that falls to its death, the animal gored to death, the animal partly eaten by a beast of prey, unless you slaughter it properly, and that which is sacrificed on stone altars, and that you seek decision by arrows. That is a transgression. Today those who disbelieved have despaired of your religion, so do not fear them but fear Me. Today I have perfected your religion for you, completed My favour upon you, and approved Islam as your religion. But whoever is compelled by severe hunger, without inclination to sin, then indeed God is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (5:3)

The verse begins with His saying, "Prohibited to you is carrion." We note that the beginning is a passive verb, although the one who prohibits is clearly God. He did not impose on anyone by force. The human being himself participated in the contract of faith with his Lord, so He obligated him, and the servant on his part committed himself. Therefore the Truth says, "Prohibited," He, glorified be He, prohibited it as God, and the servant who believed in God as his God shares in that prohibition.

Carrion (al-maytah) is that from which life has departed, or from which the soul has gone out without any destruction of the body's structure; that is, it died a natural death. The departure of life has two paths: one is death, that is, without the destruction of the structure, and the other is through destruction of the structure. When a person strangles a creature by preventing it from breathing, this is the taking of the soul by destroying something in the structure, because breathing is a necessity. A person may also take another's soul by striking it with a bullet, because the soul only dwells in a body that has special characteristics.

However, there are limbs in which the soul can remain in the body without them, such as a hand if it is cut off. But if a person's heart stops, they may open his chest and massage the heart, and it will beat again, on the condition that the brain is still alive. The maximum duration of the brain's life without air is seven minutes in rare cases. As soon as the brain is damaged, death occurs. For this reason, physicians defined clinical death as the cessation of the brain. So there is death and there is killing, and in both the soul departs.

In death, the soul departs first; in killing, the soul departs because of the destruction of the structure. Carrion is that from which life has departed without destruction of the structure. It is one of God's mercies that He prohibited carrion, because it died from a cause we do not see in any of its organs, so that we do not eat it with its disease.

Likewise, blood is prohibited. It is the fluid that flows in the veins and arteries, gives the body warmth and heat, and carries nourishment. Blood has two functions in circulation: it carries waste from the kidneys and lungs, and there is pure blood that carries nourishment. The blood vessels contain two kinds of blood: corrupt blood and sound blood. When we take this blood, it may contain the sound kind, and it may also contain the kind from which the impurities of the kidneys and lungs are expelled. For this reason it is called flowing blood (al-masfuh), that is, running. In the past, people would take it, fill the intestines of slaughtered animals with it, cook it, and eat it.

There is also blood that is not corrupt. An example is the liver, which is a single solid piece, and likewise the spleen. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Two dead things and two bloods have been made lawful for you. As for the two dead things: fish and locusts. As for the two bloods: the liver and the spleen." (1)

So the liver and spleen are exempted from blood. But as for flowing blood, it is prohibited. The wisdom in making fish and locusts lawful is that there is no flowing blood in them. There is no liquid blood in their flesh. When we cut a large fish, no blood comes out of it, but it is found only in the membranes in the head, and not in its fibres. When fish dies and is eaten, there is no harm from it, and likewise locusts.

After that comes the list of prohibitions: "the flesh of swine." Let no believer say: why did God prohibit the flesh of swine? Science has gone into every field to learn why God prohibited carrion and likewise blood, until scholars discovered that God does not want a disease to pass from a dead animal to a human being. Likewise, God prohibited blood because it contains toxic wastes, "such as urea" and others.

Every prohibition has a wisdom, which may be apparent or hidden. The Qur'an was sent down to an unlettered Messenger, in an unlettered nation that did not know highly complex scientific matters, and the first believers applied the Qur'an's teachings because the God in whom we believe as God is its wise speaker. He wants to protect His creation, and every human craftsman sets rules for protecting what he makes. We never find, for example, a furniture maker smashing a wardrobe; rather we find him exerting effort to beautify his work. As long as God is the one who created us and we believe in Him as God, we must carry out what He commands us and avoid what He forbids. This does not prevent us from seeking the causes of knowledge, out of desire to increase the causes of faith in God, and in order to respond to any meddling disputant, although no one has the right to dispute the religion of God. Whoever wishes to dispute should dispute at the summit first, which is the existence of God, and in the conveying of God's message through the Messenger. If he is convinced, he must then apply what God said. Religion cannot be examined from its tails; rather, religion is examined from its summit. We carry out God's commands. That is why we find that the first ruling does not say, "O people, it is prescribed for you…" Instead He, glorified be He, says, "O you who believe," meaning: O you who have believed in Me, take the ruling from Me.

I repeat the example I gave earlier: a person's most precious possession is his health. If his health is disturbed, he studies the causes. If food is exhausting him, he chooses a doctor of high knowledge in the digestive system, and the doctor prescribes medicine. The patient does not say to the doctor: "I will not take this medicine unless you tell me why and what this medicine will do."

So the task of reason is to arrive at the doctor in whom it has become convinced. Whatever teachings the doctor prescribes, you must carry them out. Likewise with faith in God: once a person has believed in God as his God, he must carry out the commands in the movement of life with "do" and "do not do." A patient does not argue with his doctor, so how can any human argue with his Lord, saying: "Why did You prescribe this?"

A doctor is human and may err, and may cause a patient's death. When we doubt a doctor's competence, we summon a number of doctors for broad consultation, and we carry out the doctors' orders. No one dares argue with God, glorified and exalted be He; rather we say: "All Your commands are obeyed."

We carry out the orders of doctors, so how would we not carry out the orders of God? A person places his trust in fallible humans, and so trust cannot rise above trust in the Lord of the heavens. Therefore, the wise are those who took God's commands and applied them without argument, because reason is like a mount that brings a person to the threshold of the ruler, but does not enter with you before him. When you hear from God, you carry out what He has commanded.

"Prohibited to you are carrion, blood and the flesh of swine." Analyses have shown that pork carries the tapeworm, the spiral worm, and a number of other worms that no treatment can defeat.

The prohibitions that follow: "and that which has been dedicated to other than God," meaning raising the voice in the name of other than God, as they used to say "in the name of al-Lat and al-Uzza" at the slaughter, and one does not say at the slaughter "God is greatest, in the name of God." This is because a person benefits in the universe in which he lives from the kinds of creatures that have come upon him. Man found these kinds waiting for him to serve him, because he is God's vicegerent on earth. Animals have a soul, but they fall short of humans in thinking. Plants come below animals, and inanimate matter is less than plants. When a person takes the service of the subjugated things, he must mention the Creator, the Bestower of favour. When a person slaughters an animal, he slaughters it by the permission of the Greatest, who is greater than humans, animals and the whole universe. He slaughters it in the name of the Creator.

There are those who look at meat and say: "I do not eat the flesh of animals, because I do not like slaughtering animals out of pity and mercy. I eat plants." We say: if you understood what life there is in plants, would you refrain from eating them? It has been established in our age that plants have life, and even inanimate matter has life, because when you crush a stone of flint or any kind of rock, you are, with the blows of the hammer, opposing the cohesion of the tightly bound molecules within that stone. You may do this without knowing that there is life in it.

﴿And there is not a thing but that it exalts Him with His praise﴾ (17:44).

The righteous servants of God know this, and they conduct their work and their dealings with all other creatures, whether animal or inanimate, as things that glorify God. Therefore they do not degrade things, nor do they despise them however small or insignificant. Rather they treat them gently. Even if they slaughter an animal, they show mercy to that animal: they do not sharpen the knife in front of it, nor slaughter one animal in front of another. Moreover, they feed and water what they intend to slaughter, because they know that it glorifies God. Yet they do to it what they do because God has permitted them to do so, so that they may sustain their lives by eating it. They are people charged with obligation by God, while everyone else is people of subjugation.

"That which has been dedicated to other than God" explains to us that the Truth is the one who made lawful for us to eat from that which has good motion, such as the animal that lowers itself to a human being so that he slaughters it. A human must know to thank the bestower of the favour. "In the name of God, God is greatest" affirms that you slaughtered it only in the name of the One who made it lawful for you.

﴿Do they not see that We have created for them, from what Our hands have made, cattle, and they are their owners? And We have subjugated them for them, so some of them they ride and some of them they eat﴾ (36:71–72).

So eating is part of the subjugation. When you slaughter an animal, you must mention the One who subjugated it for you. The Truth prohibits eating the strangled animal, that is, an animal that died by strangulation, because the foundation of life is three: food, drink and air. This is from the wisdom of the Creator, who made the creation and arranged the matter according to what is most important and what is important. A human may endure hunger for up to thirty days, because our Lord, glorified and exalted be He, has ordained for you, O human, the circumstances of changing conditions. He placed in your body a store for a time when you may go hungry, and He placed in humans a desire for food. Generally, a person does not eat merely to stave off hunger, but eats with appetite.

Our Lord makes clear to us: "I respect your desire for food. Let your necessary movement take from it the energy you need, and the surplus will be stored in the body as fat and flesh. If a day comes when you find no food, you will take energy from the stored fat." This is from the precision of the creation. If you compare it with a car that a human made: when its fuel runs out, it stops and does not move. But the Creator's creation does not stop if food stops; it continues for up to thirty days. Perhaps a heart of another human will have compassion on a person and provide him food, or perhaps a person will resort to some device to escape the predicament of having no food.

The Arab woman described hardship and want, saying: "A year that melted the fat, a year that melted the flesh, and a year that wiped out the bone." That is, the matter has degrees: a person feeds on his fat, then on his flesh, then on his bones. A person can endure without water for a period ranging from three to ten days, depending on the amount of water stored in the body. As for air, a person cannot endure without it beyond the duration of an inhalation and exhalation. If air is withheld from a person, he dies. Breath is the most essential necessity of life. For this reason, we find from the wisdom of the Truth, glorified be He, that He did not make air the possession of anyone, because if anyone possessed air in relation to another person, he might withhold the air in a moment of anger, and that person's life would end.

The Arabic language has such breadth and precision of expression that it indicates there are secrets of meanings that converge on one thing. For example, if you say: nafs (soul), or nafis (precious), or nafas (breath), you find that these are three words formed from a single root: "n, f, s." The nafs is the connection of the spirit to a single matter, so life arises through it. Our Lord inspires the nafs with its wickedness and its piety. And the nafs: …

(1) Narrated by Ahmad, Ibn Majah and al-Daraqutni.

Thus He, glory be to Him, forgives by concealing the punishment, and He puts forgiveness before the concealing of sin, so that a person does not part from it. Then the Truth says:

﴿They ask you what is lawful for them. Say: The good things are lawful for you, and [the game caught by] what you have taught of the trained hunting animals, training them as Allah has taught you. So eat of what they catch for you, and mention the name of Allah over it, and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning.﴾ (4)

After the Truth has explained what is forbidden and what is permitted, we find that what is permitted is not confined, but what is confined is what is forbidden. For when the Truth forbade ten things, these ten things are not all the existing things in the universe. Existing things are many. When Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, created Adam and made him reproduce and multiply for the purpose of vicegerency on earth, He decreed in this earth the means of sustaining life for that kind.

Sustenance is of two kinds: the sustenance of the individual's life, and the sustenance of the human species. The sustenance of the individual's life is by breathing and food, and the sustenance of the species is by marriage and procreation.

Thus there are two kinds of survival for the continuance of vicegerency. The first survival is that life should remain, by its sustaining means. The second is that the species of the living being should remain, by multiplication. And for life to remain and for humankind to multiply, there must be things and kinds that serve the human being and give him energy.

Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, has assured us regarding provision when He said:

﴿Say: Do you indeed disbelieve in Him who created the earth in two days, and you set up rivals to Him? That is the Lord of the worlds. And He placed firm mountains upon it, and blessed it, and decreed in it its sustenance in four days, equal for those who ask. Then He turned to the heaven when it was smoke, and said to it and to the earth: Come willingly or unwillingly. They said: We come willingly.﴾ (Fussilat, 9–11)

By this He informs us that He decreed in the earth its sustenance, and He decreed this sustenance for the human being, the vicegerent on earth, so that he may sustain his life, and the human being perpetuates his species by marriage. When the servant counts the blessings which the Truth has provided for him, he finds them uncountable. Throughout his history, no human has tried to reckon and count the blessings of Allah on earth, because the inclination to count arises from the presumption of being able to encompass the blessings. From the beginning, the human knew that he cannot encompass the blessings of Allah, so no one dared to enumerate them. Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, said:

﴿And if you would count the favour of Allah, you could not enumerate it.﴾ (part of verse 34, Surah Ibrahim)

He used "in" (إن), which is used for a matter of doubt. So they are many blessings which we cannot count. And we ask: Does the Truth tell us the permitted blessings, or the forbidden things? Since the permitted is endless, and since the forbidden is limited, He therefore mentions for us the forbidden things. And the Truth has explained to us ten forbidden things among the blessings.

We notice that when the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, spoke about the human being's inability to count His blessings, He said in one verse:

﴿And if you would count the favour of Allah, you could not enumerate it. Indeed, mankind is ever a wrongdoer and ungrateful.﴾ (Ibrahim, 34)

And He said in another verse:

﴿And if you would count the favour of Allah, you could not enumerate it. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (al-Nahl, 18)

The apparent sense of people's speech is that these are phrases said and repeated. But we say: One must be attentive that a blessing requires one who gives it, who is the Benefactor, and one to whom it is given, who is the beneficiary. So we are facing three elements: a blessing, a benefactor, and a beneficiary. As for the blessing and its individual instances, humans cannot count them, because they exceed enumeration. As for the Benefactor, He is Forgiving and Merciful. As for the beneficiary, he is a wrongdoer and ungrateful. Why does Allah present us with such truths?

If He were to deal with us according to our disbelief, denial and wrongdoing, He would withhold the blessing. But the continuance of Allah's blessing upon us is by His grace and mercy, for it encompasses us even though we are wrongdoers and disbelievers. Therefore it was necessary that He bring these two verses: as regards the blessing, we cannot enumerate it; as regards the Benefactor, He is Forgiving and Merciful; and as regards the beneficiary, he is a wrongdoer and ungrateful. Therefore, when a person commits a sin, the people of faith say to him: Do not despair, for your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful. Therefore, O servant, do not be ashamed to ask your Lord for something despite your disobedience, for Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. And when we look at the constituents of things, we know the essential constituent.

But there are constituents that serve the essential constituent. An example: we take wheat and grind it, and make flour from the grains of wheat to make bread. Wheat requires many constituents before it comes out of the earth. It is an essential constituent: wheat requires regular irrigation, ploughing, and other things. So He who created us decreed these things for us. Since He has decreed all these things for us, we must hearken to His teachings, and He has made clear: Beware lest you think that everything I have created is available to you, for I may create a creature which is not by its nature something you can consume, nor is it in your nature to consume it; rather, this creature has a function in what you consume, like ploughing, irrigation and fertilising for wheat. These are means and causes for obtaining it. So if someone says: Since He, glory be to Him, has created these prohibited things, why has He forbidden them?

We say: These things have no direct effect on you, but they have another function in the universe. If we humans make a machine, and its designer tells us: I have designed this machine, for example, to run on diesel, and another machine runs on petrol, and petrol comes in types. If we took the machine that runs on petrol and put diesel into it, what would happen to it? It would be ruined. This is in the human domain, so what of the Creator of humans?

The Truth has made His creation, which is the human being, and has set out the specifications that make this machine run. We must submit to His teachings lest our life be ruined, and we must not depart from those teachings, for when you contravene and depart from the system He has set for His creation, the machine that is of your making is ruined.

In our life there are thousands of examples. He who made electricity set marks for the negative wires and the positive wires, so that we may take light or motion. If an error occurs in these electrical connections, we are surprised by a power cut, and fires have broken out as a result of a spark from a wrong connection.

Therefore every reproduction and begetting from every negative and positive, that is male and female, must be according to the specifications of its Maker, otherwise there will be cutting off and destruction. If we marry according to the law of Allah and His Messenger, life is set right, but if something happens contrary to the law of Allah, fires break out in the universe.

Therefore you see a wonder before you when you witness a marriage contract. You find the bride's guardian smiling and expansive, inviting people, because a young man has come to marry his daughter, and he offers sweets. But if this bride were sitting at home and a young man tried to spy on her to see her, what happens in her father's heart? It boils with distress, anger and tension. And who is the one who spies? It is the one who went to the girl in a way other than that which the Creator has made lawful. But when he knocks at the door and proposes to her from her father, the father rejoices, for it has been reported in a report: "Lawful [means] cut off the nose of jealousy."

We find that the father moves from a position of jealousy to a position of joy on the day of his daughter's wedding. And the mother goes the morning after the wedding to see the condition of her daughter, to be reassured: is the daughter happy or not? So let no one say: Allah created things, so why has He forbidden them? For Allah created those things and they have a function in what is permitted, and since He, glory be to Him, has made these things have a function in what is permitted, you have no part except in the lawful.

Therefore the Truth says in reply to the question of the believers: "They ask you what is lawful for them. Say: The good things are lawful for you." That is, every good thing has been made lawful by Allah, and every evil thing has been forbidden by Allah. So do not say: This is good, therefore it must be lawful, and this is evil, therefore it must be forbidden. Rather say: This is lawful, therefore it must be good, and this is forbidden, therefore it must be evil. Beware of judging first that this is good and this is evil, and then building prohibition and permission upon that. For you do not know as your Creator knows about the manner and benefit of the arrangement of things with respect to you, lest you fall into the circle of those who find harmful things pleasant, like those who consume narcotics, poisons and intoxicants. Rather, you must be keen to understand what Allah has made lawful, and you will find it good, and reject what Allah has forbidden, because it is evil. Never think that everything that is apparently good is lawful for you, for this thing which is good in appearance may be evil.

You must leave the determination of the good and the evil to your Creator, for He knows best about it and about what is suitable for you. As for you, you know the good thing through Allah's making it lawful, and you know the evil through Allah's forbidding it. The ruling here belongs to the obligation, for Allah is the One who created, and Allah is the One who knows what is beneficial for the human being. So the matter is not the elements, but the will of the Creator concerning those elements, for He is the One who decreed and then guided.

The conclusion, then, on this subject is: the Truth has made lawful for the believers the good things, and everything Allah has made lawful is good, and everything Allah has forbidden is evil. So do not look to human opinions, some of which say of a thing that it is good and so it is lawful, and say of another thing that it is evil and so it is forbidden. For you and other humans do not know the arrangement of things, nor their benefit or harm to you. The proof is that humans sometimes intervene in forbidding things to one another. We find the doctor telling the patient: You are diabetic, so it is not right for you to consume starches and sugars.

If we listen to the words of the doctor, who is a human, should we not be ashamed and listen to the command of the Creator? Rather, we become bold and ask: Why, O Lord, have You forbidden us such-and-such a thing? Now the doctor may err, but Allah cannot err, for He is our Lord, the One entrusted over us. So what Allah has made lawful is the good, and what He has forbidden is the evil. This is a matter that many people encounter. For example, we hear someone citing, wrongly and out of place, the words of the Truth:

﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity.﴾ (part of verse 286, Surah al-Baqarah)

And he says: My work takes up all my time, and I have no leisure to establish prayer. But Allah has only obligated us with what is within our capacity. We say: Do you determine the capacity and build the obligation upon it? No. You must ask yourself: Has Allah obligated me to pray or not? If the Truth has obligated you to pray, and to the other pillars of Islam, then He is the One who knows the capacity of the human being in work. You must put the obligation first, so that you then know the extent of your capacity. Likewise, ask yourself about what Allah has made lawful, and know that it is good, and what Allah has forbidden, and know that it is evil.

"They ask you what is lawful for them. Say: The good things are lawful for you." If we ask what those good things are, we know that they are other than what Allah has forbidden, so everything not forbidden is good. Or they asked about things for which the previous answer would be the natural reply. Allah presented the general matter which we have already explained, and after that the thing asked about comes in the matter of hunting with dogs. He gave them the explanation in the matter of hunting with dogs, and this was a well-known matter among the Arabs in the pre-Islamic period, as was hunting with birds. So He said: "Say: The good things are lawful for you, and [the game caught by] what you have taught of the trained hunting animals." The Truth first laid down the general principle, then made a specific exception afterwards.

The question of hunting with trained animals was the subject of a question from 'Adi ibn Hatim, may Allah be pleased with him, about hunting with dogs and with birds. We must understand the Qur'an by understanding the text well. The Truth says here: "Lawful for you are the good things, and what you have taught of the trained hunting animals." Are the dogs, leopards and tigers with which you hunt made lawful for us because we taught them to hunt? No. "Lawful for you are the good things" is a settled matter. After that comes a new statement: "and what you have taught of the trained hunting animals (jawarih, sing. jarih, the hunting animal, lit. 'one who earns'), training them as Allah has taught you. So eat of what they catch for you."

So what is made lawful is what the trained hunting animals catch, which you have taught, not the hunting animals themselves which a person trains. That is, the Truth made lawful for us the good things, and the eating of what the dogs we have trained to hunt catch for us. The word jawarih (hunting animals) has the singular jarih, and its meaning is "earner" (kasib). For this reason our hands are called jawarih, our eyes are called jawarih, and our ears are called jawarih, because we earn perceptions through them, fa-

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 5, verse 5:

Then the Truth says:

﴿Today the good things have been made lawful for you. The food of those who were given the Book is lawful for you, and your food is lawful for them. And the chaste women from among the believers, and the chaste women from among those who were given the Book before you, when you have given them their due compensation, desiring chastity, not committing fornication or taking secret lovers. And whoever disbelieves in the faith, his work has become worthless, and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers.﴾

He, glorified be He, begins the verse by repeating the previous command: "Today the good things have been made lawful for you," and He repeats it so as to emphasize that a person may not view a good thing except from the standpoint that it has been made lawful by God.

After the Truth, glorified be He, has spoken about how lawful things are to be consumed and the manner of dealing with game, we pause here. He, glorified be He, says: "The food of those who were given the Book is lawful for you, and your food is lawful for them." Is every food of the People of the Book lawful for us? Some of them eat swine. No, rather the lawful part of the food of the People of the Book is the food that is of the kind that God has made lawful for you. It is not proper for a person to shun it merely because it is the food of the People of the Book, because the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, wants to make the human being who is genuinely connected to heaven, like the Muslims, and those who are connected to heaven even though their conception of God differs, to have among them a kind of connection, since they are all connected to heaven. They ought to be treated according to the measure of faith that has entered them, of the connection of earth with heaven.

Beware of saying that the People of the Book are to be boycotted. No, but look at their food: if it is of the kind of food that is lawful in Islam, then it is lawful, and it is not proper to prevent any one of the People of the Book from your food, because God wants to create a kind of familiarity that suits the people concerning whom heaven has previously had legislation, and who acknowledge God even though they differ about His conception.

God, glorified be He, has given us an example through the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. At the first coming of the Islamic call, he faced a godless camp that worshipped fire and did not believe in God, which was the camp of Persia, and a camp that believed in God, which was the camp of the Romans. There were two forces in the world: an Eastern force and a Western force. When a messenger comes to take people to the path of God, it is necessary that his heart and the hearts of the believers be with those who believe in God, in a method and a message, and his heart should not be with the atheists who worship other than God.

Let us observe the faith-based greatness in the Messenger, upon him be prayers and peace: he found those who believe in God and disbelieve in Him, like the Romans, closer to him than those who disbelieve in God. Therefore, when war broke out between Persia and the Romans, the victory first went to Persia, while the sympathies of the Messenger and those who believed with him were with the Romans, because they were closer to the camp of nascent faith; and although they disbelieved in Muhammad, they believed in God, and that there is a method and there is a Day of Resurrection. Therefore the Truth cites it as an example in the Qur'an to give us several snapshots, and the first of these snapshots is that the Muslims are on the side that carries the scent of faith. So He, glorified be He, says:

﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land, but after their defeat they will overcome, within a few years. To God belongs the command before and after. And on that day the believers will rejoice in the victory of God; He gives victory to whom He wills, and He is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾ (Surat al-Rum)

This verse begins with news of the Romans' defeat, then a prophecy from the Truth that they will prevail within a few years, and on the day of their victory the believers will rejoice in the victory of God. The Islamic force, which came to establish a wide and comprehensive religion, looks at a battle between two great states, both of them at the utmost of civilizational advancement. This Islamic force sympathizes with the Romans and stores up its strength, because Persia had prevailed; then the Truth brings the certain news that the Romans will prevail.

By God, who can judge at the end of a battle between two great powers? It is a judgment that does not take a single day, even if its speaker knew that reinforcements were coming to the force that would win. It is a judgment that takes a few years. So who can control a battle that will occur after a few years? The Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, could not gamble on this judgment, for he did not know the preparations of each force, the size of its armies and its weapons. But the matter comes as authenticated news from God: ﴿And they, after their defeat, will overcome, within a few years﴾ (Surat al-Rum).

This is authenticated speech, because it is a written Qur'an that the believers read in worship. When Abu Bakr al-Siddiq heard this verse, he said: "I have made a wager that the Romans will prevail after three years." The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, urged him to extend the term of the wager, because God said: "within a few years," and "bid'" (a few) is between three and nine. Therefore the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to our master Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him: "increase the stake and extend the term," so it became a hundred camels (qulus, she-camels) up to nine years. As if this matter had received complete certainty from the believers, because God, glorified and exalted be He, had announced the victory.

We have mentioned this here so that we understand that the sympathies of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, were with those who believe in a Book and in a Messenger. And here we find the Truth making lawful for us the food of the People of the Book, so that there may be a bond between us and those who believe in a God and in a method from heaven: ﴿The food of those who were given the Book is lawful for you, and your food is lawful for them.﴾

God, the Truth, has clarified this in other verses when He said: ﴿God does not forbid you from those who do not fight you over religion and do not expel you from your homes, from being righteous toward them and acting justly toward them. Indeed, God loves the just. God only forbids you from those who fight you over religion and expel you from your homes and help in your expulsion, from making allies of them. And whoever makes allies of them, it is those who are the wrongdoers.﴾ (Surat al-Mumtahanah)

So He, glorified be He, wants us to balance in the manner of our dealings, so that we do not equate an atheist, a polytheist, and a believer in the connection of heaven with earth, even if he disbelieves in the Messenger of God, and that there be a measured degree of human communication. What is lawful for the believers of the food of the People of the Book is what is lawful in the method of Islam. The Muslim must be mindful that some of the food of the People of the Book contains wine, and he must abstain from everything that is forbidden in our religion, and eat from their food what is lawful for us. A Muslim must not drink wine, nor may a believer eat swine's flesh.

Food, as we know, is a means of sustaining life, and here it passes on to sustaining the species, which is procreation. God has made lawful for us to marry their women: ﴿and the chaste women from among the believers, and the chaste women from among those who were given the Book before you, when you have given them their due compensation, desiring chastity, not committing fornication or taking secret lovers.﴾

The word "muhsanah" has two meanings: it is either the free woman as opposed to the slave woman, or it is the married woman, because ihsan means protection from being mixed in an unworthy way. In earlier times the free woman did not commit the ugly act, and prostitution was confined to slave women, because the slave woman has no father, no brother, and no guardian, and her dignity is squandered. Therefore we find that Hind, the wife of Abu Sufyan, when she heard about adultery from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked: "O Messenger of God, does a free woman commit adultery?" As if the free woman would not have committed adultery in the Jahiliyyah, because the free woman is able to refrain, unlike others.

"Muhsanah" also means the married woman. The Truth equates the chaste woman from among the believers and the chaste woman from among the People of the Book, and what is meant here is the free and chaste woman. It is a condition to give the dower (mahr) to each of them. Some scholars say: when a Muslim woman marries, it is sufficient that he name a dower for her, because a single religion provides the security of a covenant; but marriage to a woman of the People of the Book requires that a person specify the dower, determine it, and fulfill it. Giving (ita') means that a person names the dower, fixes it, and has witnesses to it, and he may make the whole dower deferred. The condition is that the man be muhsan, that is, chaste.

The Truth specifies: ﴿not committing fornication or taking secret lovers﴾, that is, friends without marriage. Sifah is pouring, and the prostitute is the woman with whom any man pours himself. The khidn is the mistress or lover without marriage, and khidn is applied to the male as it is applied to the female. Beware of thinking of entering a temporary marriage (mut'ah); rather, the approach to marriage must be with the intention of a lasting marriage, not a marriage for enjoyment alone.

The Truth then says: ﴿And whoever disbelieves in the faith, his work has become worthless, and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers.﴾ [Because the benefit of faith is that the believer receives the rulings from the One in whom he believes as God, and carries them out. If he conceals any of God's rulings in which he has believed, then he has disbelieved in the faith. The Truth is not harmed if all the people disbelieve, because He is the One who created creation at the beginning, and He is characterized by all attributes of power and perfection.

Thus the whole world adds nothing to God. Before God created man, all the attributes of perfection were present in God, and all the fruits of obedience, worship, and faith return to man. If a man comes to the rulings that God has legislated for him and conceals one of them, it is as if he disbelieved in the matter of faith; and if he denies a part of the parts of faith, this is a kind of disbelief. Would that whoever does this would say: "This part is correct, but I cannot control myself."

In this case the person is a believer who disobeys, and seeks God's forgiveness or repents; but disbelief is not so. Faithful disbelief leads to the nullification of works, and this is evidence that the Truth is addressing a person who adheres in some matters and does not adhere in others. Here the Truth makes clear to the person: the good you have done in your deeds will be taken away in its reward, and what you have refused to carry out of God's rulings nullifies its recompense. The Truth used the word "habita" (has become worthless), which indicates that the work has perished and gone away without return. A livestock animal that eats food not yet ripe, even if it is of the kind it is fed, such as young clover at its beginning, called "rabbah," when cattle graze on it, their bellies swell and they die.

The Arabs call this ailment "hibat" (bloat). Thus "hubut" is the swelling of the belly in livestock that eats food unsuited to it, and its owner thinks it has grown fat when in reality it is dying.

Likewise, work done contrary to what God has legislated is so. The Truth began the matters of faith in this surah with His saying: ﴿O you who believe, fulfill the contracts﴾ (Surat al-Ma'idah, part of verse 1).

Every covenant of faith relates to the oneness of God and to conveying from God, and every covenant made between believers with one another, and every covenant a person makes between himself and himself: these covenants must be fulfilled. Whoever disbelieves in these matters, his work has become worthless. The nullification of work comes as a result of a person ending his work and concluding it with this kind of disbelief, while thinking he has done a righteous deed. But the work is utterly nullified, just as a beast goes to graze on something unsuited to it, so its belly swells and the onlooker imagines that this is satiety and well-being, and then soon it perishes and dies. Likewise is the work of one who disbelieves in faith: he thinks he has accomplished something, but that very thing destroys him. The Qur'anic verses have spoken much about this meaning. The Truth says concerning the disbelievers in God: ﴿Their deeds are like a mirage in a desert plain, which the thirsty one thinks is water, until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing﴾ (part of verse 39, Surat al-Nur).

We know that the mirage is a reflection of light that deceives the one who walks in the desert, so he thinks it is water, and the person walks toward it and does not find water. So is the work of one who disbelieves in God's signs: they are deeds that appear to be beneficial only in imagination. The saying of the Truth, glorified be He: ﴿and finds God with him﴾ means that such a person is startled by the presence of God, as if the matter of the existence of God had never been in his imagination. A person receives his wage only from the one for whom he has worked. Did any one of these work for God so that he should receive a reward from Him? No, he did not work for God. Therefore we find that some superficial thinkers say: "How would God not reward these scholars who invented remedies for diseases, and the scholars who devised things that benefit people? How would God not give them a good reward in the Hereafter?"

We say: they did that, and God was not in their minds; humanity was in their minds, and He has given...

Then the Truth moves on to link for us all the affairs of this world with a comprehensive connection. After speaking of the foundations of life and of the foundations of human reproduction through marriage and other things, He clarifies: all these are blessings I have given you, and I want to take you by the hand, after having shown you the excellence of these blessings upon you, so that you may meet the One who bestows all these blessings. He, glory be to Him, wants to take us away from the preoccupations of this world so that we may meet the Benefactor. And so that you, O Muslim, may meet God, the Benefactor, glory be to Him, you must prepare yourself for this meeting, because it is not a sudden matter. There must be spiritual preparation, physical preparation, spatial preparation and temporal preparation.

Physical preparation is by purity (tahara). Temporal preparation is the appointed times of prayer. Spatial preparation is having a clean place in which to establish the prayer, and directional preparation is fixing the direction of prayer toward the qiblah. All of these are qualities that prepare the human soul to stand before the One who has bestowed upon man all blessings. Therefore we say: prayer is a declaration of the continuation of faithful allegiance to the Creator, the Sustainer, the Benefactor, who created from nothing and sustains from nothing. The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, has prescribed prayer five times a day, so as to cut off for man the path of heedlessness toward Him. And if a person wishes to meet God in the times between the prayers, and wishes to declare the continuation of faith while he is doing any work other than prayer, then let him remember God, because we know the legal principle that says: "That without which an obligation cannot be completed is itself obligatory."

For example, when a person prays, he needs strength, and strength is generated in the body as a result of eating food. Therefore, the process of producing food is an obligatory matter, and everything that follows from that is an obligatory process. So when someone comes and says: "I want to devote myself to worship and withdraw from the movement of life," we say to him: "Do that on one condition: that you do not benefit from the work of any one moving person in life, and that you do not eat any food. For the loaf of bread that a person offers you is the work of many people who did not withdraw from life." And we also say: "Why do you wear this robe? It is the result of the activity of other people's lives: there is the one who planted the cotton, another who ginned this cotton, a third who turned it into yarn, a fourth who wove it, and a fifth who tailored this robe. And look at what lies behind each one of them of tools." And beware of benefiting from the work of someone busy with the means if you have decided to withdraw from the movement of life.

Busying oneself with the means is worship, because worship is not completed without it, and that without which an obligation cannot be completed is itself obligatory. Therefore, learning useful life skills is a communal obligation (fard kifaya), and the obligation upon a person is of two kinds: either fard 'ayn (individual obligation), which is a matter charged upon the individual that he must perform and that no one may perform on his behalf, such as prayer; or fard kifaya (collective obligation), which is that without which an obligation cannot be completed, and so it is obligatory. So each of us needs food.

Therefore there must be a division of labor: this one plants and that one manufactures. There must be the cultivation of wheat, there must be the establishment of mills, there must be the establishment of ovens, and there must be engineers who design these machines. All of these are matters that make it easy for a person to possess the strength to perform the prayer and to stand before the Truth to perform the prayer. So all of this is an obligatory matter, and it is a communal obligation, meaning that it is an obligation which, if some perform it, falls from the rest, and if none of us performs it, the sin falls upon everyone.

Another example is the funeral prayer over the dead, which is a communal obligation: whoever prays over the deceased performs it on our behalf, and if no one prays over the deceased, the sin falls upon every Muslim. In this way the scope of sin widens. Every action without which an obligation cannot be completed is obligatory, and therefore it is a communal obligation: if some perform it, the demand falls from the rest, and if some do not perform it, the sin falls upon all.

And what is the position of the ruler (wali al-amr)? The ruler must impose the performance of a communal obligation upon some of the people, otherwise the obligations that we call religious duties would be rendered inoperative. When a Muslim goes to the market and finds no bread, he will be weakened and will not be able to escape hunger, and he will not be able to pray or work to produce, or to have savings sufficient for him to perform the pilgrimage.

Therefore: that without which an obligation cannot be completed is itself obligatory. That is why we find the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, when He exhorted us to perform the prayer on Friday, says: {O you who believe, when the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday, hasten to the remembrance of God and leave off trade. That is better for you, if you only knew} [al-Jumu'ah 62:9].

He, glory be to Him, takes us out of work to prayer, and He did not take us out to prayer from emptiness. Let us notice the precision of the Qur'anic expression when the Truth says: "and leave off trade." When a person leaves off trade, he leaves off buying all the more so, because buying and selling are two aspects of one single process. The difference is only that the buyer may buy the commodity while disliking to buy, because he is spending his money on what he buys, whereas the seller wants to obtain the price of the sale immediately, and usually obtains profit from it; and that is the peak of earning. The earning of the farmer, for example, comes to him after months of cultivation, and the earning of the employee comes to him at the beginning of the month, but the seller obtains his earning immediately. Therefore the Truth commands us to leave off trade when we hear the call to prayer on Friday. And what comes after the prayer ends?

Behold, the Truth says: {Then when the prayer is concluded, disperse in the land and seek from the bounty of God, and remember God often that you may succeed} [al-Jumu'ah 62:10].

So let no one say: "I am devoted to prayer throughout my whole life," for no one will be able to go to prayer unless he possesses the means of his own life, and the requirements of life demand that a person travel through the earth, and a person must seek from the bounty of God. Therefore, striving on the earth is worship, because that without which an obligation cannot be completed is itself obligatory. And the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, does not want to isolate a matter related to the requirements of life, such as food and marriage, from prayer.
