Or "khaida'a" means "nafs khaida'a" [a treacherous soul], or "khaida'a" like "imra'ah khaida'a" [a treacherous woman], or "khaida'a" as an intensive form, as we say "rawi" and "rawiyah," meaning a man, or we say "jama'ah khaida'a" [a treacherous group].

Thus this one word encompasses all the sources of their treachery: a man, a woman, a group, or all of them. The one who speaks here is the Lord of the worlds, speaking to the Arabs, who are people of eloquence. This is a high linguistic performance.

From the extreme precision and truthfulness of the Qur'an, the Truth says: "except a few of them." In accordance with the principle of preserving possibility (qanun siyanat al-ihtimal), when Allah addresses His Messenger (peace be upon him) to explain to him the position of the Jews toward him, does it not allow that there might be a group of Jews whom deep understanding overcomes, so that they reflect on believing in this Messenger and soften the harshness of their suspicion about him? Some of them did reflect and declared Islam.

When these people hear Allah's rulings on all the Jews, do they not say: "What is wrong with us that we should enter this category and think of uttering faith?" So His saying "except a few of them" preserved the principle of possibility that a person among them might have considered faith. Whoever considers faith will find the Truth's saying "except a few of them," and this person will see in himself that the Qur'an is a proof that descended with light, and a few of them did declare their Islam. What then would his position be, peace be upon him, after the Truth informs him that you will in future be exposed to their treachery? Does this not stir the psyche of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and the believers around him? If the Jews commit treachery, they must surely take revenge on them, in application of the basic rule for repelling aggression: whoever attacks you, attack him in return.

Allah, glorified is He, did not want to leave the situation to human emotions toward humans, but said: "So pardon them and overlook. Indeed, Allah loves the doers of good." Pardon ('afw) is, as we say, "la 'afya 'ala athari" [may no trace of mine be effaced], meaning your traces remain clear on the earth, and the wind comes to wipe them out, so the trace is effaced. The command to pardon means: wipe out the trace of the sin they committed, and consider the wrong they committed against you as if it had not happened. But will its trace remain with the Messenger of Allah? The command to overlook (safh) comes, and there is a difference between erasing the wrong and keeping its trace in yourself, remaining in a state of rage and rancour.

The Truth here commands pardon, meaning removing its trace, and commands overlooking, meaning that you remove the trace of the wrong from your mind. A person has stages. The first stage: after one of them commits a wrong against him, he does not repay aggression with its like. This is pardon. The second stage: he does not let the trace of this wrong work in his heart, but overlooking comes so that the heart of the believer is not occupied with something he has already pardoned. The third stage: an open opportunity for whoever wants to go further in the rank of excellence (ihsan) and the elevation of certainty and faith, by being good to the one who wronged him. These three stages are made clear by the saying of the Truth:

{ And those who restrain anger and those who pardon men, the

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 5, verse 14:

﴿And among those who say, "We are Christians," We took their covenant, but they forgot a portion of what they were reminded of. So We caused among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection. And Allah will inform them of what they used to do.﴾

They said they were Christians, and the Truth took their covenant from them, whether it was the covenant of the Dhar (the primordial covenant taken from the descendants of Adam) or their covenant to their prophet Jesus, son of Mary. Then they forgot a portion of what they were reminded of: they abandoned what the Injil (the Gospel) commanded them and broke the covenant, so they split into evident hostility, becoming many sects. And the command of Allah came, as He had promised:

﴿O People of the Book, there has certainly come to you Our Messenger, making clear to you much of what you used to conceal of the Scripture and pardoning much. There has certainly come to you from Allah a light and a clear Book.﴾

It is as if Allah, glory be to Him, gives them the opportunity and the excuse, so that none of them can say: "No messenger came to us with anything." There was a period in which no messenger had come, and here is a messenger from Allah coming with a complete method (*manhaj*, a divine way of life). The coming of the Messenger grants them, and gives them, an opportunity to renew the covenant of faith. They had concealed some of the rulings from their books, such as stoning and usury. Some of the Children of Israel said about usury what the Qur'an reports of them:

﴿There is no blame upon us regarding the unlettered.﴾ (part of 3:75)

That is, they permitted lending at interest to those who were not of their religion, but there was no usury in their dealings with members of their own religion. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ wanted to gather their scattered ranks and unite their hands with his hand, because he was a prophet they had awaited, and in their books there was good news of him. He also wanted the believing community to stand before the wave of atheism on earth, so that the order of heaven would govern the movement of the earth. Therefore the Truth said: ﴿There has come to you from Allah a light﴾ (5:15). This means that their concealment of part of the method of Allah has created darkness in the universe. Since darkness has occurred in the universe, especially the darkness of values, the universe has come to need someone who will light the way for it. We know that light is that by which we distinguish things.

When the Truth presents to us the matter of sensory light, He wants to take us by the hand from sensory light to immaterial light. Sensory light dispels the darkness of the path, so that we do not collide with things, fall into a pit, or break something. But when a person carries a light, he walks with clear insight into his affair. Sensory light also prevents the collision of movements among creatures, so that energy is not wasted, for the squandering of energy exhausts the universe and nothing is accomplished.

Indeed, the sun illuminates the universe during the day; then the moon comes after the sun to cast some of its light; and likewise the stars, by their positions, guide people in the darknesses of land and sea. Allah made these beings so that the material movement of existing things would not collide. If Allah has made material light so that one creature does not collide with another, then He is able not to leave values, meanings and balances without light. Therefore the Truth created the light of values to guide man to the even path. If the unbeliever or the atheist shares with the believer in benefiting from material light, which protects material movement on earth, and no one says, "I have no need to benefit from material light," then we say to the unbelievers and atheists: since you have benefited from this light, you should have said: "Allah has a light in values that we must follow." This method summarizes that light as: "Do, and do not do."

Therefore the method is a light from Allah. Let us read:

﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth﴾ (part of 24:35).

He takes us by the hand along the path with material light, from which everyone benefits, whether believer or otherwise. And He, glory be to Him, strikes for us a parable of His light:

﴿The parable of His light is like a niche in which is a lamp﴾ (part of 24:35).

The *mishkah* (niche) is the recess that is set into the wall, and it is different from a window. It is a hole in the wall in which an oil lamp or a kerosene lamp is placed, and such niches are found in primitive buildings before man invented electric bulbs and chandeliers. The area of the niche does not exceed thirty centimeters, its length is forty centimeters, and its depth does not exceed fifteen centimeters, whereas the room may sometimes exceed three meters in length, width and height.

The Truth speaks only of the niche and does not speak of the room. Any lamp in the niche is able to light the room. Let us note that this lamp is not ordinary: it is a lamp in a glass. We know that a lamp in a glass is one of the intellectual advancements of humanity. Lamps in earlier times had no glass, and tongues of soot (*sinaj*, the smoke-black that blackens what is around it) would come out of them and blacken their surroundings. Soot is the trace of a lamp's smoke on the wall and other things. A lamp could also go out because wind blew from every direction. Then man placed around the flame of the lamp a glass that protects the fire, concentrates the light, reflects the rays, and draws air through the glass in the amount needed for the burning.

﴿Like a niche in which is a lamp, the lamp in a glass﴾ (part of 24:35).

That is, the light from this lamp is stronger, because the glass reflects the rays of the lamp and spreads the light throughout the whole place. The glass in which this lamp is placed is not ordinary:

﴿The glass is as if it were a brilliant star﴾ (part of 24:35).

The star itself is luminous, and the glass is as if it were this brilliant star in its radiance and sheen. And from what is the lamp kindled? ﴿It is lit from a blessed tree, an olive﴾ (part of 24:35).

This is an advancement in the illumination of the lamp from the oil of the olive tree. And the tree is not ordinary: ﴿neither of the east nor of the west﴾ (part of 24:35).

It is a tree that possesses the finest kind of moderation: ﴿light upon light﴾ (part of 24:35).

That is part of Allah's power in the light of material cosmic things. Therefore it is not reasonable to leave values and immaterial things without light. Just as man has been guided in material matters, so he should be alert to the power of the Truth to guide in immaterial matters, as proven by Allah's saying: ﴿Allah guides to His light whom He wills﴾ (part of 24:35).

Allah guides by the light of values, method and meanings whomever He wishes. The atheist may be guided by the material light of the sun toward material things, but his sight is blind to seeing the light of the method and values. Therefore, glory be to Him, He clarifies that there is a divine light, which is the method, and He struck this parable to clarify immaterial meanings through sensory meanings. We are illuminated according to our means: the poor or the primitive person is illuminated by a small gas lamp, while the one who is at ease in life may buy an electric generator. Each person is illuminated according to his capacity. But when the sun rises, what happens to the lamp?

A person extinguishes those lamps, for the sun is a light that Allah has given to all of mankind and to the whole universe as well. If we think with our minds about what illuminates our lives, each of us thinks according to the capacity of his mind. But when a light descends from Allah, it suffices from every other light, and as we do in material matters, so we do in immaterial matters.

﴿Light upon light. Allah guides to His light whom He wills, and Allah strikes parables for mankind﴾ (part of 24:35).

What shows us that the second light is the light of values, which reveals to us by the illumination of "do, and do not do," is that Allah said afterward: ﴿in houses which Allah has permitted to be raised and in which His name is remembered﴾ (part of 24:36).

If you search for what the prepositional phrase (*jar wa-majrur*) depends upon, you will not find it except in His saying "in houses which Allah has permitted to be raised." It is as if the light comes from the risings of guidance in His mosques, for they are the houses of Allah to which we turn, so that the light of the Truth may overflow from them upon creation.

﴿In houses which Allah has permitted to be raised and in which His name is remembered; therein He is glorified morning and evening, by men whom neither commerce nor sale diverts from the remembrance of Allah﴾ (24:36–37).

The phrase "neither commerce diverts them" does not mean the prohibition of trade. A truthful person is not diverted by trade from the remembrance of Allah, and Allah should be in the mind of the believer always. When a person is mindful of Allah, Allah gives him from His support.

So, O People of the Book, the light has come to you, and the Messenger has clarified for you much of what you differ over, and he overlooks much of your sins, and he wants to carry out with you a comprehensive settlement. So you must turn and pay attention, and correct your stance toward this new religion. Consider what Allah wants by this method. Allah has struck the parable of light, and this light guides to "do, and do not do." And who tells us that this light comes from Allah? It is the Messenger. And who shows us that the Messenger is truthful in conveying from Allah? What shows his truthfulness is the saying of Allah:

{O mankind, there has come to you a proof (*burhan*, a decisive argument) from your Lord, and We have sent down to you a clear light} (4:174).

What came first from your Lord is the proof that the Messenger of Allah is truthful in conveying from Allah. And so that he may convey to us that the Book has come with the method, the Qur'an is distinguished by being the proof of the Prophet's truthfulness, and it is the luminous method, for proof is the argument for the truthfulness of the Messenger in conveying from Allah.

We know proof in our educational life while studying geometry, when we face a geometric exercise: we take the given data, then we look at what is to be proven, and we return to the data to take from it strength to demonstrate the proof of what is required. If the data do not give that, we move to another step, which is to work at proving what is required. This universe contains data, and it is a well-ordered universe, and we perceive its precision in what is outside the scope of our own movement:

﴿The sun is not to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day﴾ (40:40).

It is a universe measured by the heavens and the earth, the movement of the winds, and other things. In those matters in which man has no role, we find the laws straight in perfect uprightness and completeness. So if a person wants to take data from the universe, let him take into account the matters in which humans have a role, and he will find them exposed to corruption, because human desire has access to these things. But the Supreme Creator is not reached or touched by matters of desire. Therefore He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And the heaven He raised high, and He set up the balance﴾ (55:7).

So neither does heaven fall upon the earth, nor does one star crowd another star. And the Truth shows us how to proceed in the order of the universe:

{Do not transgress in the balance} (55:8).

If you want your movement to be orderly, look at what your hands have a role in, and do it as Allah does in what is not within your hands' scope.

﴿And establish the weight with justice and do not make deficient the balance﴾ (55:9).

If you are impressed by the balance of the higher universe, that is because it was made with a precise order. And if the Truth has set for us a precise order, which is the method, "do such and do not do such," that is so that your voluntary movement will not be corrupted if you follow the method and conduct your life according to the method of Allah, and the balance remains upright. Therefore the Truth has given us data which, when man looks at them with an unbiased natural gaze, lead his hand to faith. These ordered beings necessarily have a Creator, because man came upon them after they existed; they did not come after the creation of man, and no human claims that he created this universe.

So it is necessary to seek out who created this precise universe. And a claim, when it is free from weakness, is it truthful or not truthful? It is entirely truthful, and Allah is the One who said that He created the heavens, the earth and the universe, and no other claimant came to tell us: "It is I who created." Therefore the matter is established for Allah until a claimant appears, and with the passing of ages and their lengthening, no one has claimed that.

It was necessary that the task of the human mind be to think and to stir the intellect in order to recognize the Creator of this universe, and it was necessary that it turn in gratitude to the One who came to solve this riddle for it.

The messengers came to solve this riddle and to guide us to a rational and innate objective. If we were to arrange existence in a chain, we would find that man is the lord of this existence, because all creatures work and strive in his service. The categories of existence as we know them, which serve man, are animals, and man is distinguished from them by reason. Beneath the animals is the plant kingdom, in which there is growth, and beneath that is a lower category, the inanimate. The inanimate is not the merely motionless: air is inanimate, the sun is inanimate, and the soil is inanimate. All of these carry out their function in existence for the service of the higher categories above them, and man benefits from all of them. Animals benefit from the inanimate, and likewise plants benefit from the inanimate, and animals benefit from plants, and the ultimate outcome of all of them is the service of man.

Is it not then fitting and obligatory that man ask himself: who bestowed upon him this status? So if the Messenger came to solve this riddle and to inform us that the One who created the universe is Allah, and these are His attributes, and to inform us that this method came from Allah

Almighty God then says:

﴿Through it, God guides whoever follows His good pleasure to the paths of peace, and brings them out of darkness into light by His permission, and guides them to a straight path.﴾ (16)

Since it is God who guides, He, glory be to Him, is exalted above the desires attached to people. Thus we ensure that Islam has no desire, because the bane of the one who legislates is that he mentions himself or what he loves within what he legislates. The legislator must be one who gains nothing from what he legislates, and this attribute exists only in God, for He legislates for all and is above all.

"There has come to you from God a light and a clear Book. Through it God guides whoever follows His good pleasure." Whoever follows His good pleasure, God guides him to the paths of peace. So there is pleasure that is followed, and there are paths of peace as a reward. And are peace paths and ways? Yes, because there is the peace of the self with itself, and there is the peace of the self with its family, there is the peace of the self with its community, there is the peace of the self with its nation, and there is the peace of the self with the world, and the peace of the self with the entire cosmos, and there is the peace of the self with God. All of this encompasses peace. So the paths of peace are many. Peace with God is that you glorify your Lord, O servant, so you do not worship another god along with Him, and you do not attach to Him any other, i.e., you do not associate anything with Him, nor say: there is no god.

That is why we find that Islam came with the middle way, even in belief. It came between people who say: there is no god, which is negation, and people who say: there are multiple gods. Evil has a god, good has a god, darkness has a god, light has a god, air has a god, and earth has a god.

Those who spoke of multiple gods relied on material sense, and each of them forgot that man is composed of matter and spirit. When the spirit leaves, the body becomes a corpse. None of them asked himself and said: where is your spirit that directs your self and your whole body? Do you see it? Where is it? Is it in your nose, your ear, or your belly? Where is it? What is its shape? What is its colour? What is its taste? You have not perceived it, yet it exists. So the creation of God within you that you do not perceive—can you perceive its Creator? This is misguidance. For if one could perceive a god, he would not be a god, because if you perceive something, you are able to determine it with your sight, and since you are able to determine it, your sight has power over it, and the Supreme Powerful never becomes the subject of power of the lesser, ever.

When God wanted to demonstrate this matter, He said: {And in yourselves. Will you not see?} (51:21).

Look into yourself: you find your spirit that directs your body; you do not see it nor hear it, yet it is in you. If it leaves you, you become a corpse and carrion. So the creation of God within you that you cannot perceive—after this, do you want to perceive who created? This is speech without taste. The other direction says there are multiple gods, because this universe is vast and everything in it needs a god on its own. Islam then brings the true matter and says: there is one God, for if there were multiple gods as you say, there would be, for example, a god for the sun, a god for the sky, a god for the earth, a god for water, and a god for air. Then each of these gods would be incapable of directing and caring for any matter other than what it is god of and sustaining it, and disputes and discord would arise among them. This is clarified by His saying, exalted is He: {Each god would have taken away what he created, and some would have exalted themselves over others} (23:91).

The god of the sun might separate it from the universe, and the god of water might prevent it from the rest of the creatures. The Truth settles the matter, saying:

{Say: If there were with Him other gods, as they say, they would have sought a way to the Lord of the Throne} (17:43).

He, glory be to Him, also says: {If there were in them gods other than God, they would both have been corrupted} (21:22).

Thus the laws that you see are also governed by the One God. The Messenger comes to tell you: there is one God. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) conveyed to us: "There is no god but God." "There is no god" negates that there are gods at all, and then he said: "but God," and this is in the interest of man, so that he is not humiliated, submissive, and a slave to the god of the sun, or the god of air, or the god of water. And the Truth said:

{God sets forth a parable: a man in whom are partners quarrelling, and a man belonging wholly to one man. Are they equal in comparison?} (39:29).

Our Lord wants to relieve us of "confusion," illusion, disturbance, and hesitation. He is one God, and when God decrees a judgment, no one contradicts it. He, glory be to Him, guides us by what He legislates for us, because He, glory be to Him, has no desire in what He legislates. The meaning of desire is that you make the movement you want serve you in something, whereas God has no need of anyone, for He created the whole existence before He created creation. None of those created, however much knowledge and soundness of intellect he is given, has any power or any part in the process of creation or its ordering.

"Through it God guides whoever follows His good pleasure": since he has followed His good pleasure, He guides him to the paths of peace. So there are two guidances: God guides by it whoever follows His good pleasure to the paths of peace. And He said in another verse:

{And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their God-consciousness} (47:17).

So beware of thinking that God-consciousness will not attain its reward and recompense except in the Hereafter, for every time you do a thing and turn back, you find its effects in yourself. You pray and find your affairs lighter upon yourself. You do not commit an evil act while people are heedless; your heart is not preoccupied with anything, and the believer lives in peace with himself forever. So the paths of peace are many: the paths of peace with God, the paths of peace with the whole universe, the paths of peace with his society, the paths of peace with his family, the paths of peace with himself.

The Truth says:

{And this is My path, straight, so follow it, and do not follow other ways, lest they separate you from His way} (6:153).

So there are paths of peace and paths of misguidance.

In this verse the Truth says: "and brings them out of darkness into light by His permission, and guides them to a straight path." Darkness is the place of collision. When He brings them out of darkness into light, they see the correct path leading to good and the path leading to other than good. After they come out of darkness into light, their movements become mutually supportive, not mutually opposed, and there is no collision or anything that inherits for them hatred and rancour. Or it is meant that He guides them to the straight path, which is Paradise.

The Almighty then says:

﴿Those who say, "Indeed, God is the Messiah, son of Mary," have certainly disbelieved. Say, "Who then has any power against God if He wished to destroy the Messiah, son of Mary, and his mother and everyone on earth entirely? And to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them. He creates what He wills, and God is over all things competent."﴾

And He, glorified is He, had said before: ﴿So We caused among them enmity and hatred to continue until the Day of Resurrection﴾ (Qur'an 5:14).

So the Ya'qubiyah said one thing, the Nestorians (al-Nasturiyah) said another thing, and the Malakiyah said a third thing. Then came the summit: "Those who say, 'Indeed, God is the Messiah, son of Mary,' have certainly disbelieved."

His saying, glorified is He, "Say," is a reply to them: "Who then has any power against God?" That is, who can prevent the decree of God from descending upon the one you have made a god, "if He wished to destroy the Messiah, son of Mary, and his mother and everyone on earth entirely."

They claimed that God is the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary. In this there is audacity against the station of divinity, which is exalted above likeness and above incarnation in anything. In this noble statement is a message to these people that no one can prevent God from destroying Jesus, his mother, and all who are on earth. He is the Real, the King, the Creator of the heavens and the earth, and whatever is between them; He creates what He wills as He wills. If He created the Messiah without a father, then the message has already come to us that He, glorified is He, created Adam without father or mother, and created Eve without a mother. Exalted is His majesty and His power, nothing can overcome Him. Jesus, peace be upon him, is a human being, subject to death like all humans.

"To God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them; He creates what He wills." The Truth here mentions the heaven as the higher kind and the earth as the lower kind. His saying "He creates what He wills" answers the doubt with precise brevity. The trial came from the angle that Jesus, peace be upon him, was distinguished in the manner of his creation by something that was not common among people. So the Truth clarifies: do not suppose that the creation I bring about requires of Me that there be male and female and fertilization. This is the common custom that presumes the existence of male and female. Otherwise, the trial would have had to occur before Jesus, in Adam, since he was created without father or mother. Thus whoever wants to be tempted by the idea of one born from a mother without a father should have been tempted by Adam, who had neither father nor mother. God makes clear to them: He creates what He wills, so it is not necessary or obligatory that it be from a pair, or only from a male, or only from a female.

Our Lord, glorified and exalted is He, has absolute freedom of power to create what He wills, and He has willed to create in the four logical rational divisions: either from a father and mother, as all of us are; or without both, like Adam; or from a male without a female, like Eve; or from a female without a male, like Jesus, peace be upon him. God thus arranged creation according to the four logical rules, so that you do not understand that our Lord wants special attributes in order to create. Rather, He creates what He wills. The evidence for this is that a pair may exist together and yet not produce offspring from them. Is there any greater completeness than this?

﴿To God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He creates what He wills. He bestows females upon whom He wills and bestows males upon whom He wills, or He pairs them, males and females, and He renders whom He wills barren﴾ (Qur'an 42:49–50).

So the matter is that no constituent elements are imposed upon our Lord. Rather, it is the will of the Creator, not the elemental nature of the Creator. He "creates what He wills," His will is absolute and His power is general, and therefore the statement must come: "And God is over all things competent."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 5, verse 18:

The Truth (Allah) then says:

﴿And the Jews and the Christians said: "We are the sons of Allah and His beloved ones." Say: "Why then does He punish you for your sins? No, you are human beings of those He has created. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and to Him is the final return."﴾ (18)

Did all the Jews say, "We are the sons of Allah"? Did all the Christians say, "We are the sons of Allah"? No. Some of the Jews said, "Uzair is the son of Allah," and some of the Christians said, "Isa is the son of Allah." Musaylima the Liar came, claimed prophethood, and all the people of Musaylima would say, "We are the prophets," meaning that among us are the prophets. Even the supporters of our master Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, father of Khubayb, said, "We are the Khubaybiyyun," meaning we are the followers of Ibn al-Zubayr, who is the father of Khubayb. Thus they attributed to themselves what belonged to others. So the meaning of "We are the sons of Allah" is: we are the partisans (ashya') of Uzair, who is the son of Allah, and we are the partisans of Isa, who is the son of Allah. For this we take evidence from the Qur'an, and we know the story of the believer of Pharaoh's household:

﴿And a believing man from the family of Pharaoh, who concealed his faith, said: "Will you kill a man because he says, 'My Lord is Allah,' when he has brought you clear proofs from your Lord? If he is a liar, then upon him is his lie; but if he is truthful, some of what he threatens you with will strike you. Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a transgressor and a liar. O my people, to you belongs the dominion today, dominant in the land..."﴾ (Surah Ghafir)

"Al-qawm" means a group. By Allah, were all the people (al-qawm) kings? No. The only one who was a king was Pharaoh alone. But since Pharaoh was the king, all who were his followers, supporters, and of his party are considered kings, because they live under the protection and care of the king. Also He said to the Jews: "and made you kings" (5:20). For this reason, when they wanted to define the meaning of "king" (malik), they said: the "king" is the man who has a spacious house in which running water flows. Another said: the "king" is the one who has a comfortable life, has someone to serve him, and does not occupy himself with serving himself in his home, while outside he serves himself. Another said: whoever has wealth that does not compel him to hard labor is a king. Therefore our master, Shaykh Abd al-Jalil Isa, said on this matter: "Do not be surprised at that, for the unlettered speak and in their language say: 'This is the king of his time,' meaning a comfortable man who does not do hard work, and has money that he spends as he wishes." Thus "sons of Allah" does not mean that all of them are His sons. For this reason Allah said to His Messenger (ﷺ), as a reply to them: "Say: 'Why then does He punish you for your sins?'" "No, you are human beings of those He has created," and you will enter under the will of forgiveness.

"He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills" — you will not escape the forgiving will or the punishing will. "And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and to Him is the final return."

Al-Haqq (the Truth, God) says, clarifying the doctrinal matter on earth:

﴿O People of the Scripture, Our Messenger has come to you, making clear to you, after a lull in the messengers, lest you say, "There came to us no bringer of good tidings and no warner." But there has come to you a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And Allah is over all things competent.﴾ (5:19)

The Messenger is Muhammad (ﷺ). He makes clear to you, O People of the Scripture, what you differed about first, and what you must agree upon second. What Islam added of method came to suit the affairs of life that people face until the Hour arrives. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came "after a lull in the messengers" (fatrah, the interval between prophets). Fatrah means cessation. "A lull in the messengers" means a period in which messages had ceased. This is the interval between him (ﷺ) and his brother Jesus (peace be upon him). People have calculated its length: some said it was six hundred years, others said five hundred and sixty years. The number of years does not concern us. What concerns us is the existence of a period in which messengers ceased. The exception is the saying of al-Haqq, glorified is He:

﴿And present to them the parable of the people of the town, when the messengers came to it. When We sent to them two, and they denied them, so We reinforced them with a third, and they said, "Indeed, we are messengers to you." They said, "You are not but human beings like us, and the Most Merciful has sent down nothing. You are only lying." They said, "Our Lord knows that we are indeed messengers to you."﴾ (Surah Ya-Sin, 36:13–16)

Were these messengers sent by Allah between Jesus and Muhammad (ﷺ), or were they messengers sent by Jesus to the people of Antioch? The people first disbelieved these two messengers, so al-Haqq reinforced them with a third.

The people said to them: ﴿You are not but human beings like us, and the Most Merciful has sent down nothing. You are only lying.﴾ (Surah Ya-Sin, 36:15)

Here the messengers said: ﴿Our Lord knows that we are indeed messengers to you.﴾ (Surah Ya-Sin, 36:16)

What is the difference between "Indeed, we are messengers to you" and "Our Lord knows that we are indeed messengers to you"? Information is always delivered by the speaker to the hearer in order to give him news. If the hearer's mind is free of the news, the speech is delivered without emphasis. But if he has something like denial, the speech is delivered with emphasis proportional to his denial. If his obstinate denial increases, the emphasis increases. The people of the town were sent two messengers by Allah, and they denied them, so He reinforced them with a third. This is a reinforcement of the messengership: after being two messengers, Allah made them three. The three said: ﴿Indeed, we are messengers to you.﴾ (from Surah Ya-Sin, 36:14)

There is indeed emphasis here, because the sentence is nominal and preceded by the emphatic "inna." When they denied them and said, "You are not but human beings like us, and the Most Merciful has sent down nothing," this was obstinate denial on their part. So what should the messengers' response be? Should they say, "Indeed, we are messengers to you," as was said first? No. The denial here is extremely obstinate and harsh, so al-Haqq brings a stronger emphasis on the messengers' tongues: ﴿Our Lord knows.﴾

This statement is in the form of an oath. This is the first emphasis, and the second emphasis is: ﴿Indeed, we are messengers to you.﴾

As we know, "inna" here is emphatic, and the lam in the beginning of His words "lamursalun" (indeed messengers) is for added emphasis. When a word revolves around multiple meanings, the comprehensive meaning is the original meaning. Likewise the word "fatrah": fatrah means cessation. If you say, for example, "ma' fatir" (lukewarm water), meaning water whose coldness has ceased, then water is conditioned by coldness so that it quenches thirst. When one says "ma' fatir," it means water that has lost its coolness, and therefore our saying "ma' fatir" means slightly warm water, that is, water from which the desirable coldness has ceased.

It is also said in describing a woman: "fi jafniha futur" (there is languor in her eyelid), meaning that she lowers her gaze and does not stare boldly with her eyes, but has a downcast look. Therefore fatrah is cessation. A period of time has ceased, and it was empty of revelation and of messengers. The consequence of this would be that the age of heedlessness would be prolonged and the age of the obliteration of the method would be prolonged, and the people of goodness would live in thirst and longing for the coming of a new method. Since a messenger had come, it was obligatory that people prick up their ears to what he brought. Therefore al-Haqq makes clear that He sent a messenger who came after a lull. If you are people of goodness, it is obligatory that you seek what he brought of method, and that you prick up your ears to what the Messenger (ﷺ) brings, to hear his mission and his message.

Allah sent the Messenger to them after a lull in order to cut off from them the proof and the excuse, so that they would not say, "There came to us no bringer of good tidings and no warner." There has therefore come to them a bringer of good tidings and a warner. The bringer of good tidings is the teacher or the informer of good whose time comes after the informing. As long as the one who comes is a bringer of good tidings, he encourages people to desire the method of Allah in order to take the good. There must be a period of time in which people practise the method, and there must be a period in which those who have not taken the method practise whatever is outside the method, so that evil comes to them.

An example of this is the saying of the teacher: "Give good tidings to the one who studies that he will succeed." Then the one who studies is encouraged among the students who desire success. That is, there must be a period in which he achieves what brings him to what he is promised. Likewise warning must have a period in which a person avoids what brings evil.

﴿Our Messenger has come to you, making clear to you, after a lull in the messengers, lest you say, "There came to us no bringer of good tidings and no warner."﴾ The coming of "lest you say" is a clarification that there is no opportunity for the pretext of saying, "There came to us no bringer of good tidings and no warner."

Al-Haqq says: ﴿But there has come to you a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And Allah is over all things competent.﴾ Is the Competent (al-Qadir) ever not? He made creation come into being upon a universe organised with wisdom and with all means of goodness and life, in the best order, before these creatures came into this universe. When creatures came into being upon this goodness, would the Creator leave them without guidance? No. He, glorified is He, has decreed to bring into existence all His creatures and to give them what preserves their life and preserves their kind.

Does al-Haqq not then give creatures what preserves their values?

He is able to give the provision of sustenance and the provision of principles and values, and to fulfil to His creatures their provision in every gift. The sending of messengers is one of the gifts of al-Haqq for the treatment of values. Then He returns again to the people of Moses, but this time He makes the speaker their messenger.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 5, verse 20:

When you hear "idh" (when), know that it is temporal, meaning "when/at the time that." As if the Truth (al-Haqq) says: "Remember when Musa said to his people: Remember the blessing of Allah upon you," and the Truth says this to His Messenger, because this kind of remembrance helps the Messenger (ﷺ) to bear what he is subjected to in the matter of the call and the message, whether from atheists or from the People of the Book.

When the Truth says: "And when Musa said to his people," meaning: Remember, O Muhammad; or remember, O you who follow Muhammad; or remember, O you who recite the Qur'an, when Musa said to his people: "O my people, remember the blessing of Allah upon you." Musa would not say to his people "O my people, remember the blessing of Allah upon you" except when he had seen from them an action that did not match the blessings Allah had bestowed upon them. And this, and to Allah belongs the highest likeness, is like when one of us says to a disobedient son: "Remember what your father did for you." One of us would not say this except when the son had shown signs that did not match the beginnings of blessings and the beginnings of favour upon him. So it is as if the people of Musa had exhausted him and he bore much from them, to the point that he said to them, by way of rebuke, what might make them wake up, become alert and recall the blessing of Allah upon them. The meaning of remembering the blessing is listening to the method of Allah, carrying out the commands of the Truth and avoiding the prohibitions.

"And when Musa said to his people: O my people, remember the blessing of Allah upon you." We know that "blessing" (ni'mah) is intended as a genus, and what is meant by it is all blessings. Or as if every single blessing is worthy and deserving to be remembered and thanked. The proof that by "blessing" is meant all blessings is that Allah says: ﴿And if you count the blessing of Allah, you will not enumerate it﴾ (Qur'an 14:34).

Since counting the blessing is something we cannot do so as to know its number, they are many blessings. Therefore what is meant by "the blessing" is all blessings, because it is a noun of genus.

"And when Musa said to his people: Remember the blessing of Allah upon you." Remembering the blessing leads to thanking the Benefactor, and it also leads to shame before disobeying the One who bestowed, and makes us ashamed to take His blessing and use it as a help for us in disobeying Him. "Remember the blessing of Allah upon you": they are many blessings you enjoyed. Did the Truth not split the sea for them? ﴿Strike the sea with your staff﴾ (Qur'an 26:63).

And after he struck the water with the staff: ﴿So it split, and each part was like a great mountain﴾ (Qur'an 26:63).

So the flowing water became mountains. And He struck for them the rock by the command of Allah, and water gushed from it: ﴿Strike the rock with your staff, and there gushed from it twelve springs﴾ (Qur'an 2:60).

These are many wonders in which the power of the Supreme Creator is manifest, and power shows the fields of its disposal. Musa struck the sea and it became each part like a great mountain; and as if water became stone, and Musa struck the rock and water gushed forth. These are the wonders of power. Did He not shade you with clouds? Did He not send down upon you in the wilderness manna and quail? And are not all these blessings deserving of remembrance of Allah, thanks to Allah, and shame before disobeying Him or burdening the Messenger who came to guide you?

All these blessings deserve thanks, and thanks is remembrance. "Remember the blessing of Allah upon you, when He made among you prophets and made you kings." And whenever heedlessness overtook them, the Truth would send them a prophet as a behavioural model. He did not become angry with them, nor did He say: I sent them a messenger, then two, three and four. They did not guide themselves; rather, whenever they disobeyed Allah and their illnesses became intractable, He sent them a messenger. Their case is like that of a patient whom his guardian does not begrudge a doctor, or two doctors, or three or four; rather, whenever the guardian notices something, he sends him a doctor. In that there is a favour, because Allah sent to them many messengers, and they should have known that their illnesses had multiplied and their sickness had become intractable. For if the sickness were not intractable, they would not have needed this multitude of doctors and prophets. Yet despite that, Allah had mercy on them, and whenever their illness increased He sent them a prophet.

The Truth did not suffice with making prophets among them, but said: "and made you kings." This does not mean that they all became kings, but that there were kings among them. "Malik" (king) is a word that has taken on a political technical sense, so every person is a possessor (malik) of what is in his possession: he is the owner of his garment, or the owner of the morsel he eats, or the owner of the house in which he sleeps. But the king (malik) is the one who owns and has others owned under him.

So everyone has the capacity to own something, and whoever has others under him becomes a king. A man who has shepherds who tend the herds of livestock he owns, and who has people serving in the house and people working on the farm, and who has more than one driver, and who has many people who carry out his orders and do not enter upon him except by his permission, and for whom meeting them entails no difficulty or hardship: this man must be a king. Thus the Truth has given them abundant blessing.

The Prophet (ﷺ) defined the broad sovereignty that is defined by faith, saying: "Whoever among you wakes up secure in his dwelling, healthy in his body, having his food for the day, it is as if the world has been gathered for him in its entirety."(1)

Since the world has been gathered for him in its entirety through these things, he is a king. He has given them these matters, that is, made them kings. "And He gave you what He had not given to anyone among the worlds": that is, He, glorified is He, gave them what He had not given anyone around them, and He continued that giving to them. Did Allah, glorified is He, not give the Prophet of Allah, our master Sulayman, who was of the Children of Israel, a kingdom that should not belong to anyone after him? That event was not mentioned by Musa, peace be upon him, because it happened after Musa by eleven generations.

1 Narrated by al-Tirmidhi.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 5, verse 21:

The Truth (al-Haqq) says after that:

﴿O my people, enter the Holy Land which Allah has prescribed for you, and do not turn back on your heels, for then you will turn about as losers.﴾ (5:21)

This is a message from Musa (Moses) conveying what Allah revealed to him. And when did that happen? We know that the connection of the Children of Israel (Bani Isra'il) with Egypt went back to the days of Yusuf (Joseph), peace be upon him. When Yusuf brought his father and his brothers and they lived in Egypt, they formed the Shi'a of the Children of Israel, and Allah established Yusuf in the land, and they lived in that period. What is remarkable is that the Qur'anic reference to historical events is of extreme precision, and we did not know those events until after the arrival of the French Expedition to Egypt. When that expedition came, it was accompanied by a scientific mission, and that mission was searching for archaeological information in order to learn the secret of the civilization of the Egyptians, and the secret of the ancient progress of the Arabs, which preceded Europe by centuries, and from which Europe took the sciences and the arts, while this Arab world became heedless.

Indeed, it was the Arab Muslims who invented things that astonished the Western world. History relates to us a gift from one of the Arab kings to Charlemagne, king of France, and it was a clock that struck the hours (daqqaqa). The people of France thought that there was a devil inside this clock. The idea of that clock was that the engineer who made it placed in it a vessel of water with a small hole, from which a drop would fall by its weight onto something resembling the hour hand of a clock, so that the clock would move one minute of time. The clock ran by the drop of water, and its regulation was of the utmost precision. When the people saw it in the court of Charlemagne, king of France, they thought that there were devils inside it. This is one example of many countless examples, which fall within the scope of His saying, the Truth:

﴿We shall show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the Truth﴾ (41:53).

When the French came to Cairo, that scientific mission was with them, and they had a printing press with them. These scholars displayed the magic lantern, and they made the simple people marvel at their scientific progress. That expedition also displayed performances closer to "acrobatics." The work of the scholars was to search for the secret of the civilization of the Egyptians and the Muslims, because they knew that Islamic civilization had passed into Egypt in addition to the civilization of the ancient Egyptians.

They were displaying their scientific magic games in Darb al-Jamamiz, so that people would be dazzled by French civilization, and at the same time their scholars were discovering what was inscribed on the Rosetta Stone (Hajar Rashid), the stone discovered by a young French officer named Champollion. On this stone hieroglyphic words were written, and Champollion was able to separate the hieroglyphic proper names, and through that he was able to reach the alphabet of that language. It is as if Allah wanted to subjugate the disbelievers in the method of Allah to support the method of Allah.

In every language there is something called "the logic of proper names." For example, if there is the name of a man, or a prince, or a person, this name is composed of letters that do not change. Take for example from the English language: the name of the Prime Minister of England at one time was "Churchill." It is a word which, if we translate it literally, does not indicate its owner and does not make us recognize him, because when we translate it we content ourselves with writing the name in Arabic letters instead of Latin.

Therefore, proper names do not change in pronunciation.

Champollion uncovered the letters that did not change, and was guided to unlock the riddles of the letters of the hieroglyphic language, so he knew how to read what was written on the Rosetta Stone, and he was able to present to us the beginnings of the discovery of the history of ancient Egypt, and he was able to read the language drawn on that stone.

We can see the greatness of the Qur'an when it addresses the ancients: it addressed 'Ad, it addressed Thamud, and it addressed Pharaoh; it addressed all those civilizations in Surat al-Fajr, where the Glorified and Exalted said:

﴿By the dawn, and by ten nights, and by the even and the odd, and by the night when it passes. Is there in that an oath for one of understanding? Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with 'Ad, Iram of the pillars, the like of which was not created in the lands?﴾ (89:1-8).

Iram of the pillars is the one in al-Ahqaf in the Arabian Peninsula, which we have not yet discovered, and we know nothing about it until now. It is the one of which the Truth says:

﴿the like of which was not created in the lands﴾ (89:8). Then He speaks after it about Pharaoh:

﴿and Pharaoh of the stakes﴾ (89:10).

The pyramids were indeed erected on stakes, and likewise the ancient Egyptian obelisks, the temples and other wonders that amazed people in various ages.

{the like of which was not created in the lands} (89:8). Then He brought the civilization of Thamud:

{and Thamud, who carved out the rocks in the valley} (89:9).

We have seen this civilization in which people carved houses out of rock, just as we have seen the civilization of Egypt. The civilization of 'Ad is the one we have not seen until now, and it must be buried under the earth. We know that a single sandstorm, when it blows in those regions, buries the entire caravan, so what of the long centuries that passed in which thousands of sandstorms blew? Therefore we must dig a great deal to discover the civilization of 'Ad. The Truth spoke of the civilization of ancient Egypt, saying: "and Pharaoh of the stakes." When He spoke of Musa, peace be upon him, He also spoke of his contemporaries, and one of these was a Pharaoh. He said, glorified is He, to Musa and his brother Harun, peace be upon them both:

﴿Go, both of you, to Pharaoh; indeed he has transgressed﴾ (20:43).

Musa goes to Pharaoh so that he may deliver the Children of Israel from Pharaoh's oppression. And why did Pharaoh oppress them? We know that every policy that follows a previous policy tries to efface the first policy and torments those who supported the first policy, and this is a clear matter in the universe. This is what becomes clear to us from the story of our master Yusuf, who became minister to the Aziz and invited his father, his mother and his followers to Egypt, and the story of Pharaoh does not come in Surat Yusuf.

When the Qur'an spoke of the head of state in the days of Yusuf, it said:

﴿And the king said, "Bring him to me"﴾ (12:54).

The Truth did not say "Pharaoh," although He had said before of him that he was "Pharaoh," and in the days of Musa He mentioned Pharaoh; but in the days of Yusuf He did not bring the story of Pharaoh, He brought the story of a king. When the discovery of the Rosetta Stone came, it became apparent to us that the period of Yusuf's presence in Egypt was the period of the Hyksos kings (mulak al-ru'at), that is, the Hyksos who invaded Egypt, took the kingship from the Egyptians, ruled them, and became kings, and their era was called the era of the kings.

The Qur'an said, "And the king said, 'Bring him to me,'" and it did not mention Pharaoh. When the Pharaohs regained their kingdom and expelled the kings of the shepherds, the Pharaohs tyrannized over those who had been serving the kings, namely the Children of Israel. Thus the precision of the Qur'an is confirmed when it mentions Pharaoh, because he was the ruler in the days of Musa; but in the time of Yusuf the ruler of Egypt was named by the title "king." These are matters we did not know except recently, yet the Qur'an informed us of them. They required deduction, and they fall within the signs that are countless in His saying, the Truth: ﴿We shall show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves﴾ (41:53).

So, glorified and exalted is He, after He supported Musa with signs and drowned Pharaoh, Musa said to them here: ﴿O my people, enter the Holy Land which Allah has prescribed for you, and do not turn back on your heels, for then you will turn about as losers.﴾ (5:21).

The mission had ended with the deliverance of the Children of Israel from Pharaoh, and they had freed the people of Egypt from Pharaoh, and the call was to enter the Holy Land. When the word "land" (ard) is used absolutely, it becomes a proper name for the whole globe, and the word "land" occurs in the story of the Children of Israel in many places, referring to many locations.

Behold, the saying of Allah at the end of Surat al-Isra':

﴿And We said after him to the Children of Israel, "Dwell in the land"﴾ (17:104).

Is there any dwelling except in the land? No one says "dwell in such-and-such" unless he specifies a place of the land, because dwelling will certainly be in the land, so how does the expression "dwell in the land" come? What is common is to say: "dwell in such-and-such place of the cities," such as al-Mansura or Jericho, or Jerusalem. The Truth's saying "dwell in the land" is a Qur'anic allusion, and since the Truth did not specify a particular dwelling-place from the land, it is as if He said: "Dissolve into the land, for you have no homeland; and disperse through the land, for you have no homeland," meaning that no settlement shall ever be established for you, and you will wander through the land in scattered groups. And He, glorified is He, said:

﴿And We divided them in the land into communities﴾ (7:168).

When the Qur'an brings a Qur'anic issue, let us examine whether the cosmic facts support it or oppose it. The Qur'anic issue here is the dispersal of the Children of Israel in the land as communities, that is, their division and scattering. The Qur'an did not say "We humiliated them," but said "We divided them" (qatta'na-hum), and this implies that He placed between them separations, yet they are dispersed in the lands. When we see them in any country they settle in, we find that they have a special quarter, and they do not dissolve among the citizens at all, and they have everything that pertains to them of needs by which they are self-sufficient, so it is as if they are spread throughout the land while being divided in the land, yet they are communities. Thus there are "quarters" and special places for Jews in every country.

That happened after Musa, peace be upon him. But what was the situation in the days of Musa? The Truth said to them: "Enter the Holy Land which Allah has prescribed for you," meaning: after your journey with Pharaoh, go to the land which Allah has written for you. And we note here that the expression "the Holy Land" contains a specification and determination of the land.

But what is the meaning of "holy" (muqaddasa)? The root as a whole indicates purity and purification. "Qadusa" means he became pure and free from defect. "Muqaddasa" means purified, and words, when they come, all their derivations converge on related meanings. In the Egyptian countryside we find what we call the "qads" or "qadus," which is the vessel by which water is lifted from the irrigation channel (saqiya), and they used it for purification; so the qadus in the Egyptian countryside is the vessel of clean water. When it is said "muqaddasa," it means purified.

Among the names of the Truth is "al-Quddus," and it is said "Qaddasa Allah," meaning He is exalted above imperfection. Allah is an essence, but not like the essence of man, and He has attributes that are exalted beyond being like your attributes, and He has acts, but His holiness and purity are exalted beyond being like your acts. The essence of the Truth is necessarily existent, while the essence of man is possibly existent, because over man's essence there came a first non-existence and there will come a second non-existence; and He, glorified is He, is necessarily existent in Himself, while man is necessarily existent through another. He, glorified is He, is able to end the existence of the servant. Allah has life, and man has life, but is your life, O man, like the life of Allah? No.

His life, glorified is He, is exalted, and His essence is not like your essence, and His attributes are not like your attributes; you are capable with limited capability, while He, glorified is He, has absolute freedom of power. He, glorified is He, is All-Hearing, and the servant is hearing, but the hearing of man is limited, while His hearing, glorified is He, has no limits.

Therefore His attributes are holy. Hence when you hear that He, glorified is He, is All-Hearing, All-Knowing, His hearing is not like our hearing, and He has an act unlike our act. When the Truth says that He acted, His act is exalted above being likened to the acts of men, because men are created by Allah, and the act of men is treatment (mu'alaja), and the act has a beginning, a middle and an end, and it is limited by events according to time; we carry things in various times, and whoever carries things needs strength. But the act of the Truth is different: it is an act by "Be," therefore He said:

﴿And We created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, and no fatigue touched Us﴾ (50:38),

meaning that He, glorified and exalted is He, is exalted above weariness. He says "Be, and it is," and therefore we said regarding the matter of the Isra' that we must attribute the event to Allah and not to Muhammad, peace be upon him, so that we know that those who opposed the Messenger of Allah regarding the Isra' were in error. They said: "Shall we journey to it on the backs of camels for a month, and you claim that you went there in a night?"

The Messenger of Allah did not claim this matter for himself, for he did not say: "I travelled from Makkah to Bayt al-Maqdis," so that you would say: "Shall we journey to it on the backs of camels for a month, and you claim that you went there in a night?"

Rather, the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said: "I was taken by night" (usriya bi), meaning that he, peace be upon him, had no act in the event, and the act belongs to

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 5, verse 22:

So turning back on one's heels is not blameworthy if it is for the sake of a stratagem or setting an ambush for the enemy; in that case it is no fault for a person to withdraw. Other than that, it is blameworthy. Is turning back on one's heels a returning backwards with the back turned while the face is kept toward the opponent, or is it turning the face toward the rear and fleeing from the enemy? Both meanings are valid. The command was given to the Children of Israel not to flee so that they would enter the land, so what was their stance, since the writing of this command is legislative?

﴿They said, "O Moses, indeed therein is a people of tyrants, and indeed we will never enter it until they leave it. So if they leave it, then indeed we will enter."﴾ (5:22)

How, then, did they announce this rebellion against the command of the Truth? And how did they know that therein is a people of tyrants? We should note that the Truth had said earlier: ﴿And We raised from among them twelve leaders﴾ (part of 5:12).

The leaders (nuqaba') went first, scouted, probed and learned the story of this holy land, and that therein was a group of the Canaanite Amalekites. When they saw these people, they said to themselves: "Will we be able to resist these people? Indeed, that is a matter that is not believable. Therefore we will never enter it while they are in it." So they faltered and turned back on their heels: "They said, 'O Moses, indeed therein is a people of tyrants.'"

When you hear the word "jabbar" (tyrant), you find it is a moral meaning drawn from sensible things. The jabbarah is the palm tree whose fruit a person's hand cannot reach when he wants to pick its fruit. When the fruit of the palm is within the reach of a person's hand when he picks it, it is "close-hanging" (dani al-qutuf). But the one that a person's hand cannot reach at the moment of picking the fruit is "jabbarah." Therefore this meaning was taken to express what cannot be overcome, and so it was called "jabbar." The jabbar may also be one who compels, but for the sake of setting things right. In our country we call the one who sets broken bones "al-mujabbarati."

That is, he forces the bones to return to their natural place. A person may suffer from that, but in it there is a correction of the person's life. "Al-Jabbar" is one of the names of God, because He, glory be to Him, overpowers and is not overpowered. He, glory be to Him and exalted, may compel us so that He corrects us, and He tests us with trials so that He purifies us and our lives become balanced.

Thus "al-jabbar" is an attribute of perfection in the Truth, because He uses His majesty in goodness and subdues the wrongdoers, the stubborn and the arrogant, for the benefit of the righteous and good. He, glory be to Him and exalted, is not overpowered; when He is on the side of a group, no one defeats them. As an attribute in creation, however, "jabbar" is blameworthy, because the tyranny here is without substance, like a hollow building. The tyrant may be struck by a little headache and lie down groaning.

We see examples of this in our lives: we find the tyrant struck by a heart crisis and carried on a stretcher to the hospital, and we find another tyrant struck by a little colic who runs holding his belly, so children laugh at him and say to him something like: "Play far away, you are not a jabbar, nor a strongman, nor anything." The jabbar, if he wishes to be such, must have a continuous reserve; you never see him one day not a jabbar. Tyranny is not an essential attribute except of God, glory be to Him.

The Truth says: ﴿and indeed we will never enter it until they leave it﴾. When we hear "lan" (never) preceding the verb, we know it is for negation, and negation may take a long time or may take an everlasting time. The difference between entering merely and entering everlastingly is that the first entering has a time that ends it, while the second has no time to end it, like the entry of the believers into Paradise.

When entering is specified by an end, as in their saying: ﴿and indeed we will never enter it until they leave it﴾, the everlasting negation is tied to an end, which is the departure of the tyrannical people. The "everlastingness" here is relative, because they said that they would not enter the land during the period of the presence of the tyrants.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 5, verse 23:

"If they go out from it, then we shall enter." We say: Can it be that in nations that have plunged into evil and practise it, the presence of elements of good is impossible? No, because the Truth (al-Haqq) leaves some elements of good so that goodness is not obliterated. This is what the Truth makes clear regarding the Children of Israel when they said this statement to Moses, and two men among them opposed them.

﴿Two men from among those who feared, upon whom Allah had bestowed His favour, said: "Enter upon them through the gate, for when you have entered it, you will be the victors. And upon Allah rely, if you are believers."﴾ (5:23)

These were two men who feared turning back from the command of Allah, whereas the Children of Israel, as a body, did not understand Allah rightly, for if they had carried out Allah's command to enter the Holy Land and had not turned back, Allah would have enabled them to do so. But none understood Allah in this matter except two men: Caleb (Kalib) and Joshua (Yusha') son of Nun, one of them from the tribe of Judah and the other from the tribe of Ephraim, and they were the two sons of Joseph, peace be upon him. They said: "Since Allah has decreed for you the entry, He does not ask of us except a little struggle (jihad)."

When Allah commands a person to do a deed, it suffices for him to turn towards the deed with resolve, and the help is from Allah. And Allah, glorified is He, says to the servant:

("I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me. If he remembers Me within himself, I remember him within Myself; and if he remembers Me in an assembly, I remember him in an assembly better than theirs; and if he draws near to Me a span, I draw near to him a cubit; and if he draws near to Me a cubit, I draw near to him a fathom; and if he comes to Me walking, I come to him running.")(1)

If walking is ordinarily tiring to the one who goes and travels, Allah does not wish to burden with walking the one who seeks Him and asks of Him; rather His grace and mercy run towards the servant. The first desire is that the work be yours, O servant, and among the greatest of Allah's favours is that He acts and attributes it to you. He, glorified is He, is pleased with the servant who strives towards Him. Let me give this example, and to Allah belongs the highest similitude: suppose you wished to grasp a sword. Why not analyse the matter? The sword you hold was made of iron, and the iron you extracted from the earth. And the Truth says: ﴿And We sent down iron, wherein is great might and benefits for mankind﴾ (57:25).

Indeed, it is the Truth who sent down iron, and it is He who taught us how to forge iron and shape it with fire:

﴿And We taught him the making of coats of mail for you, to protect you from your violence﴾ (21:80).

I would ask the physiologists to specify for us the moment a person grasps something, let it be a sword: with which muscle does a person grip the sword? And how does a person command it to do so? How many muscles and how many nerve cells moved in order to perform this act? Even though a person, merely by his will to grasp something, grasps it; and when a person takes a single step, with which muscles does the walking begin?

When a person moves a mechanical arm in a mechanical device, engineers design dozens of joints, tools and electrical circuits in order to move one mechanical arm; so how many muscles in a person move in walking a single step? Very many of the body's systems move merely by his will. If a person's will acts merely by his wanting, whether that will is to grasp a sword, or even to take a single step, or even to hold a pen between the fingers for writing, then let a person know that will is a gift from Allah, and a person cannot determine the locations of his will within his body; how much less then the Truth when He wills a matter?

Let us return to the verse about which we are now reflecting: ﴿Two men from among those who feared, upon whom Allah had bestowed His favour, said: "Enter upon them through the gate, for when you have entered it, you will be the victors. And upon Allah rely, if you are believers."﴾ (5:22 in his numbering of this passage, surah al-Ma'idah).

Allah bestowed His favour upon these two men with a good understanding of Allah, so they said to the Children of Israel: Help yourselves by entering this land, and Allah will give you victory. The likeness of the two men is that of a mother whose son asked her to pray for his success, and the mother said to her son: I will pray for you, but you must only assist the prayer by applying yourself to study. It is as though fear of opposing Allah's command was a favour upon these two men, and as though understanding Allah's words was a favour.

"Enter upon them through the gate, for when you have entered it, you will be the victors." It is as though by merely entering they would overcome these giants; Allah did not ask them to fight these giants, rather at the moment the mighty people see them entering upon them suddenly, terror will overwhelm them.

When they wove legends around this story, they said: one of these giants, named Og son of Anak, went out to an orchard outside the city to pick some fruit for his chief, and he snatched two of these people and hid them in his sleeve, and cast them before his chief as he was presenting the fruit to him, and the giant said to his chief: "These are of the group that wants to enter our city." This is the exaggeration that their fear of these giants produced, although two of them had understood Allah well in saying: "Enter upon them through the gate," because this is the will of Allah, and it is He who brings them victory.

Some exegetes said in explaining this verse that the two men who spoke these words were not from the Children of Israel, because these exegetes understood the wise statement "Two men from among those who feared" to mean: they were two men of those whom the Children of Israel feared, and they said to the Children of Israel: Let not the great size of these people frighten or terrify you, for the soldiers of Allah will give you victory:

﴿And none knows the hosts of your Lord except Him﴾ (74:31).

The verse concludes with this appendage: "And upon Allah rely, if you are believers," meaning: do not stop at counting numbers against numbers, and equipment against equipment, but reckon the matter as faith, for Allah is with you: "If you help Allah, He will help you." He, glorified is He, also said: ﴿And indeed Our soldiers, they will be the victors﴾ (37:173).

(1) Narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim (agreed upon).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 5, verse 24:

It is incumbent upon the believer in God to place this faith in the palm of his strength. So if these people, from the Children of Israel, who were commanded to enter that land, are truly believers, then let them put their trust in God.

So what did these people say?

﴿They said: "O Moses, we will never enter it as long as they are in it. So go, you and your Lord, and fight, while we will sit here."﴾

It is as if the essence of their words to Moses, peace be upon him, was: Do not exhaust yourself on our account, and spare yourself your effort, for we will never enter this land while these giants are in it. And if you are determined that we enter this land, then go, you and your Lord, and fight, while we will be sitting here waiting for you. Such was the extent of their fear that they mocked Moses and the Lord of Moses, and such was the depth to which their ridicule descended, that wretched level. This was not a new matter for them, for they had said earlier:

﴿Show us God openly﴾ (from verse 153 of Surah al-Nisa').

And before that too, they worshipped the calf. So what does Moses say?

﴿He said: "My Lord, I have no control except over myself and my brother, so separate us from the defiantly disobedient people."﴾

Harun was the brother of Musa, peace be upon him, and a messenger like him. It is as if Musa, peace be upon him, had announced his lack of confidence in these people to whom Allah had sent him, including Yusha' ibn Nun and Kalib, the two men who said to the Children of Israel: it is enough for you to enter the gate, and you will defeat these giant people. But was the soul of his brother his property? Or did he say, in substance: I own only my own soul, and my brother owns only his own soul; as for the rest of the people, I have heard from them, O Lord, that they will not enter this land so long as these giants are in it. So then, I and my brother are on one side and the rest are on the other side. Therefore, separate between us and these defiant people.

In this Qur'anic expression, the Truth, glory be to Him, brings these words on the tongue of our master Musa, and they may move the heart of one of Musa's followers, who would say to Musa: I am with you. Hence came Musa's saying: "So separate between us and the defiant people." The meaning of "fasiqin" (defiant ones, those who transgress), as we have known, is those who have gone out of faith, just as the date (rutabah) defies its husk (fasaqat al-ruṭbah) when it ripens: its skin widens beyond its size and the date comes out of its skin. It is said: "fasaqat al-ruṭbah." So faith is like the hide, and the hide is like the husk, a covering that surrounds the human being. When a person defies faith, he goes outside the law of protection. Such was the defiance of the Children of Israel. Therefore the Truth said:

﴿He said: "It is forbidden to them for forty years; they will wander in the land. So do not grieve over the defiant people."﴾ (5:26)

Was the prohibition for a period of forty years? Or did He say, "It is forbidden to them," and the matter ended because they refused to enter it? For this reason, all those who said, "We will never enter it as long as they are in it," did not live to enter this land. After that, the following ruling was issued: "For forty years they will wander in the land." Is this statement a continuation of the previous one, so that it is a time-clause for "forbidden," or is it a separate ruling?

Both readings are valid. Wandering (al-tih) is, as we say: "So-and-so wandered" (taha), meaning he walked without guidance, not knowing how to find an entrance or an exit for himself. When a person enters a region with intricate paths and winding roads, he does not know how to get out of it; that is wandering. But how many farsakh (parasangs) is the area of the wandering? The scholars have specified it as six farsakh, and a farsakh is three miles. How could they wander in such a narrow area of land?

God willed it, because whenever they walked and became exhausted, they slept, and when morning came they found themselves at the point where they had started. They used to place markers to clarify the way, but each morning they found the markers had been moved from their places. They remained in this place and in this wandering until the term and time that God had set, which is forty years: "For forty years they will wander in the land." When God disciplines a disobedient person, He preserves for him the sustenance and provision that keep his life going, even if he is a disbeliever, because He, glory be to Him, is the One who brought them into existence. For this reason, He did not withhold from them during the wandering what He did not withhold from the disbelievers in Him, glory be to Him.

Therefore, preserving life is a necessity. When a person commits a grave wrong against society, we put him in prison, but we feed him and give him drink. And when human society advances, it provides the prisoner with work suited to his talents and withholds from him freedom of movement in society. The guilty prisoner remains in prison, but he eats, drinks, sleeps and works. The matter differs only in the important point in life, which is that the one who moves should move according to his freedom. So what of the Supreme Truth when He imprisoned them in the wandering? God fed them and gave them drink, and sent down upon them the manna and the quails.

Someone may say: God sent down the manna and the quails so that they would live in idleness and heedlessness, drowning in arrogance and pride. We say: No. That divine arrangement is among His profound wisdoms, that He prolong the time for them. Had He made them plant and till, they would have been occupied with the affairs of daily life. But the Truth wanted to prolong their sense of time. The matter is not food and drink, but there is a dignity above food and above drink.

We see this when we hear of the detention of some individuals who have harmed society, and the authorities permit them food brought to them from their homes; yet these detainees feel distress at the restriction of movement. Thus the Truth wanted for them a severe punishment during the period of wandering. For this reason we find some of them calculating the matter and the time during the wandering, as one of them says what the Truth has mentioned: ﴿And We appointed for Moses thirty nights and completed them with ten, so the appointed time of his Lord was complete as forty nights. And Moses said to his brother Aaron, "Take my place among my people."﴾ (Qur'an 7:142).

After Moses departed from the people, they worshipped the calf which Moses the Samiri had made for them. Moses returned to them and rebuked his brother Aaron with a harsh rebuke. Their Lord punished them for their disbelief for forty years, as if each day of worshipping the calf became a year of punishment in the wandering. And because He is Lord and Merciful, He did not leave them without preserving their lives with sustenance; the sustenance was the manna and the quails. Was Moses, peace be upon him, with them in the wandering or not? Did he die with them in the wandering or not?
