For He, as He sent down the Qur'an which carries the method, also sent down iron, and it is upon man to derive iron and the raw materials that make it easy for us to manufacture scientific instruments, and to establish factories that produce steel from iron, and to convert steel into armor, and to make the most precise instruments that give the fighter the opportunity of victory. Likewise, we store food supplies to suffice in days of war.

Thus the whole movement of life is jihad. Beware of restricting the idea of jihad in your mind to the battlefield; rather, prepare yourself for the battle, for if you prepare yourself well and your enemy knows that you have prepared against him, he may refrain from fighting you. What currently prevents the world from a hot war that would destroy it is the fear of the balanced blocs, because every state prepares itself for war; and if a single power in the universe existed, it would destroy the world.

As for the saying of the Truth, "and strive in His cause," we take it to mean striving in the cause of the method of Allah. We study this method and understand it, and then we strive in it with the tongue and with the spear, and we strive in it with the book and we strive in it with the battalion.

Thus His saying, the Truth, "and strive in His cause," produces a civilized faithful nation, so that the disbeliever in Allah is not left the opportunity to take the causes of Allah and His secrets in the universe. He who worships the One God is more entitled to the secret of Allah in existence. Even if we assume that no war will take place, we still possess factories that produce, and we have agriculture that meets people's needs; then we will achieve sufficiency, and what you do not use in war will serve peace. And you must understand that all the inventions of progressive life first arise for the purpose of war, and afterward souls calm down and humanity takes these achievements for the benefit of peace.

Then, after that, the Truth (al-Haqq), glory be to Him, says:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, even if they had all that is on the earth and the like of it with it, to ransom themselves thereby from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, it would not be accepted from them, and they will have a painful punishment.﴾ (36)

Al-Haqq, glory be to Him, previously spoke of punishments, retribution (qisas), killing and cutting off (of limbs). Then He moves us from this atmosphere to (the call) that we fear Allah, seek the means (al-wasilah) to Him, and strive in His cause so that we may prosper. It was necessary for al-Haqq to bring us the counterpart: the punishment that came earlier, such as retribution and killing, is a punishment of this world, but what will come in the Hereafter is more grievous and more bitter.

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, even if they had all that is on the earth and the like of it with it, to ransom themselves thereby from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, it would not be accepted from them, and they will have a painful punishment.﴾ (Surah al-Ma'idah).

Let us imagine the disbelieving group that is arrogant in this world and rises up and elevates itself through tyranny. What then of their situation on the Day of Resurrection? You established tyranny by your strength over others, and now that strength is lost and slips away. Strength lived with you in this world through the means granted to you by Allah, and the sunan of Allah would not withhold from you the means of rising. He, glory be to Him, created the sunan (laws), and whoever seeks the causes of Allah will attain the result of the effort he exerted. But here it is, the Day of Resurrection, and here you are, you know that causes are not self-originating, and that your strength was nothing but a gift from Allah. Here you are before the living scene. So even if everything in the world were with you, and even if it were double what is in the world, and you wished to offer it as ransom from the punishment of Hell, Allah does not accept it. That is the summit of disgrace, and they will be unable to rescue themselves from the punishment of Hell.

This scene makes the soul sense that the matter is not play nor jest, but is utmost seriousness. A person must weigh the punishment before he savours the sin. What causes people to persist in transgressing against themselves is that one of them separates the crime from the punishment of the crime. If a person, before he exceeds against himself, compared the punishment with the crime, he would not have committed it. Likewise the one who is lazy in obedience: if he compared obedience with its reward, he would hasten to it.

Let me give this example, and to Allah belongs the highest example: suppose a man in a desert looked up at a mountain and saw an apple tree, and he inferred the apple from an apple that was spoiled and lying on the ground. The man said to himself: "Here I see the fates of people. This one climbs the mountain and falls at its edge, that one is attacked by wolves, and a third gets lost from the path," all in hope that there are fruits in the tree. And I must choose the right path to the fruits. The path to the fruits of this world is obedience to the method of Allah, and it is the path to the fruits of the Hereafter.

Also: the diligent student who overcomes sleepiness, performs ablution and prays, and goes out to his school in the cold of winter to attain his lessons, then returns home to find his mother has prepared food for him, yet he is preoccupied with the lesson. This young man keeps the result of this effort in mind, so every hardship in the pursuit of learning becomes easy for him. But if he neglected, slept, and did not rise early for school, or if he woke and left the house to loiter in the streets with his peers, then in such a state he would not be considering the result to which vagrancy leads. The defect in people is that they separate work from its result, and separate the crime from its punishment and obedience from its reward. If we placed the result opposite the deed, no one would commit disobedience, and no one would neglect obedience.

Let us imagine the scene of the tyrants of this world in the fire of the Hereafter. They oppressed and plundered in this world. Let us suppose that one of them possessed everything in the world, though this is impossible, and moreover took the like of it with him, wishing to offer it to ransom himself from the punishment of Hell, and the Truth rejects it from him: "it would not be accepted from them, and they will have a painful punishment." That is the summit of disgrace from which a person must keep away.

After that, the Truth (Allah) says:

﴿They wish to come out of the Fire, but they will not come out of it, and theirs is a lasting punishment.﴾

Whenever the blaze of the Fire touches them, they wish to come out of it. But how could the will to come out of the Fire arise in them? It must be that at the moment its flames strike them, and they toss and turn here and there, the tongues of fire push them close to the outside, so they think the punishment has ended. Did not the Truth, glory be to Him, say, in order to set before us the complete depiction of the horror of Hell:

﴿And if they ask for relief, they will be relieved with water like molten brass that scalds the faces.﴾ (Qur'an 18:29)

This statement first suggests that some mercy will reach them, but what comes after it draws the full terror and embodies it: ﴿they will be relieved with water like molten brass that scalds the faces.﴾ (Qur'an 18:29)

This is the peak of horror, and there is a difference between a beginning that raises hope and an ending that brings despair.

An example of this is the thirsty prisoner who asks for a cup of water, and the jailer may simply say to him: "No, there is no water here." But if the jailer wants to torture him further, he says: "I will bring you water," and he brings him a cup of clear, cool water. The prisoner stretches out his hand toward the cup, but the jailer pours the cup out onto the ground. This is the beginning that raises hope and the ending that brings despair. Likewise is their desire to leave the Fire: they have no will to leave it except when there is a presumption that they might come out as a result of the flames turning them over. For this reason the Truth also says about these people: ﴿So give them good tidings﴾ (Qur'an 3:21).

Good tidings stir in the soul the hope of pardon, so they rejoice, but the result is: ﴿a painful punishment﴾ (Qur'an 3:21).

Thus the Truth wills for them the shock of painful despair after hopeful expectation.

{They wish to come out of the Fire, but they will not come out of it, and theirs is a lasting punishment. (5:37)}

The Hand of the Thief: Commentary on Surah 5, Verse 38

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) moves us to His saying, glory be to Him:

﴿As for the thief, male or female, cut off their hands as a recompense for what they have earned, and as an exemplary punishment from Allah. Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.﴾ (5:38)

The Truth previously dealt with the punishment of highwaymen (qutta' al-tariq) and those who spread corruption on earth. Here He brings another matter, by which He wishes to safeguard the fruit of the believer's activity within his society. Faith requires that the believer move and act, and in order for a person to act, he must be assured of the fruit of his action. If a person acts and the fruit comes, and then someone comes and takes it, the one who acts will be discouraged from acting. When a person is discouraged from action, the progress of existence comes to a halt. Thus it is in our interest that the movement of life continues, and the movement of life does not continue unless a person is secure in his activity, and his activity is within what Allah has legislated.

When a person moves within what Allah has legislated and earns from what is lawful, no one has any claim over him, because the activity of this person benefits society, whether or not he intends it.

We said before: a man who possesses money and hoards it finds the Truth commanding him to invest this money, for He, glory be to Him, commanded the opening of the doors of good to whoever finds money. An idea of constructing a towering building arises in the heart of the owner of the money, so the man says to himself: "My money is hoarded, so let me build a building for myself." The Truth makes this matter attractive to him, and the man considers building a building of ten floors, with four apartments on each floor, and let the rent of each apartment be one hundred pounds, which is a monthly income that is not to be disdained.

The man calculates the matter, not knowing that Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, casts thoughts into his mind. So he hastens to buy the plot of land, and after that he brings someone to design the building and someone to construct it, and the hoarded money is spent. Thus we see that the wealthy man, before he benefits from his building, has been preceded by others who benefited from his money, even the poorest strata of society, and all of this happens merely through a thought. Every person has his thoughts: the miser has someone who squanders his money, and the generous person has someone who hoards his money. Beware of supposing that there is any movement in existence outside the will of Allah. The Truth says:

﴿Except those who repent after that and make amends﴾ (part of 3:89).

They do this because sins pursue them, so they compensate for that by reforming their deeds. Therefore we find that good comes from those who have been wasteful toward themselves, as they wish to set their affairs right, and no one can take anything from beside Allah.

﴿Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds﴾ (part of 11:114).

It is as if the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, by mere thoughts, pushes people toward what He wills. Indeed He is the Unseen, the Self-Subsisting (al-Qayyum), and therefore His management of the cosmos is unseen. In our village they set aside a day for the market. We see its courtyard on the designated day and reflect upon it, and we marvel at the originality of the Mover of the cosmos. In the morning men walk to the market carrying their staffs and carrying nothing else; these are going to buy what they need. Others drive before them calves or donkeys; these are going to sell their goods. We see women, each carrying a type of vegetable, and we know that they are going to sell at the market, and we see other women carrying empty baskets, and we know that each of them is going to buy. At the end of the day we see the matter reversed: whoever carried something in the morning has had it carried by another. So who stirred up the thoughts that led the seller to go to the market to sell?

Who moved the buyer to buy? It is the Truth, glory be to Him, who enables the one who wishes to sell to find a buyer, and enables the one who wishes to buy to find a seller. This is the arrangement of the Living, the Self-Subsisting. And we hear someone say: "Today we brought twenty tons of tomatoes to the market, and forty tons of squash, and other tonnages," and we find at the end of the day that everything has been sold. These are the balanced thoughts of Allah among people, which balance society.

Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, wants to protect the one who acts, and He also makes clear that a person should not feed himself or enjoy benefits without effort, because whoever steals is taking the effort of another, and this act discourages others from work.

In Islam there is a principle: when unemployment increases, it is said to you: do not give charity to people from the wealth you own, but rather open any project, even if you do not need it, such as digging a well and then filling it in, and give the laborer his wage, so that a person does not grow accustomed to idleness. Rather, he must be trained to work. Whoever cannot work must have a guarantee of support. A person's provision is guaranteed first by his own work. If he is unable to work, his guarantee comes from his family and relatives. If he has no family or relatives, then the people of his neighborhood are responsible for him. And if the people of the village or the neighborhood cannot provide for him, then the public treasury (bayt al-mal) is obligated to take responsibility for the poor.

Therefore the faith-based foundation urges us to guarantee work for the person, or to support him and provide what he needs if he is incapable. But the affliction is that some people love a job for its own sake: this one wishes to be appointed to a position in which there is no work, and we say to him: in the contemporary world there is a crisis of excess labor, so learn some skill, for life has never withheld sustenance from one who seeks it through work.

We have in the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) an excellent example, when he held the first auction in Islam, when a man from the Ansar came to him asking him. He said to him: "Do you not have anything in your house?" The man said: "Yes, a rough mat, part of which we wear and part of which we spread out, and a cup (qa'b), that is, a bowl, from which we drink water." He said: "Bring me both of them." So he brought them, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took them in his hand and said: "Who will buy these two?" A man said: "I will take them for a dirham." He said: "Who will offer more than a dirham?" He said it twice or three times. A man said: "I will take them for two dirhams." So he gave them to him, took the two dirhams and gave them to the Ansari, and said: "Buy food with one of them and throw it to your family (anbidhu, i.e., cast it to them), and buy with the other an axe and bring it to me."(1)

So the Prophet (ﷺ) advised the man and commanded him to bring the mat he slept on and the cup he drank from, so that the man would know that he was trading in something he owned, not receiving a gift from anyone. The man came into the presence of the Prophet (ﷺ) and found that the Prophet had fitted a handle to the axe, and the man said: "Go, gather firewood and sell it, and I do not want to see you for fifteen days."(2)

The man went out gathering firewood and selling it, in obedience to the command of the Prophet (ﷺ), and came back after fifteen days, having earned ten dirhams, so he bought a garment with some of it and food with some of it.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "This is better for you than that begging should come as a mark on your face on the Day of Resurrection."(3)

This is education.

So the essential purpose is that Islam protects the members of society. The one who cannot find his sustenance, we help him with opinion, knowledge, capacity and strength, and the best is to teach them to work for themselves. Therefore the Truth has brought us the story of Dhu al-Qarnayn, full of lessons:

﴿Until, when he reached between the two barriers, he found beside them a people who could hardly understand any speech﴾ (18:93).

That is, there was no common ground for understanding; yet they said:

﴿They said: O Dhu al-Qarnayn, indeed Gog and Magog are corrupters in the land. So shall we pay you a tribute on condition that you set up a barrier between us and them?﴾ (18:94).

And here Dhu al-Qarnayn declares that he has no need of them, but he assigns them a task so that he may fulfill their wish:

﴿Bring me sheets of iron,” until, when he had leveled [them] between the two cliffs, he said, “Blow,” until, when he had made it fire, he said, “Bring me molten copper to pour over it.﴾ (18:96).

It is remarkable that when the Qur'an narrates a matter, it narrates it only for a purpose. They asked Dhu al-Qarnayn to build a barrier (sadd), but he proposed to give them a rampart (radm). What is the difference? Modern science has shown that a barrier (sadd) may be struck by a tremor from any side and collapse entirely, whereas a rampart (radm), if struck by a tremor, grows more firm. Dhu al-Qarnayn did not work for them, but taught them how to build the rampart, so that they would not live with the feeling of helplessness. Thus the Qur'an teaches us that a person must have work. But what if he steals?

First, what is theft (sariqah)? It is taking property of value secretly. If the taking is not secret, it is usurpation (ghasb). Another time it is seizure (khatf), and a fourth time it is embezzlement (ikhtilas).

Taking has many kinds. A merchant standing in his shop to sell something, when a small child comes, snatches a piece of candy and runs away, and the merchant cannot reach the child or manage to hold him: this is seizure (khatf). As for the one who usurps, he is the one who overpowers the owner of a thing so that he leaves it to him. As for embezzlement (ikhtilas), it is when a person entrusted with property takes it from it. As for theft (sariqah), it is taking property of value secretly, from a protected place (hirz) of its kind, that is, a place which no one other than its owner can enter or dispose of except with his permission. As for one who leaves his door open or leaves his goods in the street, he is negligent. Just as the Law commands that no one steal from another, so it commands that one not be negligent. Rather, a person must tie up his belongings and rely on Allah. He, glory be to Him, is the just Legislator who establishes vigilance on both sides. The Law defined theft as involving property worth a quarter of a dinar, and a quarter of a dinar in that time sufficed for a person, his dependents and more to eat. Indeed, a dirham then sufficed to sustain a family in that era.

How do we assess a quarter of a dinar in our time? If it does not suffice for living, then the threshold must be raised to what sustains life. Since the dinar was gold in that time, the value of a quarter of a dinar rises. In the past the gold pound was worth ninety-seven and a half piasters, whereas the gold pound now is worth more than two hundred and seventy pounds. A person may steal because he is in need or hungry, and therefore the Law set for him a measure which the one in need does not exceed to preserve his life and the life of those he supports, and that is the dirham. Stealing a dirham carries no prescribed penalty (hadd), just as it carries no sin, provided that he has exhausted all lawful means of obtaining sustenance. We know that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave the dirham to the man and said: "Buy food for yourself and your family."

As we said, a dirham sufficed in that time, and the dirham is one-twelfth of the dinar, so a quarter of a dinar is three dirhams, and the dirham in our time is worth more than twenty pounds.

The superficial say: Sayyidna 'Umar suspended the prescribed penalty for theft in the Year of Ramada. We say to them: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab did not cancel the prescribed penalty; the penalty remains, but he did not apply it to the incident that took place, in which there was doubt (shubha). The incident that happened in the Year of Ramada, the year of famine, involved the presence of doubt, and with his acuteness as the first Commander of the Faithful, he did not apply to the incidents what requires the penalty. In the matter of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Hatib ibn Abi Balta'a, when his servants stole, what happened? The servants said to 'Umar: "We were hungry, and Ibn Abi Balta'a was not giving us food." And Sayyidna 'Umar averted the penalty because of doubt.

Thus the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, wants to protect the one who acts and the fruit of his action. But some superficial thinkers in understanding say, like what al-Ma'arri said:

"A hand for which five hundred gold dinars were paid as blood-money, why was it cut for a quarter of a dinar? A contradiction. For us there is only silence about Him, and that we take refuge in our Lord from the Fire."

Here a believing scholar responded and said:

"You object because we give the blood-money (diyah) for a hand as five hundred dinars, and when a person steals we cut off the thief's hand because it took a quarter of a dinar."

And the believing scholar said:

"The honour of trustworthiness is most precious and cheapest; the humiliation of betrayal, so understand the wisdom of the Creator."

We notice that criminal legislation and penal provisions are not human legislation, but are legislation of utmost precision. By God, if a legislator legislated for the male thief or female thief, and legislated for the male adulterer and female adulterer, what would the position be?

It is the Lord of the Worlds who speaks, and He says here: "As for the thief, male or female, cut off their hands as a recompense for what they have earned, and as an exemplary punishment from Allah. Allah is Almighty, All-Wise." Theft is usually an act driven by need, and it is often the man's act. As for the adulterer and adulteress, if the man had not been stirred and aroused by the beauty of a woman, he would not have thought of fornication. Thus she is the originator of the beginning, and He, glory be to Him, specifies the punishment, and He brought...

(1) Narrated by Abu Dawud in Zakat, and Ibn Majah in Commerce, and narrated by Ahmad.
(2) Narrated by Ahmad and Abu Dawud in Zakat and Ibn Majah in Commerce.
(3) Narrated by Ahmad and Abu Dawud in Zakat and Ibn Majah in Commerce.

And after that, the Truthful One (al-Haqq, subhanahu) opens the door of repentance, as a mercy to the one who repents and a mercy to society. Therefore the Truth says:

﴿But whoever repents after his wrongdoing and reforms, indeed Allah will turn to him in forgiveness. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (39)

The thief is a wrongdoer (zalim), because he has taken the right of another. So if he repents, meaning he regrets the act and resolves not to return to it, on the condition that his repentance is not by words alone but that he also sets right what he has corrupted, then repentance is accepted. But how does he do that?

If the stolen item is still in his possession, he must return it to its owner. If he has already disposed of it, he must go to the owner of the item and seek his pardon (istihlal), saying to him: "I was heedless of myself and the devil's pride overcame me, so I did such-and-such." I believe that any person who stole from another and, after a while, confessed to him and asked his forgiveness, I swear by Allah that he will pardon him willingly, and in this way the thing he took is made lawful for him. But what if the thief does not know the owner of the stolen item, like the pickpocket of the buses ("al-Atubisat")?

If he stole a wallet from a person and he finds the address, he can return the stolen item by a postal money order from an anonymous sender carrying the value of the stolen sum, and in it he asks for forgiveness for the theft. If he does not know whom he stole from, he should say: "God knows the owner of this sum, and I will give it in charity in the way of Allah, and I say: O Lord, let its reward be for its owner."

Thus the ways of reform are many. If he is ashamed to return the stolen item, let him say: "The disgrace of this world is easier than the disgrace of the Hereafter." And many verses in the Qur'an speak of repentance:

﴿Then He turned to them that they might repent﴾ (part of verse 118, Surat al-Tawbah).

It is as if Allah's repentance is written first, and then the servant repents after that. And He, glorified is He, says:

﴿And indeed I am Forgiving toward one who repents﴾ (part of verse 82, Surat Taha).

Repentance, as we know, has three stages: the Truth, when He legislated repentance, gave permission for it; after that the servant repents, so Allah turns to him, erases the sin from him, and forgiveness comes through Allah's acceptance of the repentance. Therefore the Truth says: "Indeed, Allah will turn to him in forgiveness. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful."

The attribute of forgiveness and the attribute of mercy, each in its unrestricted sense, belong to Allah alone. For the wrongdoer, it is repentance; for the one who was wronged, it is mercy. The phrase "indeed Allah is Forgiving, Merciful" makes clear to us that He, glory be to Him, has absolute power to forgive and to show mercy. So beware of saying: "So-and-so does not deserve forgiveness and mercy, because He, glory be to Him, is the Owner of the heavens and the earth." It is He who has given mankind what they deserve, by the truth which He has made binding upon Himself, and He has absolute power over the universe. Therefore He says after that:

﴿Do you not know that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth? He punishes whom He wills and forgives whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent.﴾ (5:40)

Almighty Allah uses modes of expression that rouse us from heedlessness. He did not say: "Allah has the dominion of the heavens and the earth," for had He said that, it would have been a statement from the Speaker, who is Allah. Rather, He wants the statement to come from the addressee, as an acknowledgment from the servant. A statement is not put in the form of a question unless the one making the statement is confident that the answer to the question will be in his favour. An example of this is when a person comes to you and says: "You neglect me," and you reply: "I have done you good."

But if you want to draw the statement out of him, you say: "Did I not do you good?" Thus you ask him, and a question calls for an answer. So the one being asked, when he answers, must turn his mind over in every direction, and he finds no answer but to say: "Yes, you did good to me." Had this come from the speaker, it would have been a claim; but when it comes from the addressee, it is an acknowledgment. An example of this is the saying of the Truth:

﴿Did We not expand for you your breast?﴾ (94:1) (Surah al-Sharh).

It is a statement from the Speaker and an acknowledgment from the recipient. Someone may say: "Why did the Truth not say: 'We expanded for you your breast'?" That would have been possible, but the Truth did not say it, so that the question would not contain a suggestion of an affirmative answer; rather, it came in the negative form.

In His saying, the Truth:

﴿Do you not know that Allah—to Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; He punishes whom He wills and forgives whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent.﴾ (Surah al-Ma'idah)

We find that the wording of the verse is not a claim from the Truth, but a question to creation so that they may turn over the answer in their minds. On this basis, they find no answer but to say: "To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth." This is a method of establishing the proof and the acknowledgment from the servants, not an announcement from the Truth: "Do you not know that Allah has the dominion of the heavens and the earth?"

Someone may say: "There are parts of the earth that are owned by mankind." We say: It is true that there are parts of the earth that are owned by humans, but there is a difference between a person owning something he cannot keep hold of, such as owning a house or land—this is *mulk* with a kasra on the *mim*, meaning ownership by an owner (*malik*)—and *Malik* with a damma on the *mim*, meaning sovereignty, which belongs to Allah. In this world, every person has some form of ownership, but sovereignty over the land belongs to the ruler who holds the decision over the properties of his people; this is in the world of causes. As for the Hereafter, all causes are cut off:

﴿To whom belongs the dominion today? To Allah, the One, the Subduer.﴾ (40:16)

So no one has any dominion on the Day of Resurrection.

"Do you not know that Allah has the dominion of the heavens and the earth; He punishes whom He wills and forgives whom He wills." The one who reads the Qur'an attentively finds in it expressions that combine two matters, one of which comes first and the other later; at other times the order is reversed. But this statement is the only one in the Qur'an that comes in this pattern. Everything else in the Qur'an places forgiveness before punishment, because the Truth, glory be to Him, said in the Hadith Qudsi: "Indeed My mercy precedes My wrath."(1)

So why does punishment come before forgiveness in this verse: "He punishes whom He wills and forgives whom He wills"? Is the reason variety of expression? No, because the majority of verses mention forgiveness first and then the threat of punishment for whom He wills, glory be to Him. Let us look at the context: the discussion began with the male thief and the female thief, and after that with the one who repents. Theft thus calls for punishment, and repentance calls for forgiveness. So the ordering here is logical.

We note that this statement came after the verse on theft and after the verse informing that to Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. Therefore a concluding phrase was needed that serves both together, to affirm the dominion of power. When the Truth wills to show mercy to one person, the one who is shown mercy cannot say: "I do not want mercy." When He punishes one person, the one punished will not say: "There is no need for punishment." The dominion of power confirms that no one has the capacity to repel punishment or mercy. So the verse has come to serve several purposes: if we consider it in the scale of events, all power belongs to the Truth; and if we consider it in the scale of time, then how is the matter?

We know that punishment for theft is of two kinds: punishment by implementing the prescribed penalty (*hadd*) in this world, and in the Hereafter, forgiveness. Thus the statement is logical and consistent.

I always say: beware of being deceived into thinking that the disbeliever disbelieves, and the disobedient disobeys, without receiving his punishment. For whoever is accustomed to refusing the way of Allah, disbelieving or disobeying, must face a consequence. He has rebelled against the method, but he does not dare to rebel against Allah.

A person may rebel against the method, so he does not believe or does not establish the prayer; but no one has the power to rebel against Allah, because no one can stand in confrontation with death, which is part of the power of Allah. Glory be to Him and exalted, He judges as He wills, and He has willed to give man choice in some matters and to compel him in others. O you who have become accustomed to rebelling against the way of Allah, you must try to rebel against the Owner of the way, who is Allah. You will not be able to, neither in your form, nor your colour, nor your health, nor the appointed time of your death. Let every rebel open his ears and know that he will not be able to rebel against the Owner of the way, who is Allah. Thus the saying of Allah is true: "And Allah is over all things competent."

(1) Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tawhid and Bad' al-Khalq, narrated by Muslim in Tawbah, narrated by al-Tirmidhi in Da'awat, and Ibn Majah in the Muqaddimah.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 5, verse 41:

And after that, the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿O Messenger, let not those grieve you who race to disbelief from among those who say with their mouths, "We believe," but their hearts have not believed; and from among those who are Jews, listeners to falsehood, listeners for another people who have not come to you. They distort words from their places, saying, "If you are given this, take it; but if you are not given it, beware." And whoever Allah wants to test, you cannot avail him anything from Allah. Those are the ones whose hearts Allah did not want to purify. For them in this world is disgrace, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment.﴾ (5:41)

In the call we use the particle of address, which is "yā" (O), and we place it before the one being called (al-munādā), meaning that you are seeking his attention. So do we seek his attention merely for attention, or for something else? An example of this is the saying of the Truth:

﴿Say: Come, I will recite to you what your Lord has forbidden you﴾ (6:151).

So the call here is for reciting the obligations to them. When the Truth, glory be to Him, calls, the most noble of those He called are His messengers. We find that He called all the messengers by their personal designations (al-mushakhkhisāt al-ʿilmiyya), "O Adam." The personal designation is the proper name, which gives no description, only identifying the essence without its attributes.

Likewise, the Truth called Abraham, peace be upon him: ﴿O Abraham, you have fulfilled the vision﴾ (37:104-105).

Likewise, the Truth called Noah: ﴿O Noah, descend in peace﴾ (11:48).

Likewise, the Truth called Moses, peace be upon him: ﴿O Moses, indeed I am Allah﴾ (28:30).

Likewise, the Truth called Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him: ﴿O Jesus son of Mary, did you say to the people...﴾ (5:116).

All the messengers were called by the Truth with the personal designation, which gives only identification. But the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the seal of the messengers, was never called by his name; rather Allah called him by a description beyond the identifiers of the essence, saying: "O Messenger" (5:41, 5:67), and He says: "O Prophet" (33:1).

Truly, all are messengers, but He, glory be to Him, wants to inform us that Muhammad (ﷺ) is the messenger who came abrogating all and confirming all. He is the one who deserves to be called with a description beyond the identifiers of the essence, "O Messenger." He is the messenger upon whom the Hour will be established, and therefore we find the Truth's address to His messenger is always "O Messenger" or "O Prophet." This is a kind of honour.

The Truth says here: "O Messenger, let not those grieve you who race to disbelief." That is: do not grieve, O Messenger of Allah, over those who race to disbelief. When the Truth addresses His messenger about not grieving, we must know what grief is caused by. He, glory be to Him, makes clear to His messenger: beware of grieving, for I am with you; your opponents' evil will not reach you, and it is not possible that I choose you as a messenger and then forsake you; they will not gain anything from you.

The grief of the Prophet (ﷺ) may also be a grief of another kind, called elevated grief (al-ḥuzn al-mutasāmī), about which the Truth said: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over their footprints if they do not believe in this message﴾ (18:6).

Because if the Truth had willed to make them believers, He would not have given them the capacity for disbelief.

﴿If We willed, We could send down upon them a sign from the heaven, and their necks would remain humbly subjected to it﴾ (26:4).

Does Allah want necks? Rather He wants hearts, because the dominion of power can do what it wills. The proof: the heavens, the earth, the mountains and all creatures came to the Creator in obedience. The universe cannot refuse its Creator. Power produces compulsion, control, might and dominance throughout the whole cosmos. But Allah loved that His servant should come to faith willingly, He being the Lord, because the first faith is the faith of compulsion and power, while the second faith is the faith of love.

We have previously given an example, and let us clarify it: suppose you have two servants. You tie one of them to a chain, because if you leave him a little he will flee; when you want him you pull the chain and he comes. He comes because your power controls him and compels him. As for the other servant, you leave him free, and he comes to you at once upon the call. Which of them do you love more? There is no doubt you love the one who comes out of love, not out of compulsion. All kinds of creatures in the universe are subjected by power, but the Truth willed to make man free, therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to bear it and feared it, and man bore it﴾ (33:72).

So all kinds refused to bear the Trust out of fear and apprehension that they might not be able to carry it. The Truth says to His messenger: "Let not grieve you." As for grief caused by fear for the methodology (al-manhaj) from them, then the Truth supports it and will not let them have it. But if the fear is for them, then no, because He, glory be to Him, created man free, not compelled to carry out the teachings of the methodology, and He, glory be to Him, loves to be known by those who come to Him in love and honour.

And the Truth says to His messenger Muhammad (ﷺ): "Let not grieve you those who race to disbelief."

This is the lordly (rubūbiyya) expression. We know that racing is toward a thing, not within it, as the Truth said: ﴿And race to forgiveness﴾ (3:133). But here He says: "race in disbelief." Had the Truth said "race to disbelief," it would have meant that they had faith established and afterward went to disbelief. No: the Truth wants to clarify for us that they race within the circle of disbelief, and He informs us that they are at the beginning in disbelief, and they race toward a more intense disbelief. We know that "in" (fī) in the Qur'an is something for which volumes could be written; we said before that Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Travel in the earth﴾, and did not say "upon the earth."

And the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And do not give the foolish your property⁠﴾ (4:5). They are not the property of the addressees, but originally the property of the foolish. Yet He, glory be to Him, informs us that the foolish cannot be trusted with property. Therefore the Truth brings the guardian and custodian of property and commands him to regard the property as his own until he preserves it, and commands him not to hoard the property so that the foolish one eats from it, because if the foolish one consumes it and is given zakat, it may be depleted and exhausted. Therefore the Truth said: ﴿And do not give the foolish your property which Allah has made for you a means of support⁠﴾ (4:5).

Then, after that, the Truth says: ﴿and provide for them from it⁠﴾ (4:5).

Some exegetes say, regarding this verse: "I will surely crucify you upon the trunks of palm trees." We say: those who said that did not explain this verse, and they should have said in explaining it: "I will surely crucify you upon the trunks of palm trees with a strong crucifixion, which causes the crucified to enter into that in which he is crucified." An example: if we bring a match and tie it to a finger with a thin thread and tighten the tie, the matchstick sinks into the finger until it becomes as though it were inside the finger. When the Truth says: "And I will surely crucify you in the trunks of palm trees," this must be understood only as crucifixion upon palm trunks with a strong crucifixion, which causes the crucified to enter into that in which he is crucified. That is the reason for the presence of "in" (fī) and the absence of "upon" (ʿalā).

The Truth says here: "Let not grieve you those who race to disbelief." So racing is either with "to" (ilā) or with "in" (fī). If it is with "to," it is a movement to a thing which was not there at the beginning of the race; if it is with "in," it is a movement into the depth of the thing that they were in before the racing began.

"Let not grieve you those who race to disbelief from among those who say with their mouths, 'We believe,' but their hearts have not believed." Faith has its seat in the heart, and Islam has its seat in the limbs, which is why He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿The Bedouins say, "We have believed." Say, "You have not believed; but say, 'We have submitted'"﴾ (49:14).

They race to the first row in prayer, and this is Islam; but faith's seat is the heart. So those who said with their mouths "We believe" should know that the place of faith is not the mouths but the hearts. They said it with their mouths and it did not pass through their hearts. As long as they have said with their mouths "We believe" and it has not passed through their hearts, these are the hypocrites (al-munāfiqūn). This means that every day things will appear from them which will lead them into disbelief, because from the beginning they concealed disbelief, and afterward they race within the field of disbelief.

"From among those who say with their mouths, 'We believe,' but their hearts have not believed, and from among those who are Jews" — they are therefore two categories racing in disbelief: the hypocrites who said with their mouths "We believe," and those who are Jews, whom the Truth describes by saying: "listeners to falsehood" (sammā'ūna lil-kadhib). When you hear the root "s-m-ʿ" (sīn, mīm, ʿayn), it means the ear has received a sound from a speaker. That speaker either speaks true speech, which the believing ear takes in attentively, and then listening extends to acceptance, so the believer says: "I listened to so-and-so," not meaning merely that he heard from him, but that he heard and accepted what he said.

We know that many scrupulous people hear falsehood, but the decisive matter is accepting or rejecting falsehood, and it is not important that a person merely be a hearer; rather it is that he believe what he hears. In daily life we see a man who wants to repair some furniture in his house, so he brings the necessary tools for that, and it is said of this man: "najara fa-huwa nājir" (he did carpentry, so he is a carpenter-by-occupation/doer of carpentry), and he is not called najjār (carpenter by profession), because the najjār is the one whose craft is carpentry.

So the phrase "listener to falsehood" (sāmiʿ lil-kadhib) does not convey the meaning, but "listeners" (sammāʿūn) conveys the meaning, meaning that their trade is eavesdropping. When the Truth says: "listeners to falsehood, listeners for another people who have not come to you," they have become accustomed to turning falsehood over, and what is the disposition of one who accepts falsehood? It must be a disposition sick by nature.

What is the meaning of falsehood here, and who are the listeners? Either they are the rabbis and monks who told their followers words without basis in reality, in order to preserve their positions; or they are listeners to falsehood not for their own benefit, but for the benefit of another people, as if they were doing espionage. Espionage, as we know, is done by the eye or the ear, and these means have advanced in our time until espionage is by sound and image. It is as if the Truth wants to inform us that they are listeners to falsehood, that is, they listen on behalf of another people. The other people for whom they listen are those whom pride and arrogance afflicted, who disdained to attend the gathering of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), while at the same time they could not bear waiting and wanted to know what the Messenger of Allah was saying; so they sent spies to the gathering of the Prophet (ﷺ) to report to them.

Those listeners to falsehood are listening on behalf of another people who did not come to the gathering of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) out of arrogance. These arrogant ones are the great Jews, who do not go to the Messenger of Allah's gathering so that their standing before their followers will not weaken. When the words are conveyed to them, they try to shape them toward the aim they want. That is why the Truth says of them: "They distort words from their places." That is, they distort words after they have settled in their places, and they extract them from there, displacing them and removing them from their places after Allah placed them there, by altering the rulings of Allah. The Truth said of them earlier as well: ﴿They distort words from their places⁠﴾ (5:13).

That is, they distorted the words before they became settled. "Listeners to falsehood, listeners for another people who have not come to you, they distort words from their places, saying: 'If you are given this, take it; but if you are not given it, beware.'" These are the ones who say to their followers, the spies listening to the gathering of the Messenger of Allah: "If you are given this, take it, and if you are not given it, beware." It is as though they approached the Prophet with this: if they take from the Messenger of Allah a meaning they can distort, they do so; and if they find nothing to distort, they must beware.

From studying the history of man-made laws we know the meaning of temporal authority (al-sulṭa al-zamaniyya). Laws which people agreed upon to govern the system of life were slow to become a reality compared with the system of priests. The priests claimed a connection with heaven, and therefore rule belonged to them; that is, legislation in origin was the rule of heaven. What led people to set up laws of their own was that they tried the priests and found them judging in a matter

Then the Almighty says:

﴿Listeners to falsehood, devourers of what is unlawful. So if they come to you, either judge between them or turn away from them. If you turn away from them, they cannot harm you at all. And if you judge, judge between them with justice. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly.(42)﴾

In the language there are single words. For example, "sajanjal," and when you open the dictionary you find its meaning is "crystal." Likewise "al-Safa" and "al-Marwa." When you look up the word "marwa" in the dictionary, you know that the meaning of the term is distant from predication (nisba). So the first task of language is to know the meanings of words apart from their predication. The task of the dictionary is to explain to you the meaning of a term apart from its predication, without affirmation or negation. For example, "al-jaww" (the atmosphere) means what surrounds you of air or other things, but the dictionary does not explain whether the atmosphere is gloomy, clear, or cold.

If we advance to another stage and take the word to make a predication with it, as when we say, "The atmosphere is clear," here we move from understanding the meaning of the word "jaww" to our attributing clearness to it. Useful speech comes through predications, and predications come only after knowing the meanings of the words. Predication means that you attribute a judgment to a thing, either affirmatively or negatively. For example, when we say, "Muhammad is diligent (mujtahid)," here we have attributed diligence to Muhammad, after we have known the meaning of the word "Muhammad" by itself and the meaning of "mujtahid" by itself.

So useful speech comes through predications, and benefit may come by joining one word to what precedes it. When someone asks you, "Who is with you?" and you say, "Muhammad," this answer is useful, because it was joined to another word and the meaning became: "Muhammad is with me."

Thus there are predications, and predication is that you attribute a judgment to a thing, either affirmatively or negatively.

Predication is divided into two kinds: an actual (waqi'a) predication and a non-actual (ghayr waqi'a) predication. If the predication is actual, do you believe it? And can you establish a proof for it? If the actual predication is established by proof, it is knowledge ('ilm). If it is an actual predication and you believe it but cannot demonstrate it, this is imitation (taqlid), like the child who imitates his father and says, "Allah is One," and the child in this case cannot establish a proof for this predication.

Knowledge is the highest rank of predications, because it is a believed predication that is actual and has proof for it. But if it is a believed predication that is not actual, this is ignorance (jahl), because the ignorant person is one who knows a thing in other than its correct form. As for the illiterate (ummi), he is one who knows nothing, and we find it difficult to explain things to the ignorant. An example of this is one who says, "The earth is flat," and defends it. He states a predication he believes, but it is not the reality, because the earth is spherical.

Ignorance, then, is that you know a predication you believe while it is not actual, and only the ignorant person troubles the world, not the illiterate, because the illiterate has an empty mind; it suffices to tell him the truth and he accepts it. But the ignorant person needs us to remove from his thinking the wrong idea and put in its place the correct idea.

As for a predication that is not actual, negating it is equivalent to affirming it. This is doubt (shakk). If there is a predication that is more probable, this is opinion (zann), and the less probable predication is illusion (wahm). So there are a number of predications: knowledge, imitation, ignorance, doubt, opinion, and illusion. Accordingly, falsehood is a predication that is not actual. If you believe it, then you are among the ignorant.

Falsehood is opposed by truthfulness (sidq). When the Truth says, "Listeners to falsehood," the predication here does not correspond to reality. Those who deceive (al-mulabbisun) seize upon some predications that occur in some style of the Qur'an and say: "In the Qur'an there is speech which, if we examined it, we would find imprecise." An example of this is: ﴿When the hypocrites come to you, they say, "We bear witness that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah." And Allah knows that you are His Messenger﴾ (63:1).

The speech of the hypocrites here agrees with the speech of Allah. But why does the Truth say afterward: ﴿And Allah bears witness that the hypocrites are indeed liars﴾ (63:1)?

The predication is one, but Allah calls the hypocrites liars, even though we notice Allah's words quoting them: "We bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah" (63:1).

That is, Allah denies their testimony, because Muhammad is in fact the Messenger of Allah, but they are liars because they do not believe it. Testimony is when the tongue agrees with what is in the heart.

So His statement, "Listeners to falsehood, devourers of what is unlawful," means that their practice is listening to falsehood and devouring what is unlawful, as though they are exhausted if they eat what is lawful. The word "akkal" is a form of intensification, and it may refer either to the act itself or to the repetition of kinds of the act. One says, "So-and-so is akkal," and "akul," which means a person who eats with greed or eats a great deal. Intensification, then, may be either in the act or in the repetition of the act.

"Devourers of what is unlawful" (akkalun li-l-suht). The root "s-h-t" means "to uproot and erase," but it adds that it uproots it in such a way that no trace of it remains, and the uprooting extends to its container. For example, when a stain of oil or food appears on a garment, we can remove the stain, and we can go to the extreme of uprooting it until it is cut out of the garment. "Suht" is an uprooting carried to excess, to the point of slightly harming the origin, that is, it uproots what came along with some of the origin as well. Therefore the commentators came to this meaning in explaining riba (usury), because Allah describes it by saying: ﴿Allah destroys usury﴾ (2:276).

In our understanding, riba is an increase, but the Truth has made clear to us that it is not an increase, because it enters, uproots, consumes, and scrapes away the principal of wealth. The outward appearance of riba is increase, but its inward reality is destruction and uprooting.

As for zakat, its outward appearance is decrease, but it is growth. Thus we see the difference between the measures of creatures and the measures of the Truth. A clear example: the soul always turns to the provision that comes as a gain, and does not turn to the provision that comes as a loss. A man whose salary is five hundred pounds and another whose salary is one hundred pounds: the one with five hundred has doors opened for him that require a thousand pounds, while the one who takes one hundred pounds has the Truth close doors to him, so that his whole salary is not taken from him, but ten pounds remain for him.

So there is a provision of gain that increases income, and a provision of loss, in which the Truth removes from you the expenditures in calamities and destructions, and blesses for you what He has given you.

Unlawful gain (suht) is everything you take from other than a lawful way, such as bribery, usury, theft, embezzlement, or seizure by force, and every kind of gambling and betting. All of this is called suht.

"Listeners to falsehood, devourers of what is unlawful." This statement is evidence that their ears have become accustomed to hearing falsehood and welcome it. When we say in prayer, "Allah hears the one who praises Him" (sami'a Allahu liman hamidah), we are asking Allah to accept the praise. And they are "listeners to falsehood," that is, they accept falsehood. Hearing is an organ, and eating is the building up of what the organ is made of, because it sustains it, just as one eats in order to grow, and if one is mature, it preserves for him energy and capacity.

Growth, then, means that what enters his body is more than what leaves it. After a period, what enters his body equals what leaves it. Then in old age we find that what leaves is more than what enters. As long as they are listeners to falsehood and devourers of what is unlawful, they are in constant ruin, because eating unlawful gain is one of the grounds for the hearing that accepts falsehood, since they have built the particles of their bodies from what is forbidden. How, then, would their ears reject falsehood? Rather, their ears summon falsehood, their tongues practice it, their eyes seek what is forbidden, and their hands seek theft. These are the parts that their owners built from the unlawful.

The Truth did not say of them "sami'un" (hearers), but "sammA'un" (listeners, an intensive form), meaning they made eavesdropping their trade, and they are the spies. Otherwise, if the matter were otherwise, everyone who heard a lie would be counted among these. The phrase is intended to refer to one who has made listening his profession, and no one makes listening his profession unless he is a spy for others. A spy for others sneaks on the trust of gatherings, and every gathering has a trust. If a person attends a gathering, he has no right to transmit what was said in that gathering to others, unless that is his profession and his assigned task.

"Listeners to falsehood, devourers of what is unlawful." Here there are two questions: Is listening to falsehood caused by devouring unlawful gain, or is devouring unlawful gain caused by listening to falsehood?

When the Truth, glory be to Him, created man from the clay of the earth and fashioned him in the form of Adam, He breathed into him from His spirit. And when He fashioned him from the clay of the earth, He made all the components of the movement of his life from the nature of the clay of the earth. So when a person takes something lawful, the particles in his self are balanced in the form in which Allah created them. But if he interferes with them by taking the unlawful, He causes a structural imbalance in the particles, and this structural imbalance is what makes the one who eats the unlawful a listener to falsehood. Had there not been that structural imbalance that he produced himself, he would never have listened to falsehood.

Or it may be that when he devours unlawful gain he becomes a listener to falsehood, or when he hears falsehood he becomes a devourer of unlawful gain. Let us note that the Truth did not say "the eater of unlawful gain" nor "a listener to falsehood," but said: "Listeners to falsehood, devourers of what is unlawful." That is, they have become accustomed to listening to falsehood and accustomed to devouring unlawful gain. So each of them took the unlawful from the very beginning. When he became at once a devourer and a listener to falsehood, the particles of his constitution became unbalanced, and there is no longer light in his depths to reject falsehood. Rather, he welcomes it, and falsehood tempts him again to devour unlawful gain, and the matter revolves between listening to falsehood and devouring unlawful gain.

The question of falsehood is the question of the struggle of falsehood against truth. As long as falsehood does not conform to a cosmic restraint or a methodological, obligatory reality, this produces a disturbance in the cosmos. When the Almighty wished to strike a parable for us about this, He brought the parable in a tangible matter so that we could all see it: ﴿He sends down water from the sky, and the valleys flow according to their capacity﴾ (13:17).

That is, every valley carries according to its capacity. Then the Truth says: ﴿So the torrent carries a swelling foam﴾ (13:17).

Before the torrent descends from the mountains into the valleys, it takes all the things it meets on the mountain, such as traces of the winds and leaves of plants, and brings them down into the valley. These are the things that produce foam (zabad), which we call in our colloquial language "al-raghawi" (froth).

﴿He sends down water from the sky, and the valleys flow according to their capacity, and the torrent carries a swelling foam﴾ (13:17).

"Rabiyan" means floating, high, and riding above the water. Why? Because, as long as it is foam, it contains bubbles of air that make its volume greater than its weight, and its density becomes less than that of water, so it floats on top of it. And what is the situation after that?

﴿So the torrent carries a swelling foam, and from what they heat in the fire, seeking an ornament or a commodity, comes foam like it﴾ (13:17).

Remarkably, He made the two parallels in water and their opposite in fire. Water produces foam and scum that float on the surface, and likewise fire, when we put metals into it. Whoever has seen the blacksmith blow into his bellows on a piece of iron sees the dross and the foreign materials mixed with the iron, which separate from the iron during smelting so that it becomes pure. Thus there is foam in iron that fire expels when it is smelted, and foam that floats on water.

﴿And from what they heat in the fire, seeking an ornament or a commodity, comes foam like it. Thus Allah strikes the parable of truth and falsehood﴾ (13:17).

For this reason we see falsehood, at a time, rising to float on the surface, and the dross rising to float on the pure iron. But does falsehood remain so? The Truth reassures us that He protects the truth, saying: ﴿As for the foam, it passes away as scum, but what benefits people remains on the earth﴾ (13:17).

When we see falsehood rising to the surface, we are surprised after a time that the foam disappears and the water becomes clear. Likewise the foam that floats on iron is shaken off by the iron, so that it remains pure. So when we see falsehood rising once, let us know that this height has no permanence, because what benefits people remains on the earth.

Why does the Truth not announce itself from the beginning? Allah wished this, so that falsehood would become one of the soldiers of truth. If falsehood did not afflict people and trouble them, would they turn toward the truth? No. Therefore it was necessary that falsehood come to them and trouble them, so that they would seek the truth. Thus we see falsehood as a soldier of the truth. We gave the example before and knew that the pain felt by the sick person is one of the soldiers of health, for without that pain the disease would spread without his feeling it, the

Then, after that, He (glory be to Him) draws our attention with His saying:

﴿And how do they make you judge while they have the Torah, in which is the judgment of Allah? Then they turn away after that. And those are not the believers.﴾ (43)

He (glory be to Him) makes clear: How do they come seeking judgment from you while they have the Torah, and they do not believe in you, O Muhammad, as a messenger from Allah? How would one accept as judge someone he does not believe in? There must be some interest in that contrary to what is in the Torah. Had that interest not been contrary to it, they would have implemented the ruling they had. They came to you, O Messenger of Allah, hoping that you would grant some leniency, and they thought, God forbid, that you would provide them with the eating of illicit gain (suht) and the listening to falsehood.

"And how do they make you judge while they have the Torah" is a remarkable matter that must be noticed, because they have the Torah, in which is the judgment of Allah. So if they had asked you to judge in a matter that is not in the Torah, the matter would have been acceptable. But that they ask you to judge in a matter that has a ruling in the Torah, and then Allah informs you of it so that you expose it, and you say, "O Messenger of Allah, bring Ibn Suriya so he may come with the judgment of Allah," and Ibn Suriya acknowledges the existence of the ruling of stoning in the Torah. So they desired trickery, and Allah wished to establish for His Messenger (ﷺ) a clear sign in informing about these apostates from the commands of Allah. They know that the Messenger was unlettered, who neither read nor wrote, so who informed him of the ruling existing in the Torah?

Thus, the One who sent him informed him. And since they had wished to seek a lenient ruling, Truth (al-Haqq) willed this to be a cause of their disgrace: ﴿And how do they make you judge while they have the Torah, in which is the judgment of Allah? Then they turn away after that. And those are not the believers.﴾ (Surat al-Ma'idah).

This is evidence that when the Messenger judged in a way other than what they sought for ease, they turned away from the judgment; and had they been seeking judgment from the outset, they would have accepted the ruling of stoning as the Messenger of Allah stated it to them. But they are not believers, not even in their own Torah.

Almighty Allah says after that:

﴿Indeed, We revealed the Torah, in which there is guidance and light. By it the prophets who submitted (to Allah) judged for those who were Jews, and the rabbis and the scholars (judged) by what they were entrusted to preserve from the Book of Allah, and they were witnesses over it. So do not fear people but fear Me, and do not exchange My verses for a small price. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, those are the disbelievers.﴾ (5:44)

Al-huda (guidance) is the path or the road that leads to the goal. Upon the road come the periods of the night and the day. The road is dark at night, and obstacles may confront the traveller on it, or the traveller may not walk in the middle of the way (sawa' al-sabil), so he falls into a pit or strikes a stone.

Here the Truth clarifies: He has made the road for you and illuminated it for you so that you do not stumble upon anything or encounter obstacles. This is represented by the method that the whole procession of messengers brought. In former times the world was fragmented and scattered into communities; there were no means of transport, and each community lived in isolation and near independence. If diseases occurred in one region, they remained confined to that region, and a messenger would come to treat these diseases: one treats the matter of idol worship, another treats the matter of measure and weight, and a third treats the matters that organise married life among the Jews.

These diseases were many according to the number of directions. When the Truth, glorified is He, wished to make people perceive the secrets of His creation so that they might derive from them what shortens distances and prevents hardships, so that nations would meet, and when nations meet there is no separation between diseases; one disease occurs in the East and passes to the West, as if the diseases were also unified in the world.

Therefore there must come the comprehensive Messenger to treat all the diseases. Thus comes the Prophet (ﷺ), the all-encompassing and all-preventing. When the Truth says that He revealed the Torah, in which there is guidance and light, the Gospel too contains guidance and light, and all guidance and light in any book is only for the diseases present in the isolated environment. For example, Sayyidina Ibrahim existed, and at the same time Sayyidina Lut was present; and here is Sayyidina Musa existing, and likewise Sayyidina Shu'ayb. Thus the messengers were contemporaneous at times, because each one treated a specific disease, and so the messages used to come limited in time and limited in place.

As for Muhammad (ﷺ), Allah sent him to all people, all their races, and the Hour will be established upon his method. Therefore the earth no longer needs another messenger, and it became logical that he be the Seal of the Prophets.

"Indeed, We revealed the Torah, in which there is guidance and light, by which the prophets who submitted judged..." Why then does the Truth mention the submission of the prophets here? He mentioned the matter of the prophets' submission to honour Islam, because it is the essence of the method of every prophet.

We find poets delighting in this meaning: "Since I praised Muhammad with my statement*, rather my statement was praised through Muhammad." Another poet says: "They said: Abu al-Saqr is of Shayban. I said to them: No, by my life, rather Shayban is from him."

So the tribe, with respect to Abu al-Saqr, is the one that is attributed to him, not he who is attributed to it. And he adds: "How many a father has been elevated by a son of lofty honour, just as Adnan was elevated by the Messenger of Allah."

Thus when the Truth describes the prophets as having submitted, the Truth intends to honour Islam by stating that the prophets submitted their reins and their leadership to Allah, because they found it to be good for them. The submission of the prophets is Islam in its complete meaning, that is, compliance with the commands of Allah. Whenever a prophet among them thinks that some evil will come to him because of his call, or that someone will persecute him, or that someone will be pleased to harm him, he entrusts the matter to Allah, because the messenger among them only speaks the word of truth and does not care what happens after it.

"By it the prophets who submitted judge for those who were Jews" — they judge by the Torah among those who were Jews, that is, the Jews. Likewise the rabbis (rabbaniyyun) and the scholars (al-ahbar) judge by it. The rabbani is one attributed to the Lord (Rabb), meaning that all his conduct is attributed to Allah; and the ahbar (scholars) are the learned who carry vessels of knowledge. But whether they implement it or not is another matter. It is true that every scholar is a vessel of knowledge, but he may benefit by his knowledge, or he may not benefit, yet he transmits his knowledge to one who benefits from it. For this reason one of the scholars says: "Take my knowledge and do not rely on my practice; gather the fruit and leave the wood for the fire." So do not say that this scholar tells us such-and-such while we see him in his conduct doing the opposite of what he says, for you must take the fruit of knowledge and leave the wood to the fire. But the scholar must be the first to comply and apply what he says, so that he is not punished and does not fall under the saying of the Exalted: "O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do? It is most hateful in the sight of Allah that you say what you do not do."

"And the rabbis and the scholars, by what they were entrusted to preserve from the Book of Allah." We have known that the Torah contains light and guidance, and the prophets, rabbis and scholars judge by it, by the means that Allah asked them to preserve it, and by what their messenger asked of them to preserve this Torah. The Truth said "istuhfizu" (they were entrusted to preserve) and did not say "hafizu" (they preserved), to show us the difference between every book prior to the Qur'an and the Qur'an, because we know that every messenger came with a miracle indicating that he was truthful in conveying from Allah.

All the messengers before the Messenger of Allah had a miracle separate from the method. For example, Sayyidina Musa's miracle was the staff and the splitting of the sea, while his method was the Torah. Sayyidina 'Isa's miracle was healing the blind and the leper, and the method he brought was the Gospel. As for the Messenger of Allah, his miracle is identical with his method, and it is the Qur'an. The matter concerning each messenger was tied to his time and his community and needed a suitable miracle and a suitable method. But the messenger whom Allah sent to all people and as Seal of the Prophets must have his miracle be identical with his method, so that any Muslim can say until the Hour is established: Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and this is his miracle, and it is identical with his method.

The Qur'an will remain a manifest miracle until the Hour is established, because Allah willed it to be different from the rest of the methods and miracles. The previous miracles were like a match that ignites only once: whoever saw it at the moment of ignition, the matter was clear to him, but whoever did not see it would not believe that miracle unless someone he trusted informed him. Allah entrusted the rabbis and the scholars with the Torah, that is, He asked them to preserve it, and this was a commanded obligation (amr taklifi). A commanded obligation is subject both to being obeyed and to being disobeyed. Allah entrusted them with the Torah and the Gospel: "So they forgot a portion of what they had been reminded of" (5:14).

The matter of the method became forgotten and not much on their minds, for when a matter repeatedly comes to mind and settles far down in the depths of consciousness, it remains in the mind; but forgetting comes when the matter is far from the mind.

The Truth asked them to preserve the method, but except for the prophets they did not comply, and every commanded obligation falls within the sphere of choice. Therefore we find that the rabbis and scholars forgot, and what they did not forget they concealed. The first stage of failing to preserve was that they forgot; the second stage is concealing what they had not forgotten; and the third is that what they did not conceal they distorted, twisting their tongues with it. Would that they had been limited to these stages alone! But they brought things and said: "This is from Allah," and it was not from Allah: "So woe to those who write the Book with their own hands and then say, 'This is from Allah'" (2:79).

Thus their preservation was not accomplished. Therefore Allah did not entrust the Qur'an to be preserved through the commanded obligation of creatures, because He had tested mankind before, and because He willed the Qur'an to be a lasting miracle. Therefore Allah, glorified is He, did not leave the matter of its preservation to creation, but He undertook its preservation Himself: "Indeed, We have sent down the Reminder, and indeed We will be its guardians" (15:9).

As evidence for this text: some Muslims have been extravagant against themselves in abandoning the method of Islam and the method of the Qur'an, yet you find a marvel: the further they are from applying Islam's method, the more they guard the Qur'an in form, writing it in every style and every size. There is a golden size that women wear on their chests, and a size that is placed in the hand. After that, you find the disbelievers themselves inventing a method to write the Qur'an on a single page.

Thus Allah makes even non-Muslims serve the preservation of the Qur'an, and that is an inspiration from Allah. We see every day people who, by their conduct, distance themselves from the method, yet they allocate money for preserving the Qur'an, and we find the Qur'an realized by a thousand means of preservation. A man places a copy of the Mushaf in his car and a copy in his bedroom; and a woman may be unveiled with her chest exposed, yet she hangs a golden Mushaf. This proves to us that preserving the Qur'an is not a commanded obligation but the will of Allah.

Had it been a commanded obligation, forgetting the Qur'an would have been possible, because Muslims have distanced themselves in some of their affairs from it as a method; it would be fitting for them to be separated from it in preservation. But the matter has become the opposite despite the Muslims' distance from the method; the preservation of the Qur'an does not decline at all. Remarkably, many of those who are extravagant against themselves, if one of them hears that something touches the Mushaf, he raises the world and sets it down; the matter is not his concern but the concern of the Preserver, glorified is His majesty. If any slight distortion of the Qur'an occurs by the enemies of Islam, the community of Islam stands as one man. Some deceivers wanted to insert into the Qur'an what is not in it, and they came to a verse in Surat al-Fath, which is:

﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him are severe against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves﴾ (48:29).

And they said: "Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)," as though they desired to increase the honour of the Messenger of Allah. When the Muslims learned of that, an uproar arose, they burned those copies, and the Muslims prevented distortion by whatever door it might enter.

"So do not fear people but fear Me." Khashya (fear) is a supposed dread of one whom you think capable of harm, and none other than Allah is capable of benefit and harm. Therefore it is not proper for a person to fear anyone other than Him. Whether you think the ruler or one close to him is capable of harm, this is not correct; each person should fear the Truth, glorified is He, and He, majestic is He, has advised us that the fear should be of Him alone.

If someone alters the rulings of the method for the sake of the ruler, or the ruler's relatives, or the ruler's friends, that is the very essence of corruption, and afflictions and evils come from that. Indeed, the ruler may know nothing of it, and a relative of the ruler may intervene without the ruler's knowledge to ask the scholars to change some of the method, and only the weak among them submit to him. Sayyidina 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) perceived this matter and said: "Corruption may not come from the ruler, but from those around the ruler."

Here the fear is of other than Allah. Therefore 'Umar would gather his relatives and those who gathered around him and say to them: "I have resolved to issue such-and-such; by Him in whose hand is my soul, whoever of you opposes me in anything of this, I will make him an example for the Muslims."

This is the method of one who wants to serve, to rule, and to bear burdens; and we see the forms of corruption arising only from violating the wise principle: "So do not fear people but fear Me."

The Truth continues after that: "And do not exchange My verses for a small price." The price of Allah's verses, however much it is exaggerated in valuation, will never exceed its benefit in this world, because the world, as we said earlier, is not measured by its true lifespan, that is, until Allah causes mankind to perish, but the world of each living being is measured by his lifespan within it.

Suppose life lasted millions of years: what benefit would a person of limited lifespan gain from those millions of years? Thus the world of each person is the measure of his life; and a person's lifespan in the world has a limited, unknown end to anyone but Allah. For every term has a decree, and therefore you find one living the average lifespan, which is seventy years; lifespans differ from one person to another; one dies at sixty, another dies at forty, a third dies at a hundred, and a fifth dies as an infant at the breast.

Thus the world of an individual may be a moment, and since the matter of lifespan is governed by neither time nor cause, it is then, by the will of the Truth, unseen.
