And the Truth (Allah) says after that:

﴿And We prescribed for them therein: a life for a life, and an eye for an eye, and a nose for a nose, and an ear for an ear, and a tooth for a tooth, and for wounds is legal retribution (qisas). But whoever gives it as charity, it is an expiation for him. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed - it is those who are the wrongdoers.﴾ (5:45)

The Truth has prescribed upon the Jews in the Torah, which He described earlier as guidance and light, that He prescribed and obligated upon them that a life is for a life, and upon us that we take each matter together with what corresponds to it of the event. That is, a soul is killed for a soul. But when the Truth says "and an eye for an eye," does that mean the eye is to be destroyed? No, rather an eye is to be gouged out in return for an eye. Likewise "a nose for a nose," meaning a severed nose in return for another severed nose, and likewise His saying, the Truth: "and an ear for an ear," meaning injuring an ear so that it becomes deaf in return for injuring an ear so that it becomes deaf. Thus for each there is its counterpart: there is the soul killed for a soul, there is the eye gouged for an eye, and likewise the matter of the severed nose and the cut-off ear.

The expressions of language are broad, giving each description what suits it. A person, for example, may be hungry, but for what? If he is hungry for food, he is "ja'an" (hungry). If he desires a specific food and craves it, such as meat, he is not called "ja'an" but is said to be "qaram" (craving meat). If he longs for milk, he is called "ʿaymān." If he is in need of water, he is called "ʿatshān" (thirsty), and if he is hungry for sex, he is "shabaq" (sexually aroused).

This reveals to us that humanity needs many things, and every matter has a name, and everything has an expression. Another example: "fulān jalasa," meaning he sat, which is the general sense; but julūs is from reclining, whereas qaʿada is from standing, i.e., he was standing and then sat down. For this reason the Truth said: "standing and sitting" (qiyaman wa qu'udan).

Another example: one says "naẓara" (looked), "ramaqa" (glanced), and "lamaḥa" (glimpsed), and every word has its own position. Naẓar is with the whole of one's eyes; "ramaqa" means to look with a light glance; and "lamaḥa" means to steal a look at him. Likewise the saying of the Truth means: We prescribed for them therein that the soul is killed for a soul, the eye is gouged for an eye, the nose is severed for a nose, the ear is cut off for an ear, and the tooth is pulled out for a tooth. Then the Truth says about wounds: "and for wounds is qisas," because a wound may be in any place, and qisas is to be by its like and equal to the thing. It is derived from "qass al-athar," meaning to follow the track exactly as the earlier foot went, without deviation. Since qisas is something which requires equivalence, it is a difficult matter. True, the Truth said: "So whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in the same manner as he transgressed against you" (2:194).

But qisas is a difficult matter: a slap from the hand of a hungry, feeble person is different from a slap that comes from the hand of its owner in complete vigor and strength. So how can qisas be suitable to the strength of the one who committed the act?

Therefore a person should not enter into a maze, and he may give qisas as charity and not take it. We know the story of "The Merchant of Venice," that usurer and Jew who lent money in return for a pound of the borrower's flesh; the two wrote the contract and brought witnesses. The man could not repay the money on time, but the judge, may God enlighten his insight, said: "Take the pound of flesh from the man, but if you take off an ounce more or less, we will take it from you." The usurer said: "I do not want it."

The Truth has legislated for the crime, yet He did not close, glorified be He, the door of faithful aspirations, and said: "whoever gives it as charity, it is an expiation for him." The meaning of "tasaddaqa" is that he paid and gave something not due, nor obligatory upon him, that is, he donated it seeking the face of God. What wearies humans in their legislations is that they prolong litigation procedures: when a crime occurs, the investigation continues through the judiciary for more than a year, so the atrocity of the crime settles in the human soul. It is also necessary that the matter be left to the heir of qisas, because if you empower him, he would be satisfied with the first cure. When a person is given that ruling, he may come to renounce it, since when the matter is in his hand and he is able to exact qisas, it is likely that he will pardon.

The one who is given charity will remain all his life indebted, with his life or with one of his limbs, to the owner of qisas; instead of the incitements of vengeance, affection arises. When the Supreme Legislator legislates, He clarifies for us: do not judge that you are always the one wronged; rather imagine once that you are the wrongdoer. Would you not, in such a case, like the owner of qisas to show you charity? So if governments wish to end blood feuds, they have in the supreme legislation a clear ruling.

In Upper Egypt, when a person is killed, the one owing the blood-debt takes his shroud and goes to the family seeking vengeance; at the moment he enters upon them carrying his shroud in his hands, the souls are healed from seeking vengeance, and he lives, while the owner of the vengeance bestows upon him life. "Whoever gives it as charity, it is an expiation for him": the charity here is from the heir of qisas, and the verb "tasaddaqa" requires two parties: "mutasaddiq" (the giver) and "mutasaddaq ʿalayhi" (the recipient). Glorified is the Truth, who expiates for the giver of sins to the degree that he forgave his brother; here God makes creation tender toward one another, so the matter here is addressed from the side of the owner of qisas, to encourage him to give charity.

The Truth concludes the verse with His saying: "And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed - it is those who are the wrongdoers." We have already known previously the necessity of judging by what Allah has revealed.

Then the Truthful Lord says:

﴿And We sent, following in their footsteps, Jesus son of Mary, confirming what was before him of the Torah, and We gave him the Gospel, in which was guidance and light, confirming what was before it of the Torah, and a guidance and an admonition for the God-fearing.﴾

Wa-qaffaynā (we caused to follow): i.e., We made them follow, so Jesus came after Moses. When one man walks behind another, the front of the first is turned toward the back of the second. When the Truth says: "And We sent, following in their footsteps, Jesus son of Mary, confirming what was before him" — i.e., confirming Moses, who brought the Torah — "and We gave him the Gospel, in which was guidance and light," we understand that "guidance and light" suit the environment into which that guidance and that light were sent down.

There is what are called "relative statements" (al-maqūlāt al-idāfiyya). For example, a person in a village says to his son: "Light the lamp," and the boy lights the kerosene lamp. But if a person in a city says to his son: "Turn on the light," the son presses the switch so that the electric lamp shines. These relations may cause a word to carry two meanings. A clearer example: a person lives in a house and knows that the ceiling is high relative to him, but it is a floor relative to the occupants of the second story. It is height and lowness, and this is the relative meaning. Likewise, when we say: "So-and-so, son of so-and-so," this does not prevent that son from being a father in relation to his own son.

Thus "guidance and light" are relative meanings, and each "guidance and light" suits the environment in which it was sent down. The first material environment was in need of legislation, so the Torah came. After that, this material environment came to be in need of a spiritual energy, so the Gospel came with all the spiritualities. When Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him, was asked about the matter of inheritance, he said: "I was not sent as an inheritance-divider." He knows that he came with a spiritual charge containing ecstatic experiences (mawājīd) and admonitions.

Almighty God continues:

﴿And let the People of the Gospel judge by what God has revealed therein. And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed, those are the defiantly disobedient (al-fasiqun).﴾ (5:47)

The truth is that the Gospel was revealed to confirm that rulings are to be taken from the Torah; that is, the Gospel included, alongside its spirituality, the foundations of the rulings found in the Torah. For this reason God made clear: whoever does not judge by what God has revealed is a fasiq (one who has departed from obedience). If someone departs from obedience in a matter of divinity and lordship (uluhiyyah and rububiyyah), he is a kafir (disbeliever). And whoever departs from the rulings concerning judging among people is a zalim (wrongdoer). So the matter is all interrelated, and shirk is also a great wrong (zulm).

And after the Truth (Allah) spoke of the Torah and the Gospel, He came to what was sent down to the Final Prophet.

﴿And We have sent down to you the Book in truth, confirming what was before it of the Book and as a guardian over it. So judge between them by what Allah has revealed and do not follow their desires away from the truth that has come to you. For each We have made a law and a way. And if Allah had willed, He would have made you one nation, but [He did that] to test you in what He has given you. So race to [all that is] good. To Allah is your return, all of you, and He will inform you about that over which you used to differ.﴾ (5:48)

When we hear "We have sent down" (anzalna), we know that there is a legislation that came from above. And there are those who want to dress people in their own desires, saying: "Islam is a progressive religion," or saying: "Islam is a reactionary religion." Both try to clothe Islam in what is not in it. We say: do not say that, but say: Islam is "above" (fawqi), because it came from Allah. If progressiveness has merits, then it is progressive; if reactionism has merits, then it is reactionary; if the right has merits, then it is rightist; and if the left has merits, then Islam is leftist. For Islam has brought social justice (istitraq ijtima'i) and genuine scientific progress, because the concept of progress is that a person elevates himself in a manner that makes people equal.

Islam is not progressive only with respect to this worldly life, but also with respect to another, eternal life above this life. Those who debate these ideas do not properly understand their own ideas, whether they are progressive, reactionary, rightist, or leftist. We see that the contemporary systems that cause all this conflict in the world, East and West, are: capitalism, communism, socialism, existentialism, and others.

When we look, for example, at those who led the communist revolution of 1917, we find their claim that they are still at the beginning of the road to communism, but that they chose the socialist path.

They should have turned to what they called for, but here we are, seeing that whenever they advanced in time, they retreated from their first ideas, until they turned against themselves, and that is evidence that the method they adopted for themselves is not correct.

And has the capitalist system remained as it is? No, because events compelled capitalism to give workers rights, and thus it no longer kept capital's ferocity. Communism moved toward most of capitalism's methods, and capitalism moved toward some of socialism's methods; so they both wish to meet. But Islam established this meeting from the beginning: it respected capital, respected labor, and each person kept to his limits, ensuring the existence and continuity of the movement of life. For this reason we find capitalism saying: incentives must be provided for work. Communism also did not reach its goal, but instead trampled people's rights. Then what of those whom the hand of communism did not reach before it existed, among whom were those who exploited people?

Reason would require that communism believe in an afterlife in which those who exploited people before will be punished; so it is in their interest that an afterlife exist, and they should therefore have been religious. Likewise capitalism, which recognizes nothing but material profit, its societies filled with victims who lost their moral values. The words of the Truth, "We have sent down," indicate that there is a method that descended from above. When we take the data of the Qur'anic exposition and find Him, glorified be He, conveying His teachings to us: "Say: Come" (qul ta'alaw), meaning rise up to the level of the heavens and do not descend to the lowness of the earth.

Therefore the Truth said: "And We have sent down to you the Book in truth." We see that the verses of the Qur'an support one another and each serves the other. The sending down of the Book in truth requires the evidence of truth, that it truly descends from Allah, and that all laws of truth in the movement of life come in harmony, not in discord. There is a verse explaining the word "truth":

﴿And with the truth We sent it down, and with the truth it descended﴾ (17:105).

That is, it descended from Allah and is not a product of human manufacture. "And with the truth it descended" means it descended with the method from Allah that establishes the logic of truth in every soul and every place, and guarantees every right that sustains the movement of life.

Here the verse summarized, saying: "And We have sent down to you the Book in truth, confirming what was before it of the Book." That is, the Qur'an confirms the earlier heavenly books. What is the difference between the first word "the Book" that came in the verse's opening and the second word "the Book"?

We know that there is "al" for the genus and "al" for the specific referent, as one says: "I met a man and I honored the man," meaning the known man whom you met. So the first word "al-Kitab" has the "al" of specific reference (al-'ahd), meaning the known, familiar Book, which is the Qur'an; and the second word "al-Kitab" is intended in the generic sense (al-jins), meaning the books sent down upon the prophets before him. So the Qur'an is a guardian and overseer over them, because they have been subjected to distortion and falsification.

The word "truth" therefore means that the Book of Allah, the Final one among His revealed books, which is the Qur'an, descended with the truth that is established in all matters of the cosmos and the required movement of humanity, and it descended in such a way that no distortion or alteration has touched it.

So truth is in its content and in the certainty of its descent. The Qur'an descended after books that Allah had sent down, suited to the times in which they descended, because He, glorified be He, created creation for the task that they should bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that they should build up this universe, with the reasoning mind He gave them, energies that act, and matter in the cosmos that responds. If they seek the bare origin of life without any elevation or happiness, then in the elements of the earth there is what will give it to them; but if they want to elevate themselves, they must employ the mind that Allah bestowed to serve the energies Allah created in the matter Allah created, and then they will take the secrets of Allah from existence.

The secrets of Allah in existence are many and they work for us, even if we do not know the secret. We find the gravity that holds the celestial bodies works for us, even though we did not discover gravity until recently; and the electricity flowing through the cosmos, negative and positive, works for us, even though we do not know what secret it contains.

When the Truth, glorified be He, wills the birth of a secret in the cosmos, He equips creation with the causes for that secret to emerge. Know that every secret of the cosmos subjected to man has a birth like the birth of man himself. Either this birth coincides with the mind working on premises that lead to it, and then the birth comes together with premises that humans used to arrive at the result—just like the geometry exercise that the student solves after the teacher gives him some data, which he uses as premises to deduce what the teacher wants him to deduce from the thing to be proven. If it happens that the mind investigates the matter experimentally and empirically, the birth of the secret arrives together with the research. But if the birth of a secret in the cosmos comes without the human occupying himself with researching premises that lead to it, and that birth is willed, what then is the position?

Does Allah prevent the secret because we did not work? No, rather He, glorified be He, brings the secret into existence, as we always hear of the birth of something by accident at the hand of a researcher who was investigating something else, and we say: this secret came into existence by accident.

When you look at innovations and inventions and foundational matters that were discovered, you will find them to be of the second category. You find the thinker or scientist deeply immersed in a certain inquiry, then Allah gives him a secret of the cosmos he was not seeking, and the new discovery is called: it came by chance. When Allah made a birth for every secret, He gave His creation life from His vast bounty, gave it power from the overflow of His might, gave it knowledge from Himself ("and We taught him knowledge from Us"), and bestowed wisdom by which it brings good: "And whoever is given wisdom has indeed been given much good." He, glorified and exalted be He, wants His creation to interact with the cosmos to bring things out, and if He, glorified be He, wants us to be affected in this way, He must set down the method that preserves our energy and thought from dissipation.

What dissipates people's thoughts and energies is the conflict of desires: desire collides with desire, and an idea may collide with an idea, and people's desires differ. Therefore the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, wanted to guarantee for us the agreement of desires so that we act in all our movements from one desire, namely what the Supreme Creator has sent down, which the desires of men cannot alter. As for what desires do not differ about, He left it for us to investigate, because we will agree on it against our will. Therefore we always say: there are no differences in experimental, empirical, material ideas. We never found an "Russian electricity" and "American electricity," because the laboratory does not flatter and inert matter does not favor, and the laboratory result emerges clearly as one. We see the agreement of scientists, East and West, on the data of empirical matter, and each country tries to steal from the other the results it has reached in order to add them to its own civilization. In human desires the matter differs: each country tries to push the desire of the other beyond its borders, because desires never meet. The Truth established the movement of life so that it is shaped by "do this" and "do not do that" in matters where desires differ, to guarantee our unity and to prevent our energies from opposing one another, so that instead they support one another.

﴿And if the truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them would have been corrupted﴾ (23:71).

Thus Allah's method in His cosmos came only to regulate human movement in matters where desires differ. As for movement in matters where desires do not differ, He left it free and unrestricted, because humans agree on it against their will, since matter does not flatter and the laboratory does not favor.

For this reason we said: when Allah sent the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, as the Final Prophet, he gave [guidance] by "do" and "do not do." As for the material, laboratory matter, its command was placed in the Prophet's own person, peace and blessings be upon him. When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, arrived in Madinah, its people were pollinating the date palms, that is, fertilizing them so they would bear fruit. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, passed by a people who were pollinating and said: "If you did not do it, it would be fine." 

So they stopped pollinating the palms, and the palms produced shees, that is, poor-quality unripe dates, and the palms failed. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, passed by them and said: "What is wrong with your palms?" They said: "You said such and such." He, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "If that benefits them, let them do it, for I only conjectured a conjecture; do not hold me to conjecture, but when I tell you something from Allah, take it, for I have never lied about Allah, the Mighty and Majestic." In another narration, he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "I am only a human being. When I command you with something of your religion, take it; and when I command you with something of my opinion, then I am only a human being."

Then the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, to establish it as a cosmic, material, experimental, laboratory principle: "You are more knowledgeable about the affairs of your worldly life." (1)

That is, he, peace and blessings be upon him, left to the community the management of its experimental affairs, and that statement was not an abandonment of the reins in matters of the method. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, placed the criterion for what the heavens intervene in and what the heavens leave to humans. The ages of people, as we know, differ: we say a human has childhood, then has youthfulness and vigor, and then attains the completeness of manhood and maturity. Therefore the Truth gives rulings suited to each stage of society: first He gives the material needs of childhood, then at the age of vigor He gives intellectual matters, and when he reaches maturity He gives him the reins of movement in the cosmos in light of the method. Thus the message of Islam came at an appointed time with the maturity of the reins. Allah, glorified be He, entrusted the followers of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, to stand guard to protect human movement from the desires of men. Previously, the messengers came from Allah to deliver to the societies before Islam, and the heavens were what disciplined; but when the maturity of humanity was complete, we saw the Messenger delivering, and Allah entrusted him to discipline whoever departs from Allah's method in the movement of life, because he, peace and blessings be upon him, had become trustworthy in that.

And if you look at the cosmos in ancient times, you would find it a cosmos of isolation: each community in its place knew nothing of the other community, and each community had its own system, movement, livelihood, and ailments. Islam came for the gathering of all humanity.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 5, verse 49:

It might be said: Allah, glorified and exalted, has already said: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Book in truth, confirming what was before it of the Scripture and as a criterion over it﴾ (part of verse 48, Surat al-Ma'idah).

The answer is that the truth makes clear that the Qur'an has been sent down as a criterion (muhaymin), and the Messenger must carry out the task of implementation. Therefore His saying here comes as a communication to the Messenger and a clarification: "And judge between them by what Allah has revealed" — I have sent down to you the Book confirming what was before it of the earlier scriptures and as a criterion, so judge. If a people come to you with something contrary to what has been revealed in the Qur'an, judge between them by the Qur'an.

What the verse adds is His saying, the Truth: "And beware of them lest they tempt you." Caution (hadhar) is a person's precaution and guarding himself against one who wants to inflict harm upon him in a matter that has benefit. The one who desires harm may adorn for himself and for others the harm as if it were good, although what is within him is all evil.

So caution is the necessity of attentiveness toward one who wants evil for a person, lest harm enter upon him in the form of benefit. For example, an opponent comes and says to you: "I will do such-and-such for you and act on your behalf in such-and-such a way." Here you must say to him: "No."

Caution, then, requires a composite intelligence. This is why people knew caution from the crow. Thus the crow teaches its young in a folk tale, and the crow says to its son:

"Beware of the human, for when the human bends down to pick up something from the ground, he is picking up a piece of brick to throw at you." Here the young crow says to its father: "And what should I do if this human hides the piece of brick in his pocket?" It is a story that suggests that the crow is cautious by its nature.

We see something similar in the appearances of things, such as the usurer who makes it attractive to people to place their money with him and gives them a profit of twenty percent. This is a picture of something that appears beneficial but is in fact harmful, because it increases money in appearance, yet the saying of Allah applies to it: ﴿Allah destroys interest﴾.

This is a harmful matter that the opponent adorns as if it were beneficial, and the Truth asks the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to be cautious. So what is required of the followers? It is caution itself, because the best of mankind was directed by Allah to caution: "And beware of them lest they tempt you." The picture in which they approached was one that adorned deception. They said: "We have come to you so that you may judge for us; if you judge in our favour, we will follow you." This matter appeared in the form of something beneficial, and the Word of Truth came to settle the question: "And beware of them lest they tempt you away from some of what Allah has revealed to you." Here Allah warns His Messenger against being seduced away from some of what He has revealed to him, glorified is He.

The Truth continues: "But if they turn away, then know that Allah only intends to afflict them for some of their sins. And indeed, many of the people are defiantly disobedient." If they turn away, know that Allah protects you from slipping into the suspicion of falsehood. They have chosen to plunge into disbelief and to distance themselves from the method of Allah, and He will afflict them with some of His punishment in return for their sins. He, glorified is He, does not afflict them unjustly; rather He afflicts them for some of the sins they committed, and He knows them best, for He is the most knowing of all people.

The Truth concludes the verse with His saying: "And indeed, many of the people are defiantly disobedient," meaning they have departed from obedience to their own scriptures and their messengers, because obedience to the scriptures before the Qur'an enjoins the necessity of belief in the Messenger, the Prophet, the Unlettered (ﷺ). And the Truth says: ﴿Those who follow the Messenger, the Prophet, the Unlettered, whom they find written in what they have of the Torah and the Gospel, who enjoins upon them what is right and forbids them what is wrong and makes lawful for them the good things and prohibits for them the evil and relieves them of their burden and the shackles that were upon them. So those who believe in him, honour him, support him, and follow the light which was sent down with him — it is those who will be the successful﴾ (Surat al-A'raf, 157).

So the path of success was written in the Torah and the Gospel, and the command to follow Muhammad (ﷺ), the Unlettered Prophet, was present in the scriptures before the Qur'an, and the good news of Muhammad as a messenger from Allah was there, who enjoins all good and forbids all evil, and makes lawful for people all the things that human nature finds good to receive, and forbids them to distort and alter the method brought by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and forbids them to submit to obstinacy. Muhammad (ﷺ) came to remove from them the burden of distorting the method. Whoever follows the light of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) feels deliverance and success, and whoever does not follow this light is one who departs from obedience to the Book of heaven, and an attempt to deny the message of the Messenger of Allah is doomed to failure. Those who know the Torah and the Gospel recognise the description of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in these books. ﴿Those to whom We have given the Book recognise him as they recognise their own sons; but indeed, a party of them conceal the truth while they know﴾ (Surat al-Baqarah, 146).

We all know what 'Abd Allah ibn Salam did when he came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to declare his Islam. 'Abd Allah ibn Salam said: "I am more knowing of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) than I am of my son."

'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "And how is that, O Ibn Salam?"

'Abd Allah ibn Salam said: "Because I testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah truly and with certainty, and I do not testify to that about my son, because I do not know what the wombs of women have brought forth." 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "May Allah grant you success, O Ibn Salam."

However, some scholars and rabbis of the Children of Israel concealed the good news of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), for they hoped for leadership and coveted the gifts that people offered them. So they targeted the description of Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and concealed it. Since they did that, let us know that Allah afflicts them for some of their sins.

We notice that when the Truth put into the mouth of His Messenger an address to the Jews, He did not place upon his tongue a comprehensive accusation against the Jews, but only against some of them, even if this group is large. We should know that this is the method of preserving the possibility (of faith), for some of them manage the matter of belief in their hearts. It is true that many of them are defiantly disobedient, but a few of them are not like that.

Here is Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) relating what happened: A Jewish man committed adultery with a woman, and some of them said to others: "Go with us to this Prophet, for he is a prophet sent with leniency. If he gives us a ruling other than stoning, we will accept it and present it as a proof before Allah, saying: 'It is the ruling of a prophet from Your prophets.'" They came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who was sitting in the mosque with his Companions, and said: "O Abu al-Qasim, what do you say about a man and a woman who committed adultery?" He did not speak to them until he went to their study house.

There the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked a young man who refused to speak anything other than the truth that his people were speaking. The young man said: "We find stoning in the Torah." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ruled for stoning.

From al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said: A Jew blackened and flogged was passing by the Prophet (ﷺ), so he called them and said: "Is this how you find the punishment of the adulterer in your Book?" They said: "Yes." He called a man of their scholars and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I adjure you by Allah who sent down the Torah to Moses: is this how you find the prescribed punishment for the adulterer in your Book?" He said: "No, and had you not adjured me by this I would not have told you. We find it is stoning, but it became widespread among our nobles, so when we seized a noble we left him, and when we seized a weakling we enforced the punishment on him. So we said: 'Come, let us agree on something that we apply to the noble and the lowly alike,' and we agreed on blackening and flogging in place of stoning." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, I am the first to revive Your command when they have let it die." He then ordered him to be stoned, and Allah revealed: "O Messenger, let not those who race to disbelief grieve you..." up to His saying: "And if you are given this, then take it; and if you are not given it, then beware." (They say: "Go to Muhammad; if he orders you to blacken and flog, accept it, and if he gives you a ruling of stoning, beware.") (1).

So many of them are defiantly disobedient, and a few of them are not, because they want the idea of believing in the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Had the accusation been comprehensive, that all of them are defiantly disobedient, those who think about believing in Muhammad (ﷺ) and in the light he brought would not feel it. When the Truth said: "And indeed, many of them are defiantly disobedient," it means that those who turn over in their minds the idea of believing in the Messenger of Allah will find the light clear in his words.

1 Narrated by Muslim.

We ask ourselves: why did they want to distort the rulings of God, in order to secure for themselves temporal authority and a paltry price from those things they take as bribes? Why do they do this?

Here is the saying of the Truth, glorified is He:

﴿Do they then seek the judgment of the Jahiliyyah? And who is better than Allah in judgment for a people who are certain?﴾ (5:50)

Al-Jahiliyyah is a nisba (relative adjective) derived from jahil (ignorant). Had the nisba been taken from jahl (ignorance), the word would have come as "jahliyyah." But the Truth says here "jahiliyyah," a nisba to jahil. To know the exact meaning of jahil, we must recall and review the division of nisba (predication) that we discussed earlier, and know that every word we utter has a meaning. When we hear a word, its meaning comes to mind in isolation: just as when we hear the word "jabal" (mountain), the image of a mountain leaps to mind, but there is no clear state of the mountain, because the word was not accompanied by a judgment (hukm).

So there is a meaning to the word, but this meaning does not stand alone as useful. If we say that Cairo is densely populated, or that its services are exhausted, then we have brought a judgment that clarifies what we mean by "Cairo."

There is a difference between a word that leads to a single meaning with no judgment, and a word that carries a judgment. That is why the ancient Arab, when a word came to him without a judgment, would not accept it. A certain Arab man said: "I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God," with a fatha on the lam in the word "rasul" (Messenger). With this utterance, "Messenger of God" becomes an attribute of Muhammad, and there is not in it the required predicate. Therefore another Arab said: "And what does Muhammad do?", to draw the speaker's attention to the fact that he had not conveyed the predicate. So every word has a meaning, and this meaning is singular and must have a predication.

As when we say to a friend, "Muhammad," and the friend knows Muhammad, and asks you, "And what about Muhammad?" By this he seeks the predicate, to know what happened to him or from him. You say, "Muhammad visited me yesterday," and thus the benefit is complete.

So every single word has a meaning when it stands alone. When a judgment comes, a predication arises from it. If the predication corresponds to reality and its speaker believes it and can establish proof for it, this is the predication of knowledge ('ilm), because knowledge is a predication that is affirmed, corresponds to reality, and for which we can establish proof, just as we say "the earth is spherical." The word first suggests the image of the earth, and we add to it a predication, "spherical," because we believe it to be spherical and reality confirms that. When we bring the proof for it, this is a predication of knowledge. So knowledge is a believed predication that corresponds to reality and has proof.

As for when the predication corresponds to reality and is believed, but we cannot demonstrate it, that is taqlid (imitation), as a child repeats some truths from his father without being able to establish proof for them; he imitates one he trusts. So the stage below knowledge is taqlid. If a person believes a predication has occurred but reality is otherwise, this is jahl (ignorance). Ignorance does not mean that you do not know; rather, it is that you know a proposition contrary to reality. The jahil differs from the ummi: the ummi is one who does not know, whereas the jahil is one who knows a proposition contrary to reality and clings to it.

"Do they then seek the judgment of the Jahiliyyah?" Here the Truth asks: do they desire to persist in the false, ignorant belief? The matter with the ummi, as we have known, differs from the matter with the jahil, because it suffices to tell the ummi the knowledge you want to teach him and he accepts it from you. But with the jahil, dealing with him requires two acts: first, that you make him delete and remove the false proposition from his mind; and second, that you make him convinced of the correct proposition. What exhausts those calling to religion are these ignorant people who hold false beliefs containing baseless propositions.

But what if the predication is open to both negation and affirmation? If negation equals affirmation, it is doubt (shakk); if affirmation prevails, it is conjecture (zann); and if negation prevails, it is illusion (wahm). Thus it becomes clear to us that the matter of ignorance is a difficult matter, and what causes weariness in this world is the ignorant, because they believe in false propositions. If there is a judgment from God, why then do they not accept it? Do they want the judgment of the Jahiliyyah? And the People of the Book themselves used to disparage the judgment of the Jahiliyyah.

Note that this disparagement was in a time of confrontation between the Jahiliyyah and the People of the Book, and they used to seek victory over the people of Madinah and Makkah, and often said: "The time of a prophet has drawn near whom we will follow, and with him we will kill you, the killing of 'Ad and Iram." But as soon as the Messenger of God (ﷺ) came, they said the opposite. What did they say about the ignorant ones? Here the Truth tells us what they said: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book? They believe in idols and false deities, and say to those who disbelieve, "These are better guided in the way than those who believe."﴾ (4:51, Surah an-Nisa)

Some of the Jewish rabbis went to Quraysh, and some of the chiefs of Quraysh asked them: "You are the People of the Book and the people of ancient knowledge; tell us about us and about Muhammad." The rabbis said: "What are you and what is Muhammad?" The chiefs of Quraysh said: "We slaughter the great she-camels, we give milk mixed with water to drink, we free the captives, we maintain the ties of kinship, we give water to the pilgrims, and our religion is ancient, while Muhammad's religion is new." The rabbis said: "You are better than him and better guided in the way." And thus they distorted the saying.

The narrators relate another account at this point: that one of the Jewish rabbis said to Abu Sufyan: "By God, you are better guided in the way than he is upon." And the rabbis said that out of envy of the Messenger of God.

So do the People of the Book accept the judgment of the Jahiliyyah? No, but it is contradiction and inconsistency. And since they contradicted themselves, it became easy for them to contradict the Book that was sent down to them. Therefore the Truth asks:

"Do they then seek the judgment of the Jahiliyyah?" Then He brings after it the counterpart, His saying: "And who is better than Allah in judgment?" Glorified is He did not say, "The best in judgment are the Muslims," because some Muslims may deviate. So He referred the matter to what never changes, which is the judgment of God. And when He, glorified is He, decrees this, He knows from eternity that there will come Muslim people who will deviate from the method.

Sometimes we see deviant behavior from a Muslim: do we attribute this behavior to Islam? No. Rather we look to God's judgment in His Book, and when we see that God's judgment prohibits an act and prescribes a punishment for it, the punishment falls on the deviant Muslim too. The example is His saying: ﴿As for the thief, male or female, cut off their hands﴾ (from 5:38, Surah al-Ma'idah).

This ruling applies to Muslim and non-Muslim alike. So we do not say, "This is the judgment of the Muslims and that is the judgment of the Jahiliyyah," but we say: it is the judgment of the Lord of the method, who is God.

We note that there is an interrogative in His saying: "And who is better than Allah in judgment?"

The interrogative is the conveying of the image of a thing into the mind, not the conveying of the reality of the thing. When the speaker asks the addressee to convey understanding to him, we say: did the speaker not know the judgment? This may be valid in ordinary life, and we may see it when a person says to another: "Who visited you yesterday?" and you are facing a question about what we see; that is the reality of the interrogative. But what of when the one speaking and inquiring has nothing hidden from him? He, glorified is He, asks us to answer His question: "And who is better than Allah in judgment?" And that is the greatness of the expression.

Let me give another example, and to God belongs the highest similitude: when a person comes to you and claims that you did not do good to him, because he was a prisoner, for example, and you are the one who got him out of prison, you say to him: "Who went and paid your bail and got you out of detention?"

It is you who did it, and you do not want to tell him, "I did this and that for you," but you want him to utter what you did for him. You only say that while confident that he will find no answer but to acknowledge that you are the one who did such and such for him; and thus the matter becomes an acknowledgment rather than an announcement.

"Do they then seek the judgment of the Jahiliyyah?" The Truth knows that when they turn their heads in answering, they will find nothing but to say: "O Lord, You are better in judgment." This is an acknowledgment from them and also an announcement. As for the believer, the matter is entirely different, because the believer acknowledges and confesses God's favor upon him.

"And who is better than Allah in judgment for a people who are certain?" Those who understand that God's judgment is the best are the people who have entered the stage of certainty (yaqin). We know that the stages of certainty differ among themselves. When a truthful person informs you of a matter, you know that matter, as if he says to you: "I went to New York; this city lies on a number of islands, has towering buildings, violence is widespread in it, and people seem possessed by excessive obsession with wealth." When you hear this truthful one, you take him seriously and consider his words certainty, and this is the knowledge of certainty (ilm al-yaqin), that is, information from a person you trust because he is truthful.

Then this person comes to invite you, so you board the plane with him, and the plane flies at an altitude of forty thousand feet, and after eleven hours the plane descends slightly, so you see the lights of a bustling city, and your companion says: "This is New York, and those are the skyscrapers." Thus the knowledge of certainty becomes the eye of certainty (ayn al-yaqin).

When you both descend together into the streets of New York, you walk to the island of Manhattan and ascend the Trade Center, the highest of the skyscrapers in New York, and this is the truth of certainty (haqq al-yaqin).

So the stages of certainty are three: knowledge of certainty, if a truthful person informs you of a matter; eye of certainty, if you yourself see this matter; and truth of certainty, if you enter and are immersed in the content and details of this matter. Long ago I said to my students, to clarify the difference between the shades of certainty, a specific example: I said to them, "I saw in Indonesia a banana fruit whose single fruit reaches half a meter in length." Naturally, the students believed me, because they trust what I say, and I conveyed to them a scientific picture, and they had knowledge of certainty. Then I enter a room, open a bag, and take out a banana fruit half a meter long, and thus the knowledge of certainty becomes the eye of certainty. Then I took a knife, peeled the banana, and distributed a piece to each of them, and thus they had the truth of certainty. When the Truth says "certainty," it includes the one who knows and the one who has realized.

So the people of proofs attained the knowledge of certainty, the people of observation and witnessing attained the eye of certainty, and the people of overflowing grace and manifestations attained the truth of certainty. And the believers in God, one of them says: "By mere knowledge of certainty I am entirely certain, and I do not await the truth of certainty, for I do not dare to deny." Therefore we find that our master, the Imam Ali, may God honor his face, says: "Were the veil lifted from me, I would not increase in certainty."

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, gives us this picture in His saying: ﴿Competition in worldly gain has diverted you, until you visit the graves. No! You will come to know. Then, no! You will come to know. No! If you knew with certain knowledge, you would surely see the Hellfire. Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty.﴾ (102:1-7, Surah at-Takathur)

The beginning is the knowledge of certainty, then we see the Hellfire as we walk over the Sirat, and it becomes the eye of certainty. And by God's kindness He made us Muslims not see it with the truth of certainty, and He is the One who said: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾ (from 19:71, Surah Maryam).

He gives us the picture of the Hellfire. But when the Truth wanted to give us the picture of the truth of certainty, He brought it in His saying: ﴿So I swear by the positions of the stars. And indeed, it is a great oath, if you only knew. Indeed, it is an honored Qur'an, in a Book well-protected, which none touches except the purified, a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. Then is it this discourse that you disdain, and make your provision denying it?﴾ (56:75-82, Surah al-Waqi'ah)

All of that is preliminary, for the Truth to say: ﴿Indeed, this is the truth of certainty.﴾ (56:95, Surah al-Waqi'ah)

What the Truth mentions here about the station of the believing one who affirms is that this station is Paradise, and he sees that as the eye of certainty. As for the station of the disbeliever, he has his place in the Fire. Therefore every person will see the Fire as the eye of certainty. As for the one whom God casts into the Fire, may God forbid, he will suffer from it the truth of certainty, and the believers will enjoy Paradise with the truth of certainty.
