Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 5, verse 56:

And after that, the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted is He, says: ﴿And whoever takes Allah and His Messenger and those who believe as allies—then indeed, the party of Allah, they are the victorious.﴾

We notice that the Truth made clear in the previous verse that Allah is the Walī (Protector, Ally), and here you, O servant who believes, are among those whom Allah takes as allies, exactly like His saying: ﴿He loves them and they love Him.﴾

When Allah is at your aid, He gives you from His limitless power. So how could you take Allah as an ally? The decisive word on this matter is the saying of the Truth: ﴿If you support Allah, He will support you﴾ (part of verse 7 of surah Muhammad).

The Truth, in the verse we are concerned with, came in contrast to what came in the verse before it, for He had said earlier: ﴿Your Walī is only Allah and His Messenger and those who believe.﴾

And in this verse He comes in contrast, saying, glory be to Him: ﴿And whoever takes Allah and His Messenger and those who believe as allies—then indeed, the party of Allah, they are the victorious﴾ (surah al-Mā'idah).

This contrast clarifies for us how Allah supports the servant, and how the servant gains victory for Allah. He, glory be to Him, did not say in describing those who take Allah, His Messenger and the believers as allies merely that "they are the victorious," but He stated this victory in a general sense, saying: ﴿then indeed, the party of Allah, they are the victorious.﴾

The word ﴿ḥizb﴾ (party, faction) means: a group whose members have gathered together around a method in which they see good. A people cannot unite with the strength of each individual among them and the thought of each individual among them unless this matter is a good upon which they have gathered. Therefore, the party of Allah, in any situation and in any formation, when it is an allied cause, is the victorious party. On the individual level, we find in the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "When a matter distressed the Prophet (ﷺ), he would stand to prayer."(1)

So what is the meaning of "ḥazabahu" here? It means a matter that exhausted him, wore him down, and occupied his thoughts greatly. Through this, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) teaches us not to limit our vision to our own opinion alone, but to turn to Allah, and so we defeat the matter that distresses us and that we cannot master by establishing a "ḥizb" with Allah through prayer.

When we take from the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) the example and the model, and we know that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was not distressed by a matter concerning his worldly life, but by a matter concerning the method of Allah and the religion, we see that he went to the One who gives him and the people of faith all strength. He went to prayer. And he announced that his means had run out and he could no longer bear this matter which distressed him; and because nothing overcomes Allah, He, glory be to Him, lifts the worry from His Messenger (ﷺ) and overcomes every difficult matter. If such a matter distresses us in our souls, then let us prostrate in wonder.

Thus, when the means become scarce for the believer in some matter, and he has given all his effort, and the matter still distresses and oppresses the believer and wears him down, the believer must stand to prayer, and the Truth will make this matter easy for the believer with good. When a matter distresses the believer, he goes with prayer to the Causer, who is Allah. But the Muslim should not turn to Allah except after exhausting all the means, for the means are only the outstretched hand of Allah, and the believer cannot reject the hand of Allah and seek the Essence of Allah. So if the taking of means has come to an end, let him turn to the Causer: ﴿Is He who responds to the distressed one when he calls upon Him, and removes evil, and makes you successors on the earth? Is there a god with Allah? Little do you remember﴾ (surah al-Naml, 62).

He, glory be to Him, is the One who answers the distressed, the One who removes evil, the One who made mankind successors on the earth, and He has no partner in His dominion. He says: ﴿Say: None in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen except Allah, and they do not perceive when they will be resurrected﴾ (surah al-Naml, 65).

If someone says: "But I call upon Allah and He does not respond to me." We say: You have not made the supplication of the distressed one, because you have not exhausted the means. You must exhaust all the means. If the means have been exhausted, the Truth will answer you, as long as you are distressed.

Thus, the party of Allah, when it prevails, gives us a proposition composed of (the emphatic "inna" with its noun and its predicate). This is a Qur'anic proposition, and it differs from the cosmic proposition that describes the reality of life. The Truth says:

﴿And whoever takes Allah and His Messenger and those who believe as allies—then indeed, the party of Allah, they are the victorious﴾ (surah al-Mā'idah).

He, glory be to Him, knows what occurs in His dominion, and the Qur'anic proposition will not differ from the reality of the cosmos. Whenever you find a people gathered who, in their official and outward form, claim to be the men of Allah, and yet they are not victorious, we must know that they have deceived themselves and deceived people into thinking they are the party of Allah, while the reality of the situation is that they are not so; for He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Indeed, Our soldiers—they are the victorious﴾ (surah al-Ṣāffāt, 173).

This is a Qur'anic proposition. We always take the matter by asking: Have you been victorious or not? If you have been victorious, then your soldiery for Allah is true. And if you have not, then you are deceiving yourself that it is soldiery for Allah, when it is not so. We have a clear example from the life of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he was among his companions at the battle of Uhud and ordered the archers to take a specific position. When the archers saw the beginning of the victory of the believers over the disbelievers, and that those who fight below them were taking the spoils, they too went for the spoils and opposed the Messenger's command when he had said to them: "If you see us being snatched by the birds, do not leave your place until I send for you, and if you see us defeating the people, do not leave your place until I send for you."(2)

When they opposed the command of the Messenger of Allah, were they truly soldiers of Allah? No, rather their soldiery for Allah became corrupted. The presence of the Messenger of Allah among them did not prevent the law of Allah in His cosmos, the law of faith, from taking effect. Had they remained victorious despite opposing the Messenger, the command of the Messenger would have seemed light in their eyes; therefore the Truth willed to strike them with the pain of temporary defeat, so that they would learn discipline, and so that they would hold fast with their teeth to the command of their master and our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Truth brought about that matter while the Messenger was among them, for the sake of the interest of Islam, for had He given them victory despite their opposing the Messenger of Allah, that would have emboldened them to oppose.

(1) Narrated by Aḥmad and Abū Dāwūd from Ḥudhayfah.
(2) Narrated by Ibn Isḥāq in his Sīrah.

Then the Truthful One says after that: ﴿O you who believe, do not take as allies those who have taken your religion as a mockery and a diversion, from among those who were given the Scripture before you, nor the disbelievers. And fear Allah, if you are believers.ﴩ (5:57)

Mockery (al-hazw) is ridicule and derision. The mockery of the People of the Book toward the People of the Truth is a form of reverse reaction. When some of the People of Falsehood see one individual who is committed, who prays and does not stare at women, they may describe him with unseemly attributes, because they receive his commitment only with a kind of mockery, and so that it is not understood that he is better than them. They may also try to mislead him so that he follows them.

Let us suppose that three young men were bound together by friendship, then two of them deviated while one of them became committed. One of the deviants had a sister, and his deviant companion asks for this sister's hand, and the companion who did not deviate comes to ask for the same sister. Here we find that the brother does not agree to his sister marrying the deviant, but agrees to her marrying the one who did not deviate, because he will not deceive himself. When the deviant reproaches him, he replies: "Would I entrust you with my sister? I know you thoroughly."

Thus we see that values are values. When there is a person upon the truth who meets people upon falsehood, we find they do not leave him alone, and because they will not be able to be like him, they at least mock him, so that they may preserve their corruption for themselves. When we look at the harmful habits that spread, such as sniffing heroin or smoking narcotics, we find that the one who has fallen into the trap of these calamities wants to drag others into the same swamp. And we find in the Qur'an what the Creator of dispositions and the One who knows them tells us: ﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed. And when they passed by them, they winked at one another.﴾ (Surat al-Mutaffifin, 83:29–30)

Like the saying of the People of Falsehood to the believer: "Carry us to Paradise on your wing," or: "Do you want to become a saint?"

﴿And when they returned to their families, they returned jesting.﴾ (83:31)

One of them returns to his family and recounts with delight: "We met a man drowning in faith and we mocked him."

﴿And when they saw them, they said, "Indeed, these are misguided." But they had not been sent as guardians over them.﴾ (83:32–33)

Indeed, we may find that the people of misguidance accuse the believer of being astray. So what will the recompense be on the Day of Gathering?

﴿So today those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers, upon couches, looking on. Have the disbelievers been recompensed for what they used to do?﴾ (83:34–36)

It is as if the Truthful One asks the believers: "Have I not taken your right for you?" So those who take the religion as mockery and diversion, and who claim faith as hypocrisy, beware lest you entrust yourselves to them. The Truth had already warned you at the outset: ﴿Do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies; they are allies of one another.﴾ (5:51)

Here He commands not to take as allies those who make the religion a subject of mockery, and the believers must be alert and cautious, because the Truth says: ﴿Fear Allah, if you are believers.﴾ So if you are truly believers, then you must act with the vigilance of faith. You must not befriend the Jews and the Christians, nor those who cloak themselves in faith hypocritically, seeking to benefit from the privileges of Islam to obtain their outward rights while their hearts are with the non-believers. The fear of Allah begins with the believer implementing the methodology, and striving to preserve for the methodology the immunity of its power before its adversaries, by not allowing the believer to place the protection of the methodology in the hands of those who do not believe, among the Jews, the Christians, the disbelievers and the hypocrites.

Then the Truth (Allah) says, after that: ﴿And when you call to prayer, they take it as a mockery and a diversion. That is because they are a people who do not reason.﴾

Al-nida' (calling) is a summons made aloud. Its opposite is al-munajah (private, intimate address). This verse establishes that the adhan (call to prayer) is legislated by the Qur'an. This is a refutation of those who say that the adhan was legislated by the Sunnah, or that the Qur'an, by this verse, merely affirmed the legislation of the adhan.

﴿When you call to prayer, they take it as a mockery and a diversion.﴾ This is because they used to say of the adhan: "They shout like the braying of donkeys." The Truth described them with His words: ﴿That is because they are a people who do not reason.﴾ And reason ('aql), as we know, is the faculty that performs the task of choosing between alternatives; that is, it selects what is good among matters, studies the advantages and disadvantages of each matter, and chooses the profitable course.

Indeed, desire (hawa) is what drives reason to choose a contrary matter, so it inclines reason toward error. The blight of opinion is desire. A person does not deviate from the path of rightness except when he wants to serve his desire. Therefore the believer must restrain the unbridled force of his desire by his reason. The word 'aql is taken from 'iqal (the tether) of the camel: the camel's owner ties its leg with a piece of rope so that it does not bolt. A person needs reason to restrain the unbridled force of desire, and to rescue the person from error, not to justify desire. As for those who want reason as a liberation from thought, we say to them: you do not understand the meaning of the word "reason." The word 'aql came to prevent desire, not so that a person may use his desire to embolden his opinion and conduct against what is upright; reason is what prevents thought from becoming a justification for desire.

So if they were people who reason, we would say to them: the deeds you are calling to have a presumed benefit, and they may benefit you in your worldly life; yet no one can determine the lifespan of the world with respect to himself, for the worldly life of an individual may not exceed a hundred years. The worldly life of a person is his lifetime in it. God has concealed the cause and manner of death from creatures, so that a person knows his lifespan is uncertain and may end before his eye blinks. And if they were people who reason, they would not have sold their Hereafter for their worldly life. And if they reasoned, they would have turned the matter of alternatives over in their minds, and would have known that with this stance of theirs toward the question of faith and Islam, they are taking a losing position that is not in their interest.

Almighty God then says: ﴿Say, "O People of the Scripture, do you resent us only because we believe in Allah and in what has been revealed to us and what was revealed before, and because most of you are defiantly disobedient?"﴾ (5:59)

"Qul" (say) is an address to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When the Truth addresses the Messenger, the address is also to his ummah (ﷺ), so we too say: {Say, O People of the Scripture, do you resent us only because we believe in Allah

and in what has been revealed to us and what was revealed before, and because most of you are defiantly disobedient} (part of verse 59, Surat al-Ma'idah).

"Naqama yanqimu" means he disliked, or held something against, someone for doing something. So why do you dislike our faith, O People of the Scripture? Is faith something to be disliked? The Truth here poses a question they cannot answer. We believe in Allah, His messengers, what was revealed to us and what was revealed before. What is there in this to dislike? Our master Muhammad (ﷺ) informed the Jews that we believe in Allah and in the Messenger, and among the messengers is our master Jesus son of Mary (peace be upon him), and they became very angry with him. So how can the People of the Scripture dislike the Muslims' belief in Allah?

An example of this: when a person invites you to some improper conduct or to go to a suspicious place and you refuse, that person dislikes you, and you say to him: "Do you dislike in my conduct that I be upright?" We know that the trustworthy person is a treasure to those who know him, and what deserves resentment and dislike is harmful action. As for belief in Allah, it is a beloved matter, because it teaches a person good manners with all of Allah's creation, teaches a person to guard people's honour, teaches a person not to transgress against people's property and blood, not to backbite, not to take bribes, to be sincere in work, and not to break an appointment. So what in this deserves dislike?

Therefore, whoever dislikes a person for any reason of this kind is disliking without logic, and it was obligatory that the cause of dislike become a cause of love. Someone may come and say to you: "There is no fault in so-and-so except such-and-such."

He may mention a reasonable cause, but no one ever says: "There is no fault in so-and-so except that he is chivalrous," because chivalry cannot be a fault. It is as if the speaker has exerted his mind to discover a fault and found nothing but a wonderful quality, and said of it: "If you consider this quality a fault, then this is his fault." The Arabs call this one of the literary methods of expression: emphasising praise by means of something resembling blame. A speaker says: "There is no fault in so-and-so except such-and-such." When the listener hears this, he thinks the fault to be mentioned is an ugly trait, and is surprised to find it is a beautiful quality. Thus the speaker emphasises praise through what resembles blame: ﴿Say, O People of the Scripture, do you resent us only because we believe in Allah and in what has been revealed to us and what was revealed before, and because most of you are defiantly disobedient.﴾

You say that you are People of the Scripture and that you have the Torah, and it was necessary for you to know how faith refines souls and drives evil away from them, because you have precedence in faith: you believed in Allah and in the messengers before Moses and Jesus, and you believed in Moses. The Muslims believed in Allah, believed in what was revealed to them, and believed in the messengers, including Moses, Jesus and Muhammad (may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them all). So how can this be disliked?

And if this is something to be disliked, we as believers must ask you: why do you hold this against us? There is no doubt that you hold our belief in Allah against us because the matter is unclear in your minds. Had it been clear in your minds, you would not dislike our faith. Therefore the matter of belief in Allah is not settled in your consciences as People of the Scripture, as proven by the fact that you dislike those who believe in Allah. The evidence for this is that you have placed Allah in a position unworthy of His perfection: you have anthropomorphised Him, and you said: ﴿Until we see Allah openly﴾ (part of verse 55, Surat al-Baqarah),

and you said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich﴾ (part of verse 181, Surat Al 'Imran), and ﴿The hand of Allah is chained﴾ (part of verse 64, Surat al-Ma'idah).

So you dislike that we should believe in Allah with a belief befitting the perfection of Allah, because you have not believed in Allah with correct belief; had our belief matched yours, you would not have disliked us. Likewise, you did not believe in the Scriptures, as proven by the fact that you distorted them. And you did not believe in the messengers, because you took the positions you took regarding Jesus (peace be upon him). Therefore you hold against us matters that are not disliked by a sound nature, and this is evidence that your nature is corrupt. And if you dislike this faith, what do you possess against those you dislike? You have no power to do anything to us. But when Allah dislikes you, what will He do to you? When you dislike us, you have no ability to punish us, but the one who dislikes you is Allah, with the all-powerful might to take vengeance on our behalf against you.

So your dislike of us has no value. And if we are competing with you, and such competition is a kind of disputation with opponents, what does it matter to you that we are believers?

An example: a person accuses you of being stingy, and you say to him: "Suppose I am indeed stingy; what concern is it of yours?" This is what we call "accommodating the opponent" (mujarat al-khusum). Therefore we say to the People of the Scripture: suppose your dislike of us has some substance and you are able to harm us, then there is something worse than this for you, which is the punishment of Allah. We will see what will happen to you when Allah dislikes you, and He is capable of everything. And supposing your harm to us is evil, the more effective is the punishment of the Truth against you, because when He dislikes you He is able to punish you as He wills. So the bargain, your bargain of disliking us, is a losing one on your part.

Therefore the Truth said: ﴿Say, "Shall I inform you of something worse than that as recompense from Allah? Those whom Allah has cursed and with whom He became angry and made of them apes and swine and those who worshipped the Taghut. Those are worse in position and further astray from the right way."﴾ (5:60)

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 5, verse 60:

Even if we grant, for the sake of argument, that you, People of the Book, consider that your scheming against us will bring us some harm, despite the fact that you cannot repay us with anything. Behold, the Truth informs you through the tongue of His Messenger of something worse than this, namely the punishment that Allah has prepared for you, and He is able to bring it down upon you, and it is the greater harm. This is a kind of "playing along with the opponent," as we have said. Allah teaches us this through the tongue of His Messenger when He says to his opponents: ﴿And indeed, either we or you are surely upon guidance or in clear error﴾ (part of verse 24, Surah Saba).

The Messenger is certainly upon guidance and his opponents are certainly upon error. But the Messenger of Allah leaves the matter open, asking his opponents to examine themselves so that they may discuss the values to which Islam calls. They will find that the values of Islam are guidance and that they themselves are in error. We know that guidance and error do not coincide: we as Muslims are upon guidance, and you are upon error. The means of distinguishing is that a person employs his intellect on the matter, and thereby sees who is upon guidance and who is upon error. You do not dispute with the opponent over the fundamental claim, but you concede to the opponent for the sake of argument. The final distinction is the decisive criterion. Whoever distinguishes will find the grounds of the opponent's error as clear as the grounds of the guidance of the Muslims.

﴿Say: O People of the Book, do you blame us only for believing in Allah, and in what has been revealed to us, and in what was revealed before, and that most of you are defiantly disobedient?﴾ (Surah al-Ma'idah 5:59).

If you find fault with us, or dislike us, or regard our faith as a reproach, then this is a matter for which a person should not be disliked, because you yourselves claim that you believe in Allah. Likewise, one cannot be reviled for believing in what Allah has sent down in a Book, because you also say that you believe in the Torah. And you say that you believe in the prophets who came before Musa. The point of disagreement is that Isa, peace be upon him, came after your Prophet, and you disbelieved in him, but we believed in him. Thus we are consistent with ourselves and with our Lord.

Then the Truth conveys: ﴿and that most of you are defiantly disobedient﴾. We know that caution in judgment requires that the Truth not pass a sweeping verdict upon them that they are all defiantly disobedient, because among them are some people whose souls are inclined to faith in Allah and in Islam. For this reason, the Truth never generalized the judgment of defiant disobedience to all People of the Book, so as to give an opportunity to whoever is considering declaring his faith.

After that, the announcement of their punishment comes through the tongue of the Messenger: (Say: Shall I inform you of something worse than that in terms of reward from Allah?) So there is then something more harmful for you, because it was not proper for you to dislike our faith. And more harmful than this is the curse of Allah (whoever Allah has cursed and grown angry with, and made of them apes and swine). He, glorified is He, mentions the attributes that are in them: the curse of Allah upon them, His anger against them, and His making some of them apes and swine. And how can Allah bring such attributes as a "reward"? This is a kind of opening the door of hope and expectation, and then, after that, the verse of the Exalted shatters them completely: ﴿So give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾ (part of verse 21, Surah Ali 'Imran).

The painful punishment is what they are warned of, and likewise the curse cannot be a reward. But the Qur'anic style gives the opposing soul a kind of expansion, then gives it the contrary of that, which is contraction, so that the contraction is more eloquent and more painful.

An example of this, as we have said before, is the prisoner who asks for a cup of water. The guard brings him the cup and brings it close to his mouth, then pours the water out on the ground. This action first plants in the prisoner's soul hope of quenching his thirst, then the spilling of the water on the ground becomes a cause of torment and intensification of it. But if the guard had refused at first to provide the water, the prisoner would have lived in despair, which is one of the two comforts.

We see this also in one who awaits a verdict which may be execution and may be acquittal, and the period of waiting is the one filled with anxiety. When they place the one awaiting on the scale, they find his weight decreased. And after the sentence of his execution, his weight begins to increase, because despair is one of the two comforts. So the expansion of the soul followed by the coming of contraction is the more grievous and the harder on the soul. For this reason the Truth says: ﴿So give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾ (part of verse 21, Surah Ali 'Imran).

This glad tidings brings expansion to the soul, and contraction follows it. Similarly, the Truth's saying:

﴿And if they call for help, they will be granted relief with water like molten brass that scalds the faces﴾ (part of verse 29, Surah al-Kahf).

That is, a kind of punishment has already befallen them which calls for relief, and after that they are given relief not with what would save them, but with what increases their punishment.

When they hear "they will be granted relief," their faces brighten, they are calmed, and their souls are reassured; then afterward contraction strikes their hearing: ﴿with water like molten brass that scalds the faces﴾. So the word "reward" brings them a measure of expansion followed by punishment.

Furthermore, the comparative form (af'al al-tafdil) comes in the pattern "af'al," such as "akram" (more generous), "ajwad" (more bounteous), "ashja'" (more courageous). This is a kind of increase of the attribute in one party over the other. Except for a few words that came in the language in a form other than the comparative, such as the word "khayr" (good) and the word "sharr" (evil): the form "akhyar" (better, in the sense of more good) does not occur from them, nor does "asharr" (worse, in the sense of more evil). Sometimes the word "khayr" is used and its opposite is the lesser good. What distinguishes the meaning, which is the presence of the word "min" (than), as in our saying: "So-and-so is better than so-and-so." But if one says: "So-and-so is good" (khayr), its opposite is "sharr" (evil), because there is no word "akhyar."

Thus we find the word "khayr" used for description at one time, and used for intensification of description at another time, and what separates the two is the presence of "min." One says: "So-and-so is better than so-and-so," and likewise the word "sharr." The use of the word "khayr" both in the comparative and in the non-comparative has come in the saying of the Exalted:

﴿O Prophet, say to those among your captives: If Allah knows any good in your hearts, He will give you better than what was taken from you and will forgive you, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (Surah al-Anfal 8:70).

The Prophetic hadith says: (The strong believer is better (khayr) and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, and there is good (khayr) in each) (1).

There is good in every believer, but there is more good in the strong believer than in the weak believer. And the example that the word "khayr" is opposed to the word "sharr" is the saying of the Truth:

﴿And let not those who withhold what Allah has given them of His bounty think that it is good for them; rather it is evil for them﴾ (part of verse 180, Surah Ali 'Imran).

Here "khayr" is not the comparative form but a plain description; when "min" comes, one knows it is comparative, and the absence of the word "min" indicates that it is plain description, and its opposite is the word "sharr." Here the Truth says: ﴿Say: Shall I inform you of something worse than that?﴾ The word "sharr" here is in the comparative sense, and this does not mean that the believers are in "sharr," but it is accommodation to the opponent and treating what the opponent says as conceded for the sake of argument. In reality there is something worse, and before Allah, and this is what is meant by the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Those whom Allah has cursed and with whom He is angry, and of whom He made apes and swine, and who worshipped the Taghut; those are worse in place and further astray from the right way﴾ (part of verse 60, Surah al-Ma'idah).

Why then is the destination of these people to be worse? Because they disliked the conduct of the believers and could not vent the rancor in their breasts by punishing the believers. But Allah hates them and possesses punishment for them, and their destination is the destination that the Truth clarifies in His saying: ﴿Allah has cursed them, and He is angry with them, and made of them apes and swine﴾. The curse is expulsion from mercy, and expulsion from mercy means being deprived of good.

An example of this, and to Allah belongs the highest similitude, is when there is a servant in the service of a person who lodges, eats and clothes himself at the master's expense, and if this servant does not discharge the duties of service in the required manner, his master is not pleased with him and dismisses him from service. When a man dismisses his servant, he announces to the people that this servant did not discharge his duty of service, so no one employs him after that. This is anger. Thereby we know the difference between being expelled from mercy only, with nothing following that, and the anger continuing with an announcement of the reason for the removal from mercy. This means that after He expelled them, Allah pursues them with His anger and wrath, and His curse upon them does not cease from them.

Allah, glorified and exalted is He, announces to the People of the Book: My expelling you from My mercy and the continuation of My anger upon you is a great evil. And the anger of Allah, as we know, entails things in every movement of their lives: it prevents guidance from reaching their hearts, by sealing their hearts so that faith does not enter them and disbelief does not leave them; or by making of them apes and swine. And if we ask: how is their offspring? We know that one who is transformed does not reproduce; he is transformed until he is seen as transformed and then taken to death.

Are they those who transgressed on the Sabbath, or those who worshipped the calf, or those who disbelieved after the descent of the table of Isa? They are all of these. Or they are apes, that is, in the qualities of apes, such as frivolity, lightness of movement, and exposure of nakedness; or their natures and qualities are like swine, for these have foulness, stench, and a crude vigor like that of the swine. The most important characteristic of the swine is that it is not jealous of its female. This exists among them, and the habit has spread among them of employing their daughters in prostitution and other works of falsehood.

Thus we understand the Truth's saying: ﴿And made of them apes and swine﴾, either on the basis that it is actual transformation, and actual transformation does not remain constant and fixed; rather transformation is for a limited time, in which people see them transformed and then they die and it ends; or we understand it as meaning that their conduct is like the conduct of apes and swine.

The Truth continues: ﴿and worshipped the Taghut﴾. Worship is nothing but the obedience of the worshipper to the worshipped in what he commands and what he forbids, and the taghut are those who adorn for them evil, hypocrisy, consuming of the unlawful, and sin. Their destination is the saying of the Truth: ﴿Those are worse in place and further astray from the right way﴾, and this is the reality in which they live, which is all evil, and they do not think of walking on the sound path.

And when we read the Truth's saying in full in this verse: ﴿Say: Shall I inform you of something worse than that in terms of reward from Allah? Those whom Allah has cursed and with whom He is angry, and of whom He made apes and swine, and who worshipped the Taghut; those are worse in place and further astray from the right way (60)﴾ (Surah al-Ma'idah).

We know that they are in a state of heedlessness of the path of guidance that leads to the truth, because "sawa' al-sabil" (the right way) is the level path that leads to the goal. The routes of the Arabs were either sandy or between mountains, and they would choose to walk in the middle of the road so that they would not be harmed by a yawning sandy precipice that might collapse upon them, or that a rock from the mountain might fall upon them.

Therefore the Truth said: ﴿A speaker among them said: Indeed I had a companion (51), who used to say: Are you really among those who believe? (52) When we die and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be recompensed? (53) He said: Would you like to look down? (54) So he looked down and saw him in the midst of the Hellfire (55)﴾ (Surah al-Saffat).

That is, he was in the midst of Hell.

1 Narrated by Ahmad 2/370, and Muslim in Qadar, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra, and Ibn Majah in Zuhd, and Malik in al-Muwatta (al-Tamhid of Ibn 'Abd al-Barr 9/287).

Speaking of those with whom He is angry, the Truth (al-Haqq) then says: ﴿And when they come to you, they say, "We believe," but they had entered with disbelief and they had gone out with it. And Allah is most knowing of what they were concealing.﴾ (5:61)

These are the ones who took the religion as ridicule, play, and mockery. When they enter upon the believers, they enter with disbelief with them, and when they sat with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they went out with disbelief as well. That is to say, disbelief clung to them both entering and leaving, as though their sitting with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) added nothing to them at all. Yet it was possible that a person might enter the gathering of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while an unbeliever, and then the care of guidance would touch him, so that he leaves as a believer.

An example of this is Fadalah ibn Umayr al-Laythi, who came to kill the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the year of the Conquest. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by Fadalah, he said to him: "What were you saying to yourself?" He said: "Nothing; I was remembering Allah, Mighty and Majestic." The Prophet (ﷺ) smiled and said: "I ask Allah's forgiveness for you," and he placed his hand upon Fadalah's chest. Fadalah would say: "By Allah, he did not lift his hand from my chest until there was nothing on the face of the earth more beloved to me than him."(1)

The care of guidance touched him: he entered first with his disbelief and left second with deep faith. But these people entered with disbelief and left with disbelief, as though their entering was hypocrisy. This is shown by His saying, the Truth: ﴿And Allah is most knowing of what they were concealing﴾, and this statement is proof of their hypocrisy, for they declared belief but entered with disbelief and left with disbelief. They were concealing that their entering upon the Messenger was pure hypocrisy. This is a characteristic of those who said "We believe," yet their entry into Islam was hypocrisy, because their disbelief was a settled matter in their hearts that could not be shaken. In the style of speech, it would have sufficed for the Truth to say: "and they had entered with disbelief and gone out with it," but He said "they" (hum), and this specifies their disbelieving identity. Thus the process of entering with disbelief and leaving with disbelief is a process decided in advance; therefore the Truth exposes them: ﴿And Allah is most knowing of what they were concealing﴾.

He, glorified be He, used the superlative form "most knowing" (a'lam), as though the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), through the illuminations of Allah upon him and His enlightenment of him, also knew that they were hypocrites. But the Messenger of Allah's knowledge did not reach the knowledge of the Truth, glorified and exalted be He; Allah's knowledge is essential, and the Messenger's knowledge is an overflow from Him, glorified be He.

Thus His saying, the Truth, ﴿Allah is most knowing﴾ does not prevent there being people who knew that they were hypocrites. It became settled in the Prophet's mind that they were hypocrites, and that Allah is most knowing of what they were concealing. Concealment (al-katm) is holding back an inner feeling from coming out and appearing clearly, and the attempt at concealment is an unnatural process because it is forced. Their disbelief nearly appears and comes out, so they try to hide it because they are eager not to be exposed, but Allah's knowledge, nothing is hidden from Him.

Al-Sha'rawi said: Then the Truth (Allah) says: ﴿And you see many of them hastening toward sin and transgression, and their consuming of the forbidden [gain]. Evil indeed is what they have been doing.﴾ (5:62)

Hastening toward sin (al-musara'ah fi al-ithm) means that from the very beginning of the matter they are in sin, and they hasten to it. That is, they were at the start of sin and proceed toward its end. Their disbelief is evident from the outset, as if their very nature exposes them, despite their attempt to conceal it. They find themselves hastening to commit sin, meaning their deeds incline toward disbelief, and the Truth makes them neglect concealment, so there appear from them things that are more scandalous than speech. This is because sin has stages: a stage of speech and a stage of action, and action exposes more than speech.

﴿You see many of them hastening toward sin and transgression﴾. The Truth says: ﴿many of them﴾, to safeguard the possibility that faith may exist in the heart of a few of them, and to exonerate any person who disbelieves in faith. They also hasten toward transgression (al-'udwan). If sin (ithm) is wrongdoing of any kind, then transgression is sin by which a person takes the right of another. An example of this is the person who harbors envy (al-hiqd): his sin falls upon himself, and therefore he suffers from conflict among his faculties, until he appears to be devouring himself bit by bit.

Envy (al-hiqd), as we know, is a psychological crime that has not overstepped its limit. It is said of envy that it is the crime whose punishment precedes it, unlike any other crime, for any crime's punishment comes after it, except envy and jealousy; the punishment of envy befalls its possessor before he envies, because the envious person envies only because his heart and feelings are torn apart when he sees the one envied in good. Therefore it is said in the narration: "It is enough punishment for the envier that he grieves at the time of your happiness."

Thus whoever commits a sin against himself does not transfer the effect of his sin to others, whereas whoever commits transgression transfers a person's right to another. Transgression is of two kinds: there is one who oversteps to give a right to one who has no right, and there is one who oversteps by keeping silent about the oppressor. The oppressor is seized by the desire to oppress, but one who sees the oppressor and remains silent without forbidding him is also committing transgression, because the oppressor has within himself what drives him to oppress, whereas the witness who keeps silent has nothing within himself driving him to silence. So who, then, is the greater evil? It is the one who keeps silent instead of alerting the oppressor that he is oppressing.

﴿And you see many of them hastening toward sin and transgression﴾: we notice that the word (sara'a, hastened) like the word (nafasa, competed) indicates that there are people in a race, as if they are competing for sin and transgression, as if sin and transgression were a goal set up in their minds and agreed upon by their hearts.

﴿And their consuming of the forbidden [gain]. Evil indeed is what they have been doing.﴾ As-suht (the forbidden gain) is every wealth whose source is unlawful, whether it is bribery (rishwah), usury (riba), theft (sariqah), embezzlement (ikhtilas), snatching (khatf), or usurpation (ightisab). All these are forms of as-suht, and what resembles them, for they are the taking of another's right. The taking of another's right has many forms: if someone takes it secretly, that is theft. If a person hastens to snatch something from another's goods, that is snatching. If the owner of the goods pursues him and they pull and struggle with each other, this tugging turns the snatching into the realm of anger. If a person is trusted with something and takes it, that is embezzlement, and all of that is consuming wealth by forbidden means. Evil is this kind of action.

Then the Almighty says: ﴿Why do the rabbis and the scholars not forbid them from uttering sin and consuming what is unlawful? Evil indeed is what they have been doing.﴾

The rabbaniyyun (those who are devoted to the Lord, the godly ones) are those who attribute themselves to the Lord (Rabb) in all their conduct, and likewise the ahbar (rabbis, the learned ones) who know the religion. Neither these nor those forbid these people among the People of the Book from committing sin and consuming what is unlawful. How, then, do these rabbaniyyun and ahbar set themselves up as leaders of the religious conscience without performing their duty of admonishing the people? This emphasises that the rabbaniyyun and the ahbar only want the power of domination over people.

The rabbaniyyun are the heads of the Christians, and the ahbar are the heads of the Jews. Among the Jews and Christians there were those possessed by the desires of consuming what is unlawful, of wrongdoing and of speaking sin. So why did those attributed to God not stir to forbid that, when they are the ones who have taken their share in this world by being attributed to safeguarding the method of God against human deviations? Was it not their duty to forbid the wrongdoers and sinners from wrongdoing and sin?

Indeed, the one who wrongs has a desire to benefit from the wrong, but as for you, O rabbaniyyun and ahbar, why do you not move to stop that? Without doubt they were filled with delight at this sin, that transgression and consuming what is unlawful, and the source of their delight is that if one of them were sound in his conduct and judgments, he would be jealous for the method, but he accepts deviation, because it is in his interest that others deviate so that no one blames him. The Almighty used (lawla) at the beginning of this verse as an exhortation (tahdid), meaning it intends urging to action... that is, the rabbaniyyun and the ahbar ought to have forbidden them from consuming what is unlawful, from speaking sin and transgression. Then the precision of the Qur'anic expression is manifest, as it always is, in His saying: ﴿Evil indeed is what they have been doing.﴾

We note that in the preceding verse, concerning the conduct of the common People of the Book, the Almighty said: ﴿Evil indeed is what they have been doing (ya'malun)﴾. Thus the Almighty distinguishes between "bi'sa" regarding a craft (sun'a) and "bi'sa" regarding an action ('amal). The evil of the rabbaniyyun and the ahbar is an evil of craft. We know that each limb of a human being has a specific function: the eye's function is to see, the ear's is to hear, the hand's is touching and handling action, the foot walks, and the tongue's field of work is speech. The limbs divide into two kinds: the tongue, whose function is saying, and the rest of the limbs, whose functions are deeds, as evidenced by God's saying:

﴿Greatly hateful it is in the sight of God that you say what you do not do (3)﴾ (Surat al-Saff).

Thus saying is the counterpart of doing. Saying is an action, and doing is an action. And since there is saying and doing among the common People of the Book in that domain, the Almighty says: ﴿Evil indeed is what they have been doing.﴾

Concerning the rabbaniyyun and the ahbar He said: ﴿Evil indeed is what they have been crafting﴾ (yasna'un), to clarify the difference between one who works and one who crafts. Whoever tears his garment and comes with a needle and thread to mend it is a tailor (khayyit) in the sense of one who sews, but the one who practises that as a profession is the (khayyat, tailor). The possessor of a trade is the one who takes its description, because he has mastery of it; as for one who practises it only once, he takes from the craft only to the extent that shows he has not perfected it.

The rabbaniyyun and the ahbar had made the matter of religion and priesthood into a craft, with great refinement. That is what caused the legislative authority in the whole world to pass from the method of heaven to the method of earth. When we return to the history of law, we find that the origin of legislation was from the priests, who were attributed to God and knew the news of heaven, and they were the ones who judged between people. But they became corrupt, and society saw that they would rule in one case by one judgment, then in a similar case rule by the opposite of the previous judgment, and that they took bribes for that, distinguished between people, and people came to know that the priests could not be trusted with justice. Therefore they abandoned the priests and began to enact laws of their own, far from the priests' rulings. Thus the matter passed from the legislation and rulings of priests to a society that no longer adhered to religion because of the deviations of the priests' rulings from justice, and because they sold judgments to whoever paid more, or ruled in favour of the one with influence. In this way the matter became a craft for them. And evil is that craft.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 5, verse 64:

And after that, the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿And the Jews say, "The Hand of Allah is chained up." Their hands are chained up, and they are cursed for what they say. Rather, both His Hands are outspread; He spends as He wills. And what has been sent down to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief. And We have cast among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection. Whenever they kindle the fire of war, Allah extinguishes it, and they strive throughout the land to cause corruption, and Allah does not love the corrupters.﴾ (64)

We know that the hand is a limb with free movement: it moves to the right, moves to the left, moves downward and upward. It has fingers, and Allah has given each finger a task together with its fellows. Let each of us observe his fingers during any work, and he will find them spreading apart and coming together in a harmonious, voluntary motion to carry out the task. The fingers are formed with joints and phalanges, and the size of each phalanx differs from the others, so that they may perform the task in harmony. When something prevents this limb from performing its task, you have thereby shackled it, that is, bound it from the action required of it.

The meaning of His saying ﴿The Hand of Allah is chained up﴾ is that the Hand of Allah – God forbid – is paralysed in its movement.

They said this before the emergence of our master Muhammad (ﷺ) and before Islam advanced upon them to refute their falsehood. It happened that they devoted themselves to manufacturing instruments of war, building fortresses, and farming, and they became preoccupied away from agriculture, so their crops failed, and when the time of harvest came they found nothing. Then Finhas (Phinehas), who was one of the Jews, said: "Why has Allah withdrawn His hand from us? The Hand of Allah is chained up." We note that the one who said this was a single person, yet the Truth says here: ﴿And the Jews say, "The Hand of Allah is chained up."﴾ The meaning is that when Finhas said that, they heard him, his words pleased them, and they agreed with him.

Or they saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at the beginning of the Hijrah, when he established brotherhood between the Emigrants and the Helpers, and nights would pass over the Muslims without food. The Jews would see them and mock that state, saying: "The Hand of Allah is chained up from Muhammad and his family."

Or they said: "The Hand of Allah is chained up in the Hereafter from our punishment, because He will punish us only for a number of days." Whoever permits himself to make Allah subject to the events of His creation is in fact a disbeliever in Allah, because he brings Allah down from His station. If the Hand of Allah were chained up, then this restraint, shackling, and prevention would come from the creation of Allah. How could a creature of Allah be able to bind the Hand of Allah? They have presumed upon the station of divinity, and this is from bad manners, just as they said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich﴾ (part of verse 181, Surah Al 'Imran).

When they said ﴿The Hand of Allah is chained up﴾, the Truth replied to them: ﴿Rather, both His Hands are outspread﴾, and before that He said ﴿Their hands are chained up﴾. Does the Truth curse them? Certainly not, because He is the source to which creation turns in supplication, and He is capable of all creation. But when the Truth relates what they said, He is alerting the faithful mind that receives His speech: whenever it finds a description that does not befit Allah, it must reject that speech even before seeing the reply to them.

﴿And the Jews say, "The Hand of Allah is chained up." Their hands are chained up﴾. This teaches us that when we hear a description that is not fitting, we must refute it, because the Truth does not curse His servants; cursing (du'a') is that a helpless one raises his request to one who is capable, so that the request may be fulfilled for him.

So, if the Truth said it, it is either information or instruction for us. If it is information, we note that Allah had decreed stinginess upon them at the moment they said this and from the moment of this saying. If the intention is to teach us, then we learn faithful manners and reject every description that does not befit the majesty of Allah.

This matter has a parallel. When Allah, glorified and exalted is He, knew the longing of His Messenger and the believers to go to the Sacred Mosque, He said to His Messenger:

﴿You will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if Allah wills﴾ (part of verse 27, Surah al-Fath).

Is this information from Allah, or is it instruction for us? It is instruction for us, that we should do so when we long to do something. Likewise here: ﴿And the Jews say, "The Hand of Allah is chained up."﴾ Therefore He, glorified is He, teaches us to say ﴿Their hands are chained up﴾, just as He taught us to say "In shaa' Allah" (if Allah wills), so that we attribute every decree to Allah. The philosophers have tried to make us forget the determination of the Will, saying: Allah created the natural laws and the cosmos and made for them laws operating in the universe. Did the Truth exercise His authority at the moment He created the laws and then leave matters to themselves? No. Therefore He, glorified is He, brought miracles that break the laws, to show us that the laws did not take the word to act; rather the Hand of Allah is still in His universe. Fire, for example, which burns, is commanded: ﴿O fire, be coolness and safety﴾ (part of verse 69, Surah al-Anbiya').

And water, which drowns, is commanded: ﴿So We revealed to Musa: Strike the sea with your staff, and it parted, and each part was like a great mountain﴾ (63, Surah al-Shu'ara').

And He said: ﴿So strike for them a dry path through the sea, not fearing being overtaken, nor being afraid﴾ (77). ﴿Then Pharaoh followed them with his soldiers, and there covered them of the sea that which covered them﴾ (78) (parts of verses 77 and 78, Surah Taha).

And the staff, which was made from the branch of a dry tree, turned into a serpent: that is, it transferred all of it into another kind, from plant to animal. This is the breaking of the laws.

The Truth says about those who claimed that the Hand of Allah is chained up: ﴿Their hands are chained up, and they are cursed for what they say﴾, meaning that they were expelled from the mercy of Allah, because they themselves gave glad tidings against themselves and said the Hand of Allah is chained up, while He, glorified is He, is able to withhold His giving from them.

He, glorified is He, continues: ﴿Rather, both His Hands are outspread; He spends as He wills﴾, and He gives to whom He wills. The word "hand" (yad) in the language is applied to the limb and is applied to blessing. A man says: "I have a hand (yad) owed to so-and-so that I will not forget," meaning he has done a favour that cannot be forgotten. The hand is used in this sense because all taking and receiving occurs by the hand. "Hand" is also used to mean ownership, as He, glorified is He, says: ﴿or the one in whose hand is the marriage tie should pardon﴾ (part of verse 237, Surah al-Baqarah).

That is, the one who has the power to marry the woman is the one who pardons. In fighting we find the wise saying: ﴿Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands﴾ (part of verse 14, Surah al-Tawbah). Or "hand" is applied to one who has authority in some matter, as the Truth has said: ﴿What prevented you from prostrating to what I created with My Hands?﴾ (part of verse 75, Surah Sad).

Adam is the first creation, and all of us after him are created by procreation from the marital pair. Allah has honoured the human being in that He created him with His Hands, and He created everything by ("Be!"). So the word "hand" is applied to multiple meanings. The Messenger said: "The Muslims' blood is equal, the least of them may give a pledge of protection on their behalf, and they are a single hand against all others" (1).

That is, when hands are joined, they become the hand that has power. And when we read the phrase "the Hand of Allah," do we restrict it to His blessing or His dominion?

﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion, and He is over all things capable﴾ (1, Surah al-Mulk).

Allah, glorified and exalted is He, knows His own essence best, so let us stop at the description: yes, He has a hand, He has two hands. Beware of imagining that everything related to Allah is like what relates to you, because the principle is that you have existence now, and Allah has existence, but your existence is other than the existence of Allah; likewise His hand is not like your hand. Lest we liken Him and say that He has a hand like our hands, let us say that what is meant by "hand" is power or blessing, and the lofty aim is to declare Allah transcendent. There are those who say that Allah has a hand but not like our hands, because we take every attribute of Allah as "There is nothing like unto Him," and interpretation is possible, just as the Truth explained: He made Musa "under My eyes."

Any matter concerning a description of Allah is taken either as it came, that He has a hand but not like hands, and He has existence not like human existence, and He has eyes not like eyes; and every description of Allah we take within the frame of "There is nothing like unto Him." Or we take the description by interpretation, meaning blessing or power. The Truth says: ﴿Rather, both His Hands are outspread﴾, and what is meant here is (blessing). He, glorified is He, did not suffice with replying that He has one hand that gives; no, He replies with something stronger than what is possible, for He gives with both His hands, and He said: ﴿He has completed His blessings upon you, apparent and hidden﴾ (part of verse 20, Surah Luqman).

He gives the apparent and gives the hidden. Beware of saying "that is the right hand and that is the left hand," because both hands of Allah are right. ﴿Rather, both His Hands are outspread; He spends as He wills﴾: that is, He, glorified is He, cannot be stingy, and even when He withholds, that is giving, bestowal and spending; because whoever transgresses through blessing may be led by transgression to affliction and evil end; therefore He, glorified is He, withdraws His blessing from him to give him security from deviating through the blessing. And so we find the true saying in Surah al-Fajr: ﴿As for man, when his Lord tests him and honours him and blesses him, he says, "My Lord has honoured me." (15) But when He tests him and restricts his provision, he says, "My Lord has humiliated me." (16)﴾ (Surah al-Fajr). The Truth replied after that with His saying: "No!" (kalla).

So giving here is not honour, and withholding is not humiliation. How can giving be a proof of honour when Allah may give you and you do not fulfil the right of the blessing? And how can withholding be a proof of humiliation when He has withheld you from a means of deviation? So He has given you by withholding at times; He has given you the more lasting thing, which is guidance. Thus His withholding is also giving.

﴿Rather, both His Hands are outspread; He spends as He wills﴾. People always look at Allah's giving through positive giving, and do not look at the giving of negation, that is withholding, which is that the Truth diverts from you an evil course. I have previously given the example of the man who seeks what is lawful in the source of his wealth, fears Allah in his work, takes his income, and runs the movement of his life within the frame of this income. This man may return to his home and find his son's temperature slightly raised, because his wealth is lawful and the particles of his body know that his wealth is lawful; so he receives the matter calmly, takes the son to a doctor in a charitable clinic for a few pennies, the doctor prescribes medicine for a few pennies, and the son is healed.

The state of this man differs from the state of another man who brought his wealth from unlawful gain (suht), and when he sees his son's temperature has risen, his mind turns among a thousand evil thoughts, and he takes his son around doctors and does not believe a single doctor.

The first man was granted by Allah tranquillity, by preventing the agitations of hastiness from his heart and thoughts; as for the second man, he spends many times what he ate of unlawful gain. So ﴿Rather, both His Hands are outspread﴾: that is, there is the giving of negation. The giving that man loves is the giving of wealth, and that is giving which goes to the perishable. As for withholding, it prevents a person from committing sins. Afterwards the person takes his bliss in the Hereafter. We find many people who supplicate, but they do not know that Allah has given by withholding.

The Truth, blessed and exalted is He, says: ﴿And man prays for evil as he prays for good, and man is ever hasty.﴾ (11, Surah al-Isra').

Therefore the Truth sometimes gives things that the servant had insisted upon, and afterwards the person realises that they were evil, as if the Truth, when He withheld from the person for a period, was preserving him.

﴿Rather, both His Hands are outspread; He spends as He wills﴾. Thus all of it is spending. He, glorified is He, spends as He wills, so He never withholds out of stinginess even when He withholds, for withholding in its proper place is itself spending. Thus is the giving of Allah: the giving of blessing, whether apparent or hidden. If by "hand" you mean power, then the two hands of Allah are outspread, with reward for some people and punishment for other people; and He, glorified and exalted is He, gives to His Excellency the Prophet (ﷺ) faith-based immunity against every rebel against him, or against every refuser and arrogant one among the disbelievers or the People of the Book.

As if He, glorified and exalted is He, is clarifying: prepare yourself, O Muhammad, and let your community prepare itself, that these disbelievers will not be content with a small and slight amount of hatred for you; rather, whenever a blessing of increased guidance comes to you from Allah, they will envy you, hate you, and their rebellion and rancour against you will increase, so prepare yourself for that. In this is a faith-based immunity that blocks every avenue of the whispering of the soul and makes the soul ready to receive whatever happens, even if it is among the disliked things.

Let us bring this matter closer to the mind. Not as a comparison, but merely to bring the matter closer to the mind, and to Allah belongs the highest similitude, let us look

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 5, verse 65:

And after that, the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted is He, says:

﴿And if the People of the Book had believed and been mindful of God, We would have removed from them their misdeeds and admitted them into Gardens of Bliss.﴾ (5:65)

This statement indicates that the People of the Book, all of them, are outside the enclosure of faith. The Truth clarifies for them: your corruption preceded the appearance of Islam, and for this reason Islam came to deliver people from your corruption. You had a method from God, but you distorted it; you had messengers whom God sent to you, but you mistreated them; and you invented religious rituals. Islam came not only to guide the atheists, but also to guide those whom the lords of the People of the Book had led astray. After Islam, they fought Islam through Orientalism (al-istishraq), and they wrote books to slander Islam. But they found that people were turning away from them, so they brought in those who praise Islam, and slip into the midst of the praise that which corrupts the creed of the Muslims.

We find some writings that speak of the greatness of Islam coming from the West, but they attempt to slander from a hidden door, such as saying: "Muhammad is a rare genius in the history of mankind," and they build the whole statement on the basis that what Muhammad brought is a matter of human genius, not a matter of messengerhood and prophethood. An example of this is a European man who writes writings about one hundred great figures in the world and places Muhammad (ﷺ) at the head of them all. We say to him: "Thank you. But why did you not believe in the message of Muhammad ibn Abdullah?"

Their testimony for us does not concern us in the slightest. They attacked us before, openly, and now they attempt to attack us covertly. They have taken some of the sons of the Islamic lands to raise them in the schools and universities of the West, so that they might make of these youths advocates of their causes in corrupting the Muslims, and they succeeded only with a few. Therefore we say to our youth: beware lest you be the corrupters while claiming to be the reformers. Do not take the matter by its outer varnish, but look into the depths of the issues, and remember the words of the Truth:

﴿Say: Shall We inform you of those who lose most in their deeds? Those whose effort is lost in the life of this world, while they think they are doing good work.﴾ (18:103–104)

We must watch over every corruption in the universe, and we will find that the fingers of the enemies of Islam have a clear effect. Such was the audacity of Zionism, to the point of impudence, that it said: "Let the people of God, the Chosen, be reassured: eighty percent of the media in the world is subject to our will, and nothing may be known in it except what we wish to be known." And the Truth, glory be to Him, when He says:

﴿And if the People of the Book had believed and been mindful of God, We would have removed from them their misdeeds and admitted them into Gardens of Bliss.﴾ (5:65)

So by this verse, glory be to Him and exalted is He, He offers an opportunity to these people to enter the enclosure of faith and seek forgiveness of God for their past sins, and to begin a good life in purity and clarity instead of distortion and misguidance. And that they may know with true knowledge His saying concerning His Messenger: ﴿And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds.﴾ (21:107)

This statement should be what non-Muslims rush toward along with Muslims, to draw from the spring of mercy, and in that is a comprehensive purification of creed that enables every human being to begin the path of reforming himself.

And His saying, the Truth: ﴿And if the People of the Book had believed and been mindful of God﴾ only calls them to faith and piety. Faith has its seat in the heart, meaning that belief in the existence of a Supreme God becomes settled in the heart, and that we believe in the communication from the Supreme God through the messengers, and that we believe in the messengers and in the methods they brought, and that we follow these methods, and that we believe that the return is to God. This faith is reflected in the believing movement on earth, and faith combined with piety achieves the orientation of the human being toward righteous action, and keeping away from what is not righteous action, in compliance with the words of the Truth:

﴿By time! Indeed, mankind is in loss, except those who have believed and done righteous deeds and enjoined one another to truth and enjoined one another to patience.﴾ (103:1–3)

For this reason we find a saying of one of the righteous scholars of the Arabs: "Faith is like the pillar, and deeds are like the ropes." He knew that every house has a foundation of pillars, and it has pegs that fix it. The Arab tent is a house of thick cloth on a wooden pole, and the tent is tied to the pegs with ropes, and these ropes are the ropes (atnab), and the tent does not stand unless it is tied with ropes and drawn to pegs. The Arab would take down this tent, carry it on the back of his camel to erect it in any place. And the Arab would choose the cloth which, if rain fell upon it, would absorb the water and prevent its falling inside the tent.

So faith is a pillar, and deeds are ropes. Thus is the call of the Truth to the People of the Book, that they believe and be mindful of God, so that He may remove from them their misdeeds. Covering (kufr), as we know, is concealment and veiling, and pardon (afw) is the erasing of the trace, as if the Truth would cover over their misdeeds and then erase their trace, by pardoning them; for Islam came only as a mercy, which must be exploited so that the Truth may remove from them the misdeeds by which they misled their peoples.

It was incumbent upon them to know that the coming of the Messenger (ﷺ) is an opportunity to retract from disbelief and calumny. He (ﷺ) came to establish a comprehensive purification of creed in the universe: the atheist must come to know the Creator of existence and believe in Him, and the one who alters the method of God must return to the method of God. This is the comprehensive purification of creed.

Al-Sha'rawi, Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66), on surah 5, verse 66:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿If they had truly established the Torah and the Gospel and what has been sent down to them from their Lord, they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet. Among them is a moderate community, but many of them—evil is what they do.﴾ (66)

That is, if they had applied the Torah and the Gospel without distortion, and had believed in the Qur'an, it would have been better for them. The Torah is the book of the Jews, and the Gospel is the book of 'Isa (peace be upon him). After them, God sent down the comprehensive and decisive Book, which is the Noble Qur'an. He willed for them the truth through belief in what came in the Torah and the Gospel of the glad tidings of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), because belief in the Torah and the Gospel—before their distortion—leads only to belief in Muhammad (ﷺ) and in what God sent down to him. The Jews—as we have known—are the ones who threatened the Arabs with the coming of the Messenger of God, but the Arabs preceded them in believing in Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah: ﴿And they had been seeking victory over those who disbelieved; but when there came to them what they recognised, they disbelieved in it﴾.

The People of the Book possessed the natural gateway to belief in the Qur'an, which is belief in the sound Torah and the sound Gospel, because in them is the description (na't) of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Our master 'Abd Allah ibn Salam, who was one of the rabbis of the Jews, used to say: "I recognised Muhammad when I saw him as I recognise my own son, and my recognition of Muhammad is even stronger." When the Truth promises the People of the Book that if they believe and are God-fearing He will expiate their evil deeds and admit them into the Gardens of Bliss, He—glory be to Him—will not merely expiate their evil deeds and protect them from the punishment of the Fire, but will erase these evil deeds and admit them into Paradise. He, glory be to Him, is the most knowing of them, and He knows that among them are the materialists bound to this world; therefore He brought them the good of faith in this world too, saying: ﴿If they had truly established the Torah and the Gospel and what has been sent down to them from their Lord, they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet.﴾ So He, glory be to Him, extends to them also the hand of means in this world, and the believer is the one who advances in taking the means, so he takes the bounties of this world and the Hereafter, whereas the disbeliever takes the means without thanking the Creator for them.

The Truth wished that the People of the Book would first be good by means of the sound Torah and the sound Gospel, so that this would be the natural gateway to belief in the Qur'an; this is the path to expiation of evil deeds, so that they do not enter the Fire but instead enter Paradise in the Hereafter. By believing, they take not only the good of the Hereafter but also the good of this world, because the Truth does not withhold from one who strives in the means, and He is the One who said: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We will increase him in his tilth; and whoever desires the tilth of this world, We will give him thereof, but he will have no share in the Hereafter.﴾ (30) (Surat ash-Shura).

As for whoever among them remains upon disbelief, he takes from the means of this world but never takes at all from the gift of the Hereafter: ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make it scattered dust.﴾ (23) (Surat al-Furqan).

Thus the Truth clarifies the fate of the people of disbelief in the Hereafter first, and then clarifies their fate in the immediate world. If they take the means, God gives them the results of the means; He is the One who keeps absolute power (qudrah). He may nullify the means and strip things of their properties. The farmer may take all the means: ploughing the land, fertilising it, and selecting the seed strains, yet a hurricane may come and uproot everything, or a flood may drown the crop, or a deadly insect such as the cotton worm may devour the harvest. Therefore, behind the means is a Causer who possesses absolute power, and He, glory be to Him, is the One who set the cosmic laws, and He is also the One who strips them of their properties.

You, O human, are the master of the cosmos by the will of God, yet you are subjugated in many decrees to the compelling force of the Almighty (al-Jabbar). It is true that you have some choices in some matters, but there are compulsions in matters over which you have no control: illness may kill, and a sudden accident may kill, and these are among the compulsions of God that take a person out of the means.

The Truth, glory be to Him, shows us that our land was once constantly rained upon, then drought struck it. Why? Because people become deluded by the monotony of blessing. Therefore the Truth holds the cosmos in His hand, and He, glory be to Him, never hands it over to anyone at all. So He comes in some occurrences and withdraws His means, lest man be tempted by the means and their monotony.

Examples of this in our lives are many. We see a farmer who owns tens of feddans, and the worm attacks him and leaves nothing green or dry, while his neighbour who owns only a small, meagre piece of land yields all its good to its owner, because he paid what the people of the countryside call *ghafrat al-ard* (the "forgiveness of the land"), that is, its zakah. In this case the worm is one of the soldiers of the Truth: it devours the unlawful wealth and does not touch the lawful wealth.

﴿And none knows the soldiers of your Lord but He﴾ (part of verse 31, Surat al-Muddaththir).

Therefore the Truth offers His means to whoever strives in them, and He increases the believer. He says: ﴿If they had truly established the Torah and the Gospel and what has been sent down to them from their Lord, they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet.﴾ Sustenance, as we have learned, is of two kinds: a direct kind and a kind that brings the direct sustenance. The direct sustenance is what we benefit from immediately, such as food we eat or water we drink; the other is the wealth with which we may buy the direct sustenance. He, glory be to Him, has brought in matters of actual life so that we understand that the method was sent down to organise human movement in this life, while the Hereafter is the recompense for good action in this world.

After He promised them Paradise as a reward for faith, He extends to them the means in this world: ease, abundance, luxury, and happiness. Someone may ask: "How could they eat from above them?" We say: eating is the fundamental manifestation of human life, because every movement a person makes is a branch of the existence of his life. The existence of human life depends on three important elements: eating, drinking, and breathing. If we wish to preserve life and procreation, these three sources must be provided.

When we look at the ranking of these three in importance, we find that a person may endure without food for a month, and may endure without water for a period ranging from three to ten days, but as for breathing, a person cannot bear to be without air for even a few minutes.

It is among the mercy of the Truth toward creation that He made the possession of these kinds, which sustain life, arranged according to their importance. Thus we see someone who controls another person's food and dominates him, but the Truth has placed in the human body what may sustain him for a month. We find that possession of water is less than possession of food; therefore the Truth has granted ownership of it only rarely, because a person cannot endure thirst except for a period ranging from three to ten days. As for air, the Truth has not made it the property of anyone at all, because a person cannot do without it except for the duration of inhalation and exhalation, and a person cannot store it in the size of his lungs; therefore the Truth did not entrust any of creation with ownership of air.

His saying, the Truth: ﴿they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet﴾ means that steadfastness in applying God's method subjects the cosmic means to them. But if a person rebels against God's method, God may give him the flower of the worldly life and then seize him with the seizure of the Mighty, the Capable, for the cosmic laws have not been severed from the hand of the Truth.

Therefore He, glory be to Him, addresses creation with an address, and if they respond to the address, He eases for them everything He subjected to them in the cosmos. If they do not respond, He holds the means and can break their laws; neither the earth nor the air nor anything else departs from obedience to God. If a group rebels against the blessings of God or against God Himself, He makes them an example for others and withholds the means from them.

Man is the master of these creatures in this cosmos, and he is also affected by the power of his Lord: he may fall ill, he may die, he may break, he may drown. If man, who is affected by "Be" (kun) from his Lord, is like this, what of the things lower than him? They too are submissive to "Be." The Truth is able to say to the earth: "Become barren," and He is able to stop the rain, because He, glory be to Him, is the One who makes things move in a regular motion. Did not the Truth, glory be to Him, say in His address to all His creatures concerning the earth: ﴿For your Lord has inspired her﴾? If the Truth has inspired the earth to bring forth its treasures or to quake, what of everything else? Indeed everything moves by God's command, for everything glorifies God's praise, but man does not comprehend the languages of other creatures: ﴿But you do not understand their glorification﴾.

The address of God to each of His creatures is understood by whatever is affected by it, of any kind of existence. Had God taught you this being-affected, you would have heard the language of the other creatures. An example of this is our master Sulayman (peace be upon him), who heard the saying of an ant to the rest of the ants:

﴿Enter your dwellings, lest Sulayman and his soldiers crush you﴾ (part of verse 18, Surat an-Naml). And what did Sulayman say after that? Sulayman said: ﴿My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your blessing which You have bestowed upon me﴾ (part of verse 19, Surat an-Naml).

He, glory be to Him, also says: ﴿We subjected the mountains to glorify with David, and the birds﴾ (part of verse 79, Surat al-Anbiya').

And the hoopoe said in the Qur'an: ﴿Why do they not prostrate to God, who brings forth what is hidden in the heavens and the earth?﴾ (part of verse 25, Surat an-Naml).

So every creature in existence knows the matter of faith and the matter of tawhid. Everything in existence is affected by its Lord. Likewise all the things that preserve human life or his kind. Then what of the condition of one who rebels against God? He, glory be to Him, may say to the means: "Withdraw from him." We see this in the condition of some lands in various forms: the lands situated in a region known for constant rain, God breaks the nature of the environment so that it becomes drought; and other lands that are able to reach outer space cannot withstand a hurricane. This is so that it becomes certain to us that the hand of the Creator, glory be to Him, is above the means of the cosmos.
