Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, says: ﴿If they had truly established the Torah and the Gospel and what has been sent down to them from their Lord, they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet﴾, meaning that good would come from every direction. If by eating is meant direct eating, then rain is what descends from above, watering the earth so that crops come forth; likewise the date palm rises high and brings us dates, and so do fruit trees such as orange and apple and others. As for what is beneath the feet, these are the vegetables and the fruits that grow without any of them having a stalk above the ground, such as watermelon and melon and others.

In the falling of fruit from its high trees once fully ripe there is profound wisdom: the sustenance that has ripened, even if you do not strive for it, comes to you beneath your foot.

If we broaden our understanding of the Truth's saying ﴿they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet﴾, then God has secrets upon secrets, and He has secrets in what lies beneath the earth. Do we not take everything that helps us live from the nature of the earth, whether it is iron, copper, or petroleum? Thus we find that everything in existence that serves the survival of the human species or the preservation of its life is a gift from God.

So if the People of the Book had established the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an and walked the method, God would have bestowed upon them every good. The Truth confirms this meaning in another verse, saying: ﴿And if the people of the towns had believed and been God-fearing, We would have opened upon them blessings from heaven and earth﴾.

We see that the Truth has bestowed upon some people a great and abundant share of blessing, and then its people become arrogant with the blessing, so our Lord gives them respite until their affair rises, then seizes them with the seizure of the Mighty, the Capable. Our contemporary life is the best witness to this: every country that took God's blessing to argue with God and to stand against God's method, you find it reaping corruption, the might of its people turns harsh among themselves, and they ruin their homes with their own hands. How many countries once were the delight of people who went there for luxury or licentiousness, and then the violence of its own people broke out among them and it was ruined by the hands of its sons. In the reality of the cosmos there is what confirms the truth of this, as though the Truth says to us: ﴿So take warning, O you with insight﴾.

And he says:

Then the Truth says, after that: ﴿O Messenger, deliver what has been sent down to you from your Lord. And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And Allah will protect you from the people. Indeed, Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.﴾ (67)

The verse begins with an address to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Among the greatness of our chosen Messenger, may the prayers and peace of Allah be upon him, and the exaltedness of his station with the One who chose him as the seal of His messengers on earth, is that Allah mentions the messengers in His address to them by calling them by their names only, as in His saying, the Truth: ﴿O Adam, inform them of their names﴾ (part of verse 33, Surat al-Baqarah).

Or His saying, the Truth: ﴿O Musa, indeed I am Allah﴾ (part of verse 30, Surat al-Qasas).

Or His saying, the Truth: ﴿O Isa, son of Maryam, did you say to the people﴾ (part of verse 116, Surat al-Ma'idah).

Or His saying, the Truth: ﴿O Nuh, descend in peace﴾ (part of verse 48, Surat Hud).

So He, glorified is He, calls each messenger by the name that identifies the essence, regardless of any attribute. But the Messenger of Allah was never called by his name; rather, the Truth addressed him with a designation that identifies by attribute: ﴿O Messenger﴾. Or His saying, the Truth: ﴿O Prophet﴾.

As if, O Messenger of Allah, all the matters of prophethood have been gathered in you, because you are the bearer of the religion at which the world will end, and there will be after that no message of God on earth except that which Allah grants to someone in the Book of Allah.

And among the greatness of the Messenger (ﷺ) is that Allah swore by his life, although the Truth does not swear by the life of any human being except His Messenger; He swore by his life. He, glorified is He, swears by whatever He wills concerning whatever He wills. He swore by the wind, the forenoon, the night, and the angels, but He never swore by the life of any human except the life of Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿By your life, indeed they are in their intoxication, wandering blindly﴾ (Surat al-Hijr, 72).

That is: by your life, O Muhammad, they are in their intoxication, wandering in bewilderment. The Truth here addresses the Messenger: ﴿O Messenger﴾. And since Muhammad is the final Messenger who came confirming what was before him of the scriptures, this means that every good found in any scripture preceding the Qur'an is present in the Qur'an, and it also contains additional provisions required by the emerging interests of life. And since the address is to the Messenger, this means that he is a messenger sent by Allah with a methodology for His creation, to convey it to them: ﴿Deliver what has been sent down to you from your Lord﴾. And how does the Truth say to His Messenger "deliver" when He knows that the Messenger's task is conveyance?

He, glorified is He, intended by that to inform people that if he conveys to them what some of them dislike, he conveys it in obedience to the command of Allah; he does not speak from himself. The Messenger is obligated to convey, and if he conveys to someone something that troubles them, he has no personal interest in it. He, glorified is He, states this so that when the Messenger conveys a ruling, they must receive the ruling on the basis that it comes from Allah. He, glorified is He, knows that His Messenger does not conceal the message, but so that the Messenger may have an excuse before humanity. When He addresses them with something they may dislike, it is a message from Allah: ﴿O Messenger, deliver what has been sent down to you from your Lord, and if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message.﴾ That is, if he does not do so, even in a small part of the methodology, this means the conveyance is incomplete, and Allah wants the conveyance to be complete with the complete religion.

The structure of faith requires that the statement come in this manner so that the conveyance is fully coherent. The methodology was sent down in its entirety, and it must be applied in its entirety so that the universe is set right and so that the movement of man in the universe is not corrupted. He, glorified is He, sent down the methodology and perfected it so that the world proceeds according to His design without disruption. Therefore the Truth says: ﴿If you do not, then you have not conveyed His message.﴾ Thereby He gives His Messenger complete immunity. The message of Muhammad (ﷺ) was not brought except for the good of people.

Allah had already created Adam and given him the methodology. It was incumbent upon Adam to convey the methodology to his offspring, and he did. But some generations of the children of Adam became heedless of the methodology; so the Truth sends messengers to remind them of the methodology. No messenger comes except after corruption has spread and proliferated among people. Allah has placed in the human soul a self that blames (al-nafs al-lawwamah), a self that commands evil (al-nafs al-ammarah bi'l-su'), and a self at peace (al-nafs al-mutma'innah).

The task of the self that blames is to respond to everything the self that commands evil whispers. But if the self that blames does not blame, the self that commands evil persists, and no restrainer restrains it. As for the self at peace, it is the self that finds tranquility in the methodology of Allah. An example of this is a person whose desire presses him to commit some sin, so he commits it; afterward he regrets, blames himself, and repents of the sin. This person restrains himself by himself. But if the self that commands evil prevails, there is no restrainer.

And what if corruption dominates among the general population? And what if they do not forbid one another from the wrong they commit? Here the Truth must send a messenger with a new miracle to lead the world to the logic of guidance and the methodology of truth.

The Truth chooses a messenger only when the messenger knows that he is conveying from Allah. And He, glorified is He, in the verse under discussion, gives His Messenger an excuse if he conveys to his people something that displeases them; the Messenger's only duty is conveyance, in His saying: ﴿If you do not, then you have not conveyed His message.﴾ We know that the notion of a message entails: the sender, who is Allah; the recipients, who are the creation; the messenger, who is the Prophet (ﷺ); and the thing sent, which is what was sent down to the Messenger to convey. In every such matter we find that the verb "arsala" (to send) takes two objects: the sent (al-mursal), as in "I sent so-and-so to so-and-so," and the one to whom it is sent (al-mursal ilayhi), who is so-and-so. So here there are two objects: the first is one to which the verb reaches directly, and the other is one to which the verb reaches by a preposition.

The preposition here is "ila" (to). Naturally, the Messenger knows that he is sent to people by Allah for the sake of their interests; there is nothing in the matter of the message that benefits Allah. If you see the verb transitive with "ila," it is to specify the end to which one is sent, as in the saying of the Truth: ﴿and a messenger to the Children of Israel﴾ (part of verse 49, Surat Ali 'Imran).

This shows that Isa (peace be upon him) came sent with a methodology to the Children of Israel for the benefit of the Children of Israel. Likewise the Truth says: ﴿And We sent to the people a messenger﴾, that is, for the benefit of the people. And the "lam" here conveys both meanings: benefit and purpose.

﴿Deliver what has been sent down to you from your Lord, and if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message﴾: that is, if he, may the peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, does not convey the message in its entirety, this means the conveyance is deficient. Far be it from Allah that the conveyance of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) should have left anything incomplete, for the methodology of Allah is wholly complete.

Someone may say: but people do perform the obligations of Allah at their appointed times, and the example of that is the prayer. We say: this is a failure in people's management of their lives according to the methodology of Allah. It is the duty of societies to organize people's daily movement from after the dawn prayer until noon. In that there is an immense amount of vitality and energy, and work ends at noon, so people's movement does not collide with the methodology of Allah, and there is no obstruction or discord in their movement.

Then the Truth says: ﴿And Allah will protect you from the people.﴾ This wise statement had to come, because we know that the Messenger does not come except after evil has become widespread and corruption has prevailed. For if corruption had not prevailed and evil had not become general, Allah would have been content with society restraining its own parts, or the Truth would have been content with the self that blames restraining the self that commands evil, so that the self at peace would be established on the throne of human conduct.

But when corruption engulfs the universe, the heavens send a messenger with a methodology that reforms the condition of humanity. Naturally, the corrupt society will not leave the Messenger alone but will oppose him, because such a society wants the balance of the universe to be unequal, since there are those who profit from corruption and evil, and they are the defenders of corruption. So if someone comes who stands up for the weak and the oppressed, he must face the hardships that come from the powerful corrupters.

These hardships begin first in the self. Because the Messenger is addressed by Allah, he is able to bear them, for the Truth has prepared him for this task. Similar hardships also come to the followers, so Allah reinforces them with the support that enables them to bear them. And the Truth preserves the Messenger's own person despite everything that happens: ﴿And Allah will protect you from the people.﴾

It is as if the Truth says to His Messenger: be at ease, O Muhammad, for the One who sent you as guidance for people will not leave you to the people. No one will dare end your life. Rather, I will grant you life until you complete your message. Beware lest it enter your mind that people have power over you. True, you may suffer, and you may experience the symptoms of fatigue during the call, but there is a divine protection for you. We know the extent of the hardships the Messenger (ﷺ) endured. Was his front tooth (rubaiyyah)(1) not broken, peace and blessings be upon him, at the Battle of Uhud? Was his face not wounded? Was his finger not bled, so that he said: "You are only a finger that has bled, and in the way of Allah you have suffered what you have suffered"(2)?

But the Truth's saying to His Messenger: ﴿And Allah will protect you from the people﴾ did not mean prevention of jihad in the way of Allah and of the hardship in spreading the call. Rather, the Truth clarifies to His Messenger that no one is able to take your life.

Nor did He, glorified is He, withhold hardships from His noble Messenger so that there would be no caller to Allah who bears less pain than His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him. Let us listen carefully to what 'A'ishah, the Mother of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with her, narrates about this verse. She said:

"The Messenger of Allah stayed awake one night while I was beside him. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what is the matter with you?' He said: 'I wish a man from my companions would guard me tonight.' She said: While we were in that state, we heard the sound of weapons. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Who is this?' They said: 'Sa'd and Hudhayfah; we have come to guard you.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then slept until I heard his snoring, and this verse was revealed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out of his tent of leather and said: 'Disperse, O people, for Allah has protected me.'"(3)

There is a Belgian researcher who devoted herself to studying the biography of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) until she reached this point, and she paused there to say: "If this man were deceiving all people, he would not have deceived himself in his life; and if he were not certain that Allah guards him, he would not have done that as a real experiment demonstrating his trust in his Creator." The Belgian researcher added: "Therefore I say with full certainty: 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.'" The woman embraced Islam merely from standing before one glimpse of the life of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Then the Truth says: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.﴾ We know that guidance means the indication that leads to the goal, and it is also the aid that brings the seeker of guidance to the goal. The disbelievers were plotting against the Messenger and exhausting themselves in scheming, planning, and conspiring, and the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, cuts off every path for them and grants victory over them. The practical application of Allah's victory for the believers came at Badr: 

﴿How many a small company has overcome a large company by the permission of Allah﴾ (part of verse 249, Surat al-Baqarah).

They plotted, but at the confrontation they could not overcome Muhammad (ﷺ) and his companions, nor were they able to harm him, despite their deceit and scheming; for the Truth cut off every path for them to harm Muhammad. No means of treachery and wickedness will be able to kill the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). This was embodied on the day the Messenger of Allah went out as a migrant, and Allah covered the eyes of the young men of the tribes who carried their swords to kill Muhammad and to spill his blood among the tribes, so they did not see him, for Allah had placed a veil over their sight.

Thus, whenever they thought of a way, Allah blocked for them the avenues for carrying out their plan. It is as if He says to them: you will not be able to oppose Muhammad in his methodology, neither openly nor secretly.

1 Rubaiyyah: the tooth between the incisor and the canine.
2 Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah.
3 Narrated by al-Qurtubi; Muslim narrated: she said — i.e., 'A'ishah — "While we were like that, we heard the rattling of weapons (i.e., its sound), so he said: 'What is this?' It was Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, and the Messenger of Allah said to him: 'What brought you?' He said: 'Fear for the Messenger of Allah came into my heart, so I came to guard him.' The Messenger of Allah prayed for him, then slept."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 5, verse 68:

And the Truth (al-Haqq) says after that:

﴿Say, "O People of the Scripture, you are not upon anything until you uphold the Torah and the Gospel and what has been revealed to you from your Lord." And that which has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in rebellion and disbelief. So do not grieve over the disbelieving people.﴾ (68)

"Say" (qul), as we know, is an address to him, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family, and what follows it is a communication from Allah to the People of the Scripture: that they have no methodology (manhaj), because they do not uphold the Torah and the Gospel; rather, they have distorted them, and they have not believed in the Qur'an, which is the complete methodology revealed to Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah.

When the Truth says, ﴿you are not upon anything﴾, the word "anything" (shay') is used for the least individual of any kind. A straw is a "shay'," and a leaf of a tree is a "shay'." Thus, what is called "shay'" is the least.

And the saying of the Truth, ﴿you are not upon anything﴾, means: beware lest you think that when you carry out a part of the teachings of the Torah and the Gospel while concealing and neglecting the rest, you have taken some of the guidance. No; you are not upon anything until you uphold the Torah and the Gospel and believe in the Book that was revealed to Muhammad. The methodology is not something from which you take what pleases you and leave what does not please you.

When it is said, ﴿you are not upon anything﴾, we know that "shay'" is the lowest rank of existence, and therefore we say: "a thing is better than nothing" (shay' khayr min la shay'). And it is said colloquially: "hash khayr min la sh" — and "hash" is the worn-out, torn household clothing; that is, one who owns torn clothes is better than one who owns nothing at all.

And the saying of the Truth, ﴿you are not upon anything until you uphold the Torah and the Gospel and what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾, is a clarification to them that they are in the lowest rank of created beings, because they have no methodology. He adds: ﴿And that which has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in rebellion and disbelief﴾, meaning that they will not remain at one fixed degree of rebellion and disbelief; rather, whenever Allah sends down a verse to you, O Muhammad, and whenever Allah grants you victory in a matter, they increase in rebellion and disbelief. It was expected that the increase in the revelation of verses to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family, would weaken their obstinacy and soften their hearts, but He, glory be to Him, willed that their ferocity and resentment in the matter of acknowledging Islam should intensify.

It happened that Khalid ibn al-Walid, who was the knight of the Jahiliyyah against Islam, said to 'Amr ibn al-'As: "The matter has settled for Muhammad." And the two of them turned toward Islam, although each of them knew his strength and his standing among his people. After Khalid and 'Amr saw that defeat is the lot of whoever stands against Muhammad, however high his station, they went to Islam. This is the stance of one who reflects upon the matter without resentment and contention. As for one who is filled with suffering, resentment and contention, the signs of Allah, supporting His methodology, increase him in resentment, contention and rebellion, because Allah willed that they not be guided. Therefore every verse in the ranks of faith and the believers becomes a source of agitation, rage and bitterness in the souls of the disbelievers. Thus the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family, prepares his resolve toward these disbelievers.

Indeed, O Messenger of Allah, you do not face a limited power, but you face a power of growing evil. Every verse guides the one who has within his depths a seed of good; as for the one from whom good has been stripped away within, the matter only increases his ferocity in his heart. The wicked one ascends in evil and his crime and sin increase, whereas good descends from the summit of crime to the lowest degree. We have the example in the story of our master Yusuf, peace be upon him, where the Truth says on the tongue of the brothers of Yusuf:

﴿Joseph and his brother are more beloved to our father than we, although we are a group. Indeed, our father is in manifest error.﴾ (Part of verse 8, Surah Yusuf)

And after that they said to their father: ﴿What is [the matter] with you that you do not entrust us with Joseph?﴾ Then they began plotting and devising, and they said: ﴿Send him with us tomorrow; he will frolic and play.﴾ And the first of their schemes was what the Truth related about them: ﴿Kill Joseph.﴾

The meaning of killing is the taking of life, and this is the highest degree of evil, yet they retreat from it and say: ﴿Or cast him to some land.﴾ They did not desire to kill him; they were content to leave him in a distant place, and they imagined that some caravan might pick him up, thereby removing Joseph from his father. So they began their scheme with killing, then ended their thinking with the salvation of Joseph:

﴿Kill Joseph or cast him to some land, and the face of your father will be clear for you.﴾ (Part of verse 9, Surah Yusuf)

The third stage is their saying: ﴿Throw him into the depths of the well.﴾ The well contains water, and there are many people who go to water sources. Thus the Truth shows us how good grows from within deceit.

So, the saying of the Truth: ﴿And that which has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in rebellion and disbelief﴾ means that the majority of them will continue the journey of escalation in evil, so prepare yourself, O Muhammad, for that.

We notice that the Truth has placed a safeguard against the possibility that a few of them might think of faith, so He did not include all of them in the judgment, but the judgment covered the majority of these disbelievers. Therefore the Truth says to His Messenger: ﴿So do not grieve over the disbelieving people﴾, meaning: do not grieve over them, O Messenger of Allah. Despite the enmity and ferocity of those who confronted his call, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family, and their attempts at every such effort, he did not cease to pray for them: "O Allah, guide my people, for they do not know,"(1) and he did not cease to say: "Perhaps Allah will bring forth from their loins someone who worships Allah,"(2) and that indeed came to pass.

After the early battles, the Companions would say to one another: "I am grieved that 'Amr escaped me and I did not kill him." The other would say: "And I am grieved that 'Ikrimah escaped me." The third would say: "And I do not know how Khalid ibn al-Walid escaped us." The Truth did not enable the early Companions over these fierce fighters, because He was reserving them for Islam; so the non-enabling of the Muslims over them was an enabling of Islam, so that they would bear the sword for Islam, defending it and spreading its call. Here is 'Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl receiving the last blow of his life, laying his head on the thigh of Khalid ibn al-Walid and asking him: "Is this a death that will please the Messenger of Allah for me?" Thus Allah willed that the Muslims not be enabled over them in the early battles so that they would become soldiers of Islam by their combat abilities, and He preserved them alive to serve the call.

(1) Recorded by al-Zabidi in Ithaf al-Sada al-Muttaqin, and by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur.
(2) Narrated by al-Bukhari in Bad' al-Khalq, and Muslim in al-Jihad.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on surah 5, verse 69

Then the Truth (Allah) says, after that:

﴿Indeed, those who believed, and those who were Jews, and the Sabeans, and the Christians — whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day and does righteous deeds — no fear shall there be for them, nor shall they grieve.﴾ (5:69)

So they are four categories of those who did not believe in the message of the Messenger of Allah. This verse has come in its general form three times: once in Surat al-Baqarah, once here in Surat al-Ma'idah, and once in Surat al-Hajj.

In Surat al-Baqarah the Truth says: ﴿Indeed, those who believed, and those who were Jews, and the Christians, and the Sabeans — whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day and does righteous deeds — for them is their reward with their Lord, and no fear shall there be for them, nor shall they grieve.﴾ (2:62)

Let us note that the word (al-Sabi'in) in this verse is in the accusative case.

In Surat al-Ma'idah we find the Truth's words: ﴿Indeed, those who believed, and those who were Jews, and the Sabeans, and the Christians — whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day and does righteous deeds — no fear shall there be for them, nor shall they grieve.﴾ (5:69)

Let us note that the word (al-Sabi'un) here is in the nominative case and is placed before (al-Nasara).

In Surat al-Hajj the Truth says: ﴿Indeed, those who believed, and those who were Jews, and the Sabeans, and the Christians, and the Magians, and those who associated partners [with Allah] — Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, Allah is over all things Witness.﴾ (22:17)

Here there is information about four groups, and the Truth added two more in the verse of al-Hajj. We find that the information differs, and likewise the style differs: sometimes the Christians precede the Sabeans, and sometimes the Sabeans precede the Christians. Sometimes the Sabeans are in the nominative, and sometimes in the accusative with the ya'.

As for the difference in the predicate: He, glory be to Him, informs us in Surat al-Baqarah, saying:

﴿whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day and does righteous deeds — for them is their reward with their Lord, and no fear shall there be for them, nor shall they grieve﴾

(part of verse 62, Surat al-Baqarah)

The predicate in Surat al-Ma'idah is: ﴿whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day and does righteous deeds — no fear shall there be for them, nor shall they grieve﴾ (part of verse 69, Surat al-Ma'idah).

The predicate in Surat al-Hajj is: ﴿Indeed, Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, Allah is over all things Witness﴾ (part of verse 17, Surat al-Hajj).

The three verses together address one meaning, but the styles differ and so do the purposes within them.

Here we note that the Truth said (āmanū, "believed"), and the belief here is verbal belief, that is, with the mouth and not with the heart. Those who are described by it are the hypocrites. Those who were Jews (alladhīna hādū) are the followers of Musa (Moses), and the Christians are the followers of Isa (Jesus). The Sabeans (al-Sabi'un) were not followers of any one prophet: they were followers of Nuh (Noah), then they turned away (sabi'ū) from the religion of Nuh and worshipped the stars. Or they are a people who deviated from Judaism and Christianity and worshipped the angels, and the Magians, who are the worshippers of fire. Thus the Truth wishes to carry out a faith-based purification in the cosmos: whoever hastens and enters this purification and is saved from the evil of what he did before the coming of Islam. For they misled people or ruled with injustice.

In Surat al-Baqarah the Truth says: ﴿for them is their reward with their Lord﴾, meaning that He, glory be to Him, forgave them what evil they did and rewarded them for their righteous deeds, which they did not nullify by going on with evil deeds and sins. This is what relates to the two verses: the verse of Surat al-Baqarah and the verse of Surat al-Ma'idah. We note that the verse of Surat al-Ma'idah does not include the phrase ﴿for them is their reward with their Lord﴾; perhaps that is because it was sufficient to mention it in Surat al-Baqarah, and there is a parallel to this in the Noble Qur'an, such as carrying the unrestricted (mutlaq) upon the restricted (muqayyad), and the like.

As for the verse of Surat al-Hajj, it is the one in which the judgement comes: ﴿Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection﴾, as if they will never believe nor do righteous deeds, and this is the doctrinal purification in the cosmos.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to purify the matter of faith on earth, and [the verse] speaks of those who believe with their tongues, who are the hypocrites: ﴿Indeed, those who believed﴾, which is the beginning of the predicate, and in it ﴿those who believed﴾ is in the accusative position because it is the subject of (inna), as the grammarians say. And He, glory be to Him, said here: and (al-Sabi'un), which is conjoined to an accusative. This is a breaking of the i'rab (grammatical case). The i'rab requires that the word be in the accusative, so it would be (al-Sabi'in). Why, then, did the Truth depart from revealing the word according to its grammatical context and reveal it with a breaking of the i'rab, although in another verse He said: ﴿Indeed, those who believed, and those who were Jews, and the Christians, and the Sabeans﴾?

It came here in its place without breaking the i'rab; it came once before the word (al-Nasara) and once after the word (al-Nasara). Here we must recognise the chronology of the Sabeans: they were a people who came before the coming of Christianity. If we wish to know their time, we find that the true word places them before the Christians; and if we wish to know their rank, we read it in another place in the Qur'an and find them coming after (al-Nasara). So when the Truth dated their time, He placed them first, and when He dated their number, their quantity and their amount, He placed them after the Christians, because they are fewer in number and do not represent a large multitude like the Christians.

The Truth brought the word once in the accusative and once in the nominative, so that we would know and turn our attention to them. The breaking of the i'rab was for the sake of drawing attention. The Sabeans were a people who worshipped the stars and the angels, and this is a kind of misguidance.

So there are the Jews, who recognised that there is a God, and Musa (peace be upon him) came as His messenger; and there are the Christians, who recognised that there is a God, and Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) came as His messenger; and there are the hypocrites, who professed faith with their tongues but faith did not touch their hearts.

The Truth wished to draw our attention to the fact that the Sabeans are a people who went out of the circle of submission to the existence of an unseen Creator God, and the Truth tells us that He forgives them if they believe and do righteous deeds. Faith in Allah is a basic condition for the acceptance of righteous deeds and for being rewarded for them. He placed them before the Christians out of caution and precaution against the suspicion that He would not pardon them if they believed and did righteous deeds.

We note that they also came in a context in which Allah gathers them together with those who worship other things besides Allah, because whoever attributes divinity to other than Allah is like one who worships the stars and has gone out from monotheism.

He, glory be to Him and exalted, allows every human being to enter the enclosure of faith and to make a doctrinal purification in which all enter into the expanse of faith and cut off their ties to association (shirk). So if the hypocrites, the Jews, the Christians and the Sabeans believe and do righteous deeds, then for them is the reward and recompense from Allah, and no fear shall there be for them from the punishment of the Hereafter, nor shall they grieve over what they missed of the world. The righteous deed came after faith, because faith, if it is not accompanied by righteous deeds, becomes exposed to being stripped away, and Allah forbid, and there is no benefit in it. He, glory be to Him, wishes that faith should govern the movement of life through righteous deeds, so He commands every believer to do righteous deeds, so that for them is their reward with their Lord, and no fear shall there be for them, nor shall they grieve.

As for those who persist in their disbelieving stance, Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection, for He is over all things Witness. The word (yafsilu, "will judge/separate") shows us that He, glory be to Him and exalted, will issue the ruling that makes clear who has the right from others. We know that one who judges only judges on evidence (bayyina). The evidence is confession, and confession, in the language of law, is the "lord of proofs." Or judgement by witnesses, or judgement by oath. He, glory be to Him, separates between the different positions. Separation is the rendering of a verdict. And when the One who judges is the One who witnessed, He is the Just. Therefore the Truth said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is over all things Witness﴾.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 5, verse 70:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says: ﴿Indeed, We took the covenant of the Children of Israel and sent to them messengers. Every time a messenger came to them with what their souls did not desire, a group they denied, and a group they killed.﴾

The mithaq (covenant) is a confirmed, solemn pact that demands strict fulfilment. Covenants are only secured because there is a fear of breach. Covenants in belief in God are many. There is the first covenant, when we were all in the loins of our fathers:

﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, and made them testify concerning themselves, "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we testify."﴾

(Part of verse 172, surah al-A'raf)

Or the covenant that God took for the support of the Messenger of God (ﷺ):

﴿And when God took the covenant of the prophets: "Whatever I have given you of Scripture and wisdom and then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and support him." He said, "Do you affirm and accept My commitment on that condition?" They said, "We affirm." He said, "Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses."﴾ (81)

(Surah Al 'Imran). Or the particular covenant taken from every nation. In every detail of religion a covenant is taken, and so in Islam many covenants are taken from us. Likewise, we see the Prophet (ﷺ) took a covenant for himself at al-'Aqabah. The Messenger saw that what bound him to the Aws and the Khazraj was great, as it binds him to every people who yearn for unity under the banner of one faith. The Jews regarded the Arabs of the Aws and the Khazraj as mere barbarians and servants who worked for them, and they judged sovereignty to be theirs. Whenever they disagreed with them, they threatened them with the coming of a messenger whom they would believe in and by whom they would kill them with slaughter.

Each of the Aws and the Khazraj tried to win the Jews to its side: the Aws allied with Banu Qurayza, and the Khazraj allied with Banu Qaynuqa' and Banu al-Nadir. Both received the Jews' threats after the appearance of the coming Prophet, and this made each of the Aws and the Khazraj hasten to become acquainted with the Messenger of God (ﷺ). In the season of the Hajj there came a group of six men, and the Prophet (ﷺ) invited them to Islam, and they believed in him (ﷺ) and said: "We have left our people, and no people have among them enmity and evil as they have. Perhaps God will unite them through you, and we will go to them and call them to your cause and present to them this religion which we have accepted from you. If God unites them upon you, there will be no man mightier than you."

They came the following year to the season of the Hajj, and they increased until they became twelve men. The pact was that none of them would associate anything with God, would not steal, would not commit adultery, would not kill their children, would not bring a slander they had fabricated between their hands and feet, and would not disobey the Messenger of God in what is right. They returned to Medina with them Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr, who taught them the Qur'an. In the third year there came seventy-three men and two women, Nusayba bint Ka'b, Umm 'Umara, and Asma' bint 'Amr ibn 'Adi. Their pledge of allegiance to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) took place, and the confusion of the Quraysh increased this. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to them:

("I pledge to you that you protect me as you protect your women and your children.") Al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur took his hand and then said: "Yes, by the One who sent you with the truth as a prophet, we will protect you as we protect our waists. So pledge to us, O Messenger of God, for by God we are the sons of war and the people of the armour (weapons)." Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihan spoke and said: "O Messenger of God, between us and the men there are ties, and we will cut them—meaning the Jews. Would you perhaps, if we do that and then God makes you victorious, return to your people and leave us?" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) smiled and then said: ("Rather, blood for blood, and destruction for destruction. I am of you and you are of me. I fight whom you fight and make peace with whom you make peace.") He (ﷺ) extended his hand and they pledged allegiance to him. The Pledge of al-'Aqabah was a covenant guaranteeing the people of the pledge Paradise if they fulfilled it. And they fulfilled it. This is a kind of covenant and pact. When the Truth informs us here that He took the covenant from the Children of Israel, this means there is a solemn, confirmed pact.

﴿Indeed, We took the covenant of the Children of Israel and sent to them messengers﴾ (surah al-Ma'ida).

The Truth took the covenant and sent messengers with the method, but whenever a messenger came to them, they deliberated: is the method that he brought according to their desires or not? If the method was not according to their desires, they killed the messenger or denied him, although the covenant is a confirmed pact to follow the messenger if he comes with a miracle and a method that conveys the message from God and implements it in the movement of life.

But the Children of Israel used to rebel against the methods of the messengers because they do not bring what their souls desire, and the first step of rebellion is denial. It is the first step on the path of breaching the covenant. They did not suffice with denial, but tried to besiege the Messenger so that the method would not reach ears that could be guided by it. Therefore they do not suffice with denial; they may even kill the messenger because he brought what their souls do not desire.

What is hawa (desire)? It is from the root (ha', waw, and the alif maqsura, which is written as ya'), and we find it pronounced sometimes hawa and sometimes hawa'. And hawa with a damma on the ha', a kasra on the waw, and a shadda on the ya', and all of these indicate penetration and inclination. Hawa is the subtle liking of a thing in the soul and inclination toward it. So you find a thing pleasing in yourself and you incline toward it with a strong inclination, and it may be disliked or unacceptable and unlawful.

Is all hawa like that? No, because there is the hawa of faith, which the Messenger of God (ﷺ) taught us when he said: ("None of you believes until his desire is subject to what I have brought.")(1)

So it is possible for desire to turn toward good, and it is the desire that moves a person to walk in accordance with the Truth. As for hawa' (air), it is what a person breathes, and from which he extracts oxygen to nourish the body and by which life proceeds. Therefore the saying goes: "And she came forward like a returning soul."

It is a gentle coming-forward. We know that if we eat something we love, we feel its taste, and when we drink something we love, we savour its flavour; but breathing is an involuntary matter, and when we breathe something we love, it is a gentle sensation.

There is a third pronunciation, which expresses falling: hawa from hawa yahwi, with a kasra on the waw, and from it one says "hawa al-dalw," meaning the bucket descending into the water in the well. Which kind of hawa does the verse intend?

The Truth says: ﴿whenever a messenger came to them with what their souls did not desire, a group they denied and a group they killed﴾. So the hawa he speaks of here is the desire of the soul stripped of the method, which governs the movement of this soul and leads it to disobedience to God. Did the Truth leave the human soul without a protector? No, because He sent messengers bearing a method whose summary is (do) and (do not). Thus the method can become a guardian over the impulses of the soul.

But since the Truth wanted the method to be a guardian over the impulses of the soul, why did He create the soul? Glory be to Him, He created the soul because its existence entails that a person desires what is lawful and permitted, for the preservation of the species and the perfection of work for lawful sustenance. Thus instinct exists, and God created it for a purpose, but He protects it through the method from departing from its purpose.

Someone may say: since God created the sexual instinct..... why not leave it to express itself? We say to him: fear God, and know that the sexual instinct came only for the preservation of the species, and using it in what angers God is the annihilation of the species and a deviation for which the method punishes.

Likewise the Truth created the instinct for food so that a person may sustain his life, and did not create it to end life through gluttony, excess and greed. Likewise the instinct of curiosity is not present for spying on people, but for discovering the secrets of the universe and deducing what is new and beneficial to people. So every instinct exists for a purpose, and if it goes beyond its purpose, the law governs and says: no. There is a framework within which instincts may be used, and the law does not come to erase instincts, but to refine them so that a person uses them for what benefits and not for what harms.

It is said in the Arab proverb: "The bane of opinion is desire." If two people stand before a judge, one wronged and the other a wrongdoer, the just judge is the one who lifts the injustice from the wronged, even if he has a desire for the wrongdoer. Therefore we find that the Truth protected His Messenger, and said: ﴿Nor does he speak from desire﴾ (3) (verse 3, surah al-Najm).

The superficial are those who do not attend to the greatness of this expressive style, and they ask: since the Truth corrects Muhammad, how then does he not speak from desire? We say: you do not understand well about God nor about the Messenger of God. When God corrected His Messenger, the Messenger had not departed from a ruling willed by God, nor did he alter a ruling of God according to his personal desire. Rather, in his humanity (ﷺ) he would reach a ruling he saw, and then heaven would show a correction to it, and Muhammad would state the correction as God revealed it. He (ﷺ) did not oppose his Lord in any matter. The divine correction came in matters on which God had given no prior ruling, and every correction came from human ijtihad by the Messenger of God, and there was no desire in that.

When the Truth said: ﴿Nor does he speak from desire﴾, He only informs us that Muhammad had no ruling from God which the Messenger then opposed following desire. The meaning of desire is that there is a method and then one deviates from it, and every correction God made came in matters where there was no ruling. Therefore we find the Truth's correction of His Messenger is gentle in character, and He says: ﴿God pardon you! Why did you give them permission until it became clear to you who were truthful and you knew the liars?﴾ (43) (surah al-Tawba).

This pardon was not the result of violating a ruling from the heavens, but a gentle pardon, because the Messenger of God acted by human ijtihad in matters where there was no ruling of God. This is the saying of the Truth: ﴿O Prophet, why do you prohibit what God has made lawful for you?﴾ (verse 1, surah al-Tahrim).

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) had prohibited certain things upon himself, and had not prohibited them upon people, and there the Truth clarifies to him: do not prohibit upon yourself what I have made lawful for you. So this is a matter for the Messenger's benefit. When Zayd ibn Haritha came, to be given the choice between being with the Messenger of God as a slave to him, or being with his family, Zayd preferred the Messenger of God, so the Prophet (ﷺ) rewarded him by placing him in the station of a son. Adoption was well known among the Arabs, and people called Zayd "Zayd ibn Muhammad." When God willed to annul adoption He said: ﴿Call them by their fathers' names; that is more just in the sight of God.﴾

The word (aqsat) means more just, and its meaning is that justice (qist) is also within the sphere of 'adl. When it is said: "So-and-so has qist," it means he has justice. Thus qist belongs first to the Messenger of God, and the more just is the ruling of God. It is as if you, O Muhammad, acted with qist among humans, but God wants for you the most just.

So His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿nor does he speak from desire﴾ is a statement that no one who opposes the method of Islam can object to. If someone opposing the method of Islam says: "God corrects Muhammad, so how does Muhammad not speak from desire?" We say: do you know the meaning of desire? To judge by desire means that he found a ruling of God and altered the ruling to suit his desire, and this did not happen from our master and lord, the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Every correction from God did not come through the tongue of another man, but came through the tongue of the Messenger of God himself. This is the utmost trustworthiness in conveying from God.

The Truth says concerning the Children of Israel: ﴿Every time a messenger came to them with what their souls did not desire, a group they denied and a group they killed.﴾ So they are two groups: some of them do not accept belief in the method because of a desire in their souls, and so they deny. And some of them have souls filled with obstinacy and fierce hostility toward the Messenger, and they fear that the Messenger will live to convey to other peoples, so they try to kill the Messenger.

Denial is the first point of obstinacy; then there are those who progress from obstinacy and fear that the message will reach other peoples, so they try to kill the Messenger. And the denial

1 Narrated by al-Baghawi in Sharh al-Sunna, al-Tabrizi in Mishkat al-Masabih, and al-Muttaqi al-Hindi in Kanz al-'Ummal.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 5, verse 71:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says, after that: ﴿And they supposed that there would be no trial, so they became blind and deaf; then Allah turned to them, then they became blind and deaf again; many of them, and Allah is Seeing of what they do.﴾

"Wa-ḥasibū" (وحسبوا): if it is read with a fatḥah on the ḥā' and a kasrah on the sīn, its meaning is "to suppose" (al-ẓann); if it is read with a fatḥah on both the ḥā' and the sīn, it means "to count" (ʿadd). The ḥusbān is that you suppose and conclude that a thing exists. Those to whom Allah took a covenant, namely the Children of Israel, supposed that denying the messengers and killing them would not be a trial (fitnah). It means that they did not know with certain knowledge, and they judged that there would be no trial. The root meaning of fitnah, as we have said, is placing gold on fire so that it is purified of impurities. Fitnah, as we know, is a test: a person either passes it or does not pass it. So how did this supposition come to them that this is not a test? This supposition came to them from the error they fell into when they said: ﴿We are the children of Allah and His beloved ones﴾ (part of verse 18, surah al-Mā'idah).

And from the error they persisted in when they said: ﴿The Fire will not touch us except for a few countable days﴾ (part of verse 80, surah al-Baqarah).

They supposed that the Truth would punish them only for worshipping the calf, and would not punish them for anything else. This was a mistaken supposition. The method (al-manhaj) did not come to save people by their persons, whatever they do; rather, the method came to hold every human being accountable for what he has done. It is strange that they supposed the mistaken supposition and did not reckon the matter with its correct reckoning, although they were people of excellence in covenant and reckoning, for reckoning is what guarantees the soundness of a matter or refutes it. And it is strange that the mercy of the Truth toward creation is that when He takes them to account, He says: "For you such-and-such, and against you such-and-such." But when He provides for them, He provides for them without reckoning.

However, they did not heed that, and the Truth said about them: ﴿And they supposed that there would be no trial﴾, meaning they supposed that in that matter there is no test, that they would not be held accountable for it. We know that "an" (أن) puts the verb in the subjunctive. A questioner said to me: "I heard the Qur'an reciter on the radio pronounce it ﴿wa-ḥasibū allā takūna fitnah﴾."

I said to him: there are three of the great reciters of the early Islamic period: (Abū ʿAmr), (Ḥamzah) and (al-Kisā'ī), and each of them had a distinctive style. When we know that "an" puts the verb in the subjunctive, the verb following it must not indicate knowledge, certainty and clarity; for "an" after knowledge does not put in the subjunctive, as in His saying: ﴿He knew that there would be among you sick ones and others traveling through the land﴾ (part of verse 20, surah al-Muzzammil).

Ibn Mālik's Alfiyyah says: (And "bi-lan" put it in the subjunctive, and "kay" likewise, and "bi-anna" not after knowledge). As for "an" that comes after supposition (ẓann), it is possible for it to put the verb in the subjunctive and it is possible for the verb after it to be in the nominative. Whoever considered the existence of the verb and perceived it with a dominant perception is put in the nominative; whoever did not have this dominant perception is put in the subjunctive. The nominative is the reading of al-Kisā'ī, Abū ʿAmr and Ḥamzah. They based the matter on the idea that dominant supposition approaches certainty. Since that has happened, the "an" here is the emphatic "an" (an al-mukhaffafah), not the subjunctive-governing "an"; they call it the lightened form of the heavy "an," its origin being "anna." ﴿wa-ḥasibū allā takūna fitnah﴾. The word (fitnah) comes in the nominative because it is the subject of (takūn). And (takūn) is from (kāna).

(Kāna) has a nominative subject and an accusative predicate. Here it has no predicate, because it is (kāna al-tāmmah, the complete kāna). There is (kāna al-nāqisah, the incomplete kāna) and there is (kāna al-tāmmah). We say this so that we master the understanding of the Qur'an, just as we read His saying: ﴿And if there is one in hardship, then a postponement until ease...﴾ (part of verse 280, surah al-Baqarah).

(Kāna) is a past-tense verb, and (dhū ʿusrah) is the subject of the complete kāna; therefore it has no predicate, because what is meant is to say: "if one in hardship exists, then a postponement until ease." We must know what "complete" (tāmm) means and what "incomplete" (nāqis) means. We know that every word we utter revolves around one of two matters: either a word that is meaningless and not used, or a word that is used. The used word is one that has a meaning reaching the mind at the moment of its utterance and that is understood independently. If time has no part in it, it is a noun (ism), like the words (arḍ, "earth"), (shams, "sun") and (qamar, "moon"). There is also a word that is not understood independently, like the preposition (fī, "in") for example. It is true that it indicates one thing within another, but it is not understood independently; therefore it must be joined to something, as in our saying: "the water in the cup" or our saying: "the student in the classroom." A word that has a meaning which is independently understood, and in which time has a part, is the verb (fiʿl).

For example, our saying: "the sky" (al-samā'). The sky was in the past, is in the present, and will be in the future. So time has no part in it. And the word "eat" (kulū) we find comes from eating, and it is a meaning independently understood, with time being a part of it. The particle (fī) indicates a meaning not independently understood, so it must be joined to something else.

Thus every word has a meaning, and this meaning may be independently understood or not. If it is independently understood, we ask: is time a part of it? In that case it is a verb. If time is not a part of it, it is a noun. If it is not independently understood and needs something else to complete the meaning, it is a particle (ḥarf).

This is how words are known. The verb is "a meaning with time added to it," as in our saying: "akala" (he ate); it means a person took food in a past time. In this way we understand our saying "kāna." If we say "kāna" in the sense of something happening in the past, as in our saying "kāna Zayd musāfiran" (Zayd was traveling), then it is incomplete (nāqisah). In light of this we understand the Truth's saying: ﴿And if there is one in hardship, then a postponement until ease﴾ (part of verse 280, surah al-Baqarah).

If you want mere existence without anything new added to it, then the verb is complete and does not need a predicate. If you want existence together with some other thing, then it is the incomplete verb, which you complete with a predicate. Like the Exalted's saying: ﴿And they supposed that there would be no trial﴾, meaning that there would not exist a trial; so it does not need a predicate.

The likeness of the Children of Israel is like the student who goes to school and does not know that there is an examination at the end of the year, so he spends the time without study, without diligence, without striving, but in idleness and play. This was a mistaken reckoning, because the method did not come arbitrarily; rather it came as a system of movement for life, for the believer to act upon. It was required that they receive the path in accordance with the teachings of the method. It is strange that they supposed and did not reckon with reckoning, although they were people of knowledge of reckoning. They reckoned (ḥasibū), with a kasrah on the sīn, and did not reckon (mā ḥasabū), with a fatḥah on the sīn. It was required that they perform the reckoning, for reckoning is what guarantees the soundness of matters.

Everything with Allah happens by reckoning: reckoning for the servant and reckoning against the servant. ﴿And they supposed that there would be no trial﴾, meaning they supposed that it was not a test. And they supposed that the messages and methods are a matter in which there is no test for them. So when they recognized (it), they turned blind to it and closed their ears to it. We know that the means of perception in the human soul are hearing, sight and hearts:

﴿And Allah brought you out from the wombs of your mothers knowing nothing, and made for you hearing, sight and hearts, that you may be grateful﴾ (verse 78, surah al-Naḥl).

So the means of perception are: hearing, sight and heart (fu'ād). What the eye sees is a person's own experience. What a person hears is the experience of every other person, and thus hearing is broader in scope than the eye. Hearing is the means of perception that first exists in a person when he is born. We find that the newborn does not react when something approaches his eyes, because he does not see with precision, and that may continue for about ten days; after that he begins to see. But when the child hears a sound beside his ears, he reacts, as if the sense of hearing is the one that first exists. For this reason the Truth mentions hearing first, then sight, then the hearts.

﴿They became blind and deaf﴾: He, glory be to Him, first asks them about their personal experience, and does not ask them only about what they heard from others. ﴿They became blind﴾, meaning they did not see even the matters concerning themselves, and did not look into the signs of the cosmos, and did not hear the bearer of good news nor the warner, nor the method from Allah, nor did they agree to implement it. He, glory be to Him, first rebukes them for what concerns their own seeing, for the ear hears from others; therefore He first reproached them that they did not use their eyes. Even if we suppose that they did not see the signs of the cosmos with their own selves, what is wrong with them that they do not look, when the Messenger came to them and called them to look into the cosmos of Allah and to take heed?

If they were first in heedlessness and so did not see, why did they not pay attention and listen with the listening of submission and compliance when the bearer of good news and the warner came to alert them? For this reason, ﴿they became blind and deaf﴾ is very logical here.

Afterward Allah accepted from them, rescued them from Pharaoh, split the sea for them, and they crossed. But as soon as they came out of the sea, they passed by a people devoted to and clinging to and attending to idols of theirs that they worshipped. They said to Mūsā: "Make for us a god just as they have gods." Mūsā ordered them to repent, and Allah accepted their repentance, despite the great number of sins they had committed. After that Allah turns to them: ﴿Then Allah turned to them﴾.

Repentance is opening a way for the sound soul to set out again toward good. For if Allah did not turn to one who sins, what would be the stance of the sinner without repentance? He would persist and feel that he is going on the path of evil with no return. When the Truth accepts the repentance of the sinner, that means that He, glory be to Him, wants to protect society from his evil. Repentance has stages: the first: when Allah prescribes repentance; the second: that the servants repent; the third: Allah's acceptance of repentance. This is what the Truth brought:

﴿Then He turned to them that they might repent﴾ (part of verse 118, surah al-Tawbah).

What does Allah's turning to them mean? He, glory be to Him, will not turn to them with accepting repentance except after they repent. So Allah's first turning to them is the prescribing of repentance for them, then their repentance, then the Truth's acceptance of repentance. But these people became blind and deaf, and despite that, Allah showed kindness to them. So what happened from them afterward? They became blind and deaf again: ﴿Then Allah turned to them; then they became blind and deaf again; many of them, and Allah is Seeing of what they do.﴾

"ʿAmū" (عموا) is derived from the verb ʿamiya (to be blind), and like it are (akalū, "they ate") and (sharibū, "they drank") and (ḥaḍarū, "they attended"). Where is the subject? The subject is the (wāw al-jamāʿah, the plural wāw). Ibn Mālik treated this matter: when you attach the verb to two or to a group, you must strip the verb of the sign of duality or plurality. So you do not say "qāmā Zayd wa-ʿAmr" (Zayd and ʿAmr stood), but you say "qāma Zayd wa-ʿAmr," and we do not say "qāmū al-talāmīdh" (the students stood) but we say "qāma al-talāmīdh," because the indication of the wāw is the indication of "al-talāmīdh." Ibn Mālik said:

"And strip the verb when it is attached to two or to a plural, as in (fāz al-shuhadā')."

That is, if the verb is attached to a dual or plural noun, it must be stripped of the sign that indicates duality or plurality. As for the word "kathīr" (many), it is parsed either as a substitute (badal) for the wāw of the plural, or by supposing an omitted subject (mubtada'), meaning "the blind and the deaf, many of them," or as a subject (fā'il), and that would then have come according to the dialect of a group of the Arabs, the Banū al-Ḥārith ibn Kaʿb. These people may attach a sign indicating duality or plurality when the verb is attached to an apparent dual or plural noun, such as: "qāmū al-rijāl" (the men stood) and "sāfara Muḥammad wa-ʿAlī" (Muḥammad and ʿAlī traveled).

Some have read the Exalted's saying ﴿Those who did wrong conferred secretly﴾ according to this. The Truth's saying ﴿many of them﴾ serves as a safeguard against the possibility that a few of them manage the matter of faith in their hearts; the word "kathīr" came so that we would notice that the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, never neglects the few who contemplate the matter of faith in their thoughts. That is, if the verb is attached to a dual or plural noun, it must be stripped of the sign that indicates duality or plurality, to affirm and reinforce what came in His saying: ﴿And that most of you are defiantly disobedient﴾.

﴿Then they became blind and deaf; many of them; and Allah is Seeing of what they do.﴾ And ﴿Baṣīr﴾ (Seeing) is like ʿAlīm (Knowing): it means "witness," and it is not with the eye, where.

The Almighty then says:

﴿Certainly they have disbelieved who say, "Indeed, Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary." But the Messiah said, "O Children of Israel, worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord. Indeed, he who associates others with Allah – Allah has forbidden him Paradise, and his refuge is the Fire. And for the wrongdoers there are no helpers."﴾ (72)

There are three verses that address this matter: ﴿Certainly they have disbelieved who say, "Indeed, Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary."﴾ The second verse – that is, that when the verb is attributed to a dual or plural subject, it must be stripped of the sign that indicates duality or plurality – is: ﴿Certainly they have disbelieved who say, "Indeed, Allah is the third of three."﴾ (from verse 73 of Surat al-Ma'idah).

The third verse: ﴿And [mention] when Allah says, "O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two deities other than Allah?'" He will say, "Exalted are You! It was not for me to say that to which I have no right."﴾ (116) (from verse 116 of Surat al-Ma'idah).

Thus the disagreement on this matter came in three forms:

One group says: the Messiah is God. Another group says: the Messiah is a god together with two others. And another group says: the Messiah and his mother are two gods. Each group has a refutation. The refutation comes from the simplest thing we observe in existence concerning a living being: the human being – as we know – is the master of creation, and what is lower than him serves him. Man needs animals for his benefits, and likewise he needs plants and inanimate things; this master – man – needs what is lower than him. The Almighty, glory be to Him, wished to refute the deification of Jesus and our lady Mary, so He said: ﴿They both used to eat food﴾ (from verse 75 of Surat al-Ma'idah).

This is an argument among the clearest proofs – not only for the philosopher, but for all levels. For as long as they both eat food, they have needed what is lower than them. And one who needs what is lower than himself cannot be the Highest, nor is he the One, the Unique. And the adherents of these three groups disagree.

The Almighty says: ﴿And do not say, "Three"﴾. The expression "third of three" is used to mean one of three, but unspecified. Whenever three people come together, each of them may be called "third of three." This saying is prohibited only in one case: that we say "third of three gods," because deity is not plural. It is correct to say "third of two," because Allah says: ﴿There is no secret conversation of three but that He is their fourth, nor of five but that He is their sixth﴾ (from verse 7 of Surat al-Mujadilah).

So it is possible to say: "He is the fourth of three," or "the fifth of four," or "the sixth of five." He is the one by whom three become four, or four become five, or five become six. If we mention a number in the form of an active participle and then add to what precedes it, this is a specification that it is the last. If someone says, "Allah is the fourth of three who are sitting," this is a correct statement. But if we say that they are gods, this is what is forbidden and prohibited, because deity is not plural.

It is noted that the Qur'an did not say: "There is no secret conversation of two but that He is their third," because secret conversation is only among three; if two sit together, they may speak together without it being a secret conversation, since a secret conversation requires that no one hear them. Secret conversation is private, and the first of secret conversations is three, which is why the Almighty began with the first number to which it applies. If you say, "third of three," this is a correct statement, provided they are not three gods.

The Almighty wished to dismiss this statement as false when He said: ﴿They both used to eat food﴾, and food sustains life and provides energy in the movement of life, because a human wants to preserve life and wants energy; food is lower than the human being since it is at his service. So if they both eat food, they are in need of what is lower. And if they do not eat, there must be hunger and emaciation.

Therefore they are not gods. Some say that ﴿they both used to eat food﴾ is a metaphor for something else, namely the expelling of waste. We say: expelling waste is not necessary, because Allah will feed us in Paradise and no waste will leave us. So this is not evidence. The Almighty elevates the discourse with people in argument: the Jews said about the Messiah – peace be upon him – what is not fitting for his station as a messenger prophet, and they said about Mary – peace be upon her – what is not fitting for her election by the Almighty.

The Jews, then, are the adversaries of the Messiah, and the supporters of the Messiah are the disciples! So if he could not do to his adversaries anything harmful, nor for his disciples anything beneficial, how could he be a god? The Qur'anic text says about Mary:

﴿O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord and prostrate and bow with those who bow﴾ (43) (Surat Al 'Imran).

And the Messiah himself was always with Allah, humble and worshipping. The one who worships worships someone higher than himself; a god does not worship his own self. And if this is the saying of those who ascribe themselves to heaven, believing in a god and believing in a method, what then of the saying of those who do not ascribe themselves to heaven – the atheists who deny deity?

Therefore it was obligatory that those who ascribe themselves to heaven should believe through methods, through prophets, and that they should clarify this matter among themselves. For example, the world existed and was governed before the Messiah – so who, then, was governing the world before his birth? Therefore the Almighty, majestic in His majesty, wished to settle the matter. The Qur'an teaches us: ﴿Indeed, we or you are either upon guidance or in clear error﴾ (from verse 24 of Surat Saba').

Can contradictory positions both be correct? No; for one of them must be upon guidance and the other must be in error. Therefore we say: your statement does not bind us, and our statement does not bind you. We refer the matter to the God in whom we believe. And so that we do not let this matter drag on, we mention the words of the Truth: ﴿Then let us invoke [the curse of] Allah upon the liars﴾ (from verse 61 of Surat Al 'Imran).

And we say: "Place Your curse upon the liars," so that You may bring us out of this disagreement and not let one of us dominate the other; You are the owner of the matter. Here we are, ourselves, our women, and our children, calling with one single supplication: "Let the curse of Allah be upon the liars among us." No people have ever invoked curses upon one another and called upon Allah except that Allah made the matter manifest in its time. But none of the People of the Book accepted this mutual invocation. And the Almighty says:

﴿Certainly they have disbelieved who say, "Indeed, Allah is the third of three." And there is no god except one God. And if they do not desist from what they are saying, there will surely afflict the disbelievers among them a painful punishment﴾ (73).
So then, those who do not proclaim their repentance from that fall into disbelief and are punished.

Then the Truth says: ﴿Will they not turn in repentance to Allah and seek His forgiveness? And Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.﴾ (5:74)

So it is as if this statement calls for repentance and for seeking the forgiveness of the Truth.

Then He, glorified is He, says:

﴿The Messiah, son of Mary, was but a messenger; messengers had passed away before him, and his mother was a woman of truth. They both used to eat food. Look how We make the signs clear to them; then look how they are turned away.﴾ (5:75)

"Afaka" (أفك) means to turn away or to be turned aside; i.e., others turn them away. This indicates that this is an incitement from Satan, for the Messiah, peace be upon him, was nothing but a messenger like those messengers who preceded him, and his mother was "siddiqa" (صديقة), one who affirms the truth of what he brought. The proof of their humanity is that they both have needs like all other humans, for the sustenance of their lives: food, drink, and clothing. The divinity claimed for them contradicts this belief, and this is precisely the "ifk" (إفك, falsehood), which clashes with reason free from desire.

Almighty Allah says: ﴿Say: Do you worship besides Allah that which possesses neither harm nor benefit for you? And Allah is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ (5:76)

Reason rejects that we should worship anyone other than Allah. Another being cannot bring harm upon adversaries, nor benefit to himself or to his followers and supporters. The proof is that the enemies did what they did, and Jesus (peace be upon him) and the disciples (al-Hawariyyun) were unable to harm them, and they were unable to do anything by which they could benefit themselves.

Allah concludes the verse with His words: ﴿And Allah is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ The word ﴿al-Sami'﴾ (the All-Hearing) indicates speech. The word ﴿al-'Alim﴾ (the All-Knowing) indicates something that turns over in the thoughts. And that which turns over in the thoughts: is it the influence of a temporal authority that made them say these words? He, glory be to Him, is the All-Knowing of that. If speech has occurred, He has heard it, and if thoughts have stirred within the soul, He knows them, because the rational person, before speaking, must turn words over in the soul. And every speech must have a motive. He, glory be to Him, is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from eternity to eternity.

Almighty Allah says: "Say, 'O People of the Scripture, do not exceed the limits in your religion, other than the truth, and do not follow the desires of a people who had gone astray before and led many astray and strayed from the sound way.'" (5:77)

When there is something common between the Christians and the Jews, Allah addresses them with His words, "O People of the Scripture." As for the specific matter, He speaks to each group separately. Ghuluww (extremism, exaggeration) is for a person to go to an extreme regarding a ruling, whether positively or negatively. It is either excessive elevation of a high station or excessive lowering of a low station. For this reason, we always find contradictions in ghuluww. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to our master 'Ali, may Allah honour his face: ("O 'Ali, two men will be destroyed because of you... a lover who exaggerates and a hater who exaggerates") and he said: ("O 'Ali, none loves you except a believer, and none hates you except a hypocrite") (1).

He also said: ("O 'Ali, the rebellious group will fight you") (2).

There are those who loved our master 'Ali to the point that they considered him a prophet, and said: "Revelation erred regarding 'Ali and came to Muhammad (ﷺ)," or they considered 'Ali to be a god! All of that is ghuluww; they loved him to a station that contains exaggeration and excess.

As for the Khawarij, they said about our master 'Ali that he was a disbeliever. So ghuluww came, then, from the side of the lovers, who made him a prophet or something above that, which brings them into shirk, and from the side of the haters, who say he is a disbeliever and that he is removed from the circle of religion. Therefore, we must not exceed the limits in religion, so we do not love a person and raise him above the level of humans, nor hate a person and bring him down to the depths. Rather, we must give each one his due rank and measure, which Allah has placed in him, because Allah's placing of him is his honour:

"Say, 'O People of the Scripture, do not exceed the limits in your religion, other than the truth, and do not follow the desires of a people who had gone astray before and led many astray and strayed from the sound way.'" (Surat al-Ma'idah).

A similar statement came in another verse: "O People of the Scripture, do not exceed the limits in your religion, and do not say about Allah except the truth." (From 4:171, Surat an-Nisa').

And so that we understand that the matter of ghuluww came only in claims of the divinity of humans, the Truth then said: "The Messiah, 'Isa, son of Maryam, is only the Messenger of Allah and His word which He directed to Maryam and a spirit from Him." (From 4:171, Surat an-Nisa').

So there is no need to exaggerate by ascribing divinity to him or saying that he is the third of three. If you are doubtful, and you reached this doubt because of the absence of the male element in the coming of 'Isa, then understand that all things came by "Be" (kun). For although there are precursors for a human being, this matter is traced back to one who did not come from procreation; and you will reach Adam, and Adam was from dust. So all of creation is a word. And although there are causes, what Allah concealed in the first word is what appears when a human being is created by a word. So do not say: this is something strange, for the whole universe came into being by a word:

"His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, 'Be,' and it is." (82) (Surat Ya-Sin).

And if the trial arose in the outward appearance of the mother because the Messiah has no father in the realm of procreation and the law of reproduction, this should not have been the cause of doubt, because he was created from a mother, whereas Adam was created without a father or a mother. The trial should have been greater regarding Adam. The word from Allah produces life, and life is the introduction of a spirit into matter to give it movement, sensation and the components of life. Thus the word is spoken from Allah and the spirit comes to enter into matter: "His word, which He directed to Maryam and a spirit from Him." "A spirit from Him" is like what He said about Adam: "So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, then fall down to him in prostration." (29) (Surat al-Hijr).

Thus Adam is a word, Adam is a spirit from Him, and likewise the Messiah; there is no doubt here or there. The Truth asks those attributed to heaven: "Desist; it is better for you." So if you are attributed to heaven, do not unsettle people's thinking with such matters. You should have stood with 'Isa at the honour Allah intended for him, for honour is to be a good example, and if he were of a different kind than human beings, the exemplarity would be impossible, because exemplarity is only from the kind of the one who follows it. If people saw him humble and devoted to worship, they could not do like him if he were of a different substance than human substance.

I once said: if a person saw a lion hunting in the forest, attacking and overpowering the animals, would one of the onlookers think of making himself [a lion]? No. But if he saw a brave horseman like himself in battle, attacking and overpowering the enemies, he would imitate him and try to be like him. Thus exemplarity exists only with unity of kind; if he were not of the kind of human beings, he would not be fit to be a messenger.

"Say, 'O People of the Scripture, do not exceed the limits in your religion, other than the truth.'" The Truth here speaks comprehensively to all the People of the Scripture, because each of them came with one extreme of matters. The Jews accused our lady, the chosen virgin Maryam, of what was not in her, and those others went to exaggeration on the other side. Therefore the Truth commands both of them not to exaggerate, because the truth does not contradict itself; it is a fixed thing that never changes and does not conflict. If a person sees an event with his own eyes and is then asked to recount it, he recounts it now, recounts it tomorrow, and recounts it after a year, and his account remains consistent, because he witnessed it, and the witnessed reality imposes itself on him. But the liar does not remember that; he may state a matter in which he is lying, and when he recounts it a second time he must change the reality. For this reason it is said: "If you are a liar, then be a good memorizer."

What governs the truth is a fact, because the speaker of it extrapolates from reality. But the liar does not extrapolate from reality, so he does not know what he lied about the first time. We recall a liar who sat and said: once we were travelling, leaving the village heading to the city to buy things for the Eid al-Fitr, and the world was lit by a moon like midday. His saying "a moon like midday" is what exposes his lie, for how can there be a moon on the night of Eid? The first night of Eid al-Fitr is the first night of Shawwal, and there is no moon in it at all; the crescent is almost hidden.

Thus the one who draws upon a reality does not change his speech, because it is the truth. And the one who draws upon something other than reality does not remember what he said, so he confuses himself. Therefore no person should say what is other than the truth, for his speech will contradict itself. If this contradiction occurs regarding the matter of divinity, people may doubt the method of heaven that they follow.
