And if people doubt the method of heaven, you will bear the burden of misguiding people, because one who engages this matter must not let people experience any kind of contradiction from him. For this reason our master Ibrahim, peace be upon him, said: "Our Lord, do not make us a trial for those who disbelieve." (5) (Surat al-Mumtahanah).

Why did our master Ibrahim make this supplication? Because whoever says something and then does something that contradicts it, the one who sees him may imagine that he is, Allah forbid, a liar.

"Say, 'O People of the Scripture, do not exceed the limits in your religion, other than the truth, and do not follow the desires of a people who had gone astray before and led many astray and strayed from the sound way.'" Would that they had gone astray only in themselves, but they try to mislead others. Therefore He, glorified be He, said: "Many of the People of the Scripture wish they could return you to disbelief after your belief, out of envy from themselves." (From 2:109, Surat al-Baqarah).

And He, glorified be He, clarifies to them: do not do that, lest you go astray; for your burden is that you act, and there is another burden, which is that you mislead others. Therefore the Truth says:

"That they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge." (From 16:25, Surat an-Nahl)

The Truth said that, although He also said: "No bearer of burden will bear the burden of another." And so that we understand the matter, we must know that the first burden is the burden of going astray, and the second is the burden of leading astray.

"And do not follow the desires of a people who had gone astray": that is, do not imitate people who followed desire. Hawa (desire) is the subtle proximity of a thing and its closeness to the self, so that a person does it in a manner that is not fitting. For this reason every occurrence of the word hawa in the Qur'an is in the context of loss and error. When we read His saying, the Truth: "And do not follow desire, for it will lead you astray from the way of Allah."

And He, glorified be He, said: "And follows his desire, so he is ruined."

Hawa also appears in the saying of the Messenger (ﷺ): ("None of you believes until his desire is subject to what I have brought.") (3)

That is, what is required is that a person subdue his desire to what Allah requires. And since he has subdued his desire to what Allah requires, this means that his personal desire has been restrained. "And do not follow the desires of a people who had gone astray before and led many astray and strayed from the sound way." This is the prohibition against following desire, which leads astray and becomes a cause of leading others away from the sound way.

Almighty God then says: ﴿Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed upon the tongue of David and Jesus, son of Mary. That is because they disobeyed and were transgressing.﴾ (78)

Almighty God gives His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, an example (uswa) to steady him in the face of what he encounters from his adversaries among the People of the Book. It is as if He is saying to him: this matter is not unprecedented and not strange, for the long history of the People of the Book confirms it. Behold their stance toward the Prophet of Allah, David, and likewise their stance toward Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him. This makes for you an example in these Messengers, who suffered harm from these same people. The matter is not specific to you alone; rather it is a characteristic of them. Almighty God expands in consoling His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, until He makes his position one of unshakable firmness of faith, which neither fears nor wavers. He attributes these things to Himself, saying: ﴿We know indeed that what they say grieves you; but it is not you they deny, rather the wrongdoers deny the signs of Allah.﴾ (Surah al-An'am, 33)

At one time they said of the Messenger that he was mad; at another they said "sorcerer"; and a third time they said "liar." Yet they knew their own lies. Despite their accusing the Messenger of lying, madness and sorcery, they trust no one with their interests except the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, for he is always the trustworthy one. They ought to have been astonished at this stance of theirs, and at their turning people away from the religion of Allah through disbelief. Yet despite all this, whenever there is a precious and valuable thing, it is entrusted to no one but Muhammad ibn Abdullah.

What a strange matter, then!

They recognised the truthfulness of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the reality of his message, there is no doubt about it. But because they have their desires and persisted in error, clinging to temporal authority. They know that Muhammad is the trustworthy one. This is why we see our master, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, appoint Ali, may Allah honour his face, and leave him in Mecca to deliver the trusts that were with him to all of them.

So: ﴿We know indeed that what they say grieves you; but it is not you they deny.﴾ That is, O Messenger of Allah, you are the truthful one in their eyes. You, O Messenger of Allah, are the trustworthy one in their eyes. You, O Messenger of Allah, are in their eyes at the summit of moral nobility. Had you not said that you are a Messenger from Allah, they would have raised you to the highest ranks. But by your conveying of the message from Allah, you shook their temporal authority.

They tried to turn you away from the message: they offered you kingship and offered you wealth, and had you been seeking any of that, they would have fulfilled for you what you wanted. But you chose the faithful conveying of the message from Allah.

They offered you kingship willingly, and offered you riches, and made the leadership among them appealing to you on condition that you abandon the message. But you chose the clear path that admits no ambiguity, despite the hardships in it; you chose the path that costs you your safety and the safety of those who follow you. Indeed, you follow what is revealed to you from your Lord.

After that they came to besiege you in the valley (al-Sha'b), to impose on you an economic blockade by starving you and those with you. Yet despite all this you did not give up conveying the message. They should have realised that you seek nothing for yourself, neither money nor status; rather you are a Messenger from Allah who does not eat from anyone's charity, neither you nor your family. They should have asked themselves: why do you enter this fierce war on your own? You are not seeking status, nor seeking wealth, nor seeking any of those pleasures. They should have taken the lesson: they offer him all these things and he refuses them, because he is the Seal of the Prophets; therefore the good of every prophet who preceded him is embodied in him. And there is embodied in him, for example, what Solomon said to the delegation of Bilqis, queen of Sheba: ﴿What Allah has given me is better than what He has given you; rather, you rejoice in your gift.﴾ (part of verse 36, Surah al-Naml)

So people should have realised that when prophethood comes, it comes only to draw people's attention to heaven and to its method, and to organise the movement of their lives in the universe; and that the one who benefits first and last from the method is themselves, because it is they who are wretched by opposing the method of Allah.

Let every person strip himself of everything and look at the method, and he will find that it is in his own interest. Behold Solomon, to whom the world submitted and who was given a kingdom that Allah had given to no one after him: Allah subjected the wind to him and subjected the jinn to him, doing whatever he willed. Solomon used to give the pure fine flour to the servants so that they might enjoy the good things, while he himself ate what was left of the bran of the flour. This was evidence from Allah that these methods are not for the benefit of a prophet, but that every prophet only wants by the method the welfare of those to whom he is sent.

The resistance of the People of the Book to the Prophet of Allah David, and how they transgressed on the Sabbath, was such that David, peace be upon him, invoked a curse upon them, and Allah turned them into apes; and He cursed them in the Psalms (al-Zabur). Likewise they uttered the lie against Mary the virgin, and Allah cursed them in the Gospel. The curse was only upon the basis of what they had done; therefore the Truth concludes the verse with the words: ﴿That is because they disobeyed and were transgressing.﴾

Disobedience (al-'isyan), as we know, is sin within a person's own self and in his private affairs that do not extend to others. Transgression (al-i'tida'), however, is also sin, but one that extends to others. For example: the envious person punishes only himself, whereas the thief or the bribe-taker harms others. Thus there is disobedience and there is aggression: disobedience returns upon its doer without reaching others, whereas aggression is taking the right of another for oneself, or a harm that an individual commits whose effect passes on to others.

Almighty Allah says: ﴿They used not to forbid one another from wrongdoing which they committed. Evil indeed was what they used to do.﴾

We know that safeguarding the method of Allah grants a person safety in his movement through life on earth. Allah, glorified is He, has placed in the human soul a self-immunity. Whenever a desire of any kind arises in a person, whether for sex, wealth or status, he may try to reach it by any means, and nothing prevents him except the conscience, which obliges him to walk the right path. This conscience is the leaven of faith, and it is what reproaches a person if he commits a sin, provided he is among the people of religion.

We should look closely at this Qur'anic statement, for it carries the precise description of the human soul in its changing state. Here is Qabil, of whom the Qur'an speaks: ﴿So his soul permitted him the murder of his brother﴾ (part of verse 30, Surat al-Ma'idah). Then Qabil killed Habil, and afterwards the soul calmed from the frenzy of anger and the frenzy of rancour, and Qabil passed to what the Qur'an describes: ﴿and he became among the losers﴾ (part of verse 30, Surat al-Ma'idah).

So after his anger had led him astray to the point of killing his brother and depriving him of life, Allah sent him a crow to show him how to conceal his brother's nakedness, because he did not know how to bury his brother's body. He moved from the regret of having failed to respect his brother's right in life to wanting to respect his right in death. Thus, although the human soul has desires, it also has a temperamental balance which intervenes through remorse when a person commits a sin or disobedience. That is why you find many people suffering hardships because they committed sins, yet they want to confess them to any person, and whoever receives the confession has no power to remedy the effects of those hardships, because the deed has occurred and the matter is over.

But why does a person want to confess his sins to another? It is a confession for relief, because every movement in the human soul produces an effect on its inclination. When someone angers you, you tend toward revenge, and for this reason the Shari'ah instructs you, when someone angers you, to change your position and say: (Allah is sufficient for us and He is the best Disposer of affairs). So that you discharge the frenzied energy in you. If someone angers you while you are standing, sit down; if you are sitting, lie down; and if you are fixed in one place, walk a few steps. When the Shari'ah asks you to move at the moment of anger, it is so that some of the excess energy in your body is removed, which causes you to boil, and thus the intensity of anger decreases.

For this reason, the Arab poet advises every listener to a complaint not to dismiss the hearing but to attend to the one complaining. So he says:
"There must be a complaint to a man of honour
who consoles you, or comforts you, or sympathizes."
When sharing is shown to the one complaining, you relieve him and guide him to tranquillity. The poet advises the complainant to place his complaint with a man of honour, because the man of honour gives you his ear and his feelings, and he is worthy that you entrust him with the secret, as if secrets were in a treasury whose contents no one will know. By such confession a person relieves himself and diverts his emotion to something else. When the human soul repeats evil deeds and finds no one who forbids it or forbids them, evil becomes general and spreads; here heaven intervenes by sending a messenger.

Allah makes clear that the reason for sending a messenger to these people was that they did not forbid one another from the wrong they committed, and forbidding wrong is done only through mutual counsel to truth and mutual counsel to patience. A believer must not assume that he is safe from a thought of evil in his soul, for each of us is human and exposed to changes. It is part of Allah's kindness that, at the moment a thought of evil comes to a believer, he finds a brother free of evil thoughts who counsels him to truth and counsels him to patience; for if the frenzy of desire comes to one person at the moment it comes to a friend of his, they may agree on wrongdoing. But if the frenzy of desire comes to a person whose friend is a believer free of evil thoughts, the friend forbids him and counsels him to truth and patience. And so on. Believers thus exchange forbidding through counsel: at one time a person is the one forbidding, and at another time he is the one forbidden.

Likewise, Allah gave this matter the word "mutual counsel":
﴿By time. Indeed, mankind is in loss, except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience.﴾ (Surat al-'Asr)

Allah did not designate one group to be the forbidders and another group to be the forbidden. No, each of us is exposed to become a forbidder if his friend's thoughts turn to the unlawful, and exposed also to become the forbidden if his own soul turns to the unlawful. Thus we exchange forbidding and being forbidden, and this is called (al-mufa'alah) (the reciprocal form), just as we say: "Zayd shared with 'Amr" (sharaka Zayd 'Amran). A person does not share with himself; he shares with another. This means that one person was the doer at one time and the one acted upon at another. And how is this reciprocal form? It is like (tasharaka) and (tadarraba), meaning that the action comes from two. It is therefore easy for a person to forbid a friend or for a friend to forbid him. We may also interpret it as meaning that all forbid themselves through the hidden innate force present in every soul, that is, every soul forbids itself. Thus the reciprocal action is either in the soul or in the society.

﴿They used not to forbid one another from wrongdoing which they committed﴾. Let us note here that they had actually committed the wrong. How then can there be forbidding of wrongdoing? It may be understood on the basis that they did not forbid one another from a wrong they intended to commit; that is, a person among them would see a colleague preparing to commit a wrong and would not forbid him. Similar to this is His statement, the Truth:
﴿When you rise to prayer, wash your faces and your hands﴾ (part of verse 6, Surat al-Ma'idah).

This statement does not at all mean that a person performs ablution after he has entered the prayer. Rather, it means that we begin the ablution at the moment of preparing for prayer, that is, if you intend to stand up to prayer and perform it.

His statement, the Truth: ﴿They used not to forbid one another from the wrong they committed﴾ places us in a state of attentiveness, spiritual insight and vigilance. Each of us turns to himself, watches it and monitors it, and to which direction it is moving, so that a person does not let his soul head toward any corrupt place or improper act. Likewise, a person should be mindful of his friends and companions so that we forbid any wrong and never fall into the circle of this ruling: ﴿They used not to forbid one another from wrongdoing which they committed. Evil indeed was what they used to do.﴾ It is as if all of us must live in a state of faithful wakefulness, and say "No" to every initial impulse and every movement of wrongdoing.

﴿They used not to forbid one another from wrongdoing which they committed. Evil indeed was what they used to do.﴾ When you hear "la-bi'sa" (evil indeed), know that the lam, when preceded, is the lam of oath, and when Allah swears, this is an affirmation of the matter. Is this an affirmation in our manner as humans? No. None of us is like Allah. In our lives we know the proofs of truth: acknowledgment, testimony, or oath.

A judge rules only on the acknowledgment of the accused, the testimony of witnesses, or the oath. When the Truth brings a judgment, He brings it with knowledge of creation. Not forbidding wrongdoing is an act and a statement together. Since the Truth did not say "Evil indeed was what they used to say," the reason being that saying is contrasted with doing, and both are also work: speech is the work of the tongue, while doing is the work of all the limbs, and the word "work" (al-'amal) encompasses both speech and deed. We note that the matter is not confined to speech; rather, it is a work that results from an act.

Let us look at the prophetic hadith saying: "Whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand; if he cannot, then with his tongue; if he cannot, then with his heart, and that is the weakest of faith."(1)

His statement, the Truth: ﴿Evil indeed was what they used to do﴾ is evidence that they used to commit wrong and ugliness both in speech and in action.

1. Narrated by Ahmad, Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah, from Abu Sa'id.

Al-Sha'rawi continues:

"The Truth (al-Haqq) then continues after that, saying:

﴿You see many of them allying themselves with those who disbelieve. Wretched is what their souls have sent forward for them, that Allah is angry with them, and in the punishment they will abide eternally.﴾ (5:80)

We note the difference between the Truth informing His Messenger of matters that occurred earlier, such as His saying: ﴿Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed upon the tongue of David and Jesus, son of Mary﴾ (part of 5:78),

and the reality that was taking place in the time of the Messenger of Allah. The first report is a report about something that proceeded from them with those prophets who came before. But there are things, O Messenger of Allah, that you witness yourself, and this is evidence that their disbelief was not a passing whim that ended. No, their disbelief had become a trait (malakah) in them, impressed upon their souls. How? We know that when Islam came, it faced diverse camps, and these camps were corrupting the movement of human beings in life. The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, created the universe subjected to man, and He wants man to remain a guardian of the goodness of the universe, or to increase the goodness of the universe, and not to allow corruption to seep into the good.

This is the purpose of the Truth in the existence of a method (manhaj) for man. The aim of the method is to protect the whole movement of life from corruption and to increase the fitness of the universe, so our work in the universe is always for our own benefit. No act performed by a creature adds to the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, any attribute beyond His perfections, because the Truth possesses the perfection of attributes. He is the One who created us, brought us into being, and sustained us, and our obligation from Him added nothing to Him, for He, glorified is He, is self-sufficient in His essence, independent of all His creation.

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, came therefore to fight against camps: the camp of the people of polytheism in Makkah, and the camp of the People of the Book. It was expected of the People of the Book that they have a connection with heaven and familiarity with the methods of the messengers, and with the miracles of the messengers, and that they have the good tidings of the Messenger of Allah in their books. And the camp of the hypocrites, who appeared after the strength of Islam had grown, so they declared entry into Islam while they had not believed, but rather concealed disbelief.

When we pause at the camp of the People of the Book, it was natural that the Messenger of Allah would expect them to believe, because he came with the method that strengthens the connection of heaven with earth, if they had been truthful and eager for that connection. Especially since they often boasted of the coming of the Prophet before the message came. They used to say to the Aws and the Khazraj:

'The time of a prophet has drawn near, who will come confirming what we say; we will follow him and kill you with him, a killing like that of 'Ad and Iram.'

On this the Truth said: ﴿Previously they used to seek victory over those who disbelieved. But when there came to them what they recognized, they disbelieved in it﴾ (part of 2:89).

Their scriptures also told them: the Prophet comes in a land of palm trees, and this applies to the place of his mission, peace and blessings be upon him and his family. So they knew the place, they knew the characteristics, and they knew the fronts on which he would fight, because it had previously happened to their prophets to fight in them. When Muhammad came as a messenger from Allah, their temporal authority was shaken, and they wanted to preserve it by distorting the method of heaven. Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, came with the divine method to restore the movement of the universe to faith. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, entered Madinah while they were weaving the crown as a diadem for a king they would install.

Thus the Messenger of Allah ended their temporal authority, and they no longer had standing. He united the Aws and the Khazraj, whereas the Jews had lived on the discord between them, through selling weapons and lending at interest. With the coming of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, the structure of their power collapsed. Therefore they tried to encourage the enemies of the Messenger of Allah while he was still in Makkah, to defeat the new religion so that it would not advance to Madinah and nullify their authority.

On this the Truth said:

﴿Indeed, those who sell the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price—those will have no share in the Hereafter, and Allah will not speak to them or look at them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, and they will have a painful punishment﴾ (3:77).

The small price is pomp, leadership, and the seat of rule. Here is Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, the chief of the Jews, who had wealth and eloquence, going out to Quraysh to discuss the necessity of burying and eliminating the new religion. Quraysh said to him: 'You are of the People of the Book and have a connection with heaven.'

So he said to them: 'You are more guided than Muhammad as to the way!!' How could the idol-worshipping polytheists be more guided than Muhammad as to the way?

Thus we see His saying: ﴿You see many of them allying themselves with those who disbelieve.﴾ They allied with the camp of polytheism, with which they had enmity, so that power would not slip from their hands. And they cooperated with those who associated partners with Allah to halt the advance of the new religion.

﴿You see many of them allying themselves with those who disbelieve. Wretched is what their souls have sent forward for them, that Allah is angry with them, and in the punishment they will abide eternally.﴾ (5:80)

'Yatawallawnahum' means they support them, aid them, and assist them, and claim that they are upon the truth, as if the new religion were upon falsehood. The Truth here swears that it is wretched what the commanding soul (al-nafs al-ammarah bi'l-su') adorned for them, because they lacked the self-reproaching soul (al-nafs al-lawwamah), and the commanding soul overcame them.

The verse continues: ﴿that Allah is angry with them, and in the punishment they will abide eternally.﴾ Anger leads to turning away from the path of guidance, and turning away from the path of guidance leads to everlasting punishment. As if the Truth clarifies to them: suppose you took a little enjoyment in this life, you have brought upon yourselves lasting hardships awaiting you in the Hereafter."

Almighty Allah says next: ﴿Had they truly believed in Allah, and in the Prophet, and in what was revealed to him, they would not have taken them as allies. But most of them are defiant transgressors.﴾ (5:81)

If they truly had faith in Allah through the method sent down by Allah, they would not have taken the people of polytheism (shirk) as allies. But most of these people are people of defiance (fisq). We note that "most" of them are defiant, and this means that the few are not defiant.

The Almighty says, after that:

﴿You will surely find the most intense of people in enmity toward those who believe to be the Jews and those who associate partners with God; and you will surely find the nearest of them in affection to those who believe to be those who say, "We are Christians." That is because among them are priests and monks, and because they are not arrogant.﴾

God, glory be to Him, swears to His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that the reality of life with two groups such as the Jews and the Christians will become clear, even though each side opposes the Messenger of God in some respect. Their inclinations and desires differ, but they all agree on one goal.

The Jews were the most intense in enmity because they had taken temporal authority, which made them the masters of the region. The Christians, however, had no sovereignty or temporal authority, and they were devoted to worshipping God in their hermitages and churches. The side that has no temporal authority does not become hostile to one who comes to strip the people of injustice of their temporal power and to establish justice among people. So what is the cause of this?

God says: ﴿and you will surely find the nearest of them in affection to those who believe, those who say, "We are Christians." That is because among them are priests and monks.﴾ The word *al-qissisun* (priests) is the plural of *qiss*, the one devoted to divine knowledge. *Al-ruhban* (monks) are those who devote themselves to worship. So the priest's task is to teach knowledge, and the monk's task is to carry out what knowledge requires and to live an ascetic life.

Here we find that God, the Almighty, has bestowed two favours, and by them He made them nearest in affection to those who believe. He bestowed that among them are priests who preserve the knowledge of the Book, and that among them are monks who carry out the meaning of what knowledge requires. Thus they became nearest in affection to those who believe, provided they remain in this condition, because the cause revolves with the effect, existence and non-existence alike. Since He, glory be to Him, gave as the reason that among them are priests and monks and that they are not arrogant, this is because they do not aspire to leadership, and they have no pride or haughtiness. Their religion gives them a great spiritual energy, so much so that they say: "Whoever strikes you on your right cheek, turn to him the left cheek." This gives them a charge of faith which we see radiating from them.

﴿That is because among them are priests and monks, and because they are not arrogant.﴾ The reality of the universe has confirmed this. The positions of the Jews toward the Messenger of God, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, are well known. They were overcome by baseness, malice took hold of them, and treachery drove them to the point of wanting to drop a stone on him to kill him, and they tried to slip poison to him.

When you find a person who has no way out of his opponent except by killing him, you can confront him saying: "You do not possess the courage to face him while he is alive; if you had that courage, you would not have thought of killing him." This is evidence that he is weaker than him and not braver than him. If he had to face this opponent directly in the course of life, he would not think of killing him, because the weak person is the one who sees the opponent's life as a burden on him.

The Jews were indeed characterized by this weakness during the time of the Messenger of God, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. We know that when he openly proclaimed his call, some people followed him, but these first believers suffered persecution from their own families and kin. Even one household was split. For example, Umm Habiba, Lady Ruqayya—who was the daughter of Abu Sufyan—believed, while her father was the chief of the disbelievers at that time. Umm Habiba went with her husband to Abyssinia, and the Messenger of God, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was keen on these cells of faith, because he knew they would give birth to faith afterward. By that emigration to Abyssinia he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, wanted to protect the seeds of faith so that they would become the centre from which faith would spread afterward, because they would carry out a task of faith. Courage, as we know, requires caution. Our poet Ahmad Shawqi, may Allah have mercy on him, said in one of his prose pieces which he titled *Aswaq al-Dhahab* (The Markets of Gold): "Sometimes courage requires you to be a coward for an hour?"

This courage is not directed only at the enemy; it is also courage in confronting one's own self. For example, if a group of powerful men were sitting together in a night gathering, and a vagabond entered carrying a pistol and began hurling insults at each of them, these men would then trick him until they could overpower him and punish him.

So courage requires that a person be cowardly for a moment until he can overcome his opponent. This is shrewdness and cunning. Faith is not suicide. Rather, faith requires that the believer not enter a battle unless he has calculated the gain. Here is the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, naming Khalid ibn al-Walid "the Drawn Sword of God" in a battle in which Khalid did not achieve a decisive victory, but achieved a negative victory by knowing how to withdraw the army. Ordering the withdrawal of an army requires more strength than what is needed for victory. The victor has the wind with him; the defeated has the wind against him.

We find the Noble Qur'an saying: ﴿And whoever turns his back to them on that day, unless he is maneuvering for battle or joining another company, has earned anger from God, and his refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination.﴾ (Surah al-Anfal).

So manoeuvring and craft are part of military skill, because they afterward make it possible to confront the enemy.

The divine light illuminates the insight of the Messenger of God, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, so he surveys the whole earth until he chooses a safe place for these believers to go to, and he chose Abyssinia. He did not wish to order them to go to any tribe among the tribes, because he knew that all the tribes of the Peninsula feared Quraysh, since the pilgrimage season gathered the tribes under the authority of Quraysh. Whoever stood against the will of Quraysh would be exposed to hardships. Accordingly, the Messenger of God would not feel safe for the cells of faith if they went to a tribe. The Messenger of God, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, surveyed the whole earth and chose Abyssinia. Why?

Here are the words of the Messenger of God, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, which have remained until our time: "In it is a king under whose rule no one is wronged, so stay in his land until God grants you a way out of what you are in."¹

In the narration of al-Zuhri: When the Muslims increased and the torture by the disbelievers became apparent, he, peace be upon him, said: "Scatter in the land of God, for God will gather you." They said: "Where shall we go?" He said: "Here," and he pointed with his hand toward the land of Abyssinia.²

They slipped out under cover of night onto the road heading to Abyssinia. When Quraysh learned of the news, they tried to cut off the road to bring them back to Mecca, to continue the campaign against them and to punish them in order to turn them away from Islam. But God willed a different matter, and the road was easy, and they reached Abyssinia, and God saved them from the plot of the disbelievers.

The Messenger of God, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, possessed, by what his Lord had taught him, complete knowledge of the land, and he knew which rulers oppressed and which did not. The Messenger was right in his faithful insight. When the emigrant believers went to Abyssinia, they found that they had entered a house of security, where they were safe in their religion. The madness of Quraysh grew, and they wanted to reclaim these people from the Negus, the king of Abyssinia, so they sent their chieftains with gifts and rare presents for the king of Abyssinia.

Amr ibn al-As, Abdullah ibn Abi Rabi'a, and Umara ibn al-Walid ibn al-Mughira travelled. The delegation of Quraysh asked the Negus to hand over these emigrants to them, and they tried to slander the emigrants before the Negus. They accused the Muslim emigrants of being people who had abandoned the religion of their fathers and adopted a new religion opposed to all religions. They said about Jesus son of Mary a statement that is not fitting for him or for his mother. The Negus refused to believe a single letter of this, and he asked to hear from these emigrants. Ja'far ibn Abi Talib stepped forward and said:

"O King, we were a people of ignorance; we worshipped idols, ate carrion, committed abominations, severed kinship ties, mistreated neighbours, and the strong among us devoured the weak. We remained in that state until God sent to us a messenger from among us whose lineage, truthfulness, trustworthiness and chastity we knew. He called us to God, that we should affirm His oneness and worship Him, and cast off what we and our fathers used to worship besides Him of stones and idols. He commanded us to speak the truth, to fulfil trusts, to maintain ties of kinship, to be good to neighbours, and to refrain from forbidden things and from bloodshed. He forbade us from abominations, false speech, consuming the property of orphans, and slandering chaste women. He commanded us to worship God alone and not to associate anything with Him, and He commanded us to pray, to pay zakat, and to fast. We believed in him, affirmed him, and followed him in what he brought from God, worshipping God alone and not associating anything with Him. He made lawful for us what God made lawful and forbade us what God forbade. Our people then attacked us, tortured us and tried to turn us away from our religion, to make us return to worshipping idols and abandon the worship of God, the Exalted, and to make lawful for us the wickedness we had been in. When they overpowered us, oppressed us, and came between us and our religion, we left for your country, chose you over anyone else, and hoped that we would not be wronged in your presence."

It became clear to the Negus that the Messiah, according to the testimony of the Qur'an, was a prophet, pure and chaste in honour. Thus he did not listen to the slander of the delegation of Quraysh. The heart of the Negus was filled with faith, and he did not become arrogant even though he was a king, and he stood against the attempts of Quraysh to harm the companions of the Messenger of God, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. When he heard what had been revealed to the Messenger of God, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, from the Surah of Maryam, he said: "Indeed this and what Jesus brought come from one and the same niche (lamp)."

The Messenger of God knew that faith had penetrated the heart of the Negus, as evidenced by the fact that Umm Habiba bint Abi Sufyan, when she emigrated with her husband to Abyssinia and her husband became a Christian, still remained upon her religion even though she loved him with pure love. Here Umm Habiba separated from her husband, so that the truth would establish that her emigration was for God.

God willed, through the tongue of His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to honour her and to honour the Negus for his stance of not handing over the believers to the delegation of Quraysh, and for his testimony in favour of Islam that it comes from the same niche from which the Gospel of Jesus, peace be upon him, came forth. Therefore the Messenger of God, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, made him the guardian of her marriage to Umm Habiba, because he was trusted regarding what he knew of the Gospel, trusted regarding what he heard of the Qur'an about Maryam, and trusted in that he did not hand over the emigrants. So he chose him as his agent in marrying Umm Habiba after her husband had become a Christian. This single incident illuminated more than one stance: the stance of Umm Habiba, who proved that she had not emigrated merely following her husband, for had she followed her husband she would have become a Christian as he did; and it illuminated that the Messenger of God did not speak from desire when he said in advance about the Negus: "No one is wronged in his land." When the Messenger received news of the Negus's death, he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed the funeral prayer for him in absentia.

﴿You will surely find the most intense of people in enmity toward those who believe to be the Jews and those who associate partners with God; and you will surely find the nearest of them in affection to those who believe to be those who say, "We are Christians." That is because among them are priests and monks, and because they are not arrogant.﴾ (Surah al-Ma'ida).

This is a favour from God in that He made among them priests who teach, which is a tribute to knowledge, and monks who carry out the dictates of knowledge. So let us know that we must distinguish between the scholar, whose knowledge may be taken from him even if he does not act upon it, and we must respect those who worship God in application of the knowledge of God, and leave aside those who do not act upon their knowledge, so that they may receive their recompense. But we must take their knowledge and act upon it. "Take my knowledge and do not look to my deeds; gather the fruits and leave the wood for the fire."

We also find that His saying, the Truth: ﴿That is because among them are priests and monks﴾ is a reason that makes them nearest in affection to the Muslims. So is monasticism praiseworthy in God's sight? If it is praiseworthy in God's sight, why did He, glory be to Him, say:

﴿Then We followed up on their footsteps with Our messengers, and We followed up with Jesus, son of Mary, and We gave him the Gospel, and We placed in the hearts of those who followed him compassion and mercy. But monasticism they invented; We did not prescribe it for them, but they sought the pleasure of God. Yet they did not observe it with its proper observance. So We gave those who believed among them their reward, but many of them are defiantly disobedient.﴾ (Surah al-Hadid, 27).

He, glory be to Him, is telling us about the procession of the messengers until it reached Jesus, peace be upon him, and m

The Lord says, after that: ﴿And when they hear what has been sent down to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflow with tears because of the truth they recognize. They say: "Our Lord, we believe, so write us down among the witnesses."﴾ (5:83)

This is the precision of Qur'anic expression, which came before scholars exhausted themselves studying the phenomena and conditions of the human soul in the field of psychology, through research, induction and experiment, and the effect of that on the functions of the organs. Science has said that every instrument has a function: the eye sees, the ear hears, the tongue tastes and speaks, the nose smells, and the hand touches. At the outset, scholars said these are the five outer senses, and the word "outer" (al-Zahira) was added as a precaution, because there are matters a person feels without perceiving how or from where the feeling arises, such as hunger or thirst, or when comparing two things to judge which is heavier.

Scholars tried to understand how a person distinguishes one weight from another, and they said there is a sense called the muscular sense (hassat al-adal): when a person carries something, the muscles exert effort to a degree that allows him to distinguish levels of effort. They also knew of a sense called the sense of touch-texture (hassat al-bayn), by which a person distinguishes the smoothness or thickness of any kind of cloth, even if the thickness is one tenth of a millimetre.

So there are many senses through which a person can perceive, and there are faculties that leave some trace on the human soul, such as the traces of love and inclination or hatred and aversion, whose seat is the emotion (al-wijdan). Such as perceiving the sweetness of the taste of something, or disliking something else. If a person finds something pleasant, he takes it again, and this act is an impulse (nuz'ah) that follows the emotion, which follows the perception.

So there is perceiving (idrak) that perceives, there is emotion (wijdan) that feels, and there is impulse (naz'ah) that inclines. For example, perceiving a rose of beautiful form and colour in a garden; this perception may bring love and affection to the heart, that is, an emotion. You are free to perceive what you wish and to feel what you wish, but you may not stretch out your hand to pick the rose, because the Shari'ah forbids it. The garden's guard also prevents you from that. Yet no one prevents you from looking at the rose and enjoying its beauty. Thus perception is permissible, and emotion is permissible.

As for impulse, this is the matter in which the Shari'ah intervenes. We may repeat that perception is permissible and emotion is permissible, except in perceiving the beauty of womanhood, where the Shari'ah intervenes from the outset. You may perceive a woman's beauty and find in yourself love and inclination; if you act on the impulse, how can you control yourself? After perception and emotion, you either act or suppress. If you act, you violate people's honour; if you suppress, you suffer oppression and pain. Therefore the Shari'ah intervenes in this matter from its beginning, forbidding you to perceive by a clear command, which is lowering the gaze, because the sexual matter is difficult to separate into parts: perception can be separated from emotion, and impulse can be separated from emotion and perception in the matter of the rose. But in the sexual matter it is a raging fire, which a person must meet either by chastity or by plunging into it. If a person is chaste, he suppresses and becomes tense; if he plunges into people's honour, this causes the violation of people's honour. For this reason the Shari'ah prevents the matter of perception from the start.

This noble verse came before psychologists arrived to explain the matters of perception, emotion and impulse. Here the Truth says: ﴿And when they hear﴾, and this is perception through the sense of hearing. What is heard? The Qur'an answers: ﴿what has been sent down to the Messenger﴾. This is the cause of the emotion that appears in His words: ﴿you see their eyes overflow with tears because of the truth they recognize﴾. So what is their impulse after this emotion? They say: ﴿"Our Lord, we believe, so write us down among the witnesses"﴾; this is the impulsive act. The Qur'an, which was sent down fourteen centuries ago, set out the order of perception, emotion and impulse before science came to it. When they heard with the ear, something happened in the emotion, and the change in the emotion had signs that appeared in their eyes, which overflowed with tears.

Here we distinguish two matters. The first is (ightirar al-ayn), the welling of the eye with tears, that is, the eye is filled with tears but the emotion has not reached the point where the tears fall from the eye; it is said: "the eye of so-and-so welled up," meaning his eye was filled with tears but they did not fall. The second is the overflowing of tears from the eye, and overflowing (fayd) occurs only as a result of the container being filled by its contents, as though the tears had filled it completely, just as when we fill a vessel or a cup to the brim so that it overflows.

So the cause of all this was that they knew the Qur'an is from the Truth. We notice that (min) is repeated in this expression: ﴿And when they hear what has been sent down to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflow with tears because of the truth they recognize﴾. Thus (min) precedes the tears, and (min) is assimilated into (ma), so they become together (mimma), and (min) precedes the truth.

In ﴿overflow with tears (min al-dam'),﴾ the (min) here is the (min) of origin (al-ibtida'iyya). In ﴿because of the truth they recognize (mimma 'arafu)﴾ the (min) here is causal, that is, because they recognized that this Qur'an was sent down from the Truth, may He be glorified. And (min al-haqq) in ﴿the truth (min al-haqq)﴾ is partitive, that is, they recognized some of the truth, because they did not hear the whole Qur'an.

Thus (min) occurs three times, and each occurrence has its place to contribute to the rhetorical whole that describes the three aspects of perception, emotion and impulse. These levels are the aspects of consciousness at which experimental science arrived when it sought to know the functions of the organs and the extent of their penetration into perception, emotion and impulse.

The impulse is what concerns us here. They said: ﴿so write us down among the witnesses﴾, and faith is a matter that returns to them. But being written among the witnesses is a matter that returns to others, as though the believer attains a high rank: he believes for himself, and then afterwards becomes a vessel and a tongue conveying the method of faith to others, because he is not a witness unless his testimony is an extension of the testimony of the Messenger. This is the fulfilment of His, glorified and exalted be He, saying:

﴿You are the best nation brought forth for mankind; you enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and you believe in Allah. And if the People of the Scripture had believed, it would have been better for them. Among them are believers, but most of them are defiantly disobedient.﴾ (3:110)

That is: you, O nation of Muhammad, are the best nation brought forth for people, not by lineage or descent, but by following a method. Whoever follows the method through "do" and "do not" is the one who applies the act of faith in Allah. Among the People of the Scripture are those who believe in Allah and become Muslims, but many of them go beyond the limits of faith. There is another verse in which the Truth says:

﴿And thus We have made you a middle nation that you may be witnesses over the people and the Messenger may be a witness over you. And We did not make the qiblah which you used to face except that We might make evident who would follow the Messenger from who would turn back on his heels. And indeed, it was [a change] difficult except for those whom Allah guided. And Allah would not have caused your faith to be lost. Indeed, Allah is to the people Kind and Merciful.﴾ (2:143)

So the nation that follows the method of Islam, which is the method of moderation, is the guided nation that proceeds to righteous action, performs it and applies it, because it is the method that abrogates and corrects what came before it. The Messenger, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, is the guardian over all the messengers before him, and his life, with what came in it of conduct, is a faith-based sunnah guiding believers to the straight path. In this verse the matter of the change of qiblah came to teach the Muslims that the first command to face Bayt al-Maqdis was a test, in which he succeeds who submits to the Lord of every command, who is Allah; and that was among the difficult matters except for those whom Allah guided. Then came the command to change the qiblah to the Ka'bah, which is the first house established by Allah for mankind.

So, since we are witnesses, and since the Messenger is a witness over us, the Messenger bears witness that we have conveyed, and we attain two ranks: the rank of receiving the message from the Messenger, and the rank of conveying it afterwards to other people. The believer is not a witness unless his testimony is an extension of the testimony of the Messenger, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. This is the testimony the Truth described in the description of the community of believers:

﴿You are the best nation brought forth for mankind; you enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and you believe in Allah. And if the People of the Scripture had believed, it would have been better for them. Among them are believers, but most of them are defiantly disobedient.﴾ (3:110)

So you, O nation of Muhammad, are the best nation Allah has brought forth for people, on condition that you follow the method of "do" and "do not". You enjoin obedience and forbid everything the religion has forbidden, and in this way you have applied the method that shows the sincerity of your faith in Allah, a true and sincere faith. Had the People of the Scripture been sincere in their faith as you are, it would have been better for them than what they are upon. But some of them keep the matter of faith within their hearts, and most of them go out and transgress against what faith requires.

So when they said: ﴿"We believe, so write us down among the witnesses"﴾, that was an acknowledgement that their faith was a faith of the self and a faith of conveying to others. By this they entered Islam and became of the community of Muhammad, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. And here is the Messenger, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, saying: "None of you believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself." (1)

And here the Truth defines for us the value of the good word that conveys from Allah:

﴿Have you not considered how Allah presents an example: a good word is like a good tree, its root firmly fixed and its branches in the sky. It gives its fruit at all times by the permission of its Lord. And Allah presents examples for the people that they might remember.﴾ (14:24–25)

The good word is a tree which has fruits that benefit people and shelters with its tender shade those who hear it, and it has a root firmly planted in the earth, and branches rising toward the sky. It gives fruit at every time by the will of its Creator. This tangible, material meaning is what Allah strikes as a parable for people, so that they may know the value of lofty meanings. Thus its speaker, the one who speaks the truth in conveying the method of faith to people, will continue to pluck the fruits of this word as long as a believing person remains, until we meet Allah.

﴿So write us down among the witnesses﴾: the witness is the one who conveys. When a believer asks Allah to write him among the witnesses, he is asking for himself a station with the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs and the righteous. The martyr is not only one who is killed; the martyr is one who gives his testimony. A martyr in a battle of faith that costs him his life is a person who has given testimony that what he went to is more precious than his whole life. In that he gives practical testimony.

Then the Almighty says:

﴿And why should we not believe in Allah and in what has come to us of the truth, and hope that our Lord will admit us along with the righteous people?﴾ (5:84)

When wonder is expressed here, its meaning is that a person must know that his faith in Allah is a matter that brings him good for himself. When we believe in Allah, the truth meets us with an overflowing generosity of tranquility, goodness and bounty. So beware, O people, of thinking that faith came to restrict your freedoms or that it prevents you from desiring things. Rather, faith came to elevate freedom and to elevate desire, so that a person does not take it as something fleeting that ends with the end of this world, but takes it as something everlasting for as long as the heavens and the earth endure.

Thus religion came with sensible utilitarianism (al-nafʿiyyah al-ʿāqilah), because the intelligent person takes from benefit, in proportion to his lifespan, only what is slight and harms no one. If it harms the self or others, religion commands leaving that benefit, for benefit either escapes a person or a person escapes it. The clever one is he who prefers the benefit of others over his own benefit.

An example of this: a beggar comes to you asking for food because he has not eaten for two days, and you have in your pocket only one pound, so you give it to him. By doing so you prefer him over yourself, and you are thereby among those of whom the Almighty said:

﴿And those who were settled in the abode and in faith before them love those who emigrate to them, and do not find in their breasts any need for what they have been given, and prefer them over themselves, even though they themselves were in privation. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his own soul – it is those who are the successful.﴾ (59:9)

By such conduct a person has followed the example of the Helpers (al-Anṣār), who hosted the emigrants (al-Muhājirūn) and sincerely held faith, loving its people, and who found no resentment or envy regarding what was given to the emigrants from the spoils (fayʾ) and other things. Their chief concern was that the emigrants be happy, and they had already preferred them with things that were theirs, and they accepted for themselves freedom from stinginess; Allah protected them from the evil of stinginess, and they were among the successful. The one who gives a pound in charity takes from Allah ten times its like, and this is great utilitarianism. When the Sharia commanded us to lower the gaze from what is forbidden of others, the one who carries this out is protected by Allah, and He lowers everyone's eyes from what is forbidden to Him. Is this not utilitarianism? Thus it is folly for a person to suppose that religion restricts freedom, for religion elevates freedom and develops it, and develops benefit for the believer by coming between him and foolish utilitarianism.

I always give this example: suppose a man has two sons. The first wakes in the morning and does what his father taught him: he performs ablution, prays, and goes to his studies after taking his breakfast. As for the second son, he wakes only with difficulty and keeps feigning sleep until mid-morning, then leaves the house for the café. Each of the two sons wanted benefit for himself: the first wanted deferred benefit, and the second wanted immediate benefit. After ten years the first son graduates to be successful and prosperous in life, while the second remains a failed vagabond. So both looked to benefit, but their lenses differ.

And beware of understanding that there is a person who does not love himself. No, we all love ourselves. But there is one who loves himself with a love that grants himself lasting existence, so he strives and struggles, and may become a martyr; and another who loves himself with narrowness of vision, so he preserves his life through cowardice, though he has died a thousand deaths during this cowardice, and lost his dignity out of concern for a life that will not add to its length a single day. Al-Mutanabbi says:

"I see that all of us seek life for ourselves,
eager for it, yet holding it cheap when we are patient.
The coward's love of self brings him to fear (al-tuqā),
while the brave man's love of self brings him to war."

al-Tuqā: caution and fear.

Therefore the one who reflects deeply on the matter of religion says to himself: ﴿And why should we not believe in Allah and in what has come to us of the truth﴾, and the believer sees it as strange not to believe, since he aspires to the station of the believer. ﴿And hope that our Lord will admit us along with the righteous people﴾. Thus the believer seeks the station of the righteous person.

Then Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿So Allah rewarded them for what they said with gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein eternally. And that is the reward of the doers of good.﴾

This is the word of truth that is spoken in every place and at every time. It was spoken by the Negus, the king of Abyssinia (al-Habasha), who had authority over the people of standing among Quraysh, whose falsehood had tyrannised them. Therefore this word carried its weight. When he heard what had been revealed of the Qur'an from Surat Maryam, he said: "Indeed, this and what Jesus brought come forth from one niche (mishkah)." So it is a word of truth with weight, and Allah, glory be to Him, bestows abundant giving upon everyone who supports the truth, even with a single word. He, glory be to Him, is (al-Shakur), the One who gives much in return for little, and (al-Muhsin), the One who multiplies the reward for the doers of good.

We should recognise that speech has great importance, because it is then linked to conduct. The Negus's statement was great, but his lifespan fell short of his continuing to act upon what he had said. He spoke his word, and then the authorisation came from the Messenger of Allah to contract marriage for the Messenger to Umm Habibah, daughter of Abu Sufyan. He concluded the contract for her as a representative (wakil) of the Messenger of Allah, ﷺ, and paid her dowry from his own wealth. Then he died, and the rulings of Islam had not yet reached him so that he could apply them. Therefore it sufficed him that he said this word, and for this reason the Prophet performed the funeral prayer for him in absentia (salat al-ghaib).

There is also the story of Mukhayriq the Jew. His heart had been saturated with Islam and filled with it, and he was extremely wealthy. He said to the Jews: "All my wealth is for Muhammad, and I will go out to fight alongside him." He went out to battle with the Messenger of Allah, ﷺ, was killed, and died as a martyr, though he had never prayed a single rak'ah in his whole life. Therefore mere speech opens the way to action.

﴿So Allah rewarded them for what they said with gardens beneath which rivers flow.﴾ The Truth wishes to affirm for us that every movement of faith, even if it is merely speech, takes its perfection from its duration. We know that faith in Makkah was faith by speech, for people believed before the rulings had descended, since most of the rulings were revealed in Madinah. On that basis Allah rewarded the believers merely because they spoke the word of faith. This happened before the Truth had sent down the command to comprehensive proclamation, which is His saying:

﴿And warn your closest kindred﴾ (part of verse 214, Surat al-Shu'ara').

These people, Allah rewarded with a good recompense and named them (muhsinin). And likewise the Negus did: he went to faith without being summoned to it, and that was before the Messenger of Allah, ﷺ, wrote his call to the kings to believe. On this basis the Negus is a muhsin, because he leapt to faith before being asked. Whenever the Truth speaks of a station of faith, He also addresses its counterpart, so that the admonition reaches its full aims. When He speaks of the people of Paradise, He follows it with a discussion of the people of the Fire, and when He speaks of the people of the Fire, He follows it with a discussion of the people of Paradise, because the human soul is prepared for a thing and its opposite.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 5, verse 86:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says, after that:
﴿And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs – they are the companions of the Blazing Fire.﴾

We know that the word (ṣāḥib, "companion"), the word (ṣuḥba, "companionship") and the word (aṣḥāb, "companions") all indicate constant association, and constant association in life is chosen, not compelled; no one accompanies another by force.

From His words ﴿companions of the Blazing Fire﴾ we might understand that this means a mutual passion between the Fire and its people, and this is not what is meant. It is either said in mockery and ridicule of them, or what is meant is complete attachment and lasting companionship that never separates or ends. After the Truth had spoken of the polytheists, then spoke of the Jews, and then spoke of the Christians, He now speaks of the believers. He first shakes our minds to clear away what has clung to them of the matter of the opponents and their methods, and then He brings us the rulings after that. He did this in this surah, which begins with the verse of the contracts:

﴿O you who believe, fulfil the contracts﴾ (part of verse 1, Surat al-Ma'idah).

The covenant of faith is that which rises and soars above what the polytheists say and departs from what the Jews and Christians say. After that we notice that the Truth, after speaking of the necessity of fulfilling contracts, obliges the believers to the method that protects the movement of life. The movement of life is sustained first by food and drink. Therefore He said:

﴿Lawful for you are the beasts of grazing livestock﴾ (part of verse 1, Surat al-Ma'idah).

After sustaining the movement of life through food and drink, here He says (harrama, "He has forbidden"). Here we pause: when God makes lawful some of the kinds of existence, and forbids other kinds of existence, a questioner may rationally ask: since the Truth has forbidden these things, why did He create them? In our ordinary life we know that every maker specifies the properties of his product. For example, the maker of an aircraft designs his aircraft and specifies the fuel it needs, and it cannot run on car fuel; if machines made by humans are damaged when we use what does not suit them, how then can we say to our Maker: why did You create things that do not suit us? There must be a purpose for them in the universe and another use by which they produce things beneficial to us. An example of this is the venom of the snake: it kills a human, but God inspired the human with the ability to use the venom of the snake to kill some microbes.

Thus the world was created by God with a specific composition. For example, we find the crocodile lying on the shore, and birds pick from its mouth some of their food, and it does not harm them, because these birds are the ones that alert the crocodile when prey comes to hunt it; the birds are keen on their source of sustenance and preserve the crocodile's life. And we use electricity in its field, but in its reverse field it shocks and destroys.

Therefore it is not for a human to ask: why did God forbid certain things to the human? Because those things have a role in life. It is not right to turn the means into the end. The Truth intended by the lawful and the unlawful that the human benefit from what is good for him. An example: God forbade the eating of pork. The pig was created only to eat microbes. Therefore it is not for the human to turn the means into an end. And every day the Truth gives Islam a strength of support that comes to it from the enemies of Islam.

An example of this: we find that diseases spread at high rates among the nations that consume pork and drink wine, and there is a disease called (cirrhosis of the liver) that spreads in those countries. Would we have delayed carrying out God's command until laboratories arose and told us the results of eating pork? Or was it enough for us to forbid to ourselves what God has forbidden? We must carry out God's commands for our own protection:

﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the Truth﴾ (part of verse 53, Surat Fussilat).

Every day a sign appears to us that confirms the truth of our faith in God. Therefore let no one say: why did God create those forbidden things? God created them as a means, not an end. An example: God created petroleum for us so that we extract fuel from it; does any one of us have the ability to drink petroleum?! Thus permitting and forbidding are for the benefit of the human. If the human departs from that, let him blame no one but himself. Therefore the Truth says:

﴿Say: Have you considered what God has sent down to you of provision, and you made from it the unlawful and the lawful?﴾ (part of verse 59, Surat Yunus).

It is as if the Truth denounces our making unlawful things out of what He created as lawful, and our forbidding things He has made lawful, such as the abandonment of the baḥīrah, the sā'ibah and the waṣīlah, all of which are provisions from God. He, glory be to Him, is the Creator of all things, and He is the One who determines their benefit or harmlessness for the human. The baḥīrah was the she-camel whose ear they split so that no one would touch her after she had given birth to five litters, the last of which was a male; they would let her loose in the pastures, not ridden, not milked, and no pasture or water was withheld from her. They used to say she belonged to the gods. When we investigate who benefits from her, we find that the priests are the ones who benefit. Likewise the sā'ibah: they would leave her as a voluntary offering, no one would ride her or milk her, and the one who benefited from her was also the priests. Likewise the waṣīlah, which is a female born in a single birth with a male; they said she had joined her brother, so they did not slaughter the male for their gods. Likewise they would let loose the stallion from whose loins ten litters had come, and they said: he has protected his back, so he is not ridden, nor is any load carried on him, and he is not prevented from water or pasture. And the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, clarifies for us: I did not forbid these things, so why do you forbid them?

Al-Sha'rawi, the commentary (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 5, verse 87:

He, glory be to Him, has forbidden carrion and blood because He is the One who determined and clarified what is lawful and what is unlawful. And He, glory be to Him, is the One who provides sustenance, which at times is direct sustenance and at other times is indirect sustenance. For this reason the Truth came with the noble word:

﴿O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that Allah has made lawful for you, and do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not like the transgressors (87)﴾.

So the matter of prohibition is entrusted to the Creator of the human machine, and the matter of permission is entrusted to the Creator of the human machine. You, O human being, must never interfere in that at all. For human interference sometimes takes the form of forbidding what Allah has made lawful, and sometimes the form of permitting what Allah has forbidden.

Beware, O human being, of forbidding what Allah has made lawful for you, and beware of permitting what Allah has forbidden to you. We are here facing several stages. Do not believe that there is a matter that Allah has made lawful yet is unlawful, and do not say that there is a matter that Allah has made lawful yet is unlawful; do not refrain from a matter that Allah has made lawful, thinking it unlawful; do not issue a fatwa about a matter that Allah has made lawful as being unlawful; and do not make something that Allah has made lawful into something you forbid yourself. So let no one vow not to eat lamb or oranges – by way of example – for a vow in that regard is not permissible, because making forbidden the things that are lawful by a vow is itself a forbidden act. For this reason the Truth taught us, saying to His Messenger:

﴿Why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you?﴾ (part of verse 1, surah al-Tahrim). We must be conscious of this matter and know its stages: do not believe, do not say, do not forbid, do not issue a fatwa, do not vow. Why? Because in that there is transgression.

The Blessed and Exalted Truth says: ﴿Do not forbid the good things that Allah has made lawful for you, and do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not like the transgressors (87)﴾

(part of verse 87, surah al-Ma'idah).

And what is transgression? It is going beyond the limit in what Allah has forbidden or in what Allah has made lawful; that is, Allah loves those who stop at the limits. He, glory be to Him, says once: ﴿These are the limits of Allah, so do not approach them﴾ (part of verse 187, surah al-Baqarah), and once He says: ﴿These are the limits of Allah, so do not transgress them﴾ (part of verse 229, surah al-Baqarah).

So regarding what is prohibited: do not approach; and regarding what Allah has permitted: do not exceed. Therefore the saying came on the tongue of the noble Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "What is lawful is clear and what is unlawful is clear, and between them are doubtful matters that many people do not know. Whoever avoids doubtful matters has cleared his religion and his honour, and whoever falls into doubtful matters falls into the unlawful, like a shepherd who grazes around the sanctuary, about to fall into it. Surely every king has a sanctuary, and the sanctuary of Allah on earth is His prohibitions. Surely in the body there is a piece of flesh: if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt; surely it is the heart."(1)

So every creature has its characteristics and has a role in existence. You, O human being, must not turn the means into an end. There are many creatures that are means and are not fit to be ends. For this reason the Truth commanded us to take what benefits us directly and to leave the things He forbade us; so we do not approach – by way of example – the flesh of swine, because the swine is a creature created to free you from microbes. If you eat it, you have turned the means into an end. It is incumbent on you, O human being, to keep the means as means and the end as end. And the One who determines this for you is the One who made you… it is Allah.

Evidence for this is that the opponents of Islam discover every day the characteristics that Islam brought, and they turn towards them. By Allah's prohibition, and by our faith in this prohibition, we are spared the troubles of experimentation until it is proven; and the disbelievers who did not believe were compelled by circumstances to take it. On this basis, everything made lawful or unlawful by the commands of Allah shows us its benefit or its harm, in accordance with the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted:

﴿We shall show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves, until it becomes clear to them that it is the Truth. Does it not suffice that your Lord is witness over all things? (53)﴾ (surah Fussilat).

So there is no belief that a lawful thing is unlawful, nor any saying to that effect, nor any refraining, nor does any person issue a fatwa to that effect. And the command comes: ﴿and do not transgress; indeed Allah does not like the transgressors﴾. We know that transgression is only that we exceed the limit in what He forbade or in what He permitted, and the Truth, glory be to Him, loves those who stop at the limits of Allah. So a person does not approach them, lest his soul lead him to disobedience. And when the Muslim keeps away from them, he is guarding against doubtful matters.

The Truth explains to us: "We have made lawful for you such-and-such, and We have forbidden you such-and-such," and He is the Creator. So we must take from the Creator the specifications of what preserves our life. This preservation is what we do when we invent a machine that saves us effort and gives us the fruit with the least exertion. When a craftsman makes a machine, he makes for it what provides it with the energy to perform its work, and the user of this machine cannot change the fuel of this energy; if he changes the type of energy, the machine does not perform its function. How much more so the One who created!

When He makes clear that this machine is fit only with what You have made lawful, and that what You have forbidden must not enter it, then we must obey the Creator, because He is the One who knows what is suitable for us and what is not. No one in the universe claims to have created himself. So let us refer our sustenance and the preservation of our life to our Creator, and let us take what He has made lawful and keep away from what He has forbidden. The machine – the human being – is fit to do the lawful and to leave off doing the unlawful. Thus there are things that are done and things that are not done. And there are things on which no ruling of permissibility or prohibition has come: if a person turns to them, they are fit, and if a person does not turn to them, they are also fit. The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, makes clear: you did not create this machine – the human being – and I am the One who created it, so I know what gives it the supply of energy and the supply of survival; if you make other than that, you are transgressors.

For this reason the Truth addresses those who believed: that He created them from nothing, sustained them from nothing, and provided for them to preserve their lives and their kind, and they must take these rulings from Allah: ﴿and do not forbid the good things that Allah has made lawful for you﴾. Glory be to Him, He makes clear: whoever believes that I am God should take from me the specifications for preserving his life. And when He, glory be to Him, says that, there must be a motivating cause for this saying. When He revealed His words:

﴿You will surely find the most intense of the people in enmity toward the believers to be the Jews and those who associate others with Allah; and you will find the nearest of them in affection to the believers those who say, "We are Christians." That is because among them are priests and monks and because they are not arrogant (82)﴾ (surah al-Ma'idah).

The Truth, in this noble saying, gave the grounds for praising them: their nearness in affection to us, for among them are priests and monks who renounced worldly life. When the Companions of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, heard this, they wept, and ten of the Companions gathered in the house of Uthman ibn Maz'un al-Jumahi, among them Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, Umar, Ali ibn Abi Talib, Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, Abdullah ibn Umar, Abu Dhar al-Ghifari, Salim the freedman of Abu Hudhayfah, al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, Salman al-Farisi, and Ma'qil ibn Muqarrin, and they agreed to fast by day, stand in prayer by night, not sleep on beds, not eat meat or fat (wadak), that is, grease, and to castrate themselves and wander in the earth as the monks do. When this reached the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he gathered them, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: "What is the matter with people who say such-and-such? But I pray and sleep, I fast and break my fast, and I marry women; whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me."(2)

And the Truth, glory be to Him, sent down:

﴿O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that Allah has made lawful for you﴾ (part of verse 87, surah al-Ma'idah).

The words of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to his Companions and to the people are rational. For if they wished to refrain from the good things that Allah has made lawful, in order to declare asceticism like those before them – and whoever desires monasticism, should he not pray? He prays; and prayer requires movement, movement requires strength, prayer requires covering the nakedness, and covering the nakedness requires clothing, and this clothing requires thought about where it comes from. The cloth comes from a cloth merchant; the cloth merchant must get it from the factories that weave it; the factories that weave it must get it from the factories that spun it; the factories that spun it must get it from the ginning houses that ginned it; then there must be the animals from which it was taken, if it is wool, and their rearing requires agriculture. So all these things require wide-ranging movement, which you do not perceive until you need a garment. If you wish to devote yourself to worship, beware of benefiting from the movement of one who establishes the pillars of Islam and moves in life in the light of Allah's method, seeking sustenance – and this is a matter that does not come about.

Also, does the one who wishes to devote himself to worship not eat? He eats in order to stand up to pray. And we all know how a loaf of bread comes: it is true that a person goes to the bakery to buy a loaf of bread, and the bakery brought the flour from the mill. The mill was brought the grain from the storehouses, and the grain came from the one who planted it. The one who planted needed ploughing machines, planting machines and harvesting machines, and after that he needed other things such as fertiliser and so on. This requires an immense amount of energy.

So the human being, in his movement in prayer, needs all these works; so if you wish to withdraw from life, beware of benefiting from the work of one who withdraws from life. And the work without which an obligation cannot be fulfilled is itself obligatory. For this reason, if the ruler sees a craft that human existence and faith's existence require, and people do not voluntarily take it up, he must compel a group to do it. Every craft is a communal obligation (fard kifaya): if some perform it, it is lifted from the rest; and if none of them performs it, all are sinful.

So the movement of life is necessary, and the movement of life passes from one link to another link. Do not take the fruit while withdrawing from life. The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, says:

﴿Do not forbid the good things that Allah has made lawful for you﴾. If you do that, you will have taken on the attribute of a legislator and transgressed upon His right to make lawful and to forbid, and this is transgression.

And if Allah has forbidden some things and made others lawful, this is in accordance with the suitability of the lawful things for the human being. And the human being must look at the existing forbidden things as indirect sustenance, because they are a means to direct sustenance, just as we know that we extract a remedy from the venom of the serpent. So the serpent is a creature created for a task that serves the human being. The whole world is links: animals benefit from the harm of one another until all the good reaches the believer. So let no person say, "Why was it created, if it has been forbidden?"

So do not transgress by making lawful what Allah has forbidden or forbidding what Allah has made lawful; by abandoning transgression, existence is ordered.
