Allah breaks human pride before inanimate things, which are the lowest of kinds, so He commands the human to touch or kiss the Black Stone, and if he cannot because of the crowd, he should gesture toward the Stone. Whoever cannot touch or kiss the Black Stone may imagine that his Hajj has not been accepted, out of extra attachment to the rites and caution in performing them.

All this is so that Allah, glory be to Him, may establish the path of servitude. Always someone asks: "How do we kiss the stone when Allah has forbidden us idolatry and the worship of idols?" We say: stoniness has no value in this matter, but the Lord of the human, the animal, the plant and the stone is the One who commanded us to do so, as is proven by the fact that we stone another stone, which is a symbol of Iblis. The servant, during the performance of the rites, moves from the desire of his own self to the desire of his Lord, so he kisses and venerates a stone and stones another stone. Thus servitude is purified for people, so they follow the path, and servitude is purified for animals, plants and inanimate things.

Our master 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) draws our attention when he said to the Black Stone: "I know that you are a stone that neither harms nor benefits. Had I not seen the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) kissing you, I would not have kissed you."

It is as if our master 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) is teaching us so that no one says it is idolatry. Idolatry is to worship a stone according to your own desire, whereas we venerate the Black Stone according to the desire of Allah.

"O you who have believed, Allah will surely test you with something of the game that your hands and your spears can reach, so that Allah may know who fears Him unseen. Whoever transgresses after that, for him is a painful punishment" (5:94).

What is the difference between what the hands reach and what the spears reach? What the hands reach is the young birds and easy, simple things; what the spears reach is what you hunt with effort, with the spear and good aim. Allah said "wa-linabluwannakum" because there is a difference between a person who persists in disobedience and commits it, and one who reaches a rank where he does not persist in disobedience, and even if disobedience comes upon him, he does not commit it.

It is as if Allah tests us so long as we do not persist in disobedience, and He wants to see what our conduct will be if disobedience comes to us: will we do it or not? If faith is strong, no one draws near to disobedience. For this reason Allah tests you with some game forbidden to you by placing it within your reach.

This happened at al-Hudaybiyah: the game placed itself among the hands of the believers, and they did not approach it, and this was a test. We know that trial is not blameworthy in itself; what is blameworthy is its purpose, because trial is an examination: one person may succeed and another may fail. It is as if Allah tested the believers by making the game multiply before them, so that the stalk of faith in the heart of the believer grows strong, and he does not rush into disobedience, and immunity develops within him. "So that Allah may know who fears Him unseen" — and Allah, glory be to Him, knows everything before it happens. But there is a difference between knowledge and knowledge: the knowledge of Allah is eternal and does not fail, but this knowledge is not a proof against people, because the proof against people is what actually occurs from them, and therefore there was the trial.

An example of this, and to Allah belongs the highest example: a father may look at one of his sons and say: "He plays all year, so it is better that we do not have him sit the examination, because he will fail." The son does not sit the examination, yet his audacity reaches the point where he says: "If I had sat the examination I would have been among the successful." And if his father had made him sit the examination and he had failed, that failure would have been a proof against him.

So the knowledge of Allah does not by itself establish the proof; rather, actual knowledge is what binds us to it.

Such trials have occurred frequently in the prophetic histories. For example, Allah tested the Jews with the prohibition of hunting on the Sabbath. The fish would come on that day, surfacing, as if pressing them to catch them. On other days the fish did not come, so they devised a trick to disobey the command by inventing a kind of wire trap into which the fish would enter, and the fish would remain trapped in it until Sunday, when they would take it. Their trick was itself evidence of their folly, because the hunting was accomplished through intention, action and prior preparation. In Islam the trial is with some game: "So that Allah may know who fears Him unseen. Whoever transgresses after that, for him is a painful punishment."

We have already known His saying: "These are the limits of Allah, so do not transgress them" (part of 2:229).

If things are commanded, we must carry them out. If they are prohibitions, we must not approach them, lest we fall into them and they become a proof against us, because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The lawful is clear and the unlawful is clear, and between them are doubtful matters that many people do not know. Whoever guards against doubtful matters has cleared his religion and his honour. Whoever falls into doubtful matters falls into the unlawful, like a shepherd who grazes around the sanctuary, about to fall into it. Surely every king has a sanctuary, and surely Allah's sanctuary on earth is His prohibitions."(1)

(1) Narrated by al-Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir.

Al-Sha'rawi said, after that, the Truth (may He be glorified) says:

﴿O you who have believed, do not kill game while you are in the state of ihram (pilgrim's sanctity). And whoever of you kills it intentionally - then the penalty is an equivalent of what he has killed, of livestock, as judged by two just men among you as an offering to reach the Kaaba, or an expiation of feeding poor people, or the equivalent of that in fasting, that he may taste the detriment of his affair. Allah has pardoned what is past. But whoever returns to it, Allah will take retribution from him. And Allah is Exalted in Might, Owner of Retribution.﴾ (5:95)

That is, do not kill game if you have entered the state of ihram for Hajj or 'Umrah or both. And if you have not entered ihram, game is still forbidden within the bounds of the sacred area (al-Haram). He (glory be to Him) has made the sacred area a time and a place of sanctity. It is a refuge to which people resort from arrogance and from the pride of one people at the expense of the humiliation of other peoples. In the past some of them used to fight one another, and therefore the Truth made four months sacred in respect of time, meaning that there is no fighting in them, so that the weary may rest from war, and whoever fears for his honour may rest, or so that everyone may taste the pleasure of peace and security, and they may continue to enjoy peace and safety. Likewise the Truth made the sacred area a secure place, in which no one is to be harmed by anyone. A person could meet the killer of his father in the sacred area and not touch him. All of this is to protect people's dignity from being broken before others.

An example of this: two parties, each in dispute with the other, and each of them desires reconciliation with the other party. Here some outsider intervenes and succeeds, because the two parties are inclined to reconciliation. Each of them wants to end the war, but pride in sin seizes him, zeal takes hold of him, and he disdains to be the one who begins by asking his opponent for reconciliation.

The Truth wanted there to be, in the sacred months, an opportunity for harmony and reconciliation, by people resorting to the Sacred House, so that humanity may shake off rancour from itself, and so that people may rest from fighting, and judgments may be issued with deliberation, balance and calm nerves.

The Truth (exalted is He) says:

﴿O you who have believed, do not kill game while you are in the state of ihram. And whoever of you kills it intentionally - then the penalty is an equivalent of what he has killed, of livestock, as judged by two just men among you as an offering to reach the Kaaba, or an expiation of feeding poor people, or the equivalent of that in fasting, that he may taste the detriment of his affair. Allah has pardoned what is past. But whoever returns to it, Allah will take retribution from him. And Allah is Exalted in Might, Owner of Retribution.﴾ (Surah al-Ma'idah)

Something is not considered game unless it is edible. As for what is hunted and is not edible, such as a predatory beast and the like, some scholars said: it is not prohibited and not forbidden. But we say: game is everything that is hunted, whether it is edible or even inedible, so that we teach ourselves, our limbs and our members good manners while we are in a state of sanctity. The meaning of (ḥurum), "in a state of sanctity," is that we are in ihram or within the sacred area, and the sacred area has known boundaries. Inside the sacred area it is forbidden for a person to hunt anything from the moment he reaches the miqat of Hajj and 'Umrah.

Thus the scope of game-prohibition applies to everyone who enters the noble Meccan sacred area, whether he is in ihram or not. The scope of game-prohibition for one who intends Hajj or 'Umrah is a wider and more extensive area, since the prohibition begins from the time of entering ihram for Hajj or 'Umrah or both. But what is the ruling if a person transgresses the command and hunts?

﴿whoever of you kills it intentionally﴾. But the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) applied the rule for unintentional killing to intentional killing, so that every Muslim may be mindful of every act while he is in ihram, or while he is in the Sacred House.

Suppose you wished to scratch your scalp with your fingernails while you are in ihram; here some of your hair may fall out. If that is established, then upon you is an offering to the Kaaba, or fasting, or feeding the poor, because the Truth wants you, when you enter ihram, to be mindful with all your limbs that every movement of yours is preserved and counted against you, and to be in the utmost vigilance of faith; and any error, however slight, requires expiation. Therefore whoever kills must render the penalty, because he has transgressed against something Allah has forbidden. The penalty is limited by the explicit words of the Truth: ﴿then the penalty is an equivalent of what he has killed, of livestock﴾, and at the word "equivalent" the scholars also paused: is the equivalence in value, or equivalence in form?

Equivalence in value means that the killed thing is valued at its price, and with the price one buys some livestock and slaughters it. Equivalence in form means that we match the killed thing with a counterpart of livestock that is slaughtered and is closest to its form. The proof of this is that when a Muslim killed a hyena, the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered the Muslim to ransom it with a ram. The Companions (may Allah be pleased with them): 'Ali, 'Umar, 'Uthman and 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar ordered a man who had killed an ostrich to ransom it with a camel (badanah: a she-camel or a camel), because it resembles the ostrich in height. When a person killed a gazelle (zabi), he ransomed it with a sheep; the zabi or ghazal is the male, and the ghazalah is the female, and when he killed a female gazelle the ruling for the ransom was a she-goat. And whoever killed a jerboa (yarbu') — which is among the reptiles and slightly larger than a mouse — the ruling was that the ransom be a jafrah, which is the young of a goat after it has become independent of its mother's milk and is able to eat.

Thus the equivalence here is equivalence in form. Abu Hanifah permitted that the equivalence be in value if no counterpart exists. On that basis, whoever hunts in order to feed himself pays the price of his error to others among the needy. And if the equivalence is in value, then the one who determines this value is people of insight, two from among those of justice. ﴿as judged by two just men among you as an offering to reach the Kaaba﴾: they are those who do not incline away from the truth and who uphold the scale.

The Truth commands us to judge with fairness, so that we may be among those of justice: that is, when a person faces two adversaries, he gives half of his attention to one and half to the other, and does not lean by desire toward either of them. Nor does a person turn his face toward one opponent more than he turns it toward the other.

If someone asks: how do we bring about just men? We say: look at their justice in themselves, and see whether a person's conduct is upright or not, and whether he is extravagant or moderate, whether in food, anger, or any kind of behaviour. Whoever is trustworthy with himself is trustworthy with others, and he must also be experienced in this matter. Therefore people must be mindful of these questions, because we see a wave of hypocrisy toward the youth sweeping some societies, and we hear voices saying: the youth must take over leadership.

We say to the owners of these voices: slow down and examine such a statement carefully, because the young man must carry on his own work in the years of youth, and we must observe him while he performs his work. If he succeeds, and we see in him trustworthiness over the movement of his own self, and justice with himself, and no extravagance against himself, then we nominate him afterwards to serve his nation after he has proven that he is trustworthy in the justice of his own self. It is not right to test upon the nation someone who does not rest on a store of prior experience.

It is not right to entrust the command in any sector to those whom they have called "wonder children." Whoever wants to experiment, let him experiment on himself, and with what he owns, not with nations and peoples. The young man should begin his life with serious activity for its own sake, to derive the benefit close to him, and not to deceive himself. If he succeeds in that, we take from him some of his time, or all of his time, to serve his nation after he proves to us that he has reached sufficient mental maturity, his experiences have increased, he has lost the appetite for personal ambition and small pleasures, and has reached the capacity for detachment to judge between people.

So if the Truth has commanded us to choose just men to judge over the neck of a sheep, then what of human necks and human interests?

We are therefore obliged to distinguish the just among people through observing a person's conduct with himself, over himself, and over his family. When we discover that he has become trustworthy over himself, then we can entrust him with the affairs of others and with public service, so that the nation will not be disappointed, for nations are only disappointed by the undeliberated choice of leaderships in its various posts.

We may note in our work the precision of the meanings that came in the noble Qur'an. Here we are dealing with a sheep or an animal, and we seek a ruling from just men. ﴿as judged by two just men among you as an offering to reach the Kaaba﴾, and what the just men judge goes entirely to the Kaaba, to be eaten by those present in the Sacred House for the worship of the Most Merciful. And Allah wished to guarantee the sustenance of those who dwell in a valley without vegetation, even from the errors of those who transgress against the game Allah has forbidden. But what is the solution if the one who erred does not have the capacity to offer an offering reaching the Kaaba?

The Truth (exalted is He) does not leave such matters without statement or detail; here He sets the expiation of feeding the poor, whose number is determined by two just men. And whoever cannot feed the poor shall fast for days equal to the number of the poor who deserved food had he given it out. ﴿or an expiation of feeding poor people, or the equivalent of that in fasting, that he may taste the detriment of his affair﴾. Wabal (detriment) is burden and consequence.

And why the detriment? Because when a person pays from his wealth the price of buying the equivalent of what he killed, his wealth will be dear to him; likewise, if he feeds the poor, he will buy the food with money that is dear to him, and fasting causes him exhaustion. This kind of expiation makes a person taste the detriment of what he has done. And the Truth wanted by this that the sense of responsibility should not be a mere formality, nor that wrongdoing should remain a mere formality. And He (glory be to Him) willed to arrange benefit for good and harm for wrongdoing, so that affairs in the universe may be set right. In the story of Dhu al-Qarnayn we have a clear example of this:

﴿They ask you about Dhu al-Qarnayn. Say, "I will recite to you about him a mention." Indeed, We established him upon the earth and gave him of every thing a means.﴾ (18:83-84). The Truth established Dhu al-Qarnayn upon the earth and gave him of every thing a means. Yet Dhu al-Qarnayn did not rely on what was given him; he did not slacken or grow lazy. Rather, the Truth tells us: ﴿So he followed a means.﴾ (18:85)

Dhu al-Qarnayn took from Allah's establishing him upon the earth, and took from Allah's giving him a portion of every means. He took energy and a sense of responsibility to carry on his mission:

﴿Until, when he reached the setting place of the sun, he found it setting in a muddy spring, and found near it a people. We said, "O Dhu al-Qarnayn, either you punish them or you treat them with kindness."﴾ (18:86)

He reached the place of the sun's setting in the view of his eyes, because when a person stands at sunset in an open field, the sun sets before him as though it falls at the edge of the horizon. The reality is that this is the limit of the power of sight. The authority was given to Dhu al-Qarnayn: either to punish these people, or to deal with them with kindness. Let the deeds of each of them be weighed, and let each of them be recompensed according to his deeds. He does not do this out of whim, because he is empowered upon the earth by the Truth (glory be to Him and exalted); therefore the Truth said: ﴿He said, "As for one who wrongs, we will punish him; then he will be returned to his Lord, and He will punish him with a terrible punishment."﴾ (18:87)

Every person, even the pragmatist, when he sees that committing an evil deed brings him hardship and loss, turns back from it, even if he is not a believer in the Last Day. As for one who believes in the Last Day and does righteous work, what then is the nature of his treatment? Here the Truth (glory be to Him and exalted) says:

﴿And as for one who believes and does righteousness, he will have a reward of the best, and We will speak to him from Our command with ease.﴾ (18:88)

He receives honour and encouragement, and honour and encouragement must be received by the one who holds the right to them, not by the hypocrite or the one who fawns at doorways. Thus is the constitution of every person empowered upon the earth. And thus is the observance of Allah's commands and prohibitions. When the Truth commanded us to forbid hunting in the Sacred House or while in ihram, and set a penalty for whoever erred, He (glory be to Him and exalted) is just with us: there is no punishment except by text, and no prohibition except after the text. Therefore He (glory be to Him) said: ﴿Allah has pardoned what is past. But whoever returns to it, Allah will take retribution from him. And Allah is Exalted in Might, Owner of Retribution.﴾ He pardons what is past, but whoever returns to commit the prohibitions of Allah in this domain, the Truth punishes him. His offering, his feeding of the poor, and his fasting are not accepted from him, because repetition of the violation is persistence in it. Therefore Allah takes retribution from him, and He is the Mighty whom none can overcome.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 5, verse 96:

After the Truth (al-Haqq) had spoken about the game of the land and its ruling, He wished to make clear to us that this ruling does not apply to every kind of game. So He forbade the game of the land if we are in the state of ihram (iḥrām, the sacred state of pilgrimage), or within the sacred precinct (al-ḥaram). The words of the Truth come:

﴿Lawful for you is the game of the sea and its food, as a provision for you and for the travellers; but forbidden for you is the game of the land as long as you are in the state of ihram. And fear God, to Whom you will be gathered.﴾

This is a precise statement that explains the permissibility of the game of the sea and its food, and the prohibition of the game of the land for one in ihram, just as the hunting within the sacred precinct is forbidden to both the one in ihram and the one not in ihram. This is because the matter is not a flat permissibility or a flat prohibition; rather, it is a departure from the desire of the self to the desire of God. The game of the sea is what we catch by stratagem and eat fresh, and the food of the sea is what is prepared to be food, by salting it. For this reason He said: ﴿as a provision for you and for the travellers﴾. Hence the Truth brought the food of the sea conjoined (ma'tūfan) to the game of the sea. A thing is not conjoined to itself; so when conjunction comes, it is the conjoining of one thing to another thing, for conjunction implies difference.

Thus the resident eats fresh fish, while the one on a journey and travel takes fish and dries and salts it as food for himself, just as Sayyidina Musa (Moses) did with the fish. But there are kinds of game that are not for eating, such as pearls, coral, and creatures we extract from the sea for their bones, teeth and other things. So what is the position regarding these? God has indeed permitted us to enjoy all the game of the sea. This ruling comes here by the style of laff wa-nashr (the wrapping and unfolding device), just as the Truth said:

﴿And of His mercy He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest therein and that you may seek of His bounty﴾ (Surah al-Qasas 28:73).

We all know that the night is for rest and the day is for toil. The night yields to the day and the day yields to the night. Thus the dwelling belongs to the night, and seeking bounty through effort belongs to the day. So the ruling came in the orderly laff wa-nashr pattern. I have previously explained how the Arab poet did this when he said:

"My heart, my eyelid, my tongue and my Creator: contented, weeping, grateful, and forgiving."

The heart is contented, the eyelid weeps, the tongue is grateful, and the Creator is forgiving. But the poet brought the rulings unfolded after he had wrapped the first four words. That is, he folded together the things judged, then unfolded the rulings after that. In our lives, during travel, we buy gifts for the children and arrange them according to the order in which the children came into our lives; that is, we wrap the gifts and then unfold them afterwards.

After the Truth had made lawful the game of the sea, He came with the prohibition of the game of the land if we are in ihram, and that is a fresh affirmation of the prohibition of the game of the land during the state of ihram or the presence within the sacred precinct.

The Truth concludes the verse with His words: ﴿And fear God, to Whom you will be gathered﴾. That is, make between yourselves and the punishment of God a shield, for you are not able to bear the punishment of the Fire. The Truth, as we said before, has attributes of beauty, which bring about what facilitates and benefits, such as expansion (al-basṭ), forgiveness and mercy; and He, glorified and exalted, has attributes of majesty (qahr), such as al-Jabbar (the Compeller) and Shadid al-'Iqab (Severe in Punishment), and others. Every attribute of the Truth has a corresponding requirement. So when a human being sins, the manifestation of God's attributes is in the attributes of majesty (jalal), and among the soldiers of the attributes of majesty is the Fire.

So beware lest you think you have escaped from God, for the margin of freedom granted to every human being lies in the space between two arcs: the arc of birth and the arc of death, and no one controls his birth or his death. So beware, O human being, of falling captive to delusion, for you are free to choose within the two arcs, and governed by two compulsions: the compulsion that He created you at the beginning, and the compulsion that you will return to Him, glorified and exalted, at the end.

The Most High then says:

﴿Allah has made the Kaaba, the Sacred House, a means of standing for the people, and the sacred month, and the offerings, and the garlanded animals. That is so that you may know that Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, and that Allah is Knowing of everything.﴾ (97)

(جعل) means to make clear and manifest. So He said: the Kaaba is sacred, and it has a dignity that makes it incumbent upon the believer to feel safe within it. Or (جعل) means bringing into being attributes of things after the substance of the matter already exists, as in His saying, glorified is He:

﴿And He made for you hearing and sight and hearts, so that you may be grateful.﴾ (verse 78, Surat al-Nahl)

That is, He, glorified is He, designated one part of the cells of a human being to be an eye, another part to be an ear, and a third part to be a tongue. The Most High says here: ﴿Allah has made the Kaaba, the Sacred House, a means of standing for the people.﴾ We know that all names for abstract meanings are derived from perceptible things.

Al-Ka'b (الكعب) is the thing that protrudes beyond the limit of evenness. An example of this is the ankle (الكعب في القدم), which is raised. Likewise, a girl is called a (طفلة), a child, while she is below puberty. When she reaches puberty and her breasts appear, we say she is (كعاب وكاعب), that is, her breasts have become raised. The Kaaba is a protrusion, and a protrusion is a height, and this height is the sign of the House. The House is an area of ground, but height determines its volume.

An example of this: when we want to calculate the area of land, we measure its length and width, and multiply the length by the width to reach the area. But if there is height, this means moving from area to volume. The Most High says:

﴿And when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House, and Ishmael...﴾ (verse 127, Surat al-Baqarah)

That is, our master Abraham, by his action, intended to give the House height and volume, and this construction indicates the creation of volume from an area of land. Therefore, the Kaaba is the House after it has come to have height. The word (بيت), house, means the place prepared for spending the night. A person wanders the earth all day, and when he wishes to rest he goes to the house.

So Allah made the Kaaba a house for the people so that they may rest in it from the toil of their lives and the hardship of their striving, because it is the house of their Lord by the choice of their Lord, not by their choice. Every mosque is a house of Allah, but by the choice of the creatures of Allah. As for the Kaaba, it is the house of Allah by the choice of Allah, and it is the qiblah for the houses of Allah that were established by the choice of the creatures of Allah.

﴿Allah has made the Kaaba, the Sacred House, a means of standing for the people.﴾ The phrase (البيت الحرام), the Sacred House, indicates that it has many sanctities. Allah made the Kaaba a sacred house, a means of standing for all Muslims. Qiyam (القيام) is standing, and standing is standing upright over a matter. One who stands over a matter preserves its sustenance, its existence.

Thus we understand that He, glorified is He, wanted the Kaaba to be the Sacred House so that He might preserve for people the sustenance of their lives, through food, drink, the continuation of offspring, and the warding off of harm. Beyond that, it provides dominance, sovereignty, prestige and empowerment. For this reason faith gives a lofty life. Life is a matter shared by the believer and the disbeliever, and it begins with the presence of the spirit in matter, so that matter passes to the state of sensation and movement. The believer is the one who elevates his life, giving it benefits through faith and stripping it of harms, so he attains sovereignty. In this way his worldly life connects with his life in the Hereafter, and life never ends for him.

Allah, the Most High, has indeed made the Kaaba, the Sacred House, a means of standing for the people, that is, a means of sustaining their lives, whether the worldly life that ends with death or the life that begins in the Hereafter. The Most High says about this:

﴿O you who believe, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life.﴾ (verse 24, Surat al-Anfal)

Thus faith in Allah becomes a link between two lives: the material life in this world and the life of the Hereafter. Through this, the Most High intended to ward off harm and bring benefit, prestige and sovereignty to the believers. We know that the Sacred House is the first house established for the people:

﴿Indeed, the first House established for people was that at Bakkah, blessed and a guidance for the worlds.﴾ (verse 96, Surat Ali 'Imran)

We also know that Abraham, peace be upon him, was the one who raised the foundations of the House, but the House itself had been established before that. Since the Most High said: ﴿established for the people,﴾ (verse 96, Surat Ali 'Imran), this means that Allah did not deprive people, before Abraham, of having a house. The people (الناس) means mankind from Adam until the Hour is established. Abraham, the Friend of the Most Merciful, established the third dimension, which is raising the foundations of the Sacred House. The Most High says:

﴿And when We settled for Abraham the place of the House...﴾ (verse 26, Surat al-Hajj)

That is, the Most High revealed the place of the House to Abraham, peace be upon him. We know that Abraham associated his son Ishmael with him in raising the foundations of the House, and we know that Ishmael came to this place as an infant with his mother. After raising the foundations, Abraham said, turning to his Lord in supplication:

﴿Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in a valley without cultivation, near Your sacred House.﴾ (verse 37, Surat Ibrahim)

Abraham knew the place of the House and that it was a valley without cultivation, with neither water nor plants. The Most High brought this allusion so that we would know that there is no life without vegetation, and water is necessary for vegetation. Thus Abraham, peace be upon him, answered the call of Allah to come to a place that had no blessing to sustain life, and in which there was nothing but the Giver of blessings. For this reason, we see our mistress Hajar, peace be upon her, when she received the command from Abraham to dwell with her son in that place, calling out to him: "O Abraham, to whom are you leaving us?" He said to her: "To Allah." She said: "I am content with Allah." Here our mistress Hajar left him to go as he willed, for Allah would not waste her or her son, because she had said: "I am content with Allah."

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) related to us her story, and the striving she undertook between al-Safa and al-Marwah, and how her trust was that the Most Generous Creator would not waste her or her son, but would provide for them. She ran between al-Safa and al-Marwah, perhaps she would find a bird that would show her the location of water, and she returned to al-Marwah, perhaps she would find a caravan passing by. She was taking the means while knowing that she was in the company of the Supreme Causer. She ran seven circuits. She was a woman at that age, and that was from her eagerness to secure a sip of water for her infant.

Striving, as we know it, is a difficult process. Had Allah given her the water on al-Safa or on al-Marwah, her saying, "Indeed Allah will not waste us," would not have been firmly established. But the Most High gave her the water at the feet of her nursing infant. Thus, glorified is He, has alerted us and guided us to two matters. The first is that a person must strive according to his capacity. The second is that striving alone does not give the fruit; the fruit is given by Allah. Allah made the running between al-Safa and al-Marwah a practical lesson for us that we should take the means and not forget the Causer, because the trial of people comes from being deceived by the means.

﴿No! Indeed, man transgresses, when he sees himself self-sufficient.﴾ (verses 6-7, Surat al-'Alaq)

It is never right for the means to isolate you from the Causer. Do not say, "I will remain with the Causer until the means come to me." No, always be with the means, and always remember the Causer. For this reason we say: the limbs work, but the hearts put their trust. This is the purpose of the Most High's giving water to Hajar at the feet of her son. Thus Abraham's supplication to Allah was answered:

﴿Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in a valley without cultivation, near Your sacred House, our Lord, that they may establish prayer. So make hearts among the people incline toward them and provide for them from the fruits, that perhaps they will be grateful.﴾ (verse 37, Surat Ibrahim)

Abraham, peace be upon him, supplicated for provision from the fruits, because the valley was without cultivation. Therefore, the Most High made the hearts of people yearn toward the Kaaba and the Sacred House. He, glorified is He, says:

﴿Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary to which are brought the fruits of all things as provision from Us?﴾ (verse 57, Surat al-Qasas)

The word (يجبى), is brought, indicates to us that people do not bring these fruits to the Sacred House by choice, the House that Allah made a means of standing for the life of those in it. Rather, they bring the fruits by compulsion.

There are people who have large farms and abundant gardens, and their fruits are in al-Ta'if and other lands. When a person wants to buy from the produce of their farms, they say to him: "It is reserved for Makkah. If you want to buy it, go to Makkah."

Allah responded to Abraham's supplication: ﴿So make hearts among the people incline toward them.﴾ The word (تهوى), with a fatha on the waw in the sense of pulling, indicates falling from a high place... that is, from a high, steep location. It is as though longing for the Kaaba throws a person toward it. For this reason we find that the one passionate about Hajj, one who loves it and is attached to it, has his soul yearning for Hajj.

We must distinguish between (يهوى), meaning he loves to go, and (يهوي), with a kasra on the waw, meaning he goes headlong by force. A person who falls from a high place cannot say, "I will stop at some point in the middle of the distance of the fall," because whoever falls from a place cannot hold himself. For this reason the Most High said:

﴿So make hearts among the people incline toward them, and provide for them from the fruits.﴾ (verse 37, Surat Ibrahim)

This is evidence that desire is not a product of the body, but a product of the hearts. The hearts are in the hand of Allah, glorified is He, who made them incline. The Kaaba is the Sacred House, and it is a means of standing for people's lives, and He, glorified is He, says:

﴿Whoever enters it is safe.﴾ (verse 97, Surat Ali 'Imran)

Whoever enters the Kaaba is safe, even if he were a killer. A man would meet the killer of his father in the Kaaba and would not be harmed by him. Thus the Most High gave them the beneficial among the means of life and withheld from those present among them the harm.

As for sovereignty and prestige, we know that Quraysh dominated the Arabs, and its men were the custodians (سدنة) and servants of the House of Allah. Everyone came to them, and no one would attack their caravans going to Syria or Yemen. Whoever attacked the caravans of Quraysh would find that Quraysh could take revenge on him when he came to them. That was the pinnacle of sovereignty. Thus the sustainer of life either brings something beneficial, such as provision, or prevents harm, through the security that reaches everyone who enters it, and through the sovereignty Quraysh held over all the Arabs. Allah gave Quraysh an example of His protection of the Kaaba when Abraha came to demolish the Kaaba:

﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?﴾ (verse 1, Surat al-Fil)

He, glorified is He, repelled the plot of the companions of the elephant, because if they had demolished the Kaaba, Quraysh would have lost its sovereignty. For this reason the Most High said, describing that:

﴿And He made them like eaten straw.﴾ (verse 5, Surat al-Fil)

﴿For the security of Quraysh, their security in the caravans of winter and summer.﴾ (verses 1-2, Surat Quraysh)

The Most High made the companions of the elephant like eaten straw, that is, like chaff or something similar that animals had eaten and then dropped as dung. He, glorified is He, did this so that Quraysh would be familiar with the Kaaba and reassured that no harm would touch it, and that the caravans of winter and summer would be protected by the necessity that all the tribes needed Hajj. He, glorified is He, said:

﴿So let them worship the Lord of this House, who has fed them against hunger and made them safe from fear.﴾ (verses 3-4, Surat Quraysh)

That is, He bestowed upon them blessing through food and removed harm from them through fear, and He preserved for them sovereignty and prestige through serving the Kaaba, which Allah made a means of standing and security for all people. Indeed, those who go to Hajj to the House, He, glorified is He, expiates their misdeeds and removes them from sins as on the day their mothers bore them. This is a means of standing for their life in the Hereafter as well.

Thus Allah made the Sacred House a means of standing for all aspects of life. The Sacred House is a place, as we know. The Most High also made the Sacred Month a means of standing for life, and the Sacred Month is a time, as we know. The Sacred Month is one of the four sacred months: one of them is solitary (فرد), that is, not connected to the other sacred months, and it is Rajab, which is why it is called Rajab al-Fard. The other three are consecutive (سرد), that is, following one another, and they are: Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah and al-Muharram. The intended meaning of "the Sacred Month" is the genus, covering each of the sacred months.

We know

Be mindful of God's commands, and be obedient to His will. Whoever opposes God should know that He, glorified and exalted, is severe in punishment. And whoever obeys God should know that He, glorified, is Forgiving and Merciful. God, glorified, has mentioned one attribute of majesty (jalal) so that it corresponds to two attributes of beauty (jamal): the attribute ﴿severe in punishment﴾ corresponds to the two attributes ﴿Forgiving and Merciful﴾. This is because not all people are good, and not all people are evil. Therefore He gives the good what suits them of forgiveness and mercy, and gives the evil what suits them of severe punishment. His mercy and forgiveness overcome His anger and punishment. We observe that this comes from the mention of one attribute of majesty, ﴿severe in punishment﴾, which corresponds to two attributes of beauty, namely ﴿Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

The Messenger's duty is only to convey (the message), and Allah knows what you disclose and what you conceal. (99)

The Messenger is the one sent by the Truth, glory be to Him, to us, the servants. The Truth, glory be to Him, is the First Agent, the Absolute, with no agent competing with Him. The first object of the message is the Messenger, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, and the second object is us. In grammar there is also the object with (waw of) accompaniment (al-maf'ul ma'ahu), the object of purpose (al-maf'ul lahu), the object of place (al-maf'ul fihi), the direct object (al-maf'ul bihi), and also the object of direction (al-maf'ul ilayhi). An example of the object of direction is His, the Exalted, saying:

﴿By Allah, We certainly sent (messengers) to nations before you, but Satan made their deeds seem fair to them﴾ (part of verse 63, Surat al-Nahl)

There is also the object of origin (al-maf'ul minhu). An example of the object of origin is the saying of the Truth:

﴿And Musa chose from his people seventy men for Our appointed time﴾ (part of verse 155, Surat al-A'raf)

Here "qawmihi" (from his people) is the object of origin, because he chose from among his people seventy men who had not worshipped the calf, so that they might apologise on behalf of those who had worshipped the calf and ask Allah to remove the affliction from them.

The task of the Messenger, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, is conveyance ("ma 'ala al-rasul illa al-balagh"). As for carrying out the conveyance, that is the role of the believers in the message of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace. If they discharge it, they will have Paradise, and if they fail to discharge it, they will face punishment. The Truth willed that the conveyance from His Messenger be accompanied by the behavioural exemplar (uswa) from him, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace. The Messenger conveys and, before us, carries out what he conveyed, so that we may follow him. Therefore the Truth said:

﴿Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent example﴾ (part of verse 21, Surat al-Ahzab)

This refutes the claim of divinity for a human being. For if there were a divine messenger, people would say: how can we follow this messenger when he has attributes and characteristics that differ from ours as humans? A messenger cannot properly be a god, because he is the exemplar and model for those to whom he is sent. He prays, fasts, gives zakat, performs the Hajj and does other acts, and he commands those to whom he was sent to follow him in what he does. If he were a god, those to whom he was sent, who are human, would not be able to do what he does, because he is a god whose nature differs from theirs, and so they could not emulate and follow him. Exemplarity is only possible if the Messenger is of the same kind as those to whom he is sent... that is, he must be human with all the attributes of humanity.

And the Truth, glory be to Him, said:

﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said, "Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?"﴾ (94, Surat al-Isra')

That is, people asked, out of ignorance, what prevents Allah, glory be to Him, from sending them a messenger who is not of the human kind, and why He sent them a messenger of their own human kind. Here the command comes from Allah, glory be to Him:

﴿Say: Had there been in the earth angels walking securely, We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger﴾ (95, Surat al-Isra')

Thus the Truth conveys to His messengers the necessity of informing people that the messenger to them must necessarily be of the human kind, because angels do not walk securely upon the earth. Had the messengers come as angels, humans would have said: we cannot follow what the angels brought, because they are not fit to be an exemplar for us, since they are of a different kind from humankind. Moreover, angels belong to the unseen realm, so how would Allah send the unseen to humans to be a messenger? And if that happened, the Truth would necessarily make him appear in human form.

In another verse the Truth says:

﴿And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man and would have obscured for them that which they obscure﴾ (9, Surat al-An'am)

They asked that Allah send down an angel to them. Had Allah responded to them and sent His messenger as an angel, the angel would have embodied himself in human form. And they, after that, might persist in disbelief, being obstinate and not believing; then the punishment of Allah would be due to them and would destroy them. So the task of the Messenger is conveyance, and for us in him is the exemplar.

The verse continues: ﴿And Allah knows what you disclose and what you conceal﴾. It is as if He, glory be to Him and exalted, is warning us against taking the outward form of faith without truly believing, because outward form may deceive people, but He looks upon us with His self-subsistence (qayyumiyya), for He is not overtaken by drowsiness or sleep. In this statement there is a challenge to the hypocrites that He, glory be to Him, will hold them to account. If a person conceals disbelief in his heart and shows outward faith, he will receive the punishment of Allah. The Messenger, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, together with the community of believers, must judge by the outward appearance of matters and leave hidden matters (al-sara'ir) to Allah.

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, forbids us from judging a person who has declared faith to be a disbeliever, even if he is a hypocrite. He, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, informed us that he is a human being, and he knew that human capacity is limited. Therefore he said: "I am only a human being, and you bring disputes to me. Perhaps one of you is more eloquent in his argument than another, and I judge for him according to what I hear. So whoever I give him something of the right of a Muslim, it is only a piece of the Fire, so let him take it or leave it."(1)

Thus the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, warns us not to attribute to him a power beyond human power. When a Companion killed a man who had declared faith, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said to him: "Why did you not split open his belly so that you would know what was in his heart?"(2) So we have the outward matters, while the hidden matters are entrusted to Allah. Therefore Allah says: ﴿And Allah knows what you disclose and what you conceal﴾. We know that the phenomenon of hypocrisy grants the hypocrite the outward rights of a Muslim, limited to his life and time, but the remainder of the Hereafter is long, and in it he will receive the reward of what disbelief he concealed within. Concealment (al-kitman) is not the same as hiding (al-ikhfa').

For concealing a thing means that the thing is clearly evident but its owner conceals it, whereas hiding (ikhfa') is what passes through the thoughts, which a person may conceal, but with the passing of time he cannot do so. The Arab poet says:
"Whatever a man's disposition may be, if he hides it, it will be known to people in the end."
And it is said: "The suspected person almost confesses: take me."

1. Narrated by al-Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah.
2. Narrated by Muslim, Abu Dawud, Ibn Majah and Ahmad.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surat al-Ma'ida, verse 100:

Since God knows all that people reveal and all that they conceal, and He is severe in punishment, forgiving and merciful, and rewards a good deed tenfold and repays an evil deed with its like, what then should we do? The decisive word comes in God's command to His Messenger to inform us:

﴿Say: The bad and the good are not equal, even if the abundance of the bad impresses you. So be mindful of God, O people of understanding, that you may prosper.﴾ (100)

So the bad is never equal to the good. The proof is that when one of us goes to buy goods, he sorts the merchandise to choose the good and avoid the bad. This is a cosmic principle, exactly like the inequality of the blind and the seeing, and the inequality of darknesses and light. God brings in tangible things to clarify for us a matter that is abstract. For this reason He warns us not to be deceived by the quantities and amounts of things, for a small good is greater, more increasing and better than much bad. A good matter may bring a person its benefit in this world, and it is certain that its benefit in the Hereafter is far greater than anyone can imagine, because the life of the Hereafter has no end, whereas the life of this world is limited.

Many people, when they attend a division of something, each one wishes to take the largest share for himself, because abundance tempts a person. This greed spreads the bad into everything the greedy one takes. One who covets a handful of wheat beyond his right, for example, corrupts his life with this bad thing. This is like mixing pure water with impure water, so that the impurity overcomes the water. Therefore it is not right to judge things by their quantity and measure; rather, we must judge things by their quality, their attribute, and their outcome in goodness.

The example I never tire of repeating is the student who toils for twenty years and so graduates a person with a fitting standing, whereas the student who spends twenty years in play and amusement receives and attains a failed and painful future. So each of us should value usefulness by its permanence, and not be deceived by the abundance of the bad.

This example recurs in our lives, and we must keep it before our eyes so that we may be mindful of God and not be led, as many people are led, to their destruction. Some people do not accept God's apportionment in their inheritances: one gives to the males and withholds from the females, or diminishes the females' share. To whoever does this we say: you do not know what you are doing. If your son, the male, knew that God's hand is in all things, he would say to you: "Have mercy on me and do not increase me," because the Exalted and Glorified One said:

﴿Your fathers and your sons: you do not know which of them is nearer to you in benefit.﴾ (part of verse 11, Surat an-Nisa')

Therefore people must realize that God's apportionment is the most just apportionment. Beware of wronging a son of yours or a relative by giving him more than what God has decreed for him, for this is pure injustice. If the testator has passed away while he was still alive, we say to the recipient: beware, do not accept what exceeds God's law, and return what exceeds your right. Do this with the presence of faith. And beware of thinking that the thing that will keep your children protected is this surplus to which you have no right, for by this surplus you will sever the ties of kinship and sow the seeds of hatred and enmity.

If you look at this matter and establish it according to what God has legislated, you will find that provision will overflow to you from every direction, so long as you have observed God's right in His will, which He decreed so that family continuity would arise and divine justice would appear. Therefore no one should dare to presume upon God's apportionment. So I say to everyone who reads these words and considers presuming upon God's apportionment: repent to God, and do not allow your faithful uprightness to be spoiled. And let no person think, as a father, that he can secure his children's future. We have often seen people whose families left them wealthy yet who ended in want, poverty and destitution, and we have seen people whose families left them poor, while God poured out His provision upon them. Glorified is He who said:

﴿And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would be anxious for them. So let them be mindful of God and speak words of rectitude.﴾ (9) (Surat an-Nisa')

So the believer must beware of abundance if there is something bad in it. We have a lesson in the story that happened with Abu Ja'far al-Mansur when he was pledged allegiance to the caliphate, and people went to congratulate him on the commandership of the believers. Sayyidina Muqatil ibn Sulayman entered upon him, and he was one of the preachers.

Here Abu Ja'far said to himself: he has come to disturb the clarity of our day. I will begin with him before he begins with me. So he said to him: "Admonish us, O Muqatil." Muqatil said: "Shall I admonish you with what I have seen or with what I have heard?"

This is because hearing is more extensive than seeing, for sight is limited and confined to what the eye perceives, whereas hearing is manifold, since a person may also hear the experiences of others.

Abu Ja'far said: "Speak with what you have seen." He said: "O Commander of the Believers, Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz died and left eleven children, and he left behind eighteen dinars. He was shrouded with five of them, the grave was bought for four, and then he distributed the remainder among his heirs. And Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik died, and the share of one of his four wives was eighty thousand dinars, apart from the estates and palaces. The share of the four wives came to three hundred and twenty thousand dinars, and this was the value of the estate alone. By God, O Commander of the Believers, I have seen with these two eyes of mine, in a single day, a child of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz's children being carried on a hundred horses in the way of God, and a child of Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik's children asking people on the road."

So each of us should know that he did not enter this world with wealth, and he should be courteous toward God, observe God's right, and not interfere in God's apportionment.

﴿Say: The bad and the good are not equal, even if the abundance of the bad impresses you. So be mindful of God, O people of understanding, that you may prosper.﴾ (100) (Surat al-Ma'ida)

The Muslim, therefore, must summon all his intellectual faculties so that he may distinguish the bad from the good and reject the bad thing, for if we reflect upon the ruling with our minds, we would arrive at the conclusion that God's ruling is the true and just ruling.

﴿That you may prosper.﴾ Falah (prosperity, success), as we know, is derived from a tangible matter, which is tilling the earth. A person takes a grain of wheat and plants it, and it gives him seven ears, each ear bearing a hundred grains. The Truth, Glorified is He, names for us every act of the Hereafter as falah, because the word has its beautiful impact. If the earth, which is one of God's creatures containing all the elements necessary for planting and necessary for all life, gives us in return for one grain of wheat seven ears, with a hundred grains in each ear, then how much will the Creator of the earth give you? So be mindful of God, O Muslim, and do not interfere in God's apportionment. Place before you this wise guidance that has come in a report: "Your worst is one who leaves his dependents in goodness and comes to God in evil."

As for the sons who have been afflicted with this, they should reconsider the matter with faithful chivalry, for when a father loved a son of his and increased his inheritance, it was the most foolish kind of love. The son should respect the feeling of love, repay his father for it with mercy, and restore the matter to its proper place, giving every rightful person his right, so that his father will not be exposed to the punishment of the Fire that he would incur as a result of his interference on his behalf in God's apportionment.

Almighty Allah then says:

﴿O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if they were made known to you, would distress you. But if you ask about them while the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be made known to you. Allah has pardoned them, and Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.﴾ (5:101)

This is a prohibition against asking (too many questions). The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Leave me alone as long as I leave you alone, for those before you were destroyed by their excessive questioning and their disputing with their prophets. So when I order you to do something, do of it what you are able; and when I forbid you from something, avoid it."(1)

We know that the Children of Israel made things hard for themselves when they began to stall regarding the slaughter of the cow, asking about its color, and they made it hard, so Allah made it hard for them. Had they slaughtered any cow at all, it would have been acceptable from them, but they made it hard, so Allah made it hard for them, until the cow described came to be an orphan's property. This orphan was the son of a righteous man, and he had a young cow. He brought it to a place abundant in trees and pasture and said: "O Allah, I entrust it to you for my son until he grows up." And when they haggled with the orphan over its price, he sold it to them for a hide filled with gold.

Some people have also been overly insistent in questioning the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), such as Abdullah ibn Hudhafah ibn Qays al-Sahmi, who asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Who is my father?"

The Messenger (ﷺ) answered: "Your father is Hudhafah." Suppose this questioner had been attributed to someone other than his father; would that not be a scandal for his mother? His mother said to him: "I have never seen anyone more disobedient than you. Did you feel secure that your mother had committed what the people of ignorance committed, so that you would disgrace her before people?"

Allah wished to lighten the questions of people on matters that lead them to hardship and toil and harm them. From His Messenger He accepts the questions of believers about the legal foundations, such as their questions about wine, the crescent moons, menstruation, the sacred month, and others. As for other questions, Allah has said concerning them: ﴿Allah has pardoned them, and Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.﴾

For some had become accustomed to asking, as if testing the Prophet (ﷺ). Therefore the command came that believers should not deliberately ask about what Allah has concealed from them, lest their honor be exposed. ﴿But if you ask about them while the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be made known to you.﴾ So if the Qur'an is revealed bearing the answer, then the answer is given. And if no answer comes, let no one say: "The Prophet does not have an answer." Or it may refer to questions about the things they proposed, claiming that they would establish the truth of prophethood. Allah has related their words:

﴿And they said: "We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth from the earth for us, (90) or you have a garden of palms and grapes and cause rivers to gush forth within it abundantly, (91) or you cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces as you claim, or you bring Allah and the angels before us as a guarantee, (92) or you have a house of gold, or you ascend into the sky. And we will not believe in your ascent until you bring down to us a book we can read." Say: "Glory be to my Lord! Am I anything but a human messenger?"﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 17:90–93)

From this statement the evil intent concealed in them has become clear. The Messenger does not bring the signs; rather, signs come to him with the command entrusted to him, because the Messenger does not choose the signs that come with him, but Allah is the One who sends the appropriate signs.

(1) Narrated by Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah and Ahmad.

Therefore the Truth says:

﴿Certainly a people before you asked about such things, and then they became disbelievers in them.﴾ (5:102)

The Truth did not send down these verses out of mercy toward those who asked the Messenger (ﷺ) about them. A people asked about a she-camel, then they hamstrung her, so God annihilated them. The people of Jesus (peace be upon him) asked for a table spread with food; it came down to them, and the Truth then threatened them that they would be punished if they did not believe. It has been God's way with His creation that when a people demand a sign for themselves and do not accept it, the Truth destroys them or punishes them. And to the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), He gives a guarantee:

﴿And God would not punish them while you are among them﴾ (part of 8:33, Surat al-Anfal)

So the questions they asked about were not answered for them, because He, glorified is He, had pardoned them. And pardon (al-'afw), as we know, is derived from "'afa al-athar," meaning he removed the trace. The pardon of God is part of His forgiveness and mercy.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 5, verse 103:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿God has not ordained any bahira, sa'iba, wasila or ham. But those who disbelieve invent lies against God, and most of them do not use their reason.﴾

This verse comes in the surah in which God made lawful the beast of cattle and made unlawful certain of them. He, glory be to Him, is the One who created man and created for him what sustains his life of sustenance, and what sustains his kind through procreation. And if the Truth is the One who made man a khalifa (vicegerent) on earth, then He prepared for him all these foundations of life from before Adam, peace be upon him. He, glory be to Him, prepared for His creation the earth, the heavens, the water and the air, and of the provisions He stored, concealed and brought into being in the earth, sustenance that does not end until the Day of Resurrection.

We may turn our attention to an important distinction between (khalq) (creation) and (ja'l) (ordaining/appointing). Creation is one thing, and ordaining is another. Creation is bringing into being from non-existence. Ordaining is directing a creature to its mission in life. The creation of God: no one creates anything; creation and bringing into being belong to Him alone, glory be to Him. And it is incumbent upon us, the creatures, to assign everything to its mission in the life that God willed, that is, to leave (ja'l) to God and not interfere in it. The meaning is that the Creator, glory and exalted be He, created the pig, for example, to eat filth and to protect man from many diseases and harms. Therefore man should assign the pig to this mission and not divert it from its mission, such as by eating it, for example; because diverting a creature of God from its mission is a matter that harms man, whom God willed to be a master and a vicegerent in the cosmos.

He, glory be to Him, informed people that He has made some things lawful and some things unlawful, and man must submit to what God has made lawful, so he embraces it, and must submit by keeping away from what God has forbidden. The Creator, glory and exalted be He, is the One who (created) and is the One who (ordained), and He is the One who said:

﴿God made the Ka'ba, the Sacred House, a means of standing for mankind﴾ (part of verse 97, surah al-Ma'ida)

And He is the One who said:

﴿Praise belongs to God, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light﴾ (part of verse 1, surah al-An'am)

And the Truth, glory and exalted be He, forbids us from making rivals for Him.

﴿O mankind, worship your Lord, who created you and those before you, that you may become righteous. Who made for you the earth as a bed and the sky as a canopy, and sent down from the sky water and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you. So do not set up rivals to God while you know [better].﴾ (surah al-Baqara)

So He, glory and exalted be He, exists and is One, the Unique; it is not valid for you to set up rivals for Him, because that is futility. He also establishes for us that the issue of corruption on earth arises from people's transgression into the (ja'l) of God's creatures, so that they divert them from what God created them for.

In their daily lives, people are keen to use things for what they are designated. An example: you receive from the cheese-maker a block of cheese, and from the soap-maker a block of soap. Then you bring the cheese and soap home and tell the household that the cheese is for eating and the soap is for washing, and everyone obeys these instructions. But if someone uses the soap for eating and the cheese for washing, corruption occurs in the health of the family members. Likewise, the Truth, glory and exalted be He, made for us children from our own loins; so how can we take children who are not from our loins and make them our children? This is an error in ordaining.

Therefore the Truth said:

﴿Nor has He made your adopted sons your sons﴾ (part of verse 4, surah al-Ahzab).

The adopted son is in reality not from your loins, and your wife is not his mother. How then do you make him your son, and enable him to sit in the lap of a woman who is not his mother and grow up on that, and look at women who are not his mahram, while considering that lawful and permitted for him? By that he loses the distinction between the lawful and the unlawful. Therefore adoption is a corruption of the (ja'l).

Every corruption that arises in the cosmos occurs when we make a creature of God serve a mission other than the one God assigned to it. The Truth, glory and exalted be He, informs us that He is the One who created man, and created for him what sustains him and what preserves his kind. So it is incumbent upon us to follow what the Truth commands, namely following what is lawful and keeping away from what is unlawful. If someone says: "Why did God forbid some things that He created?" we say: The One who created them assigned them to a mission other than the one man wants to direct them to; an example is the prohibition of eating pork.

When man sees a scene of animal life in the jungle, he wonders: the waste of one animal is food for another animal. The venom of a snake is protection and treatment. We know that man extracts snake venom to obtain a treatment for some diseases and to kill some germs.

Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Say: Have you considered what God has sent down to you of provision, and you made from it the unlawful and the lawful? Say: Has God permitted you, or do you invent lies against God?﴾ (surah Yunus, 59)

How then do we make ourselves legislators, making the unlawful lawful and the lawful unlawful? God, who created everything, has not granted us permission for that. And we must affirm that everything is created for a mission, so it is not valid for us to direct anything to other than its mission. Directing things to other than what they were made for produces harmful effects; an example is our use of insecticides in the fields. Those insecticides destroyed what we see as harmful, and destroyed the beneficial as well. Therefore man must be very attentive, not equating the unlawful with the lawful, and must be thoroughly careful not to transgress the (ja'l) ordained by God. He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿God has not ordained any bahira, sa'iba, wasila or ham. But those who disbelieve invent lies against God, and most of them do not use their reason.﴾ (surah al-Ma'ida)

The bahira is the she-camel whose ear is slit as a sign that it is forbidden, so no one approaches it. It is not turned away from pasture, nor from water; its milk is not drunk, it is not ridden, and its wool is not shorn, because they said: it gave birth to five offspring, the last of which was a male. The (sa'iba) is the she-camel that a man sets free if he recovers from his illness or returns from his journey, as a loose vow; he does not tether it, and it eats as it wishes, drinks what it wishes, sleeps wherever it likes, and no one ever bothers it. It was named sa'iba in the sense of being taken from "flowing water" (al-ma' al-sa'ib). We know that the essential property and nature of water is to spread out: if water falls on mountain tops, it first fills the valleys, then rises to the heights. This is how water spreads, unless man controls it by building dams, pumps and water distribution networks.

The wasila is the she-camel that connects with its sibling: when the she-camel becomes pregnant and gives birth, the owners look at the sex of the offspring. If it is male, they eat it; but if the offspring is female, it is theirs and they keep her, because she is a vessel for new offspring, and one stallion suffices to fertilize dozens of females. If the she-camel gives birth to a male and a female in one birth, they do not slaughter it, and it is said: "The female has connected with her brother," so he becomes unlawful for us.

In our Egyptian countryside, we find children wishing that the newborn of the water buffalo or cow would be male, so they could eat its meat and drink the milk of the buffalo or cow as they desire. That is because the child looks to his immediate benefit, whereas the adults always wish that the newborn of the beast be female, because the female is a vessel for new offspring.

The ham is the stallion whose back is protected from being ridden; they leave it to roam as it wishes. It is the one that has mated with ten generations of females, or the one from whose loins ten litters were born. Among the conditions of this practice was that they knew the grandson of this stallion, his son's son, could also mate.

All these matters: the bahira, the sa'iba, the wasila and the ham, are inventions of the people of disbelief who invent lies against God. The Truth, glory and exalted be He, created these livestock so that man may enjoy eating them, drinking their milk, and harnessing them for what benefits him.

The meaning of (yaftaruna al-kadhib, "they invent falsehood") is that one fabricates a lie and claims it, to dress up a falsehood in order to conceal the truth. Falsehood is a cover over a reality that exists, and the reality that has existed since God created creation is that all these livestock are subjected to serve man. God, glory be to Him, informed Adam of His method, and it was required that each generation convey it to the next; but the length of time and heedlessness are the two causes behind people forgetting some rulings. Therefore God sent the messengers to remind people of the method, and to remove disbelief from people's awareness. The disbelievers are people who concealed God's method and concealed the message from God, and by that they invent falsehood against God.

An example is the story of the entry of idols into the Ka'ba. A man named Amr ibn Luhayy traveled to the lands of al-Sham, found idols and images there, and carried one idol called Hubal to Mecca. He was the first to bring idols into Mecca. Just as Amr ibn Luhayy did, others did by establishing laws and rules that God had not brought, such as the wasila, the bahira, the sa'iba and the ham. That was a fabrication against God's method and a alteration of the Truth's method. And even supposing no method had reached them from God, was it not a necessity of reason to examine these innovations and misguidances?

The Truth, glory and exalted be He, did not prevent reason from reaching a sound cosmic truth. But reason may exert itself and tire through long experimentation until it reaches some truth. Therefore He, glory be to Him, wished to protect people from the suffering of harsh trials, so He sent down His method to define the lawful from the unlawful. He, glory be to Him, said:

﴿It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion, though the polytheists dislike it﴾ (verse 32, surah al-Tawba), and He says in another place in the Noble Qur'an:

﴿It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion; and sufficient is God as witness﴾ (verse 28, surah al-Fath).

And one may say: then why are there other religions in the world, such as Judaism and Christianity, and why are there atheists, since God has decreed that no other religion should exist alongside Islam?

We say: You have not understood the intended meaning of the two noble verses. The Truth, glory be to Him, affirms that the religion will prevail even though the polytheists dislike it. This means that there are disbelievers and polytheists, and people of other religions, and Islam will prevail over them, and God will make it dominant by proof and demonstration, and by the testimony of the disbelievers, atheists and idolaters themselves, because the affairs of life will exhaust them in all their life matters. They will find no solutions to these hardships except by turning to the cause of Islam, not because it is Islam, but because the manner and rules of Islam are what will free them from their problems. Their resort to judgments that accord with Islam, despite their disbelief in Islam, is a strong testimony that Islam came as the religion of the natural disposition (fitra) and the religion of reason, and that all will need it whether they wish or not. Whoever does not take it as a religion will be compelled to take it as a system.

And since the Truth, glory be to Him, appended to the noble verse that we are concerned with in our faith-inspired reflections the words: ﴿and most of them do not use their reason﴾, it is because He, glory be to Him, alerts us that if they had reasoned about the matter, they would not have made the bahira, the sa'iba, the wasila and the ham forbidden to themselves.

And we may ask: Did you make these things unlawful out of honor for them, or out of renunciation of them? If it was renunciation, then it means they removed them from what God created; for God created them so that we eat their meat and benefit from them. And if it was honor, is it honoring to leave the animal that served man without protection from a wolf, and without food prepared for it, letting it wander into another's land? This is a method that shows a lack of loyalty to the animal that served man, and such conduct does not preserve the animal's life but exposes it to danger. Therefore sound reason rejects this renunciation and that honor. If Amr ibn Luhayy or others brought things and traditions that God had not ordained, then we must thank the Truth, glory be to Him, for sending Islam to correct these matters.

The one who examines the verses of the Qur'an closely finds that they represent a reassuring program for human life on earth, as though they were a computer that regulates the rhythm of human movement on earth with a precision that surpasses, by every measure, the precision of any computer made by humans, the so-called (computer). There is a divine "computer" that guides the human being so that he does not go astray or lead others astray. The heavens correct a person's conduct if he strays far from the straight path. Let no one say: "I only follow what my fathers were upon," because the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And when it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has sent down and to the Messenger," they say, "Sufficient for us is what we found our fathers upon." Even though their fathers knew nothing and were not guided?﴾ (104).

Rather, a person should notice that the first alteration of Allah's method came from one of the fathers who had been overtaken by heedlessness. The statement of a person, "I only follow what my fathers were upon," is a refuted claim, because the one who made the first alteration did not say, "Sufficient for us is what we found our fathers upon," since he had not imitated a father of his own. Furthermore, it is likely that those fathers did not understand what they altered of Allah's method and were not guided to the truth.

In another place in the Noble Qur'an, the Blessed and Exalted says:

﴿And when it is said to them, "Follow what Allah has sent down," they say, "Rather, we follow what we found our fathers upon." Even though their fathers did not reason at all and were not guided?﴾ (170) (Surat al-Baqarah).

In the verse we are contemplating with our faith-inspired reflections, "And when it is said to them, come (ta'alaw)," Allah does not say "follow" (ittaba'u) in it, but says "come" (ta'alaw), meaning "rise up," as though they had sunk and debased themselves by their saying: "Sufficient for us is what we found our fathers upon." By that, they reject and deny everything that comes to them from any route other than the imitation of fathers. Thus they have closed the road and sealed it off against themselves.

As for the verse of Surat al-Baqarah, "Rather, we follow what we found our fathers upon," it may be that they would say: "and we also follow what the religion has brought," so the rebuke is stronger against the one who said: "Sufficient for us is what we found our fathers upon."

Accordingly, the corrective addition (istidrak) from Allah in each of the two verses came suitable to their condition. How so? Because the one who does not reason can learn through another person who has extracted, deduced, and discovered, for if he misses the use of reason, he does not miss taking knowledge from others. But the one who does not know has returned with ignorance, because he has not reached knowledge by himself, and likewise he has not learned from others.

He, glory be to Him, brought the interrogative hamza of denunciation (hamzat al-inkar) regarding the matter of following the fathers instead of Allah's method. We notice that the Truth brought the process of guidance as a common matter in both verses, because guidance comes from the heavens, whereas reasoning and knowledge are two human processes.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 5, verse 105:

The Truthful One (al-Haqq) says after that:

﴿O you who have believed, take care of yourselves. Whoever has gone astray cannot harm you once you are guided. To Allah is your return, all of you, and He will inform you of what you used to do.﴾ (5:105)

And al-Haqq, glory be to Him, had said earlier:

﴿And when it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger," they say, "Sufficient for us is what we found our fathers upon."﴾ (part of verse 5:104)

Both statements indicate that there are two groups: a group that walks in misguidance, and a group that walks in guidance. And there is a struggle between the two groups. Will this struggle last long? Yes, this struggle will continue for a long time, because the people of misguidance do not like that the believer loves for his brother what he loves for himself, and likewise they benefit from the corruption of the world.

The believer loves obedience and tries to make his believing brother love obedience too. If he sees him in an evil act, he forbids him from it and guides him toward knowledge, for the good, when it comes from a person, benefits others, and its benefit to himself may be deferred to the Hereafter. The goodness of the believer benefits society and harms the people of misguidance. The truthfulness of the believer benefits society and harms the people of misguidance. The integrity of the believer is of benefit to society and harms the people of misguidance. But if society is corrupt, the believer suffers from the corruption of that society.

Therefore, it is in the believer's interest that the good emanating from him spread to others, so that good spreads and returns to the believer through the movement of good in society. For this reason al-Haqq, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Take care of yourselves﴾, meaning: hold fast to yourselves, as if the souls of the believers were a single unit. This is an expression of the necessity of the widespread, mutual reinforcement of faith. A similar matter came up concerning the handling of the property of the foolish; al-Haqq said:

﴿And do not give the foolish your property﴾ (part of verse 4:5)
