Because the foolish person has no right to manage his wealth until he becomes rightly guided (rushd); for in reality the wealth is the wealth of all Muslims, and they must manage it so that all Muslims benefit from it. The management of the matter begins first with counsel; if the foolish person does not desist, then his nearest relatives should bring a case of restriction (hajr) against him. This is because any evil that results from the foolish person's conduct with his wealth returns to society. On this basis, the wealth remains the wealth of the people, who take charge of its management until the foolish person returns to his rectitude, whereupon his right to dispose of his wealth returns to him.

﴿But if you perceive in them rectitude (rushd), then hand over to them their property﴾ (part of verse 4:6)

Al-Haqq did not say, then: "hand over to them your property," because the one of rectitude has become trustworthy with his wealth; therefore the wealth returns to the foolish person immediately upon his return to rectitude. Likewise the saying of al-Haqq: ﴿Take care of yourselves﴾ means that you, O assembly of believers, each one of you is responsible for himself and for the rest of the believing souls, and it is part of guidance that we correct the one who is upon corruption. No believer should say: "What is it to me?" The verse continues: ﴿Whoever has gone astray cannot harm you once you are guided.﴾ So long as you have sought to correct corruption, you have discharged what is incumbent upon you, in light of the saying of the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand; if he is unable, then with his tongue; if he is unable, then with his heart, and that is the weakest of faith."(1)

But how is change by the heart effected? That is, the conduct of the believing person is to boycott whoever goes out against the method of Allah. If all the believers boycott one who goes out against the method of Allah, he must desist. And the believer should not greet a deviant man or woman with welcome or honor. Changing by the heart means that the outward behavior matches what is in the heart, so that the doer of evil senses that he is disapproved of by others. People may begin matters of evil when they encounter someone who flatters them with courtesies out of place, but if the doer of evil senses that he is shunned by the community of Muslims, even if you do not strike his hand, he must desist. Al-Haqq, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And when you see those who engage in vain talk concerning Our verses, turn away from them﴾ (part of verse 6:68)

That is, when you turn away from those who oppose the method of Allah, and when others turn away from them too, this harms them, and people do not persist in evil or grow in their harm except for the respect society shows them. In the villages, for example, we find that the one who possesses a rifle gains respect and courtesies that make him domineer with his weapon; if people turned away from him, his prestige would be lost and he would return once more to righteous conduct. What is the measure in the matter of changing by the heart and treating the doer of evil without affection and love?

We say: we must listen to the saying of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when he was asked once about this verse, ﴿Take care of yourselves﴾, and he said: "Rather, enjoin the good and forbid the evil, until you see stinginess obeyed, desire followed, worldliness preferred, and every person of opinion pleased with his own opinion; then you must attend to your own self and leave aside the common people, for behind you are days in which the patient one will be like one who grasps a live coal; the one who acts in them will have the reward of fifty men who do as you do."(2)

When you do not show a deviant from the method of Allah affection, mercy, and kindness, you have obligated yourself to positive action.

If the believer asks: "How does a person resist?" The scholars answered: whoever flees from two has fled, and whoever flees from three has not fled. That is, in fighting, if a person faces two, his fleeing is an escape from confrontation; but if a person flees while facing three enemies, this is self-preservation and not flight. The scholars derived this ruling from the promise of Allah of victory to the believers if their enemies were twice their number, i.e., as many as twice their count, from the saying of al-Haqq, the Exalted:

﴿Now Allah has lightened your burden, and He knows that among you there is weakness. So if there are among you one hundred patient ones, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are among you a thousand, they will overcome two thousand by permission of Allah. And Allah is with the patient.﴾ (verse 66, Surat al-Anfal)

So it is a ratio of one man to two men. If a believer flees from before two during combat, he has departed from Allah's promise of victory to him; he is called a fugitive, he returns bearing the anger of Allah, and his end is Hell, for Allah has said: ﴿If there are among you one hundred patient ones, they will overcome two hundred.﴾ Thus Allah promised the believing fighter who is patient victory when he faces two unbelievers. But if he flees from facing three, he has done what protects his life, for religion does not call to suicide. Therefore we say to those who seek to change evils in the world: do not cast yourselves into destruction, and do not fight an enemy that overcomes you by its multitude. Follow the saying of the Trustworthy, Truthful Prophet, concerning the continuance of his community as long as it holds fast to the method of Allah.

And changing evil by the heart is embodied, as we said, in boycotting the deviant, in confirmation of the saying of the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, take care of yourselves. Whoever has gone astray cannot harm you once you are guided.﴾ We note that ( على ) ('alā) is a preposition, the kaf is for address, the mim is for the plural, and ( أنفسكم ) (anfusakum) is in the accusative; so ʿalaykum is (ism fi'l), i.e., it is not a noun in its literal sense nor a particle in its literal sense, but a particle that entered upon a pronoun and thus performed the function of a verb-noun (ism fi'l), or it is an ism fi'l transferred from the prepositional phrase.

﴿Take care of yourselves; whoever has gone astray cannot harm you once you are guided⦆ means: hold fast to them and preserve them. It is part of guidance that we know how to confront issues with the creed of faith, so the believer looks at the numerical quantity of the guided and the numerical quantity of the misguided. If the numbers are equal, then let him proceed to confrontation. If the misguided number is double the believing number, then let the believing number proceed to confrontation also. And if the misguided number is more than double, the believer is excused if he protects himself by not confronting, but he must boycott every evil or doer of evil.

We all know well that every individual wishes to have a standing in society. If a person sees that reputation, status, and good repute belong to the truthful and upright, he tends to become truthful and upright; and if he sees that standing in society belongs to the liar and the deviant, he tends to become a liar and a deviant. Therefore the believers should honor only those who walk the righteous method. Imam Ahmad related that Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, stood, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: "O people, you recite this verse: ﴿O you who have believed, take care of yourselves; whoever has gone astray cannot harm you once you are guided,﴾ but you place it other than its proper place. I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say: 'When people see an evil and do not change it, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is about to encompass them all with His punishment.'"

﴿Whoever has gone astray cannot harm you once you are guided. To Allah is your return, all of you.﴾ Al-Haqq reassures the believers that if they encounter harm in their lives, they should know that this life is not everything; rather there is another life to which we return to Allah. Whoever is on Allah's side, Allah grants him eternal bliss in delight, and whoever is against the method of Allah, Allah gives him the torment of the blazing Fire. Al-Haqq said this because the believer cannot guarantee himself in many situations: he may enter a battle with sincerity in his intention, yet he may deviate, and harm befalls him in proportion to his deviation.

Those who walk in the light of the method of Allah must always keep this matter at the center of their awareness. We have in the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, a good example, when at the Battle of Uhud he commanded the archers not to leave their positions even if they saw the believers winning and the enemy defeated. The archers turned toward the spoils as soon as they saw the victory of the believers, so Allah did not help them, since they were in opposition to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Thereby the believers learned the lesson: that they should obey Allah and the Messenger in every step.

Had Allah, glory be to Him, not said: ﴿To Allah is your return, all of you, and He will inform you of what you used to do,﴾ what would be the position of those who did not witness the victory of Allah's soldiers, who entered the early battles and were martyred? They knew from the beginning that the return is to Allah and that He would give them another life, and that Allah would inform them of what they did. Here "informing" means recompense and honor.

(1) Related by Ahmad, Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Majah.
(2) Related by Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi.

And just as the Truth (al-Haqq) governs the believer's life while he moves through this worldly life, He, glory be to Him, also governs the believer's life in a way that secures for him the life to come, in the eternal bliss of Paradise. For this reason the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿O you who believe, let there be testimony between you when death approaches one of you at the time of bequest: two just men from among you, or two others from outside your community, if you are travelling in the land and the disaster of death befalls you. You shall detain them after the prayer, and they will swear by Allah, [saying], "We will not sell it for any price, even if it concerns a near relative, and we will not conceal the testimony of Allah; indeed, then we would be among the sinners."﴾ (106)

The Truth, glory be to Him, who governed and arranged the worldly life of the believer, has also arranged his life in the hereafter, so as to draw his attention to the fact that he must not look only at his hasty life in this world, but must arrange his affairs with regard to what he will face in the life to come. At the moment of facing death, he must not forget the bequest (wasiyya) if he owes anyone a debt, or if someone owes him a debt. Likewise, if a person travels in the land, he must make a bequest so that he does not cause his heirs to lose a right that is theirs, or so that he may settle what he owes in debt and clear his liability (dhimma), and he must have his bequest witnessed by two Muslims. If, however, a person is accompanied on the journey by non-Muslims, he must also have them witness the bequest. The Truth has left us no excuse in this matter; rather, the testimony of two persons is necessary.

Testimony (shahada) is the matter witnessed in the present, and an example of this is His saying:

﴿So whoever witnesses the month, let him fast it.﴾ (part of verse 185, Surat al-Baqara)

That is, whoever is present during the month and reaches it, let him fast. Testimony also comes in the sense of seeing, as in His saying, exalted be He:

﴿The adulterer and the adulteress, lash each one of them a hundred lashes, and let not pity for them take hold of you in the religion of Allah, if you believe in Allah and the Last Day. And let a group of the believers witness their punishment.﴾ (2) (Surat al-Nur)

That is, let a group of believers be present at the scene of the lashing. Testimony also comes in the sense of judgement, as in His saying:

﴿She said, "It was she who sought to seduce me," and a witness from her own family testified: "If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth and he is of the liars. But if his shirt is torn from the back, then she has lied and he is of the truthful."﴾ (26–27) (Surat Yusuf)

Thus testimony comes with multiple meanings, and its basic sense is the scene (mashhad), that is, the thing you witness. As we know, the bequest (wasiyya) is the entrusting of a matter that concerns the one making the bequest in relation to the one to whom it is entrusted. The believer bequeaths what is good, and he has it heard by someone who is not an heir, that is, someone who by law has no share in the estate, although a non-heir may have some cause of benefit from the one who leaves the inheritance. Nevertheless, the one who hears the bequest is discharged of his responsibility when he conveys what he heard to the heirs, because the bequest is a matter within the soul of the one making it; it may have no significance for the one who hears or receives it, but it has significance within the soul of the one who utters it. For this reason, God places the bequest before the debt in His saying, the Truth:

﴿after any bequest he has made or debt﴾ (part of verse 12, Surat al-Nisa)

This occurs even though the debt takes precedence over the bequest, because the debt is a right and the bequest is a voluntary gift. The Truth wills this, because the debt has claims that will be demanded; but the one to whom the bequest is made may be someone with a right who receives a gift by way of bequest, or his right against the one making the bequest may not be documented by a deed or testimony. For this reason the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted be He, puts it first, so that we attend to the matter of the bequest. Or the one who made the bequest may have lived in this life, and the people know the effect he had on their lives in knowledge, literature, morals or society; therefore Allah, glory be to Him, wants a person not to leave life until the believer has discharged this right of gratitude to those who had a hand in his worldly life. This is a matter that may not concern the heirs, and they may even dislike it. But the one making the bequest is the one who knows its circumstances.

For this reason the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted be He, wished to affirm the matter of the bequest even at a time when affirmation is rare. He commanded a person to make a bequest if he is among his family and people, and the Truth emphasises the importance of the bequest also if a person is travelling. If he senses the approach of death, he may call two people from among his own religion and entrust the bequest to them. If he finds no one from his own religion, let him have his bequest heard by two people from outside his religion. There is an occasion for this:

It happened that a Muslim man named Budayl ibn Abi Maryam, client (mawla) of al-As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi, was on a journey with non-Muslims, and the signs of death came upon him. He wrote a note and placed it with all the goods he had, as a precaution, and he called two non-Muslims, Tamim al-Dari and Adi ibn Badda, and charged them to deliver his goods to his family. Then the man died. But the two opened the goods and found in them a vessel that was silver-plated and gilded and had value. They took it, sold it for a thousand dirhams, and divided the sum between them, and they handed over the goods to the dead man's family. The family found the note, in which all the details were written, including the report about the valuable vessel. The family asked the two men who had delivered the goods about the vessel, and they denied any knowledge of it, and they also denied that they had seen the owner of the vessel selling it. After a while, the family of the dead man found the vessel displayed for sale, and they realised that the first sale had been made by the two men who had been present at the death of the owner of the vessel. So the family of the dead man went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to present to him the matter of the betrayal of trust concerning the bequest, and there came down the saying of the Truth:

﴿O you who believe, let there be testimony between you when death approaches one of you at the time of bequest: two just men from among you, or two others from outside your community, if you are travelling in the land and the disaster of death befalls you. You shall detain them after the prayer, and they will swear by Allah, [saying], "We will not sell it for any price, even if it concerns a near relative, and we will not conceal the testimony of Allah; indeed, then we would be among the sinners."﴾ (106) (Surat al-Ma'ida)

This is a command from Allah to His Messenger that these two should be brought, after they have performed the prayers of their own religion, and that they should swear by Allah, and that the family of the dead man should come with the note, so that the Messenger might distinguish truth from falsehood. Afterwards Tamim al-Dari became Muslim, recounted the story, and brought the five hundred dirhams that were in his possession, which he had taken as the price of half the vessel, and he brought the other five hundred dirhams that were with Adi, so that they might return the full price of the vessel to the family of the dead man.

Why did God say: ﴿you shall detain them after the prayer﴾? It is a command that we should hold them back after the prayer, because a person, usually after performing the prayer, whether he is among the People of the Book (ahl al-kitab) or among others, has his soul prepared for truthfulness, having stood before Allah, and in this state he is less bold in lying. For this reason the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿O you who believe, let there be testimony between you﴾. That is, the testimony about which people differ and about which statements diverge between two parties, because the word (bayn) [between] means the separation of two entities so that each of them becomes a party.

This testimony requires separating the two points of view. The one who carries out this separation is the one who questions the two witnesses, who are of the just men from among the Muslims or from among non-Muslims, and the questioning takes place after the prayer. If the matter to which they testified becomes clear, then it stands. But if their statement is not clearly truthful and contains doubt and suspicion, then the two witnesses must swear by Allah that they will not take any price in exchange for the signs of Allah, lest they be among the sinners.

Almighty Allah then says:

﴿Then if it becomes known that the two (witnesses) have committed a sin, then let two others stand in their place from among those who have been wronged by the first two, and they shall swear by Allah: "Our testimony is more worthy than their testimony, and we have not transgressed; indeed, we would then be among the wrongdoers."﴾

If it becomes apparent that the two witnesses have distorted the bequest of the deceased, or have concealed some of its details with falsehood, then we have the right to summon two of the nearest people to the deceased, and they shall swear by Allah that the two earlier witnesses have lied in their testimony, and that this accusation of lying is not a fabrication but is based on the truth. And if it were to appear that their testimony contains falsehood, then they themselves deserve the punishment of those who wrong others.

Thus Allah opens for us the way to establish justice by investigating the truthfulness (of testimony). If it becomes clear to us by evidence that the two witnesses who attended the death of the testator have lied, then let us bring two witnesses from the heirs of the deceased in their place. The word (ʿathara) means coming upon something unintentionally. If we come to know that sin is evident in the testimony of these two witnesses, then we have the right to investigate the truthfulness of the testimony of two others from the family of the deceased.

Concerning the incident in which this verse was revealed, ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs and al-Muttalib ibn Abi Wada'a al-Sahmi stood up and swore by Allah that the two earlier witnesses had lied, and that the testimony they were presenting was the testimony of truth, with no transgression or injustice against the owners of the first testimony. And why all of this? Because the aim is that testimony should come in its correct form, so Almighty Allah says:

﴿That is more suitable that they bring the testimony in its proper form, or that they fear that oaths will be repeated after their oaths. And fear Allah and listen. And Allah does not guide the defiant people.﴾

The first witnesses, who gave testimony because they were present at the moment of the bequest when the deceased spoke it, present their testimony after they have performed the prayer and after they have sworn that what they say is the truth. They must be careful to speak truthfully, lest the matter of their lying be exposed. Testimony, as we know, is applied to any matter we witness. And testimony, as we know, is applied to several related meanings that are all gathered by the word "presence" (al-hudur), as in His, the Truth's, words:

﴿And proclaim to the people the pilgrimage; they will come to you on foot and on every lean camel; they will come from every deep mountain pass. (27) That they may witness benefits for them﴾

(Verse 27 and part of verse 28 of Surah al-Hajj)

That is, the call to pilgrimage is heard by the people, so they come from every place and by every means of transport, even where these are difficult, "that they may witness benefits for them." And He, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him﴾ (part of verse 18, Surah Al ʿImran).

The testimony of Allah is a judgment from Allah. The angels also bear witness, and their testimony is the testimony of affirmation (al-iqrar). All of this arises from a present matter which the witness investigates. We see the witness standing before the court: the prosecution asks him and he says what he saw; the lawyer of the opposing party asks him and he says what he saw; the defence lawyer asks him what he saw. As long as the witness is truthful, he will not fear being questioned by any party. The parties that question the witness ask him to relate the incident in different ways, and as long as the incident is true, it remains as it is, however the questions vary and the methods change, because the truthful witness draws upon a reality that does not change; whereas the lying witness twists and turns and alters his statements. For this reason we see the skilful, astute public prosecutor searching the memory of the witness for the finest hidden details.

Thus we know that testimony is applied to presence. But if the witness is the one who holds the judgment, his testimony is a judgment. An example of this is the Truth's, glorified is He, words: ﴿Allah bears witness﴾. Allah bears witness, that is, He judges.

In the story of our master Yusuf, peace be upon him, we see how the Truth brought about (a test) for the brothers of Yusuf when they took Yusuf's young brother with them on the journey to Egypt, and how Yusuf arranged a matter so that his brother would be detained with him, and how there was conflict among the brothers of Yusuf, out of fear for their father, after the detention of the younger brother. Their eldest brother said to them, as the Noble Qur'an reports:

﴿Return to your father and say, "O our father, indeed your son has stolen, and we did not testify except to what we knew, and we were not guardians of the unseen. (81) And ask the town in which we were and the caravan in which we came, and indeed, we are truthful."﴾ (Surah Yusuf).

We know that the brothers of Yusuf lied the first time when they committed their shameful deed against Yusuf, but they told the truth the second time, when the brother of Yusuf was detained. Therefore they asked that their father question either the people of the town in which they had been, or their companions in the caravan.

They reported that their brother had had some of the king's equipment taken out from his bag, namely the measuring cup with which grain was measured; and for this reason their testimony this time corresponded to reality, and this is what they reported. ?

So testimony is the decisive factor in disputes. For this reason the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, instructed that a man should not testify to a matter unless he has seen it with his own eyes, as one sees the sun, and "on the like of it, testify or refrain" (1).

The Truth, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿O People of the Book, why do you disbelieve in the signs of Allah while you are witnesses (to them)? (70)﴾ (Surah Al ʿImran)

Thus we know that all testimony revolves around presence and witnessing. For this reason testimony comes in multiple implications: at times it means presence, at times it comes to mean judgment, and a third time it means affirmation. All these meanings converge.

Testimony requires two things: the first is the presence of the witness at the moment the witnessed matter occurred; the second is trustworthy transmission. For this reason Allah, in some rulings, made the testimony of two women equal to the testimony of one man. Someone may say: how does Islam equate the testimony of an ignorant or unlettered man with the testimony of two women, each of whom may be of a high degree of culture and knowledge?

We say: the matter in testimony is not the work of the intellect, but a trust in transmission, and trust in transmission has nothing to do with culture. Testimony requires the presence of the incident. Moreover, a woman's situation is always based on modesty and not intruding upon men. It may happen that an incident occurs and a woman is beside it, and naturally she will not dare to step forward and ask to learn all the details, unlike the man who sees the incident and tries to learn everything that took place. When the Truth desired testimony from two women, He did not ask this because of weak trust in women or increased trust in men, but because testimony is not an invention of the intellect, but the presence of a scene and a trust in transmission.

Some try to promote such issues as though they were a means of attacking some of those who call to Allah. To them I say: one must understand the difference between his enmity toward some of those who call to Allah, and transgressing his limits to the point of opposing Allah; for the person among them does not reject the ruling of the caller, but rejects the ruling of Allah.

The Truth, glorified and exalted, commanded, regarding the testimony of two men, that they should perform the prayer, then they are held for a period, and after that they are summoned to testify. If the family of the deceased rejects their testimony concerning the bequest, then two of the deceased's guardians are summoned to give testimony regarding the bequest. And all of this, why? So that the testimony may come in its correct form, which reveals the full truth.

The Truth concludes the noble verse with: ﴿And fear Allah and listen. And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people﴾, and this is a message to all believers and to people in general; for Allah guides only those who submit to the way of Allah, while whoever defies will not be helped by Allah, since Allah does not help a disbeliever, nor a wrongdoer, nor a defiant transgressor. As for one who believes in Allah, the Truth, glorified is He, helps him upon this path and guides him to the straight path.

And why did Allah reveal this verse after conducting the events that required it? We know that when a ruling descends in a situation that calls for it, the soul yearns for it and is attached to it, like the cup of water which the thirsty person takes eagerly and avidly. Contrast this with the person who is handed a cup of water while not thirsty, who may place it nearby without drinking it; and likewise medicine is brought to the patient at the moment of his greatest suffering from illness, and he approaches it eagerly however bitter its taste. Thus some rulings of the Qur'an came fitting events that had occurred, so that eagerness would be toward the application present in believing souls.

(1) Narrated by al-Daylami and al-Tabarani from Ibn 'Umar. Al-Najm said: al-Rafi'i mentioned that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, was asked about testimony, and he said to the questioner: "Do you see the sun?" He said: "Yes." He said: "On the like of it, testify, or refrain." Al-Hakim and al-Bayhaqi related from Ibn 'Abbas, traced to the Prophet: "If you know like the sun, then testify; otherwise refrain."

Al-Sha'rawi said, concerning the words of the Most High:

"Then the Truth, exalted is He, says after that:

﴿On the Day when Allah will gather the Messengers and say, "What was your response?" They will say, "We have no knowledge. Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen."﴾ (5:109)

Here the Truth, glorified is He, alerts us to the necessity of preparing ourselves for the Day on which Allah will gather the Messengers, the Day of Reckoning. That is, we must be mindful of being held accountable, the higher accountability, in every deed of life, because He, glorified is He, will question the Messengers on that Day: ﴿What was your response?﴾ That is, how did the people respond to the method to which you called? In this there is a rebuke to those who came after the Messengers. We know that the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, said:

﴿How then, when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you, [O Muhammad], as a witness against these?﴾ (4:41) (Surat an-Nisa')

We also know that on the Day of the Great Gathering, our Messenger (ﷺ) will come as a witness over his nation and over all the Messengers who preceded him. An example of this in our lives, and to Allah belongs the highest example, is that we find the family waiting for the son at the door of an examination hall, asking him, "How did you answer?"

Indeed, the family asks the son to give them an overall assessment of the situation. But if they ask, "What did you answer?", this means they want him to recount in detail what he answered for each question. The Truth's question to His Messengers, ﴿What was your response?﴾, is apparently a question to the Messengers, but in reality it is for those who opposed them, and it is as if this is a rebuke to those who did not believe the Messengers, since the task of the Messengers is only conveyance (al-balagh).

What will the Messengers answer on that day concerning Allah? They will give the precise answer that embodies all the etiquette of faith: ﴿We have no knowledge. Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen.﴾ And we find someone asking: how then do they say ﴿We have no knowledge,﴾ even though some responded to their call and others did not? We say: because the Hereafter involves reckoning for the intentions of hearts and the hidden matters. The Messengers knew the open matters of words and conduct, but the Truth reckons according to intention and deed, and He, glorified is He, is the most knowing of the secrets and what the consciences conceal. Also, the prophets knew those who believed in the method and were their contemporaries, but they had no knowledge of those who disbelieved or believed after their times. The answer of the Messengers is the pinnacle of courtesy toward Allah, because each of them knew that the knowledge of Allah is all-encompassing and His knowledge has encompassed everything; therefore their statement came: ﴿Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen.﴾"

Then the Truth says:

﴿When Allah said: "O Jesus, son of Mary, remember My favour upon you and upon your mother, when I strengthened you with the Holy Spirit, so that you spoke to people in the cradle and in maturity; and when I taught you the Book and wisdom, the Torah and the Gospel; and when you shaped from clay the likeness of a bird by My permission, then you breathed into it and it became a bird by My permission, and you healed the blind and the leper by My permission; and when you brought the dead forth by My permission; and when I restrained the Children of Israel from you when you came to them with clear proofs, and those of them who disbelieved said, 'This is nothing but clear magic.'"﴾ (110)

Why, then, does Allah gather all the messengers and ask them a general question, and then single out Jesus, son of Mary, to ask him a specific question about a particular incident?

The Truth wishes by this to teach us that He will question the messengers with a question that clarifies for us the manners of the messengers with the Truth, and shows us the rebuke of the Truth toward those who disbelieved in the method. As for His question, glory be to Him and exalted, to Jesus, son of Mary, that specific question about the particular incident, it is due to the fact that some of those who believed in him placed him in the position of divinity or of being the son of divinity. In this there is an encroachment upon the absolute transcendence (tanzih) of the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted. We know that the utmost that previous nations did was that some of them disbelieved in the messengers and some of them denied the messengers, but no one of these nations claimed that the messenger who came was a god; no one said that, although some sects of the Jews said: "Uzair is the son of Allah," and this sect has become extinct, and no Jew remains who says that. He, glory be to Him, has made associating partners with Him the summit of disbelief that will not be forgiven. (From verse 48, surah al-Nisa')

So it is as if Jesus, peace be upon him, would face the question among the messengers, and then the Truth asks him a specific question concerning himself. The Truth presents the question to Jesus, son of Mary, after reminding him of a number of the blessings which Allah, glory be to Him, bestowed upon him and upon his mother Mary, peace be upon them both:

﴿When Allah said: "O Jesus, son of Mary, remember My favour upon you and upon your mother..."﴾ (surah al-Ma'idah)

Here we find that the Truth, glory be to Him, enumerates some of His blessings upon our master Jesus, namely: the strengthening with the Holy Spirit, which is our master Jibril, peace be upon him; speaking in the cradle, by which the mother of Jesus, our lady Mary, peace be upon her, was cleared of the accusations they had attached to her; and the Truth's teaching him the Book, the wisdom, the Torah and the Gospel. And that He, glory be to Him, empowered him to shape from clay something like the form of a bird by a permission from Him, glory be to Him, and to breathe into it so that it becomes a bird by His permission, glory be to Him. Likewise, the Truth empowered him to heal the blind from blindness, to restore to the leper the natural colour of his skin and cure him, and He made the experiment of restoring the dead to life run through his hands by His permission, glory be to Him. Likewise, the Truth restrained the plot of the Jews from Jesus, son of Mary, and withheld the hands of those who wanted to crucify and kill him, despite the fact that he came to them with the previous miracles so that they might believe; some of them believed, and the one who said about those miracles that they were merely magic disbelieved.

When we reflect with insight upon any one of those matters, we find that the power of the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, has complete manifest clarity. The mere speech of Jesus in the cradle is a miracle, and the cradle, as we know, is the comfortable bed prepared for the infant by the family at the hour of his birth; for the infant has no ability to move from his place if there is something protruding in his cradle that bothers him, because the infant possesses sensation but has no ability to repel what sensation demands.

The newborn, for instance, cannot extend his hand to remove a pebble protruding from the ground beneath the cradle; therefore they level his bed and make it smooth for him. He is merely a spirit in a small body with no power or strength except to sustain life by clinging to the mother's breast. If an infant speaks in the cradle, that means he has possessed a will by which he controls his whole body to the degree that he can utter speech, and this never happens. We find the family smoothing the bed for the infant, because they know that the utmost expression of emotion for him is to cry. And if a tiny insect manages to bite the infant, like a flea or a mosquito, the infant has nothing but crying.

Jesus spoke in the cradle after the Truth had empowered him to do so. Then the Truth brought a reality that is the counterpart of the cradle, namely speech in maturity. If he spoke in the cradle as a miracle to clear his chaste mother, then he would speak in maturity as one who conveys from Allah. Jesus, son of Mary, did not speak in the cradle except with what the Truth said in the Noble Qur'an:

﴿He said: "Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Book and made me a prophet. And He has made me blessed wherever I am, and has enjoined upon me prayer and zakah as long as I remain alive, and [made me] dutiful to my mother, and He has not made me arrogant or wretched. And peace is upon me the day I was born, and the day I die, and the day I am raised alive."﴾ (surah Maryam, 30–33)

Jesus, peace be upon him, said these words in the cradle to clear his mother the truthful, for they had accused her in the most precious thing she possessed, and therefore no word from her would have been of any use. To save her, the Truth conveyed to her, through Jibril or Jesus, peace be upon them both, that she should say:

﴿Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast, so I will not speak today to any human being.﴾ (part of verse 26, surah Maryam)

Glory be to Him and exalted knows that the birth of Jesus from a mother whom no man had touched is a breach of the law of nature in conception; likewise the Truth wished that there be a breach of the law in speech, so Jesus would speak in the cradle with a miraculous speech that has meaning. The Truth taught him the Book: ﴿and when I taught you the Book﴾, meaning Allah taught him writing, taught him the Torah, and sent down to him the Gospel, and inspired him with wisdom, which is sound and precise speech by the inspirations of Allah; and its counterpart in Islam is the ḥadīth (sayings) of the Messenger, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace.

The precision of the Qur'anic expression came to prevent any notion of intervention from the essence of Jesus in what Allah performed upon his hands, to prevent temptation (fitnah). So the Truth said: ﴿and when you shaped from clay the likeness of a bird﴾. Thus Jesus does not create a bird; rather he shapes from clay something like the form of a bird, and the Truth alone creates the bird. For because He is the God, He is the one who creates creation in general; as for humans, they can make things and shape them like created beings, but they are not creatures.

We see this in the statues which the sculptor carves from stone or shapes from clay in the form of a camel or a sparrow, but he has no power to breathe life into it. Man may invent things, such as a cup from refined molten sand, but we have never heard of a male cup and a female cup producing by mating an offspring of cups!

We always see that man's making of something remains bound to its state: it does not reproduce, grow, or sense. The Greatest Creator creates from nothing, while you, O human, make things from what Allah has bestowed upon you of existing things buried in the earth or apparent. He, glory be to Him, did not withhold from you; rather He has described you as having created, but so that you might be mindful that He, glory be to Him and exalted, is the best of creators.

So Jesus shaped from clay the likeness of a bird, and that was from Allah; he breathed into it and it was a bird by the permission of Allah. The difference between the power of a created servant and the power of the Enduring, the All-Powerful Lord, is twofold. The first: when the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, decrees a matter, He, by the absoluteness of His power, enables some of His creation to do the thing; but a servant cannot empower another servant to make a thing like what he makes.

An example of this: if a child wants to carry a chair, he cannot; a strong young man comes and carries the chair for the child. This young man transfers the effect of his strength to the child, but does not give him his strength or transmit it to him, and the child remains weak as he is. As for the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, He empowers whomever He wills to do what He wills. By His greatness, glory be to Him, He transfers His power to one who has no power, so that he may have power. The greatness, then, in what the Messiah did is that the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, willed for him to give life, so he breathed into the clay and it became a bird by the permission of Allah. Our master Abraham had preceded our master Jesus in this when he asked Allah:

﴿My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead.﴾ (part of verse 260, surah al-Baqarah)

So Allah asked him: ﴿Have you not believed?﴾ (part of verse 260, surah al-Baqarah)

Abraham said: (Yes), meaning that he had believed, and he added: ﴿Yes, but that my heart may be at rest.﴾ (part of verse 260, surah al-Baqarah)

The speech here has a separate direction: Abraham had believed, and faith is the tranquillity of the heart in a certain creed, and what occurred increased Abraham in certainty. Abraham did not ask his Lord: "Will You give life to the dead?" Rather Abraham first affirmed the Truth's power to give life and inquired about the manner. Seeking the manner has no bearing on faith, because the manner requires an experiment. So the Truth commanded him to take four birds and gather them to himself so that he might come to know them well, and to cut them with his hands and place each piece upon a mountain and call them; and the pieces came at Abraham's call, having become the very birds they had been before.

Thus Allah willed for Jesus, peace be upon him, to shape from clay the likeness of a bird by the permission of Allah, and to breathe into it by the permission of Allah, so that the bird becomes a bird. And Allah willed for Jesus to heal the *akmah*, that is, one born blind. Someone may say: in our age, corneal transplants are performed, and some who were born without the ability to see can see. We say: what happens in our age is the advance of knowledge based on experiments, whereas what happened with Jesus was a breach of the law, which Allah willed as a miracle. Likewise Allah willed that there be performed upon Jesus the healing of the *abras*, that is, one afflicted with white patches on his skin like pieces of cloth. Likewise He restrained the Children of Israel from him when they wanted to harm and kill him. When they saw all this, some of them believed, and some disbelieved and accused Jesus, peace be upon him, of being a sorcerer. That was from them a lie and a calumny against him, because he was a prophet sent with clear miracles.

In this verse which is the subject of our reflections, we find the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, recounting His blessings upon our master Jesus, peace be upon him. The recounting of a blessing upon the Messenger does not aim to alert the Messenger to the blessing, for the Messenger knows the blessings well because they were bestowed upon him; rather it is a rebuke to those who witnessed these signs and blessings and did not commit to faith in Allah in a way that strengthens and purifies his message to his people. The first blessing upon him was that he was chosen, selected, and strengthened. We note that these verses and blessings divide into two parts: a part that convinces people of intellect, understanding, reflection and spiritual insight, and a part that convinces the materialist people who do not believe in the unseen dominion of Allah. The first part, which convinces the people of intellect and understanding, is the teaching of the Book, the wisdom, the Torah and the Gospel.

The second part, which convinces the materialists, is the material, sensible matters which whoever sees them recognizes cannot be performed by the hand of a human being: such as shaping from clay the likeness of a bird and then breathing into it so that it becomes a bird, the raising of the dead, and the healing of the *akmah* and the *abras*. These verses are a breach of the material law, and therefore the Truth follows each one of them with the phrase "by My permission", meaning that these miracles would not have occurred had Allah not permitted them. The Truth did not mention this for the other verses because they are a manifest and well-known matter, so that the matter may be clear before every person who loves Jesus and elevates him to a station higher than the station of the prophethood supported by Him who sent him; and so that the people of Jesus are not deceived by these verses and do not suppose for him an absolute excellence, but they are merely miraculous signs to establish the truthfulness of the message from Allah.

When Jesus, peace be upon him, took each piece of clay to shape from it a bird and breathed into it so that it became a bird, he did not do that by his own power and will; rather that occurred by a permission from Allah. Jesus did not master that matter as a craft; likewise the healing of the *akmah* and the *abras* and the raising of the dead were by the permission of Allah, and all of that was a breach of the law of matter; therefore the Truth repeated the statement that this breach was by a permission from Him, glory be to Him.

And the Almighty, glorified and exalted is He, says after that:

﴿And when I inspired the disciples [to believe]: "Believe in Me and in My Messenger." They said: "We believe, and bear witness that we are submitting ones (muslimun)."﴾ (5:111)

The word al-hawariyyun (the disciples) is derived from al-muhassat (the whitened ones, i.e. those who whiten cloth by washing and cleansing). Al-hawari is applied to pure, unadulterated fine flour, and it has been applied to anything purified with pure clarity. Here al-hawari means the sincere one, the one who loves the path of goodness. He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And when I inspired﴾. Wahy (inspiration), in its general sense, is the communication of something in a hidden manner. That is, the Truth inspired them to believe in the mission of Jesus, who conveyed from Allah; that is, He made them aware through the promptings of the heart, by which He informed the mother of Moses that she should cast her son into the river, and the river would cast him onto the shore. This is other than the revelation to the Messenger. The revelation to the Messenger is legislative revelation, through a messenger who conveys from Allah, our master Jibril (peace be upon him). As for Allah's inspiration to the mother of Moses or to the disciples, it is the settling of a believing impulse, after which the one inspired turns his attention and finds reality confirming it. When the inspiration of the heart does not clash with a fact, and the inspiration finds nothing in a person's soul that contradicts it, this is a kind of wahy, that is, a communication in a hidden manner, like a man who expects a friend to arrive from a journey, or a type of food he craves and then finds on the table.

Therefore, inspiration comes from Allah to the creatures of Allah as long as it does not clash with anything in the soul or in reality, because inspiration that encounters a clash is not from Allah. Satans inspire one another with ornate speech as deception.

Allah inspired the disciples to believe in Him and in the mission of Jesus (peace be upon him). And as soon as Jesus came and they heard that he was a messenger from Allah, they declared their faith in him and became his close companions. When we see ﴿idh﴾ (when), let us understand that its meaning is a reminder of the time of the event in which the disciples said: "We believe in Jesus as a prophet from Allah," and they called upon him to bear witness that they are submitting ones.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 5, verse 112:

And after that, the Truth says:

﴿When the disciples said, "O Jesus, son of Mary, can your Lord send down to us a table from heaven?" He said, "Fear God, if you are believers."﴾

It is as if Jesus said to them: "Be mindful of God, and do not ask Him for this sign, for as long as you have declared your faith, you are not proposing to God a sign to prove the truth of His messenger. What God has given me of signs as proof of the truth of my message is sufficient for you. It is incumbent upon you to bind yourselves to the method you declared you believe in."

The scholars have paused at their words, "Can your Lord..." (hal yastatee'u rabbuka), and they have asked: How could this statement be made, especially since its apparent meaning is, "Is your Lord able?" And how could the disciples say this when they had called upon Jesus, peace be upon him, to witness that they are Muslims?

The scholars have also said: Whoever speaks in the language must be discerning of the derivations of words, their usages, and their characteristics. The word (yastatee' — "is able") carries the meaning of (yuti' — "obeys"), just as they say (istajaba — "responded") in the sense of (ajaba — "answered"). So the meaning of their question would be: "Will God respond and send down to us a table from heaven?" The verb (istaṭā'a) corresponds to (istajāba). He, glory be to Him and exalted, is the One Who is capable of everything, the One Whom everything obeys, and the One before Whose judgment everything submits. The Truth does not need to be asked; He only commands, in confirmation of His saying, exalted is He:

﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ (Surah Ya-Sin, 82)

God, glory be to Him and exalted, does not say to a thing "Be" except that He knows it will obey, and the Truth does not command something to obey except that its readiness to respond is such that when it hears God's words, "Be," it must come to be. An example of this is His saying, glory be to Him and exalted:

﴿When the heaven is split open, and it listens to its Lord and it is right to do so.﴾ (Surah al-Inshiqaq)

It only waits to hear the command. As soon as it hears the command, it is moved, and to be moved means to obey. All of creation obeys its Creator, glory be to Him and exalted.

Or the meaning of "hal yastatee'" may be: "Will He do?" This is by way of expressing the cause by its effect, since capability is among the causes of bringing an act into being. It has also been said that the intended meaning is: "Are you able to ask your Lord without any impediment or obstacle preventing you from asking Him?" Al-Kisa'i and others read "hal tastatee' rabbaka" with the word (rabbaka) in the accusative, and its original form is "hal tastatee' su'āla rabbika" (are you able to ask your Lord), so the governing noun (su'āl, "asking") was deleted, and the governed noun, the word "rabb," was put in its place and given the accusative case. Al-Zamakhshari said: God did not describe them as believers and sincere; rather, He related their claim. Their words, "Can He...," are a statement that could not come from believers who revere their Lord.

The Disciples said, "We wish to eat from it, and that our hearts may be reassured, and that we may know you have spoken truly to us, and that we may be witnesses to it."

Verse 113

It seems that they wished to imitate our master Ibrahim, the Friend of the Most Merciful (خليل الرحمن), when he asked God about how the dead are brought back to life, so that his heart might be reassured. They had believed with the knowledge of certainty ('ilm al-yaqin), and now they wish to move on to the vision of certainty ('ayn al-yaqin); therefore they asked for the table, which afterwards became a clear reality.

Thus we know that there is a difference between a person believing in himself and his bearing witness to the faith before others. The one who bears witness to the faith before others needs a deeper certainty.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 5, verse 114:

Allah tells us what 'Isa (peace be upon him) said, which differs from their statement about this table (al-ma'idah). He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿'Isa, son of Maryam, said: "O Allah, our Lord, send down upon us a table from the heaven, which will be for us a festival for the first of us and the last of us, and a sign from You. And provide for us, and You are the best of providers."﴾ (5:114)

And the saying of the Truth: ﴿a table from the heaven﴾ means only that there are, for Allah, tables set up on the earth. The whole universe is a table, in which there is much good, if man is able to toil and labour.

When one of us toils and labours, and brings forth from the earth the crops and tends the animals, he comes to his wife with a store that may suffice them as a family for a year: flour, rice, honey, sugar and oil. Then the wife takes a bird, slaughters it, and cooks with it bread and vegetables.

So the whole universe is Allah's set table, from which every person takes according to the measure of his work. The word (ma'idah, table) is applied only to the tray when there is food on it. If it has no food, it is called (khiwan, a tray/stand); because (ma'idah) is derived from the root (m-y-d), and the ma'idah sways (tamid), that is, it is disturbed by the great number of things upon it. Or it gives from what is upon it; so the ma'id is the giver.

The saying of 'Isa (peace be upon him) is full of valuable meanings. He asks that the table be fitting as a festival in which the first and last of them rejoice, and a sign from the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted; and he asks, from the bounty of the lordship of the Provider, that He provide for them; and he acknowledges with gratitude that the Truth is the best of providers.

The comparison between the saying of the disciples (al-hawariyyun) and the saying of 'Isa shows us the difference between the faith of the one who conveys from Allah and the faith of those who receive the message through 'Isa. The faith of 'Isa is the strong, mature faith. As for the faith of the disciples, it is deficient faith. The strength of 'Isa's faith springs from his receiving directly from Allah, whereas the disciples are not so, even though they believed in the message from Allah, and that was accomplished through a messenger. For this reason the messenger ranks above the believers in his conveying, in the ladder of faith, a higher degree. He receives from Allah, and for this reason 'Isa (peace be upon him) corrected their request from Allah when he supplicated his Lord.

He is a chosen, selected messenger; therefore he puts matters in their fitting place, saying: (Allahumma Rabbana, O Allah, our Lord). (Allahumma) is originally (ya Allah, O Allah). When the calling with it became frequent, we removed from it the particle of address and compensated for it with a mim at its end, so it became (Allahumma). It is as if this utterance (Allahumma) prepares the soul of man for intimate communion with Allah, in sanctification and trust that He, glory be to Him, responds; it is a call founded on the servant's love for his Master, so no particle of address stands between him and the name of his Lord.

We notice that 'Isa (peace be upon him) introduced his speech to Allah with the attribute of divinity (Allahumma), for he, as a prophet sent, knows the manifestations of the attribute of Allah. These are manifestations of worship, from the Worshipped to the worshipper. As for the manifestations of the word (Rabb, Lord), they are manifestations of nurture, from the Lord to the one nurtured. The difference between the gift of divinity to creatures and the gift of lordship is that the gift of divinity is a charge (taklif) from the Worshipped to the worshipper. The worshipper obeys the Worshipped in what He commands and in what He forbids. As for the gift of lordship, it is He, glory be to Him, who undertakes the nurture of bodies, minds and hearts; and the Lord is Lord of the believer and of the disbeliever. The Lord undertakes the nurture of the disbeliever despite the disbeliever's denial of divinity. So He, glory be to Him, nurtures the material things that sustain his life.

Therefore we find the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, saying of these disbelievers: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "Allah." Say, "Praise be to Allah." But most of them do not know.﴾ (Surah Luqman, 31:25)

The Truth, glory be to Him, conveys to His Prophet, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, that he should ask the disbelievers who created the heavens and the earth, and they will find no answer to that except their saying: Allah is the Creator. It is the answer of the first nature (fitrah). In our lives we see more than one example of this, and to Allah belongs the highest likeness: when children ask about something, of who brought it, we find the answers following one another until they reach that the giver of everything is Allah. If the child asks his mother, "What shall we eat?" and the mother answers, for example, "We shall eat okra." The child asks, "From where?" The mother answers, "Your father bought it from the vegetable seller." The child asks, "And from where did the vegetable seller get it?" The mother says, "From a merchant in the market." The child asks, "And from where did the merchant get it?" The mother answers, "From the farmer who ploughed the land and sowed the okra seeds in it." The child says, "Who created the earth and made the plants grow?" The mother says, "It is Allah, our Lord, Creator of everything."

Through her dialogue with the child, the mother has arrived at the gift of lordship, which believer and disbeliever share alike. The believer is the one who takes, alongside the gift of lordship, the gift of divinity as well, which is the charge. The gift of divinity gives the believer the gift of lordship in addition to a gift that does not run out: it gives the believer a time in which he does not die, and a blessing that neither leaves him nor he leaves it; and the believer takes by the method the certainty of illumination and the eagerness to act in the light of Allah's method.

'Isa son of Maryam said, calling upon Allah: ﴿O Allah, our Lord, send down upon us a table from the heaven﴾, and he bound himself first with the call of divinity, acknowledging servitude to Allah and committing to the charge coming from Him, and then he came with the call of lordship. "O You who sent down upon us the charge, and O You who undertake our nurture, we call upon You to send down upon us a table from the heaven." He took up his weighty call, and then the aspect of materiality, which is provision. But the disciples put forward their humanity and asked of the table food and eating, saying: (We wish to eat from it, and that our hearts may be at rest, and that we may know that you have told us the truth, and that we may be among its witnesses). As for 'Isa son of Maryam, with the purity of his choice as a messenger, he delayed food behind the weighty matters, saying: ﴿O Allah, our Lord, send down upon us a table from the heaven, which will be for us a festival for the first of us and the last of us, and a sign from You. And provide for us, and You are the best of providers.﴾

It is true that provision touches on food, but provision is not all food. Provision is everything you need and benefit from: food is provision, drink is provision, clothing is provision, knowledge is provision, forbearance is provision, and everything from which you benefit is provision from Allah. For this reason 'Isa brought the general word, which includes food and is broad enough for other things.

The Truth answers the supplication of 'Isa son of Maryam:

﴿Allah said, "Indeed, I will send it down to you. But whoever of you disbelieves after that, I will surely punish him with a punishment with which I have not punished anyone among the worlds."﴾ (5:115)

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 5, verse 115:

And when the Truth says: "Indeed, I" — He uses the singular "nun" (nun al-ifrad). We know that there are two styles in the Truth's (al-Haqq, subhanahu) speaking about Himself. When He speaks of His oneness (wahdaniyyah), He uses the singular "nun," so He, glorified is He, says:

﴿Indeed, I am Allah﴾ (Surah Ta-Ha 20:14)

And when He, glorified and exalted is He, speaks of His comprehensive power that encompasses all the attributes of perfection, which require the bringing into existence of a thing, He uses the plural of majesty (nun al-ta'zim), so He says:

﴿Indeed, We, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed We are its guardians (9)﴾ (Surah al-Hijr)

Here He, glorified is He, wished to give us the meaning of tawhid, so He said: ﴿He said: "Indeed, I will send it down to you."﴾ This is because the table (al-ma'idah) will descend from the heaven, and none is able to do that except Allah alone, glorified and exalted is He.

The Truth follows this with His saying: ﴿Whoever among you disbelieves after that, I will surely punish him with a punishment I will not inflict upon anyone among the worlds.﴾ So He, glorified is He, sends His messengers after He chooses them, and beware, O servant, that you should say: "So-and-so, in himself, among the messengers, is better than so-and-so," because the Truth is the most knowing of His messengers: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message.﴾ It is incumbent upon us to follow the messengers. When some of the people of ignorance (ahl al-jahiliyyah) attempted to mock the matter of the Qur'an that was sent down upon Muhammad (ﷺ), as the Noble Qur'an informs in His saying, exalted is He:

﴿They said: "Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a great man from one of the two cities?" (31) Do they distribute the mercy of your Lord? We have distributed among them their livelihood in the life of this world, and We have raised some of them above others in degrees, so that some of them may take others in service. And the mercy of your Lord is better than what they accumulate.﴾ (Surah al-Zukhruf)

The people of ignorance said: "Why was the Qur'an not sent down to a great man of Makkah or of al-Ta'if?!" They said that mockingly regarding the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ). The Truth, glorified and exalted, has spoken the decisive word on that statement: no one has the right to choose the Messenger, because the Messenger is chosen by Allah, and none of mankind can choose as a messenger someone of power or rank.

He, glorified and exalted, prepares every messenger with the preparation fitting to his mission, and the station of messengership and prophethood is the highest in this world and the Hereafter. The Truth, glorified is He, who arranges the affairs of His creation, has apportioned endowments, out of mercy from Him, among the servants, so that they may support one another and assist one another, and each of them needs the work of the other. When He, glorified is He, sends a messenger, He chooses the sign suitable for him for the age in which he came. And no people proposed a sign which Allah then brought, and then those who proposed the sign did not believe after its coming, except that the Truth, glorified is He, sent down upon them painful punishment. And when following the messenger is conditioned on specific signs, this request carries within it evasion and escape from commitment to the method of Allah, as if those who ask for them insist on disbelief in the messenger despite their request for the sign. For this reason the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And We did not refrain from sending signs except that the former peoples denied them. And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wronged her with it. And We do not send signs except as a warning.﴾ (Surah al-Isra' 17:59)

Likewise, the proposal of the people of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he bring them signs other than the signs of the Qur'an, although the signs of the Qur'an satisfy everyone who has a thinking mind and a feeling heart, and the sunnah of Allah regarding those who ask for signs and then do not believe in them is clear, and it is severe punishment. An example of this is the people of Thamud, who asked for a she-camel as proof of the truthfulness of Salih (peace be upon him), and when the miracle occurred they disbelieved in it, so Allah punished them with the worst punishment.

And some of the people of the Messenger (ﷺ) went to extremes in asking for strange signs:

﴿And they said: "We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth (90), or you have a garden of palms and grapevines and cause rivers to gush forth within it abundantly (91), or you cause the heaven to fall upon us in fragments as you claim, or you bring Allah and the angels before us as a guarantee (92), or you have a house of gold, or you ascend into the sky. And we will not believe in your ascension until you bring down to us a book we can read." Say: "Glory be to my Lord! Am I anything but a human messenger?"﴾ (93) (Surah al-Isra')

Muhammad (ﷺ) was merciful toward his family and clan, and therefore he did not ask the Truth for signs other than those Allah had sent down to him. And Jesus (peace be upon him), in the manner of the courtesy of the messengers, asked that the table be sent down. The scholars differed: Did the Truth, glorified and exalted, send down a table or not?

Some held firmly to the saying of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿Allah said: "Indeed, I will send it down."﴾ And others said: the Truth, glorified is He, made the descent of the table conditional on the sending of punishment upon them if they did not believe, so they abandoned their request for its descent. And those who said the table descended differed about its description. Some of them said: the table descended, and upon it was a roasted fish without scales or skin and without bones, for it was a table from heaven, and with it five loaves, and on each loaf was something of what they recognized: one loaf had honey on it, another had olives on it, a third had ghee on it, a fourth had cheese on it, and a fifth had dried meat (qadid) on it.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 5, verse 116:

After that, He, glorified is He, says:

﴿And [mention] when Allah says, "O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as deities besides Allah'?" He will say, "Exalted are You! It was not for me to say that to which I have no right. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is within myself, and I do not know what is within Your self. Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen." (116)﴾

We know that this is the dialogue that will take place between the Truth and Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, on the day when the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, gathers the messengers:

﴿On the Day when Allah will gather the messengers and say, "What was the response you received?" They will say, "We have no knowledge. Indeed, it is You who is the Knower of the unseen." (109)﴾ (Surah al-Ma'idah)

Someone may ask: why did the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, bring this dialogue in the past tense?

﴿And [mention] when Allah says, "O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as deities besides Allah'?"﴾ (part of verse 116, Surah al-Ma'idah).

We all know that every event has a time and a place. The time of this event is the Day of Resurrection, and its place is the arena of the scene and the gathering. He, glorified is He, is the Creator of every time and every place, and He may speak of any matter in any form He wills, whether the past, the present, or the future. He brought everything into existence from past, present and future, and in His hand is the command of all that He created and of whoever was created. He is the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting. As for us, the children of Adam, our situation with time differs. For our actions, time is one of three: past, meaning that the event occurred before I speak, such as my saying "Zayd met me"; this means the act has been completed and become established.

And present, meaning that the event is in the state of occurring, that is, it is happening now, such as my saying "Zayd is meeting me," and you intend the present, that he is meeting me now.

This means that the eye sees Zayd, and there is no "where" with the eye. And future, meaning that the event will occur, such as my saying "Zayd will meet me." Here a person does not possess himself so that the event happens from him, nor does he possess that nothing will befall the person who will meet him that might prevent him from completing the event, nor does he possess that the cause of the meeting will remain in place. Therefore, with the future, it is not valid for a person to judge anything, because he possesses no element of the event.

The one who possesses this is the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, alone. Therefore the Qur'an teaches us the nobility of truthfulness in speech, in His saying, exalted is He:

﴿And never say of anything, "Indeed, I will do that tomorrow," (23) unless [adding], "If Allah wills."﴾ (part of verse 23 and part of verse 24, Surah al-Kahf).

A person must respect his limited capacity and always remember the power of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, over him. This does not mean that Allah, glorified is He, prevents us from planning for the future. No, rather He asks us to plan, to study all possibilities, and we must say "If Allah wills," because by that we put forward the will of the One who possesses every affair, who is Allah, glorified and exalted is He.

Some orientalists, enemies of Islam, have tried to infiltrate the minds of Muslims with their poison by questioning the non-arrangement of actions in the sequence of their occurrence in some verses of the Qur'an. One of them said: How does the Truth, glorified is He, say:

﴿The command of Allah has come, so do not seek to hasten it. Exalted is He above what they associate. (1)﴾ (Surah al-Nahl).

This is a report about the Day of Resurrection, so how can Allah bring it in the past tense, and then say after that: "so do not seek to hasten it"? Hastening a thing occurs only if it has not yet happened, so it seems there is a contradiction in the speech, because He says "has come," and then says "so do not seek to hasten it."

We say: the One speaking is the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, and not a human being like you, bound by his times. Rather, He is the speaker who is the master of all times and their Creator. When He, glorified is He, says "The command of Allah has come," it means that the command of Allah is certainly coming, because no power can prevent His will from not being. Any act of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, is stripped of the circumstances of time and the circumstances of place. If we read, for example, His saying, exalted is He:

﴿And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (part of verse 100, Surah al-Nisa').

That does not mean that the forgiveness and mercy of Allah have passed their time and their moment ended. Rather, let us say: Allah was Forgiving and Merciful and still is Forgiving and Merciful. He, glorified and exalted is He, is Forgiving and Merciful before anyone exists to be forgiven and shown mercy, and all the more so will He be Forgiving and Merciful after there exists one who deserves forgiveness and mercy. He, glorified is He, is exempt from being subject to events so that He changes, because time is created by Allah, so do not say "when" or "where," for by Him they came into being. The Truth uses the past tense because the occurrence is certain, to establish the occurrence of a matter that has not yet happened, because when Allah says of something that it will happen, it must happen.

In any speech about Jesus, son of Mary, the Truth emphasizes that he is "the son of Mary." Here the Truth asks Jesus, peace be upon him: ﴿Did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as deities besides Allah"?﴾ We know that a question comes always in one of two ways: either a question by which the questioner learns what he did not know, wishing to be informed by the one questioned, like the saying of one who says: "Did so-and-so meet you yesterday?"; or a question that comes not so that the questioner may learn from the one questioned, but so that the questioner may make the one questioned acknowledge.

An example of this, and to God belongs the highest likeness, is that a student asks his teacher in order to learn from him, and the teacher informs him of new knowledge and new information. Likewise a teacher asks a student in order to make him acknowledge the truth and agree to it, so that it becomes settled in the student. The question of God to Jesus is of the latter kind, so that it may be a proof against those who claimed that Jesus is a deity or a son of God. Some orientalists tried to cast doubt upon the Qur'an, saying: there is a contradiction in the Qur'an, God forbid, and they based this on the Truth's saying:

﴿And stop them; indeed, they are to be questioned.﴾ (Surah al-Saffat).

That is, the Truth affirms that every being is accountable for what it does and believes. But He, glorified is He, says in another place in the noble Qur'an:

﴿So on that Day, no man will be asked about his sin, nor will any jinn (39).﴾ (Surah al-Rahman).

Does this mean that they will not be asked? No, rather they will be asked so as to make them acknowledge what they did, not so that Allah may learn from them what they did, for He, glorified is He, is Knowing of everything. Those orientalists do not know that a question among the Arabs comes in two ways: one to let the questioner know, and one to make the questioned acknowledge. The Truth's questioning of people on the Day of Resurrection about what they did is so that they acknowledge what they did and what they committed, because acknowledgment is the master of proofs. The questioning of the Truth, glorified is He, is not the questioning of one who desires to know, for He, glorified is He, is Knowing of everything. A person must maintain the station in which his Lord has placed him, and so was Jesus, son of Mary. Likewise, God's question to Jesus is a rebuke, reproach and censure of those who said about Jesus what had not been conveyed to them.

Indeed, Jesus, peace be upon him, did not convey to them, nor did he ask them to take him and his mother as deities besides Allah, because Jesus, son of Mary, conveys only what is revealed to him from his Lord. Therefore, Jesus' answer comes as a response to any excess of the followers: ﴿He will say, "Exalted are You! It was not for me to say that to which I have no right."﴾ When we hear "Exalted are You" (subhanaka), let us know that it is a comprehensive declaration of God's transcendence, the transcendence from being resembled by any of Allah's creatures. God has existence, and man has existence, but beware, O man, of saying that your existence is like the existence of God, for the existence of God is intrinsic, while your existence is not intrinsic, and everything in you is granted to you by God. Therefore your wealth is not like the wealth of God; rather His wealth is intrinsic and your wealth is granted by Him, glorified is He. Nor is any of your attributes like the attributes of God, for He, glorified is He, has absolute power and might, and you must take everything related to God within the scope of "Glorified is He" ("there is nothing like unto Him").

Likewise is Jesus' glorification of his Lord and Creator: ﴿Exalted are You! It was not for me to say that to which I have no right.﴾ Jesus, son of Mary, knows that the chosen messenger from God has no right to say that he is a deity. Jesus responds to that with a matter agreed upon: ﴿If I had said it, You would have known it.﴾ Because all agree that God knows everything that proceeds from the servants of conduct, words and deeds: ﴿He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal.﴾ Everyone knows the exaltedness of the Truth and His transcendence above having any new knowable thing that He did not know before. Everyone also knows that God knows the secrets of the breasts; therefore Jesus says: ﴿You know what is within myself, and I do not know what is within Your self,﴾ and he affirms that the Truth, the Knower of everything, knows that this had not occurred to him. This is the reason for the inclusion of three forms in this verse. The first form is His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿Exalted are You! It was not for me to say that to which I have no right,﴾ and this is Jesus' glorification of his Lord. The second form is Jesus' saying: ﴿If I had said it, You would have known it,﴾ and the third is: ﴿You know what is within myself, and I do not know what is within Your self.﴾ Thus nothing comes from Jesus. Someone may ask: and what is in the self? What is in the self is what one keeps secret and does not show, for "self" (nafs) is used once to mean the essence that comprises spirit and body together, and when it is applied to the essence of God, we exalt Him above being parts, but it is His essence taken within the scope of transcendence. The example is the Truth's saying:

﴿Your Lord has prescribed upon Himself mercy.﴾ (part of verse 54, Surah al-An'am).

Thus is our understanding of the word "self" (nafs) when attributed to God: He is exalted above being like us. God has a face and we have a face, but we understand God's face within the scope of "there is nothing like unto Him," and likewise God's hand and all of God's attributes. We know that God has names, some of which He has taught us, some of which He taught to some of His creation, and some of which He has reserved for His own essence. There are also some attributes of God that come merely for the sake of correspondence, such as the Truth's saying:

﴿Indeed, the hypocrites deceive Allah, but He is deceiving them.﴾ (part of verse 142, Surah al-Nisa').

We never say that God is a deceiver, but the attribute here came for correspondence, because it is mentioned in contrast to "they deceive Allah." Therefore we do not take from it a name of God; rather it came in response to what proceeds from the enemies of God.

Jesus, son of Mary, concludes his words: ﴿Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen.﴾ "Knower" ('Allam) is an intensification of the act itself and an intensification of its repetition. He, glorified is He, knows the unseen of each one of His creatures and the unseen of everything in His dominion. Thus the Qur'an came with Jesus' answer, peace be upon him, and it is an answer that encompasses every field of denial against those who said such a statement.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 5, verse 117:
