The Qur'an, through the words of Jesus (peace be upon him), continues to counter what some of his followers said. He says:

﴿I told them nothing except what You commanded me: "Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord." And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them; but when You caused me to die, You were the Watcher over them, and You are, over all things, Witness.﴾ (117)

Through his words to his Lord, may He be blessed and exalted, Sayyidna Jesus (peace be upon him) presented the methodology he brought to all people, and he conveyed it in its entirety. He affirmed that he is a servant of Allah and His messenger. Since the Truth is the Knower of the unseen, He knows everything, even what is within the soul. It is as if he is also affirming that his own self had not produced any of those thoughts. And he declares that he conveyed only what Allah commanded.

﴿I told them nothing except what You commanded me: "Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord." And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them; but when You caused me to die, You were the Watcher over them, and You are, over all things, Witness.﴾ (Surah al-Ma'idah)

The witness (shahid) is the one who observes and who has no role in moving the witnessed thing toward anything other than what he witnessed. Jesus, son of Mary (peace be upon him), says: ﴿when You caused me to die, You were the Watcher over them﴾. The matter of his being caused to die (tawaffi) by the Truth, and of his being raised to Him, we have mentioned before in our reflections, but I will now add some further glimpses, because I see that every reader or listener of these reflections has the right to find a suitable summary that spares him from returning to what was said earlier on this matter, so that the meanings connect in the reader's mind.

The birth of Jesus (peace be upon him) caused a stir, and likewise the matter of Allah's causing him to die caused a stir. Allah made it appear to the killers of Jesus that they had killed him. When they wanted to kill him, he entered a khawkha, and the khawkha is a door within a door. This was the arrangement of old houses, where there is a large door for bringing in large things, and within this large door there is a small door that permits individuals to pass. In the roof of this house there was an opening. When a man called Tatyanus (Tatianus) entered, seeking Jesus, Jesus looked up and found that something had lifted him up. The people delayed Tatyanus, and then he came out to them, so they asked: "If this is Tatyanus, where is Jesus? And if this is Jesus, where is Tatyanus?"

Thus the resemblance became confused for them, after Allah cast the likeness of Jesus upon Tatyanus. Or, when they came upon him, Jesus was with his disciples (hawariyyun), and Jesus said to the disciples: "Which of you will take on my likeness, and he will have Paradise?" Every disciple knew that there was no messenger like Jesus (peace be upon him), so what would a disciple want for himself more than Paradise? Sarkhas stepped forward, and the likeness of the Messiah (peace be upon him) was cast upon him, and the Jews killed Sarkhas. Or, the people who went to kill Jesus and found that he had been raised feared that the story of Jesus's being raised would spread among the people and they would believe in him, so the killers brought a person and killed him. Or, the one slain was one of those who had sold Jesus to the Jews, and the capacity for repentance awoke in his soul, so he offered himself as a substitute and ransom for the Messenger.

The matter of tawaffi, as we know, is taking someone in full, without any breach of the body, through killing. We, the Muslims, know that the Truth raised Muhammad (ﷺ) through the Night Journey and the Ascension to the heavens, and he returned to us again to complete his message. Therefore we affirm the matter of Jesus's being raised, and that Allah caused him to die, meaning He took him back in full without any breach of the body, and that he will return again to pray behind a believer in Allah and in Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah.

The matter of ascension (raf') is acceptable in Islam. Allah raised the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) through the Ascension, and a dialogue took place between him and Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and likewise a dialogue took place between him and Yahya (peace be upon him), and Adam (peace be upon him), and others of the prophets, and the Truth made the prayer obligatory upon the community of Muslims during that journey.

So we fully affirm the ascent of a human being with his flesh and bones into the heavens as something that is possible and has occurred; as for the length of the duration or its absence, that does not invalidate the principle.

As for the link between the descent of Jesus, son of Mary, to the earth and the Hour, the texts on this matter in the Noble Qur'an are open to interpretation and not definitive in their meaning, and they have come in the pure Prophetic Sunnah, but they are not known as part of the religion by necessity, so we do not declare unbelievers those who find their understanding difficult. Allah, glorified is He, desires mercy for creation; therefore every matter at which reason stops, and which adds no ruling, Allah brings in a manner that does not cause trial. If we affirm that Jesus was raised, that adds no ruling upon us and removes no ruling. Thus the Truth, glorified is He, brought the matter of the Night Journey by a definitive text, whereas the matter of the Ascension did not come as an explicit text in the Qur'an, but came by implication, because the Truth, glorified is He, said:

﴿And he saw him in another descent, at the Lote-tree of the utmost boundary, near which is the Garden of Refuge﴾ (Surah al-Najm)

Thus the Night Journey is an earthly sign, and the Ascension is a heavenly sign. The earthly sign is something the Messenger of Allah could establish evidence for, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went to Bayt al-Maqdis and described it to them, with His words, glorified is He:

﴿Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque, whose surroundings We have blessed﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 1)

The Prophet (ﷺ) described the caravans he saw on the return journey. So the Night Journey was an earthly sign, while the heavenly sign, which is the Ascension, came by implication, and likewise the matter of Jesus's being raised (peace be upon him). Whoever sees that this came from the all-encompassing power of Allah accepts it. As for whoever's reason stops, we say to him: your reason's stopping does not take you out of faith and certainty. When we reflect carefully on the linguistic sense of the word (tawaffaytani), we find that tawaffa may mean "caused to die," for the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿Say: The angel of death who has been entrusted with you will take you in full﴾ (from verse 11, Surah al-Sajdah)

And the Truth, glorified is He, also says:

﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that have not died during their sleep; then He withholds those for whom He has decreed death and releases the others until an appointed term﴾ (from verse 42, Surah al-Zumar)

He calls sleep a tawaffi, and He also called it death. It is a matter that involves sending and seizing. The meaning of death, in some of its aspects, is the absence of the sense of life, and the one who sleeps is absent from the sense of life, so it is possible that tawaffi means sleep. It is also said of a debt: "I took my debt from so-and-so," meaning I took my debt in full without deficiency. Likewise, concerning the killing of the Messiah, the Truth, mighty and exalted, gave the decisive word:

﴿They did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them﴾ (from verse 157, Surah al-Nisa')

We know that death is also opposed to killing, for the Truth says: ﴿Then if he dies or is killed﴾ (from verse 144, Surah Al 'Imran).

Death is the departure of the soul while the parts remain intact, whereas killing is causing destruction in the structure so that the soul departs. And the Truth said on the tongue of the Messiah: ﴿when You caused me to die (tawaffaytani)﴾, meaning You took me in full without deficiency. This matter does not negate the raising. We know that all of this will be a subject of dialogue between Jesus, son of Mary, and the Truth, glorified is He, on the great Day of Assembly, which the Qur'an brought to us in order to inform us of what establishes the truth of faith.

Jesus (peace be upon him) says of himself that he was merely a witness over his people during his time among them, but after Allah raised him to Himself, the watch over the people belongs to Allah. The Truth, glorified is He, is always Witness and always Watcher, whereas Jesus, with his human nature, can only bear witness, while Allah alone is capable of bearing witness, changing, and preventing.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 5, verse 118:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) informs us of what came from the tongue of Jesus, son of Mary, in His noble words:

﴿If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Almighty, the All-Wise.﴾ (5:118)

One may say: Is there not a clear difficulty in this matter? Some of Jesus' followers claimed that they had been told by Jesus to take him and his mother as two deities besides God. How, then, does Jesus ask forgiveness for them in this verse?

We say: Jesus did not say, "O Lord, forgive them." Rather, he said: ﴿If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Almighty, the All-Wise.﴾ That is, Jesus left the matter to the absolute will of God. He, as a messenger from God, knows that God's mercy precedes His wrath, and that He, glorified is He, has absolute power, so no power constrains Him, and absolute will is His. "And they are servants of God by their own choice."

We know that all of God's creation are slaves of God. But those who obey God and believe in Him specifically are the servants of God (ʿibād). Thus creation is of two kinds: the servants of God, who went to God in faith, love and obedience; and the second kind, the slaves (ʿabīd) who are subdued by the dominance of their master. Even the disbeliever did not disbelieve against God's will; rather he disbelieved by the power of choice God gave him, to act or not to act. God was able to create a creation that would not disobey His command and would do what God commands them. God did this with the angels.

But the subjugation of compulsion establishes for God the attribute of al-Qahhar (the Subduer) over the subjugated, and does not establish the attribute of love. Love comes from the creature being free to believe or disbelieve, and then choosing belief. Thus he believed through love, not through compulsion. This is how God wants His creatures who believe in Him. All existence, except for humankind, is subjugated and cannot disobey: the sun, the moon, the rain, the air, the clouds, and everything in the universe is subdued to God.

So if God had wanted creatures compelled to believe in Him, no one of His creation could have disbelieved in Him. But the Truth wanted to establish the attribute of compulsion in what is other than humankind; as for humankind, God created him free to choose between disbelief and belief, so that some of the servants would do what God loves and approves, and follow God's path, knowing that God does not burden them beyond their capacity. He, glorified is He, does not obligate one to die or to fall ill, nor does He obligate one who lacks the instrument of choice, which is reason, nor one who has not attained the maturity of reason. For obligation (taklif) upon a human is not complete except with the presence of three conditions: first, that reason exists; second, that reason be in full maturity, which is rushd (discernment); and third, that there be no force threatening his life and compelling him to do something.

Thus we know that there are three who are excluded from the circle of obligation: the insane; one whose reason is not yet mature because he has not reached discernment; and one compelled by the act of another. God has given, along with obligation, reward for obedience and punishment for disobedience, and thereby no one has any argument against God. Whoever enters obligation willingly is of the servants of God. Whoever disobeys God and leaves obligation is of the subjugated slaves in everything, apart from the obligations in which they were given choice.

So the servants are those who entered servanthood by weighing faith against its opposite, disbelief... that is, between what is willed by God and what is not willed by God. How, then, does Jesus, son of Mary, say, despite knowing their disbelief: ﴿If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants﴾? We say: the meaning of ("servants") and ("slaves"), which we explained earlier, describes the state of the human being in this world and what he is in it. But the dialogue we read in the Qur'an between Jesus, peace be upon him, and God, the Truth, glorified and exalted, takes place in the Hereafter, and all of us in the Hereafter are obedient servants.

When we survey the word ("servants," ʿibād) in the Qur'an, we find that the servants are the chosen elite who chose God's will above their own choice, and so became equal to the subjugated in full. An example is the saying of the Truth, glorified is He:

﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility﴾ (25:63)

Here He mentions the beautiful qualities of this elite of servants. Even Satan declares his inability to lead the sincere servants astray, as the Noble Qur'an affirms:

﴿except Your sincere servants among them﴾ (38:83)

But in the Hereafter all are servants, and behold, the Truth, glorified is He, addresses those who led others astray, saying:

﴿Did you lead My servants astray?﴾ (25:17)

All are servants of God on the Day of Resurrection, and all carry out God's will, and no one has authority over anything of his limbs and organs. The eye, which was subjected to the servant in this world, obeys the servant's command, so he chooses to look at what is lawful or to see what is unlawful; this eye then regains its freedom from its owner, so he has no authority over it on the Last Day. Likewise the hand, the tongue, the skin, the foot, and all the limbs. In this world the human soul is like a commander over all the limbs and organs, which carry out the human's commands, whether for good or for evil, whether for obedience or for disobedience. But on the Day of Resurrection these limbs and organs are released to bear witness to all that the human did, so no one has any will except God's will.

﴿To whom belongs the Kingdom this Day? To God, the One, the Subduer﴾ (40:16)

The wills of humans have ended, and God's will remains, so all become servants of God. On this basis there is no difficulty in Jesus' words: ﴿If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants.﴾ We also know that the word ("slaves," ʿabīd) includes all of us in what we have no choice in, such as the will to breathe, or the time of birth or the time of death. But believers ascend from ("slavehood," ʿabdiyyah) to ("servanthood," ʿibādiyyah) by carrying out God's path, whereas the disbelievers and the sinners disobey God by the choice they have, and walk the road of disobedience in opposition to God's path. And so that the Truth may prove to us all that the disbelievers are merely slaves, He afflicts them with illness, poverty and deep psychological pains, and not one of them dares to oppose God's will in these events which He brings upon them. Therefore the believer thanks the Truth for his choice, because God has protected him with the instruments of choice: existence, maturity, and freedom from coercion.

We may note that all of us on the Day of Resurrection, as we said before, become servants of God, so no one among us has any refusal regarding anything, and all will is God's. The Truth, glorified is He, has cited what came from the tongue of Jesus, peace be upon him, saying: ﴿If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants, and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Almighty, the All-Wise.﴾ This appendage to the words of Jesus, son of Mary, does not come as an apology or a plea for mercy from God on behalf of those who disbelieved in God and associated partners with Him. The Almighty, the All-Wise, is He who is not overcome in His command, and whom no power dominates, and no power other than God's power protects these people. He is the Subduer, the Almighty: if He wills to forgive them, there is none to repel His will.

Some superficial people who seek out errors in the Qur'an have said: Would it not have been more fitting for him to say, "If You forgive them, indeed You are the Forgiving, the Merciful"? We respond to these superficial people by saying: every word in the Qur'an attracts its meaning, and every meaning in the Qur'an is in love with its word. Therefore the appendage in this verse came in a way that serves the absolute will in punishing them or forgiving them. If He punishes them, there is no second power that can protect them from His punishment, because He, glorified is He, is the Almighty. And if He forgives them, there is no higher power that asks Him: how did You forgive them when they were disbelievers?

Thus He, glorified is He, is not questioned about what He does, because He is the Almighty, the All-Wise. Moreover, as for their saying that it would have been more suitable to say, "indeed You are the Forgiving, the Merciful," we say to them: that suits His words ﴿And if You forgive them﴾, but it does not suit ﴿If You punish them﴾. So the appendage of the verse had to come in a way that suits ﴿If You punish them﴾ and also suits His words ﴿And if You forgive them﴾.

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿God said: "This is a day on which the truthful shall profit from their truthfulness. For them are gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. God is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. That is the supreme triumph."﴾ (5:119)

We know that there is a truthfulness that profits on the Day of Resurrection, and it is the truthfulness that is connected to the truthfulness of this world. And there is a truthfulness that does not profit on the Day of Resurrection, an example of which is the statement of the accursed Iblis, as the Noble Qur'an relates:

﴿Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you and failed you.﴾

(Part of verse 22, Surah Ibrahim)

Such truthfulness profits no one, because the Hereafter is not the abode of obligation (dar al-taklif). But the truthfulness that is connected to the truthfulness of this world is the statement of Jesus, peace be upon him: ﴿If I had said it, You would have known it.﴾ That is why Allah says concerning the connected truthfulness: ﴿This is a day on which the truthful shall profit from their truthfulness.﴾

That is because the truthfulness of the truthful on the Day of Resurrection is truthfulness connected to their truthfulness in the time of obligation, which is this world, and they receive the good pleasure of Allah: ﴿For them are gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. God is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him.﴾ If someone asks: how can a servant be pleased with his Lord?

We say: when the believing servants witness the reward prepared for them in the Hereafter, they become filled with joy and say:

﴿Praise be to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us and made us inherit the land, that we may settle in Paradise wherever we will.﴾ (part of verse 74, Surah al-Zumar)

This verse, which speaks of the day on which the truthful shall profit from their truthfulness, says ﴿That is the supreme triumph,﴾ as if there is a superficial triumph and a great triumph. The superficial triumph is what a person gives himself in the abode of obligation of short-lived and fleeting enjoyment, so that outwardly it appears he has won; but in reality it is not the great triumph, because regret will follow it, and no pleasure followed by regret is a triumph. For the worldly life, with all its bounty, is a bounty proportioned to a person's capacities and imagination, and it is a bounty threatened by two things: that the bounty be removed from a person, and we have seen many who enjoyed bounty from whom it was removed; or that a person leave this bounty by death, and we see that often. As for the bounty that is the great triumph, it is the connected bounty that no one can prevent and nothing can cut off.

Al-Sha'rawi, Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66), on Surah 5, verse 120:

The Exalted Lord concludes Surah al-Ma'idah with His words:

﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them, and He is over all things competent.﴾ (120)

The heavens and the earth are two containers for existence and for all creatures: constellations, stars, the sun, the moon, planets, air, clouds, water, animals, and humans. The earth, which is the lower dominion that we see, and what it contains of provisions, animals and humans. The heavens and what they encompass and include of the higher dominion (malakut) are both, together, Allah's dominion (mulk) and sovereignty (malak). He, glory be to Him, is the One who owns everything, and He also owns the owner of the thing. The words of the Truth, ﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾, accord with the words of the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary:

﴿If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.﴾ (Surah al-Ma'idah)

That is to say, nothing among Allah's creation can step outside the will (muradat) of Allah. As for this world, Allah has placed its means in the hands of people: one person's provision is in the hand of another, and some of us hold authority over others. There is the owner of the food and the owner of the garment, but not every owner is a king, because the king is the one who owns the owner; these are the laws of the cosmos. In the Hereafter there is one owner, the Owner of the Day of Judgment. It is as if the Truth ended this surah with speech about the end of life, because He, glory be to Him, began it with speech about the rulings of Allah, saying:

﴿O you who believe, fulfil the contracts. Lawful to you are the animals of grazing livestock﴾ (from verse 1 of Surah al-Ma'idah).

He, glory be to Him, spoke in the rulings about hunting on land and hunting at sea, about the lawful and unlawful among the livestock, about marriage, and about everything connected with the responsibilities of life, and some of us hold authority over others. But on the Last Day the matter is different. So He began the surah with a command, which is: ﴿Fulfil the contracts﴾.

Every command that comes from the Supreme Commander: the one commanded either does or does not do it. Thus there are among people those who believe and those who disobey, and this means that those commanded have freedom of choice. Had the matter been that they must act without choice, the Commander would have created creatures who were compelled to act, and He would thereby have overpowered them. But the Supreme Commander left these commands to human choice, and they are capable of obedience and of fulfilling contracts, and they are capable of disobedience.

He, glory be to Him, began the surah with the realm of choice in man, which Allah created so that moral responsibility (taklif) would arise from it. He then made clear that choice has a limited term that will end, and Allah will gather people on the day when the truthful will benefit from their truthfulness, and the whole matter will belong to Allah.

The Truth concludes the surah with His words, glory be to Him: ﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, He, glory be to Him, owns the whole cosmos, and the cosmos, as we know, is composed of many kinds. The first kind in the cosmos that serves without being served is inanimate matter (jamad), and inanimate matter may be water, mountains, iron, the sun, the moon, stars; all of these are inanimate, that is, they have no sensation. And these inanimate things serve, first and foremost, plants. Plants serve animals, and animals serve humans.

Thus inanimate matter serves everything above it of plants, animals and humans. Plants serve animals and humans; animals serve humans. All these things that serve humans have no choice, and all of them are compelled to serve humans; the sun has never once been angry with mankind so as to withhold its warmth from them, nor has the beast of burden refused its rider.

Man has two parts: one part is compelled by the Truth, so that man cannot control or dominate it, such as sickness or death, and in this he shares with animals, plants and inanimate matter; and another part in which man is free, which is the application of the method (manhaj).

When we look at the aspect in which the Truth has compelled man, we find that it is for man's benefit. Man does not choose to breathe, nor for blood to flow in his veins, nor for his kidneys to work; he is compelled in all of that. It is among Allah's mercies to His creation that He made them directed and compelled in these respects; He did not place anyone's breathing in another's hand, nor make the heart work by human will. Man, therefore, is given choice only in matters of moral responsibility. It is as if the Truth reminds man that the realm of choice is a covenant between the believer and his Lord, because choice will be taken away from the servants on the Day of Resurrection, and all servants will be compelled, and the human being will become like inanimate matter, plants and animals. This is why the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them, and He is over all things competent.﴾ (120) (Surah al-Ma'idah)

On the Day of Resurrection man will be without choice, because the Truth used the word (ma) here, which indicates non-rational things, that is, those that have no choice. It is as if reason has its function in this world, which is discrimination between alternatives, whereas in the Hereafter all are equal before their Creator. We have previously learned the difference between (malk) and (malakut). And we all read the words of the Truth:

﴿Thus did We show Abraham the malakut of the heavens and the earth﴾ (from verse 75 of Surah al-An'am).

It is as if the Truth alerts us that the world contains what falls under sense and perception, and what does not fall under sense and perception. That which falls under sense and perception is the realm of (mulk). That which does not fall under sense and perception is the realm of (malakut). We know of the realm of malakut only what Allah has informed us of. There is in the realm of mulk what Allah has hidden from us, and He alone is capable of all things, and the Truth asks us to take lesson from the visible phenomena of the world. To Him, glory be to Him, belongs absolute knowledge of the realm of (malakut), that is, of the inner realities behind these unseen phenomena. (Mulk) and (malakut) both exist in this world and in the Hereafter, except that mulk is apparent and malakut is hidden.

The Exalted Lord distributes the means of dominion in this world among His creatures, and He holds the power of disposal over what is in our hands and what is hidden from us. The Truth wills to conclude this matter from the justifications of man's vicegerency (khilafah) on earth, and so He says: ﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them.﴾ So to Allah belongs the malakut, and to you, O servants, belongs some of the mulk, in the apparent attribution of things to their causes, and that is in this world. As for the Day of Resurrection, everything returns to Allah.

But why did the Truth say ﴿wa ma fihinna﴾ (and whatever is in them), although the Truth made man vicegerent on earth, and man is rational, and it would have been right for the expression to favour the rational and say: wa man fihinna (and whoever is in them)? Because (man) is for the rational. The Truth by this intended to inform us that everything has become without choice, and has become compelled to what is willed of it. All are equal, rational and non-rational alike, so He says to us: ﴿and whatever is in them, and He is over all things competent.﴾ With this verse Surah al-Ma'idah concludes.
